Stir in the kharay masalay (whole spices: tej patta, elaichi, dalchini, laung) and enough namak so the water tastes like the sea. Bring to a rolling boil. Stir in the soaked and drained basmati chawal.

In the same degh (or a separate karahi), heat 3 tbsp tel (oil) on medium-high. Stir in the halved, peeled aloo. Cook them on each side for about 3-4 minutes until they're golden all over — you're not cooking them through, just building a crust that'll hold up.

In the same degh, Stir in the marinated gosht (meat) along with all the marinade. Turn the heat to high and bhunno (stir-Cook) for 10 minutes — hear aggressive sizzling, and the tamatar should start breaking down. and then reduce heat to low, cover with a tight lid.

Spread a layer of pudina (mint) leaves and hara dhaniya (coriander). gently spoon the parboiled chawal (rice) on top in an even layer — use a chamcha (ladle) and don't press down or you'll crush the grains.
Cook on the lowest possible flame for 25-30 minutes. Every peek releases steam and adds 5 minutes to the cooking time.

Turn off the heat but DO NOT open the lid yet. Let the biryani rest for 10 minutes — the residual steam finishes the cooking and lets the flavours settle. Try to keep the layers somewhat intact — this isn't a stir-Cook.

variants.name: Biryani with Yogurt Marination

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

ingredients.item: standard quantities zarda colour, kewra water, podina
ingredients.text: standard quantities zarda colour, kewra water, podina

instructions: In a large bowl, whisk yogurt smooth. Stir in adrak lehsan paste, lal mirch (1 tsp), dhania powder, haldi, garam masala, nimbu ras, 2 slit hari mirch, and salt. Stir in chicken pieces and mix until every surface is coated.
Take the marinated chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking.
Cook thinly sliced onions in oil/ghee to deep golden birista. In the same oil, Stir in remaining onion, soften, Stir in blended tomatoes, remaining 1 tsp lal mirch, and cook until oil rises.

Stir in the marinated chicken (along with all the yogurt clinging to it) to the masala. Cook on high heat 5 minutes, and then medium. The yogurt masala will cook down into a thick, flavourful coating on the chicken.
Parboil soaked basmati 6 minutes. Drain. Layer chicken masala in pot, Stir in rice in two layers with birista, colour, mint, and kewra.
Rest 10 minutes after dum.

variants.name: Bombay Biryani (Pakistani Style)

ingredients.text: 1 set Kharay Masalay (Whole Spices for rice water)

instructions: Warm 4 tablespoons of ghee or oil in a karahi over medium-high heat. Stir in the thinly sliced onions. Cook, stirring frequently, for 20-25 minutes until they turn a deep golden-amber colour and become crispy.
In the same ghee remaining in the karahi, Stir in the halved potatoes. Cook on medium-high heat, turning occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until the outside is golden and sealed.
In the same karahi, Stir in the meat pieces and stir over high heat for 3-4 minutes to colour the outside. Stir in the yoghurt and biryani masala. Stir well.

Stir in enough water to just cover the meat (about 1 cup for chicken, 2 cups for mutton). Cover the karahi and cook on low-medium heat until the meat is tender — chicken takes 20-25 minutes, mutton takes 45-60 minutes. If it looks too liquidy with 10 minutes.

In a large degh (pot) or separate pot, bring 3 litres of heavily salted water to a rolling boil (it should taste like mild seawater). Stir in the whole spices. Drain the soaked rice and Stir in to the boiling water.
In a large degh or pot, create layers. First, spread the meat masala as the bottom layer — scrape every last bit of sauce from the karahi. spread the parboiled rice over the top in an even layer.

Put the pot over high heat for 3 minutes until you hear active bubbling and see steam escaping. Reduce heat to the absolute minimum your stove can produce. Put a folded kitchen towel or thick tawa (griddle) between the pot and the flame — this creates a heat.
After 25 minutes, remove from heat.

variants.name: Hyderabadi Biryani
instructions: Start the marinade (minimum 4 hours before cooking — overnight is ideal). In a large bowl, Stir in your gosht (mutton) pieces. Pour in the whisked dahi (yoghurt), adrak-lehsan (ginger-garlic) paste, biryani masala, lal mirch (red chilli powder), and a generous 1.5 tsp namak (salt).

Bring a large pateela (pot) of water to a rolling boil — use at least 8 cups. Stir in all your saabut masalay (whole spices): tej patta (bay leaves), badi elaichi (black cardamom), choti elaichi (green cardamom), dalchini (cinnamon), laung (cloves), javitri (mace). Stir in enough namak (salt).

Cook the aloo (potatoes). While your rice soaks or boils, heat about 1 cup of oil in a karahi (wok) or deep pan over medium-high heat. Stir in the halved, peeled potatoes and Cook for about 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until they're deep golden all over.

Spread the RAW marinated gosht in an even layer across the bottom. Do NOT pre-cook the meat — this is kacchi biryani, and the whole point is that the meat cooks in the dum steam. Put the fried aloo on top of the meat, cut-side down.

Stir in the chawal (rice) layer. Gently spoon the parboiled rice over the meat and potato layer, spreading it evenly. Finally, pour 2-3 tablespoons of water gently down the SIDES of the pot (not over the rice).

Put the sealed degh on HIGH heat for exactly 8-10 minutes. comes the patience: reduce to the LOWEST possible flame your stove can manage. If you have a cast-iron tawa (flat griddle pan), Put it between the burner and the pot — this diffuses the heat beautifully and.

Turn off the heat completely. Let the pot sit, still sealed, for 15 minutes — this resting period lets the steam redistribute and the layers settle. Aim for some mixing, but also visible streaks of zafrani (saffron) rice, white rice, and masala-stained rice from the meat layer.

variants.name: Karachi Beef Biryani

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
2.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)
1 cup podina aur dhania (mint and fresh coriander)
3 tbsp zarda rang dissolved in milk (food colour in milk)

instructions: Beef needs time that chicken doesn't. In a pressure cooker, Stir in beef pieces with 2 cups water, 1 tsp adrak lehsan paste, 1 tsp salt, and 3 sabut garam masala pieces (bay leaf, cardamom, cloves). Pressure cook for 25-30 minutes after the first whistle, or simmer covered.
In a wide karahi, heat ghee over medium-high. Stir in thinly sliced onions (4 large) and Cook, stirring regularly, until they turn deep golden-brown. This takes a patient 18-20 minutes.

In the same ghee-rich karahi, Stir in remaining sliced onion and cook until soft. Stir in adrak lehsan paste and bhuno (Cook) for 2 minutes until raw smell disappears. Stir in blended tomatoes and cook until oil rises, about 10 minutes.

Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Stir in leftover beef stock (top up with plain water as needed), salt generously, and a few whole spices. Stir in soaked sela rice and cook 8-9 minutes — sela rice takes slightly longer than regular basmati.

In a heavy-bottomed deg or pot, start with the beef masala spread across the bottom. Stir in a layer of half the rice. Stir in remaining rice, top with remaining herbs, yellow colour in milk, and remaining birista.
Seal the pot with a tightly fitted lid (use dough rope if you have it) and Put on a tawa (flat griddle) over the lowest heat setting. Cook for 25-30 minutes.
After 30 minutes on dum, turn off heat and rest for 10 minutes. Use a large, flat spatula to gently turn the biryani from the edges inward in large folds — never stir vigorously.

variants.name: Karachi Prawn Biryani

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
1.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)
2 tbsp food colour dissolved in milk

instructions: Let them sit 10 minutes.
Warm oil in a karahi. Stir in thinly sliced onions and Cook until golden-brown, stirring regularly, about 15 minutes. Remove and drain.
In the same oil, Stir in sliced onion and cook until soft. Stir in adrak lehsan paste and Cook 1-2 minutes. Stir in blended tomatoes, lal mirch, salt, and cook until oil rises, about 8-10 minutes.
Boil well-salted water with a few whole spices. Stir in soaked basmati and cook 6 minutes to 70% done. Drain immediately.
Spread prawn masala in the pot. Stir in half the rice, scatter mint and coriander, drizzle colour and kewra, Stir in half the birista. Stir in remaining rice and repeat toppings.
Prawn biryani is at its absolute best the moment it comes off the heat. Garnish with a squeeze of fresh nimbu and a few sprigs of dhania.

variants.name: Sindhi Biryani

ingredients.text: 1 set Kharay Masalay (Whole Spices for Rice)
1 bunch each Pudina aur Dhaniya (Mint and Coriander)

instructions: Mix meat pieces with dahi (yoghurt), half the barista pyaz (fried onions), adrak lehsan paste (ginger-garlic paste), Sindhi biryani masala, and salt. Marinate for minimum 3 hours — overnight in the fridge is ideal.

Warm 3 tbsp tel (oil) in a heavy degh (pot) on high heat. Cook the halved aloo (potatoes) on both cut sides until golden — about 3-4 minutes per side. This crust prevents them from breaking apart during the slow cook in the masala.
In the same degh, Stir in the marinated meat with all its marinade. Turn heat to high. Stir in the chopped tamatar (tomatoes) and all the hari mirch (green chillies).
Bring a large degh of water to a rolling boil with kharay masalay (whole spices) and enough salt that the water tastes sea-salty. Stir in the soaked, drained basmati. Drain immediately.

Spread the meat and loose masala evenly across the bottom of the degh. Arrange the fried aloo halves prominently over the meat — they should be visible and numerous. Stir in a generous layer of pudina (mint) and hara dhaniya (coriander) — more than in Karachi biryani.
Seal the degh with foil pressed tight against the rim, and then Put the lid on top. Cook on the lowest possible heat for 25-30 minutes. Rest off heat, still sealed, for 10 minutes.

variants.name: Sindhi Lamb Biryani

ingredients.text: 1.1 lb lamb or mutton, bone in

ingredients.item: potatoes, peeled and chopped into chunks
ingredients.text: 9 oz potatoes, peeled and chopped into chunks

ingredients.item: a few pinches orange/yellow food colour
ingredients.text: a few pinches orange/yellow food colour

instructions: Prepare the garlic, minced; combine it with the yogurt, aromatics and measured spices, then allow the mixture to marinate.
Rinse and soak the rice. Boil it in salted water with the whole spices until about three-quarters cooked, then drain.
Cook the marinated mixture until the protein is tender and the masala is thick rather than watery.
Layer the masala and rice, add the reserved herbs and aromatics, cover tightly and finish over very low heat until the rice is tender.
Rest the covered pot for 10 minutes, then lift the rice gently from the bottom to serve.

variants.name: Multani Biryani

ingredients.text: 2.5 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
1.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Mix mutton with yogurt, adrak lehsan paste, lal mirch, garam masala, salt, and half the birista. Stir in soaked khubani (apricots) halved. Marinate minimum 3 hours, overnight preferred.
Warm ghee in a large karahi. Cook all sliced onions until very deep golden, 20-22 minutes. Remove, drain, and set aside.

In the reserved ghee, cook the marinated mutton on high heat for 8-10 minutes. Reduce heat, cover, and cook for 50-60 minutes until mutton is very tender, stirring occasionally. Stir in kishmish in the final 10 minutes.
Boil generously salted water. Stir in a few whole spices, the mint stalks, and soaked basmati. Parboil 7-8 minutes to 70% done.
Spread mutton masala in the pot. Stir in half the rice. Stir in remaining rice and repeat toppings generously.
Seal tightly and cook on tawa on lowest heat for 30-35 minutes. Rest 15 minutes before opening. Fold gently and garnish with remaining dry fruits and a final drizzle of warm ghee.

variants.name: South Punjab Mutton Biryani

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Mix mutton with yogurt, adrak lehsan paste, lal mirch, dhania powder, 1 tsp garam masala, salt, and half the crushed birista. Cover and marinate in the fridge overnight — minimum 4 hours if pressed for time.
Warm ghee in a large karahi. Stir in all 5 sliced onions at once. This is a large batch and will take 20-25 minutes to reach the right deep-brown colour.
In a large, heavy deg with the birista ghee, Stir in the marinated mutton. Cook on high heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring to prevent sticking. Reduce to medium and Stir in chopped tomatoes.
Bring a very large pot of salted water to a boil. Stir in mint stalks, 2 cardamom pods, and 1 bay leaf to the water for fragrance. Stir in soaked basmati and parboil for 7-8 minutes.
In the same deg used for mutton, spread the cooked masala evenly. Stir in 1/3 of the rice. Stir in another 1/3 rice.

Seal the deg tightly. If using dough to seal: take 500g atta (flour), Stir in water to make a stiff dough, roll into a thick rope, press around the rim, and press the lid firmly on top. Cook on a tawa on the lowest heat for 30-35 minutes.
REST, REVEAL, AND REJOICE: After 35 minutes, turn off heat and rest for 15 minutes before opening.

dish_families.name: Black-Eyed Peas with Spinach and Dill

variants.name: Black-Eyed Peas with Spinach and Dill
variants.dish_family: Black-Eyed Peas with Spinach and Dill
instructions: Stir in black-eyed peas to stockpot. Stir in 4-5 cups water, and salt to taste. Bring to boil, and let peas simmer until soft.
In a separate wok or large frying pan, heat oil. Stir in cumin seeds and mustard seeds. When they begin to pop, Stir in the crushed garlic, kadi pata, and chopped chili.
Cook for roughly 30 seconds on medium low heat. Begin to Stir in chopped spinach in batches, folding it in with the spices. Stir in chopped dill.
Pour over the spinach and dill mixture into the pot of black-eyed peas. Stir in 1 cup water, red chili flakes, and salt. Bring to boil.
Garnish with fresh dill and finely chopped chili, and serve with paratha or roti.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Black-Eyed Peas with Spinach and Dill

variants.name: Boneless Chicken Achari Recipe

ingredients.text: 1 medium-sized yellow onion (thinly sliced in half rings)

ingredients.item: red chili powder ((preferably Kashmiri red chili powder) )
ingredients.text: 1 teaspoon red chili powder ((preferably Kashmiri red chili powder) )

instructions: In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat oil. Stir in whole spices (fenugreek seed, fennel seeds and nigella seeds) and Cook on medium heat until aromatic.
Stir in sliced onion and continue to Cook on medium heat until evenly soft and brown, about 5-7 minutes.
Lower heat and Stir in crushed ginger and garlic. Cook for 30 seconds to 1 minute.
Stir in ground spices and Cook until they stop smelling raw.
Increase heat to high and Stir in crushed tomatoes. Mix well and stir on high heat until the oil begins to separate from the tomato-onion base.
Stir in chicken and sear on high heat until no longer pink.
Stir in 1⁄4 cup water and bring to simmer. Partially cover the pot and let the chicken cook for about 10 minutes.
Lower heat and Stir in in whisked yogurt. Mix well.
Remove from heat and stir in mixed pickle if using.

dish_families.name: Borani Banjan Recipe (Afghan Eggplant with Yogurt)

variants.name: Borani Banjan Recipe (Afghan Eggplant with Yogurt)
variants.dish_family: Borani Banjan Recipe (Afghan Eggplant with Yogurt)

ingredients.item: Italian style eggplant or 2 small ones
ingredients.text: 1 large Italian style eggplant or 2 small ones (sliced crosswise, about 1/2-inch thick)
1 large yellow onion or 2 small ones (halved and thinly sliced)
1 teaspoon red chili powder (preferably Kashmiri red chili powder)

ingredients.item: full-fat yogurt preferably 1/4 of it will be sour yogurt
ingredients.text: 2 cups full-fat yogurt preferably 1/4 of it will be sour yogurt (lightly whisked)

instructions: In a frying pan, heat 1⁄2 cup of oil over medium heat. When it begins shimmer, Stir in the sliced eggplant in batches. Cook each side until a medium brown, 1 to 3 minutes.

In a large heavy-bottom pot, heat remaining (about 1⁄4 cup) of oil over medium-low heat. Stir in sliced onions and Cook until soft and translucent, about 7 minutes. Stir in 1⁄2 teaspoon of crushed garlic, and Cook for a few seconds until it stops smelling raw.
Stir in tomatoes, green chili, salt, turmeric and red chili powder. Stir until well-mixed. Cover the pot and let it simmer on medium-low heat for 5 minutes.
Dial heat to low, cover, and let it steam for 10 minutes.
While the eggplant steams, transfer yogurt to a flat serving dish and lightly whisk until it has an even consistency. Stir in 1 teaspoon of crushed garlic.
Carefully spoon the eggplant, tomato and onion mixture, and layer it on top of the whisked yogurt. Garnish with dried mint, red chili flakes and pomegranate seeds.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Borani Banjan Recipe (Afghan Eggplant with Yogurt)

dish_families.name: Box Patties with Chicken and White Sauce

variants.name: Box Patties with Chicken and White Sauce
variants.dish_family: Box Patties with Chicken and White Sauce

ingredients.item: samosa wrappers or 12 egg roll wrappers
ingredients.text: 24 samosa wrappers or 12 egg roll wrappers

ingredients.item: Additional flour and water to create a 'glue' for the wrappers
ingredients.text: Additional flour and water to create a 'glue' for the wrappers

instructions: * Put a 8-inch saucepan over medium heat and melt the butter.
* Stir in in the flour, stirring so that the butter coats the flour as it darkens and takes on a nutty aroma.
* Slowly Stir in the milk whisking briskly to Mix.
* Once the milk is in Stir in the remaining ingredients and stir frequently till the sauce becomes nice and thick.
* Mix a tbsp of flour with two of water and stir well.
Put a dollop of the chicken mix in the centre and fold over to shut, sealing with additional flour and water.
* Once you are done and then shallow Cook them to golden brown crispness and serve hot.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Box Patties with Chicken and White Sauce

variants.name: Bun Kabab

ingredients.item: eggs plus one white, whipped together for battering
ingredients.text: 2 eggs plus one white, whipped together for battering

ingredients.item: red onions sliced into thin rings, submerge in cold water
ingredients.text: 2-3 red onions sliced into thin rings, submerge in cold water

instructions: Mix all the ingredients from the Daal through to the 1/2 cup onion in a pot, bring to a boil and simmer until the daal is cooked through. This takes 35-45 minutes but requires no active cooking.
Turn up the heat and dry the daal up until the moisture is completely gone.
Remove the herby mix and replace it with the daal, pureeing until a thick shapeable mixture forms.
Stir in the chopped mix from earlier, a squeeze of lemon juice, pulse a few times and adjust for seasoning.
Shape into 16 kababs or according to the size of your buns.
Whip your eggs well to give them some body, dip each kabab in the eggs and Cook for 1.5-2 minutes on each side on medium heat, pressing lightly.
Blend all the ingredients in a blender, adjust for seasoning.
Blend all the ingredients (but only 2 tbsp yoghurt) in a blender. Once it's combined whisk the other two tbsp in with a fork, adjust for seasoning.
Warm your bans on a hot pan on both sides, lightly greasing the pan if needed.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Drain your boiled chana dal THOROUGHLY — this is the most common mistake and the reason homemade bun kebabs fall apart. Drain in a colander, shake it well, and then spread the dal on a clean kitchen towel or plate for a full 10 minutes to air-dry.

In a large bowl, Mix the mashed chana dal with the mashed aloo (potatoes), chopped pyaz (onion), chopped hari mirch (green chillies), lal mirch (red chilli powder), zeera powder (cumin), chaat masala, namak (salt), and half the hara dhaniya (coriander). Mix everything together with your hands — squeeze.
If the edges crack while shaping, the mixture is too dry — wet your hands more or Stir in a tiny splash of water.

Warm the tel (oil) on a flat tawa (griddle) or heavy frying pan over medium heat. Don't press them down — let them cook undisturbed for 3-4 minutes. After 3 minutes, check the underside by lifting an edge with a spatula — it should be deeply golden and.

Pour about 2 tablespoons of beaten anda (egg) directly OVER the flipped patty. Cook for another 2-3 minutes until the egg side is golden and crispy, and the new bottom is cooked through. The patty should be wearing a beautiful, crispy egg coat on one side.
Put them cut-side down on the tawa (move the patties to one side or use a second pan). Press gently and toast for about 1 minute until the cut surface is golden and slightly crispy.
Spread a generous layer of hari chutney (green coriander-mint sauce) on the bottom bun. Stir in sliced raw pyaz (onion) rings and the remaining hara dhaniya (coriander).

variants.name: Bun Kebab Lahori Style
instructions: Set aside for 15 minutes — they'll soften slightly and turn pink.
Warm a flat tawa over medium heat. Spread a thin layer of ghee or butter on the cut sides. Toast face-down on the tawa for 1-2 minutes until golden and slightly crisp.
In a flat karahi or tawa, heat a little oil. Cook shami kebab patties for 2-3 minutes per side until crispy and hot.
In the same pan, Stir in a tiny drizzle of oil. Season with a pinch of salt and chilli. Cook 1 minute per side until just set.
Stir in a shami kebab patty. Stir in the egg omelette. Stir in sliced tomato and pickled onion rings.

variants.name: Egg Bun Kebab — Karachi Street Style
instructions: Split buns and toast cut-side down on a buttered tawa over medium heat for 1-2 minutes until golden.
Warm oil in a karahi over medium heat. Stir in cumin seeds — they should sizzle immediately. Stir in onion and cook for 3-4 minutes until translucent.
Beat eggs with red chilli powder and salt. Pour over the onion-tomato mixture.
Continue folding until the egg is just cooked through — not wet and liquid, but not hard and dry. Remove from heat.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Egg Bun Kebab — Karachi Street Style

variants.name: Busy Day Achari Bhindi

ingredients.preparation: roughly 2.5-3 cups , frozen & sliced or fresh.
ingredients.text: 300 g okra (roughly 2.5-3 cups , frozen & sliced or fresh.)

instructions: Mix all the ingredients in a pan.
Warm 3-4 tbsp oil in a saute pan and when it starts to shimmer Stir in all the ingredients and cook on medium high heat for 4-5 minutes.
Reduce heat a little and cook partially covered, stirring occasionally until cooked through. Do not stir too often because that will break the okra.

When it is done (15-20 minutes) and then Stir in a squeeze of lemon juice and adjust seasoning. If you like a more charred bhindi and then you can crank the heat up and saute for a few minutes to develop that depth.

variants.name: Carrot and Zucchini Fritters

ingredients.preparation: grated on the large holes of a box grater
ingredients.text: 1/2 cup carrots, (grated on the large holes of a box grater)

ingredients.preparation: grated on the large holes of a box grater
ingredients.text: 1/2 cup zucchini, (grated on the large holes of a box grater)

ingredients.preparation: grated on the large holes of a box grater
ingredients.text: 1/2 cup potato, (grated on the large holes of a box grater)
3/4 cup cold water, (divided into 1/2 cup + 1/4 cup)

instructions: Mix all ingredients, except for water, in a medium-sized mixing bowl.
Mix well to Mix, ensuring that the chickpea flour has coated all the vegetables and herbs well.
Stir in 1⁄2 cup of cold water and stir till it transforms into a thick batter.
Warm 1⁄2-inch of oil in a large skillet, on medium-high heat, to 350F degrees.
Cook about 60-90 seconds per side, until the fritters turn golden-brown and are cooked through.
Remove the fritters from the oil and transfer them to a large platter lined with paper towels.

variants.name: Cauliflower Fritters

ingredients.text: 1/2-3/4 cup finely minced onion (approx one onion)

ingredients.preparation: I usually put 1 level tsp salt
ingredients.text: salt and pepper to taste (I usually put 1 level tsp salt)
1 tbsp chopped mint (1 tsp if using dried)

instructions: Boil the cauliflower florets in a medium pan for 4-5 minutes or until tender enough to mash but not totally mushy.
Drain the florets and tip them into a bowl, mash lightly.
Gently toss in the flour, spices, baking powder, onions and and then Stir in the eggs and mix just to coat - don't over mix.
Stir in a little of the 'cauliflower water' using just enough to get a slightly runny batter.
Warm oil in a saute pan or a frying pan and when it's hot carefully Put large spoonfuls of the batter in the oil, making sure it leave space enough to flip between your fritters.
Cook for 3-4 minutes on each side until a beautiful golden.
Use a slotted spoon to remove the fritters from oil, and drain of excess grease on a wire rack or a paper towel before serving.
Mix the yogurt ingredients in a bowl, whisking well.

variants.name: Chaat Masala Recipe - Pakistani (Quick & Easy!)
instructions: Put a clean skillet on medium high heat, as soon as it's hot Stir in the coriander and cumin seeds, moving them around frequently until they smell fragrant.
While the seeds are cooling mix the remaining ingredients in a spice grinder or mini blender and and then Stir in the seeds.

variants.name: Fruit Chaat

ingredients.preparation: use with restraint since chaat masala is already salty
ingredients.text: Salt and pepper to taste (use with restraint since chaat masala is already salty)

instructions: Season with salt, pepper and chaat masala. Stir, taste, adjust.
Squeeze the juice of the orange on the salad, and stir to coat.
Sprinkle sugar, and stir to coat again.

variants.name: Papdi Chaat

ingredients.preparation: available at South Asian specialty stores
ingredients.text: ~15-20 papdi wafers (available at South Asian specialty stores)

ingredients.item: (120g)cucumber, deseeded with a spoon and finely diced
ingredients.text: 1 cup (120g)cucumber, deseeded with a spoon and finely diced

ingredients.preparation: I used Roma, and discarded the seeds
ingredients.text: 1 cup (115g) tomatoes, diced (I used Roma, and discarded the seeds)

ingredients.item: red Kashmiri chili powder or Aleppo pepper or Korean gochugaru
ingredients.text: 1 tsp red Kashmiri chili powder or Aleppo pepper or Korean gochugaru
1/2 cup 8 Tbsp fresh coriander, coarsely chopped

instructions: Warm a large skillet over medium-high heat and Stir in the vegetable oil. Carefully tip them into the skillet and sauté, stirring frequently, for 8-10 minutes, or until crispy and golden brown. Transfer the crispy potatoes to a bowl and toss with sea salt and 1⁄2 tsp ground.

Layer the chickpeas first, followed by the crispy potatoes, crumbled papdi wafers, cucumbers, diced tomatoes, onions, and pomegranate arils. Repeat with another layer of all the ingredients, creating a stacked effect.
Garnish with sliced red chili and serve immediately.

variants.name: Cardamom Tea: Pakistani Chai

ingredients.text: 0.5 cup full-cream milk, or to taste

instructions: Stir in boiling water and cover with a teacosy.
Let it steep for 10 minutes or until the colour deepens and intensifies.

variants.name: Masala Chai Ice Cream
instructions: Measure the liquid, sweetener and spices.
Simmer the spices in water long enough to release their aroma; add tea or other infusing ingredients as specified.
Add milk or the remaining liquid, heat gently, then strain or blend as appropriate.
Taste for sweetness and serve hot or well chilled according to the recipe.

variants.name: Masala Chai Recipe

ingredients.text: 5 teaspoons loose black tea or teabags

instructions: Bring 4 cups water to boil. Reduce to simmer and Stir in ground spices and tea. Let it simmer for 2 minutes.
Whisk in milk. Bring to boil.
Lower heat and let milk simmer for 8 minutes, whisking occasionally and skimming any residue from the top.
Remove from heat, stir in sugar or sweetener.
Strain and pour in mugs or teacups.

variants.name: Kashmiri Chai

ingredients.text: 2 cups ice cold water (I mix mine with ice)

instructions: Stir in all the ingredients except the ice cold water to a pot with 8 cups of cold tap water.
Bring to a boil, simmer for one hour or until the liquid is halved, it's okay if it reduces a little more but please do cook it down.
Pour the ice cold water from a height into the tea concentrate.
Pour back and forth from bowl to bowl or use a ladle to drop it back into the bowl from a height to aerate the tea.
After a full 5-8 minutes of doing this the foam the tea produces will take on a rich bodied pink.
Bring the tea mix back to a boil, bring to a boil.

To make each cup of tea: Take a ladle (about 1/3 of a cup) of the kahwa, bring to a boil, Stir in 2/3 cup milk and a splash of water. Cook for 2-3 minutes and serve topped with a scant spoon of crushed pistachios.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Stir in Kashmiri tea leaves and 4 cups of cold water to a saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Stir in baking soda — the mixture will foam up and turn from brown to a dark reddish-maroon.
Reduce heat to medium and simmer the dark brew for 8-10 minutes until it deepens further and reduces slightly.
Remove the pan from heat for 30 seconds. and then pour in cold milk all at once and stir.
Put the pan back on medium heat. Stir in salt and crushed cardamom. Stir and bring just to a gentle simmer — do NOT boil or the milk may curdle and the colour will dull.
Pour through a fine strainer into cups or mugs.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: In a saucepan, bring to boil 1 cup of water, tea leaves, salt, cinnamon, star anise and cardamom.

When it boils and is frothy, Stir in the baking soda and whisk vigorously by filling a ladle with tea and throwing it back into the pot from a height (known as phantna in Urdu). Do this for about 10 seconds, and then Stir in the rest of.
Continue to boil until the tea becomes a bright red color.
Reduce the heat to medium low and Stir in the milk. Whisk the tea vigorously until it is slightly frothy.
Stir in sugar (or salt, depending on how you like it), pour into cup and sprinkle crushed pistachios on top.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Guest Post by Hina: A Daughter's Tribute + Recipe for Kashmiri Chai

alternate_names: Guest Post by Hina: A Daughter's Tribute + Recipe for Kashmiri Chai

variants.name: Karak Chai — KP Street Tea

ingredients.text: 3 tsp pattiyan (loose CTC black tea leaves)

instructions: Stir in water to a small patila (saucepan). Stir in tea leaves and crushed cardamom (and ginger if using). Bring to a full rolling boil.
Pour in the milk. Stir and bring back to a simmer over medium heat. Do NOT let it boil over — watch it carefully.
Stir in sugar and stir to dissolve. Pour through a fine tea strainer into small glasses or cups.
On cold Peshawar days, Stir in half a cinnamon stick and one black cardamom to the water phase along with the green cardamom.

variants.name: Adrak Wali Chai — Ginger Tea
instructions: In a small patila, Mix water, crushed ginger, cardamom and black pepper (if using). Bring to a boil and simmer for 3 minutes to let the ginger's flavour fully infuse. Stir in tea leaves and simmer for another 2 minutes.
Pour in the milk. Bring to a near-boil over medium heat — watch it carefully so it doesn't boil over. Simmer for 2-3 minutes.
For a medicinal healing version, Stir in 1/2 tsp honey (shehed) to each cup after straining, a squeeze of lemon juice, and a small piece of cinnamon stick to the brew.
This slightly aerated pour creates a small natural foam on the surface.

variants.name: Doodh Pati Chai — Pakistani Milk Tea

ingredients.text: 2 tsp Chai Pati (Loose Leaf Black Tea)

instructions: In a small pateela (saucepan), Stir in 2 cups of full-fat doodh (milk). Put on medium heat.
When the milk is warm — not yet boiling, around 60-70°C — Stir in the chai pati (loose leaf tea). Do not Stir in tea to cold milk; the tea needs heat to release its tannins and colour properly.

Bring the milk-tea mixture slowly to a boil on medium heat, stirring frequently. The chai will turn from white to cream to a beautiful deep reddish-brown as the tea releases its colour and flavour into the milk.
For extra flavour and froth, experienced chai makers 'pull' the chai: use a ladle to scoop chai from the pot and pour it back in from a height of 20-30cm.
Stir in cheeni (sugar) and stir until dissolved. Strain through a fine mesh chalni (sieve) directly into cups.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Doodh Pati Chai — Pakistani Milk Tea

variants.name: Kala Chana Chaat
instructions: Mix the ingredients for the kala chana and set aside.
Whisk the yoghurt ingredients until combined and smooth.
Warm a little oil in a pan and Stir in in your potatoes, the garlic, and salt, sauteeing on medium heat until the potatoes start to develop bronzey bits.
Stir in the chili powder and cumin powder, cook for another half a minute and take off the heat.
Stir in papri or sev right before serving, but know it is delightful without!

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Drain and rinse your chickpeas. If they are not soft and then Stir in them to a pot with boiling water and simmer for 5-6 miutes or until softened and drain.
You can make chana chaat ahead of time, but if making it a day ahead and then mix in the onions and tomatoes before serving, upto a few hours before is fine.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: To prepare the chutney, Put tamarind in a large heatproof bowl and pour roughly 3 to 3 1⁄2 cups of hot water. Once you have removed all the seeds, strain the tamarind juice.
Bring to simmer, and let it cook for 45 minutes to 1 hour until you get the desired consistency. Remove from heat and Put in airtight jar.
To get started on the chaat, drain canned chickpeas and Put in large bowl. Stir in diced potato, onion, and tomato. Stir in salt, chaat masala and 4 tablespoon of tamarind chutney.

variants.name: Mixed Plate Aloo Chana Chaat - Street Style

ingredients.preparation: skip it if you don't have any
ingredients.text: 1/2 cup mint (skip it if you don't have any)

ingredients.item: strained tamarind pulp or 2 tbsp tamarind chutney
ingredients.text: 3 tbsp strained tamarind pulp or 2 tbsp tamarind chutney

ingredients.item: onion, thinly sliced and soaked in water
ingredients.text: 1 onion, thinly sliced and soaked in water

ingredients.item: potato boiled and cubed into 1 cm pieces
ingredients.text: 1 potato boiled and cubed into 1 cm pieces

ingredients.item: dry roasted and coarsely ground cumin and coriander
ingredients.text: 1 tbsp dry roasted and coarsely ground cumin and coriander

instructions: Whisk the yogurt ingredients and set aside. If you feel the yogurt is very thick and then Stir in 1/4 cup more water.
Mix your dry masala (if making) and set aside.
Warm the oil in a small pan for the chickpeas on medium heat.
When the oil is hot Stir in the mustard seeds and nigella seeds.
Stir in the chili flakes, give it a quick stir and Stir in the chickpeas.

Stir in the salt, chili powder, cumin powder and 1/2 cup of water and cook on low heat till the chickpeas are tender. If they start to dry up and then Stir in more water - Aim for the mixture to have some liquid.
When the chickpeas are tender mix in the chaat masala and set aside.
Assembly: You can start with yogurt first or just layer chickpeas and then potatoes and then yoghurt.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Mixed Plate Aloo Chana Chaat - Street Style

variants.name: Karachi Chana Chaat

ingredients.text: 1/2 tsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)

instructions: If using canned kabuli chana (chickpeas), drain them through a sifter and rinse thoroughly under cold water — canned liquid is starchy and will make your chaat gloopy. If using dried chickpeas, soak overnight in cold water (they'll roughly double in size), and then boil with a pinch.
Put in a small bowl, cover with cold salted water, and leave for 10 minutes.
In a small bartan (bowl), whisk the dahi (yoghurt) until completely smooth with no lumps. Stir in a pinch of namak (salt) and a tiny pinch of zeera powder (cumin). Whisk again.

In a large, wide bartan (bowl), Mix the chickpeas, drained pyaz, and tamatar. Stir in chaat masala, zeera powder (cumin), and lal mirch powder (red chilli). Toss everything together gently — Aim for to mix without crushing the chickpeas.
Transfer the spiced chickpea mixture onto your serving plate or into individual bowls. Spoon the cold dahi over the top — don't mix it in, just let it pool and settle.
Scatter the sev (crispy chickpea noodles) over the entire surface — this goes on absolutely last, because sev loses its crunch within 2 minutes of touching the dahi and chutneys.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: If using tinned chanay, drain and rinse well under cold water. If using dried, boil soaked chickpeas until tender but not mushy — they should hold their shape when pressed.
In a large bowl, Mix chickpeas, tomatoes, onion and green chilli. Stir in tamarind chutney, lemon juice, chaat masala and salt.
Transfer to serving bowls or a large plate.

variants.name: Aloo Chana Masala or Aloo Chole Recipe (Potatoes & Chickpea Curry)

ingredients.item: potatoes cut into 1/2 cm thick pieces
ingredients.text: 1 cup potatoes cut into 1/2 cm thick pieces (130-150g, 2 small or 1 big)
1 inch ginger (grated) or 2 tsp ginger paste

ingredients.item: garlic crushed or 1 tsp garlic paste
ingredients.text: 4 cloves garlic crushed or 1 tsp garlic paste

ingredients.item: as many green chillies as you can eat - I used 4-5 thinly sliced
ingredients.text: as many green chillies as you can eat - I used 4-5 thinly sliced

instructions: Warm 1/4 cup of oil in a large saucepan or wok on medium high heat and Stir in cumin seeds, cloves, peppers, and kalonji.
Stir in onions and Cook till the edges are caramelly but not brown.
Stir in the ginger and garlic, stir for a minute and then Stir in the rest of your dry spices i.e.
Saute for 30 seconds and then throw in the chopped tomatoes, cook till 'bhunn' i.e masalas form a cohesive paste and oil rises above them.

Stir in your chickpeas, potatoes. Stir well, and then Stir in one cup of hot water and cover your pan. Bring the mixture to a boil and then let it simmer for 15 minutes or until the potatoes are done.
Taste for SALT - you may need to Stir in more.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Aloo Chana Masala or Aloo Chole Recipe (Potatoes & Chickpea Curry)

variants.name: Chana Masala

ingredients.text: 2 medium tomatoes, (blanched, skins removed and diced1)

ingredients.item: can of pre-cooked organic chickpeas/garbanzo beans
ingredients.text: 400 g can of pre-cooked organic chickpeas/garbanzo beans

instructions: Put a saucepan on medium-high heat and Stir in oil and garlic. When the garlic begins to smell fragrant (make sure it doesn't start to brown), Stir in paprika, cumin powder and turmeric powder. Sauté for 1-2 minutes.
Stir in can of garbanzo beans, including the liquid they are immersed in. Stir to Mix.
Stir in diced tomatoes, turn flame to medium-low and cover with lid for 10 minutes and allow to simmer.
Remove lid, Stir in salt to taste and the julienned ginger. Gently stir.
Garnish with herbs and serve with lime or lemon wedges and rice or bread.

variants.name: Easy Bhuna Chana Masala - Chickpea Curry
instructions: Prepare all ingredients before heating the pan.
Warm the cooking fat and cook onion, diced finely, Kashmiri red chilli powder until softened and aromatic.
Stir in Kashmiri red chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder, whole cumin seeds, cumin powder, then add the chickpeas, drained and coat it thoroughly in the masala.
Add the listed liquid ingredients as needed, cover and simmer until the main ingredient is fully cooked.
Reduce the sauce to the intended consistency, adjust the seasoning and finish with coriander powder.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Easy Bhuna Chana Masala - Chickpea Curry
source_attributions.author: Fatima Cooks

variants.name: Lahori Channay
instructions: Drain your overnight-soaked chanay (chickpeas) and put them in a bari degh (large pot) with 6 cups of fresh water. Bring to a boil over high heat, and then reduce to medium and let them cook until tender — about 40-45 minutes in a regular pot, or 4-5. Do NOT drain them — you'll need about 1 cup of that gorgeous brown.

In a separate pateela (cooking pot), heat the tel (oil) over medium heat until it shimmers. Stir in the saabut zeera (whole cumin seeds). Immediately Stir in the chopped pyaz (onions) to the crackling zeera. Stir well to coat in the oil. Bhunno (Cook) the pyaz on medium heat, stirring every minute or so, until they turn golden brown — about 7-8.

Stir in the adrak-lehsan (ginger-garlic) paste to the browned pyaz. Bhunno (stir-Cook) for about 1 minute — Continue until the raw smell disappears and a rich, cooked garlic aroma hits you. Stir in the chopped tamatar (tomatoes), lal mirch (red chilli powder), haldi (turmeric), dhaniya (coriander) powder, and. Begins the bhunna (stir-frying) — the most important technique in Pakistani cooking. Cook this.

Stir in the boiled chanay to the masala, along with about 1 cup of their dark chai-infused cooking water. Stir well so every chickpea gets coated in that gorgeous masala. Stir in the chana masala and ground anardana (dried pomegranate). Stir to distribute evenly.

Reduce heat to low and let the channay simmer on dum (gentle steam) for 20-25 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes or so. The gravy should reduce and thicken until it clings to each chickpea like a thick coating. If it gets too thick, Stir in a splash of. Turn off the heat. Sprinkle garam masala over the top and stir gently —.

variants.name: Chapati

ingredients.text: 1 tsp tail ya ghee (oil or ghee)

instructions: If using salt, Stir in it and mix into the flour. Stir in warm water a little at a time — start with 1⁄2 cup and mix after each addition. Stir in water until the dough comes together.
Knead the dough for 7–8 minutes — longer than for paratha. Push forward with the heel of your hand, fold back, turn 90 degrees, and repeat.
Cover the dough ball with a damp cloth or an inverted bowl and leave for 20–30 minutes minimum.
Roll each piece between your palms into a smooth ball with no cracks on the surface — cracks indicate the dough needs a touch more water or kneading.

Dust a dough ball lightly in dry flour and Put on your chakla (rolling board). Use your belan (rolling pin) to roll from the centre outward, applying even pressure. Roll until the chapati is about 20–22 cm across and thin enough that you can just see your hand.

COOK ON THE TAWA — FIRST STAGE: Heat your tawa (flat griddle pan) over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes. Cook the second side for 30–45 seconds — see light golden-brown spots forming on the cooked side.
COOK ON THE FLAME — THE PUFF STAGE: This is the moment.

Transfer the puffed chapati to a roti basket or plate lined with a cloth. Cover to keep warm and repeat with remaining dough balls. Cook and serve in batches — chapati is best eaten within 5 minutes of coming off the flame.

variants.name: Chapli Kabab Recipe

ingredients.text: 6 tbsp wheat flour or gram flour (atta or besan)

ingredients.preparation: all the seeds and insides removed, finely diced
ingredients.text: 2 medium tomatoes (all the seeds and insides removed, finely diced)

ingredients.preparation: kasoori methi OR 2 tbsp fresh fenugreek, chopped
ingredients.text: 1 tbsp dried fenugreek (kasoori methi OR 2 tbsp fresh fenugreek, chopped)

ingredients.item: minced meat, finely minced and at least 20% fat
ingredients.text: 2.2 lb minced meat, finely minced and at least 20% fat

instructions: Combine the minced meat, finely minced and at least 20% fat with the yogurt, onion, of garlic, ginger, chopped green chillies and coriander seeds, cumin seeds, bay leaf, chopped green chillies, chilli flakes, black pepper; marinate for the time available.
Shape or skewer the mixture as appropriate, keeping portions even so they cook at the same rate.
Grill, roast or pan-cook until browned outside and safely cooked through at the centre.
Rest briefly and finish with coriander seeds, ginger, of coriander.

variants.name: Bannu Chapli Kebab — The Original

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp Dumba fat or cooking oil

instructions: Mix minced beef with all ingredients: dried pomegranate seeds, coriander, tomato, onion, green chilies, ginger-garlic paste, crushed coriander seeds, cumin, salt, and egg. Mix with your hands for 3-4 minutes — really work it together until uniform and sticky.
Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes minimum.
Take a handful of mixture (about 100g). The flat shape is the whole point: more surface area = more crust.
Warm oil or dumba fat in a wide, heavy pan on high heat until smoking. Stir in the chapli kebabs — don't crowd. Cook 4-5 minutes until the bottom is deeply crusted and brown.
Flip once (only once) and cook 3-4 minutes on the other side. The kebab should have a deep golden-brown, almost crispy crust on both sides. Don't fiddle — let the heat do the work.
Drain on paper towels for 1 minute.

variants.name: Beef Chapli Kebab

ingredients.text: 6 tbsp beef tallow ya tel (beef tallow or oil)

instructions: Cut tomato in half, squeeze out seeds and excess juice. Adding seeds makes chapli kebab too wet and the discs won't hold shape.
Mix all ingredients including the deseeded tomato pieces, pomegranate seeds, and crushed coriander. Mix firmly for 5-6 minutes.
Wet hands and press mixture into flat, round discs about 3-4 inches in diameter and 1/2 inch thick.
Warm beef tallow or oil in a flat pan on medium-high. Shallow-Cook chapli kebabs for 5-6 minutes per side. Do not crowd the pan — Cook 2-3 at a time for proper heat.
The top and bottom should be deep brown with the sides slightly crisper. Drain on paper and serve immediately.

variants.name: Chicken Chapli Kebab

ingredients.text: 500 g raan ka qeema (minced chicken thigh)
3 tbsp charbi ya makhan (fat or butter)
1.5 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)

instructions: Mix minced butter or fat into the chicken mince first, before adding other ingredients.
Deseed and dry the tomato. Stir in all remaining ingredients to the fattened mince. Mix firmly for 5-6 minutes.
Refrigerate for 1 hour minimum. Chicken chapli mixture is softer than beef and needs the chill to firm up enough to shape and hold in the pan.
Shape into flat discs from cold mixture — work quickly.
Shallow Cook on medium heat (not high — chicken burns). 4-5 minutes per side. Don't increase heat trying to darken it or the inside will be raw.
Once the bottom is set and brown, they flip cleanly.

variants.name: Peshawari Chapli Kebab
instructions: Put the coarsely ground keema (beef mince) in a large bowl. Stir in the diced pyaz (onion), deseeded and diced tamatar (tomatoes), chopped hari mirch (green chillies), hara dhaniya (fresh coriander), crushed anardana (pomegranate seeds), crushed dhania saboot (coriander seeds), whole zeera (cumin seeds), anda (egg), makki ka.
Wet your hands — this prevents sticking.
Put a large tawa (flat griddle pan) or heavy frying pan over high heat. Stir in the charbi (bone marrow fat) or ghee. Let it heat until it's shimmering and almost smoking — see tiny wisps of smoke.

Carefully slide the patties into the hot charbi — use a flat spatula to lower them gently, laying them away from you (so any splatter goes the other direction). Cook for 3-4 minutes WITHOUT moving them. The bottom is forming a crispy, golden-brown crust.
Using a wide spatula, flip each kebab in one confident motion. Cook for another 3-4 minutes.
Stir in a dollop of hari chutney (green chutney) if you have it.

variants.name: Swat Chapli Kebab — Valley Mountain Version

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp Sabut dhania crushed (coriander seeds, crushed)

instructions: Mix keema with all ingredients until well combined.
Cover and refrigerate 30-60 minutes.
Swat chaplis are thicker than Bannu — shape oval patties about 1.5-2cm thick.
Unlike Bannu chaplis (which cook on very high heat for a thin crust), Swat chaplis need medium-high heat to cook through without burning the outside. Cook 5-6 minutes per side.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Swat Chapli Kebab — Valley Mountain Version

variants.name: Hunza Chapshuro

ingredients.text: 1 large handful Hara Dhania (Fresh Green Coriander)

instructions: In a large bartan (bowl), mix 2.5 cups of atta (whole wheat flour) with half a teaspoon of salt. Make a well in the centre and begin adding warm water gradually — start with half a cup, mix with your fingers in circular motions, and then keep adding.

In a bartan, Mix the minced qeema (beef or mutton), very finely chopped onion, chopped green coriander (dhania), finely chopped green chillies, half tsp black pepper, half tsp cumin, and half tsp salt. Mix thoroughly with your hands — really squeeze and press everything together for 2 minutes.

Divide the rested dough into 4 equal balls — each about the size of a small fist. On a lightly floured surface, roll one ball into a circle about 20-22cm in diameter (roughly the size of a dinner plate) and about 3-4mm thick.
Fold the empty half of the dough circle over the filled half to create a half-moon shape.

COOK ON THE TAWA — FIRST SIDE: Heat a large tawa (flat griddle) or heavy frying pan over medium heat. No oil needed for the first side — dry cook on the tawa first. Cook on medium heat for 4-5 minutes until the bottom is golden-brown with darker.
The cooked side should be beautifully golden-brown. Cook the second side for another 4-5 minutes until equally golden-brown.
Transfer the tawa-cooked Chapshuro to a baking tray and Put in a pre-heated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 8-10 minutes.

BRUSH, CUT, AND SERVE: Remove from the oven (or tawa) and immediately brush the top surface with a light coating of ghee or butter while still hot. Cut each Chapshuro into 3-4 wedges, like a pizza (hence the nickname).

variants.name: Chicken Chapshuro — Valley Variation
instructions: Knead 5-8 minutes, rest 20 minutes.
Mix raw minced chicken with onion, coriander, mint, green chilies, ginger, cumin, and remaining salt. The herbs Stir in moisture to compensate for the leaner chicken meat.
Stir in 3-4 tbsp filling.
On a medium-low tawa, cook 5-7 minutes per side until golden with dark speckles.
After both sides are browned, cover the tawa with a lid and cook on low heat 3-4 more minutes.
Stir in butter around the bread in the final minute.

variants.name: Hunza Chapshuro — Beef-Stuffed Mountain Bread
instructions: Mix atta, salt, and warm water into a soft, pliable dough. Knead 5-8 minutes until smooth. Rest covered for 20 minutes.
Mix raw minced beef with onion, coriander, green chili, cumin, black pepper, and 0.5 tsp salt. Don't cook the filling — it cooks inside the bread. Mix well.
Warm a dry tawa (or heavy flat pan) on medium-low heat. Cook 6-8 minutes per side — the bread should be deeply golden-brown and speckled.
In the final minute, Stir in a small knob of butter or ghee around the bread and let it sizzle and baste the bread as it finishes.

variants.name: Charsi Tikka

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp nimbu ka ras (fresh lemon juice)

ingredients.preparation: lamb or mutton tail fat, or lamb back fat
ingredients.text: 150 g dumba charrbi / bakra charrbi (lamb or mutton tail fat, or lamb back fat)

instructions: Sprinkle the salt evenly over every surface of the chicken, including inside the slashes and under any loose skin.
Light your charcoal grill or a sigri (small coal grill) and let the charcoal burn until it is covered in a layer of grey-white ash and glowing orange underneath. This takes 20-30 minutes.
Alternatively, lay a few cubes of fat directly on the hot grill grate — they will render and drip onto the coals, which will smoke and flame up, creating that characteristic charsi flavour.
Put the chicken pieces on the hot grill, skin side down. Do not move them for 4-5 minutes. hear aggressive sizzling — if it's quiet, the grill isn't hot enough.
After 30-35 minutes total grilling time, check the thickest piece (usually the leg quarter). Alternatively, the internal temperature should read 75°C (165°F) if you have a meat thermometer.
Remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest on a plate for 5 minutes.

variants.name: Cheesy Corn & Potato Cutlet Recipe

ingredients.item: butter (if your potatoes aren't warm then melt it))
ingredients.text: 3 tbsp butter (if your potatoes aren't warm then melt it))

ingredients.preparation: keep on hand but only use if you NEED it to mash
ingredients.text: 2 tbsp milk (keep on hand but only use if you NEED it to mash)

ingredients.item: heaped cup shredded cheese - cheddar or monterey jack
ingredients.text: 1 heaped cup shredded cheese - cheddar or monterey jack

instructions: Cover the potatoes with salted water and bring to a boil.
When they are tender and then drain the water and peel when they are cool enough to handle.
Transfer to a large bowl, Stir in the butter, chillies, salt, mustard powder, and pepper and mash very very well. Stir in a splash of milk if needed.
When the mixture is fairly smooth Stir in your corn and cheese and mix well.
Please do remember that for a delicious kabab/cutlet Aim for the mix to taste a little salty, not positively briny, just a little salty.

When the potato mixture is finished and then with my left hand I pick one up give it an egg bath and move it into the breadcrumbs, roll it around with my right hand and move it to the tray (also with my right).
When you are ready to eat them and then pan Cook on medium high heat for 2-3 minutes on each side or till golden brown.

variants.name: Chicken and Cheese Casserole

ingredients.preparation: or 2 tbsp butter and 2 tbsp oil
ingredients.text: 4 tbsp butter (or 2 tbsp butter and 2 tbsp oil)
1-1 1/2 cup cut up boiled potato (1 cm pieces)
1-1 1/2 cup shredded chicken or chicken pieces

ingredients.item: chicken stock or half a boullion cube diluted in one cup water
ingredients.text: 1 cup chicken stock or half a boullion cube diluted in one cup water

ingredients.item: shredded cheese - cheddar or monterey jack
ingredients.text: 2 1/2 cups shredded cheese - cheddar or monterey jack

instructions: Preheat your oven to 400 degrees F. Melt the butter in a large pot or dutch oven on medium heat.

Sprinkle in the flour, stirring constantly until it starts looking a little darker and has an almost nutty aroma - 2 minutes. Gradually Stir in the three cups of milk, whisking constantly to ensure there are no lumps.
The sauce will start to thicken and bubble (stir frequently so it doesn't burn). Stir in in the onions, green chillies, nutmeg, pepper, and stock.
Mix well and cook to thicken - another 3-5 minutes. Fold in your chicken, potatoes and corn and take it off the heat.

Stir in 1.5 cup of the cheese and and then if your sauce is too thick looking Stir in a little of the reserved milk until you get the right consistency. SEASON! Because salt varies with stock and cheese wait till the end to season the dish.
Pour into your pan, scatter over the remaining cup of cheese and bake for 8-10 minutes, can broil for another 2 to get crispier cheese.

dish_families.name: Chicken and Rice Soup with Chillies

variants.name: Chicken and Rice Soup with Chillies
variants.dish_family: Chicken and Rice Soup with Chillies
instructions: Mix all the broth ingredients and 7 cups water in the Instant Pot on the Soup setting for 30 minutes. If cooking stove top and then bring to a boil and simmer for an hour.
Skim any dark residue off the top and strain the stock.
Pour the broth into a pot (or back into your IP).
Bruise the bottom of the lemongrass stalks to get the flavour going, cut into big chunks.
Stir in the lemongrass to the pot and bring to a boil.
Stir in the rice and simmer till it's done, about 15 minutes.
Mix the salt, pepper and juice of half a lime in the pot, taste, adjust seasoning if needed.
Stir in the shredded chicken, cilantro, chillies and scallions.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Chicken and Rice Soup with Chillies

variants.name: Chicken Bhuna Masala – Pakistani Homestyle Bhuna Recipe
variants.dish_family: Chicken Bhuna Masala – Pakistani Homestyle Bhuna Recipe

ingredients.item: boneless chicken cut unto 1.5 inch pieces ((450g) (1.5-2lb for bone in))
ingredients.text: 1 lb boneless chicken cut unto 1.5 inch pieces ((450g) (1.5-2lb for bone in))
1 inch ginger, grated or 1/2 tbsp paste

ingredients.item: kashmiri chili powder ( (if you don't have it put in 1/2 - 3/4 tsp red chili powder/ cayenne))
ingredients.text: 1 tsp kashmiri chili powder ( (if you don't have it put in 1/2 - 3/4 tsp red chili powder/ cayenne))

ingredients.item: heaped spoon roasted and coarsely ground coriander and cumin powder
ingredients.text: 1 heaped spoon roasted and coarsely ground coriander and cumin powder

instructions: Warm a cm of oil in a saucepan or pot and Stir in your onions and minced green chili.
Saute on medium heat till the onions edges are a bronze colour, 6-7 minutes.
Stir in in the garlic and ginger, give it a quick stir.
Stir in your chicken, spices, and cook medium high stirring frequently until the chicken changes colour and the masala coats it. 3 minutes or so.

Stir in your tomatoes and yoghurt, stir and cover. Simmer on low heat till tender. 20 minutes for chicken thighs, if your chicken breast is tough at this point and then Stir in in a splash of water and simmer for an additional 10 minutes.
When the chicken is done and then crank the heat up to dry up the extra water and create a cohesive masala.
Adjust the consistency to your liking and Stir in in the kasuri methi, butter, and roasted cumin and coriander powders.
Check for seasoning, garnish and serve.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Chicken Bhuna Masala – Pakistani Homestyle Bhuna Recipe

variants.name: Chicken Chapli Kabab

ingredients.item: chopped tomatoes, flesh removed before chopping
ingredients.text: 1/4 cup chopped tomatoes, flesh removed before chopping
1 tbsp chopped mint (can sub for 1 tsp dried)

instructions: Mix all the ingredients except the lemon juice in a bowl, mixing just enough to Mix.
Set aside for 20 minutes or up to overnight.
When it's time to cook heat a pan and Stir in an even coat of oil on the bottom, you don't need to deep Cook these, but you need enough oil to help develop a crust.
Dip your cooking spatula in a little oil -this will prevent the mix from sticking - and use it to flatten the kababs.
Cook for about 2 minutes on medium high heat to get a nice sear. Gently flip and and then cook for another minute and a half or until done.

variants.name: Chicken Corn Soup (Pakistani Chinese Style)
instructions: Bring to a boil over high heat, and then reduce to a steady simmer. Skim off any grey foam that rises to the surface during the first 5-10 minutes — this is protein impurities and removing it gives you a clear, clean stock. Simmer for 25-30 minutes.

Once the chicken is cooked through and tender, remove it from the stock with tongs and set it on a board to cool for 5 minutes. Strain the stock through a sieve into a clean pot — discard the ginger and garlic.
Bring the strained stock back to a gentle boil. Stir in the sweet corn kernels and the shredded chicken. Stir in the light soy sauce and white pepper.

Mix 4 tbsp cornflour with 6 tbsp cold water until completely smooth — no lumps. Pour this slowly into the simmering soup while stirring continuously in one direction. Keep stirring as you pour, or you will get cornflour lumps instead of a smooth, thick soup.

Beat the eggs in a small bowl until the yolk and white are fully combined. Reduce the soup to a gentle simmer — it should be moving but not bubbling aggressively. Hold the bowl of beaten egg about 15cm above the soup and pour it in a thin.
Taste for final seasoning — more salt, more white pepper if needed. Ladle into individual bowls and garnish with sliced spring onions. Diners customise their own heat level.

variants.name: Chicken Ginger

ingredients.text: 1 lb boneless chicken (use more for bone in)
1/4 cup julienned ginger - approx 2 inch piece

instructions: Whisk your yogurt and leave it out near the stove to come to room temperature.
Put a wok on high heat.
Stir in your chicken, ginger paste, garlic paste, and tomatoes to the pan.
Cook until the water dries up and the chicken is cooked through.
And then Stir in the soy sauce, salt, red chillies, black pepper, coriander powder, turmeric, butter, and oil.
Cook until the masala turns out a bright red hue and the oil rises above it.
Gently mix in the yoghurt, green chillies, ketchup, chopped ginger (reserving some for garnish) and garam masala.
Reduce the heat to low and cook covered for 3-5 minutes.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Warm oil on medium heat in a heavy-bottom pot. Once it begins to shimmer, Stir in chopped onion and Cook until soft, about 5 to 7 minutes.
Lower heat, and Stir in crused garlic and ginger. Cook for roughly 30 seconds or until they no longer smell raw.
Increase heat to high, and Stir in chicken and 1⁄2 teaspoon of the salt. Cook until no longer pink, about 3 to 5 minutes.
Stir in red chili powder and turmeric powder, and stir until well-mixed.
Cook on high heat until the sauce is reduced to a jammy mixture, about 10 minutes.
Stir in half of the fresh ginger and green chili.
Lower heat and stir in the whisked yogurt. Let the chicken simmer on medium-low heat for an additional 10 minutes or until you get the desired consistency.
Put in serving bowl and garnish with remaining fresh ginger and chilies, and cilantro.

variants.name: Chicken Handi Recipe - Creamy, Boneless, Restaurant Style Curry

ingredients.text: 3/4 lb boneless chicken breast (cut into 1 inch pieces )

ingredients.item: sliced ginger and green chilies to garnish
ingredients.text: sliced ginger and green chilies to garnish

instructions: Rub the chicken pieces with the spice mix and set aside. Warm your pan on medium heat, Stir in the oil and once it shimmers and then Stir in in your onion and green chili.
Stir in the ginger and garlic paste, cook for a minute to get the rawness out. Stir in in the tomatoes, kashmiri laal mirch, and 1/2 tsp salt.

Cook, covered for a few minutes to hasten the softening of the tomatoes. Uncover and cook on medium high heat to take out some of the excess moisture, when the masala comes together, it will be one cohesive delicious looking paste, and then remove it from the pan.

If your blender can handle high heat liquids and then you can puree it right away - otherwise wait for the mixture to cool a little. Stir in the chicken pieces to the pan on medium high heat and saute until the color changes completely.

Stir your pureed mix back into the pan, along with half a cup of water. Bring it to a simmer and and then let it cook, covered, and on low heat until the chicken is tender (20 minutes - more if needed). Stir in your cream to the handi and bring it to a gentle simmer.

This is when you can Stir in more spice (remaining kashmiri laal mirch), salt, some tomato paste, or even a pinch of sugar to balance out the flavours. Garnish with a drizzle of cream and your favorite toppings.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Chicken Handi Recipe - Creamy, Boneless, Restaurant Style Curry

variants.name: Creamy Chicken Handi

ingredients.text: 1 tsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)

instructions: Put your handi (clay pot) or a heavy-bottomed karahi (wok) on medium heat. Stir in 3 tablespoons of tel (cooking oil) and let it heat until it shimmers — you'll see tiny ripples on the surface.
Stir in your sliced pyaz (onions) to the hot oil. Spread them out and let them cook on medium heat, stirring every 2-3 minutes. This takes 12-15 minutes.

Stir in the adrak lahsun paste (ginger-garlic paste) to the golden onions. Stir constantly for 60-90 seconds — it'll sizzle aggressively and turn darker. Stir in lal mirch powder, dhaniya powder, and haldi.

Tip in the chopped tamatar (tomatoes). Stir everything together and turn the heat to medium-high. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes break down completely into a thick paste and you can see the tel (oil) separating and floating on the surface — about 12-15 minutes.

Stir in your chicken pieces to the masala and stir to coat every piece. Cook on high heat for 3-4 minutes, turning the pieces so they sear slightly and absorb the masala colour. lower the heat to medium and Stir in the dahi (yoghurt) — stir it in.
Stir in half a cup of paani (water), stir, and then cover the handi with a lid. Cook on low-medium heat for 20-25 minutes until the murgh (chicken) is completely cooked through.
Turn the heat down to the absolute lowest setting. Stir in the malai (cream) and stir gently. and then Stir in the makhan (butter) and let it melt into the curry.

Scatter chopped hara dhaniya (fresh coriander) over the top and Stir in a few slit hari mirchein (green chillies) if you like a little heat visible. Let the handi sit covered for 5 minutes off the heat — this resting time lets the cream fully absorb into the.

variants.name: Creamy White Chicken Handi
instructions: Blend 2 raw onions to smooth paste with a splash of water. Heat ghee in a handi or heavy pot. Stir in onion paste and cook on medium heat, stirring frequently, for 10-12 minutes until raw smell is completely gone and paste has turned slightly golden — but.
Stir in adrak-lehsan paste and crushed cardamom seeds. Cook 2 minutes. Stir in zeera powder and kali mirch.
Stir in chicken pieces, salt. Bhuno on medium heat (not high — to maintain pale colour) for 6-7 minutes until chicken is white and firm on outside.
Reduce to low heat. Stir in whisked yogurt 1 tablespoon at a time, stirring constantly. Once all incorporated, cook on medium 8 minutes.
Stir in cashew paste, stir until smooth. Stir in 1/4 cup water. Cook covered on low-medium for 20 minutes until chicken is completely cooked and tender.
Stir in fresh cream. Stir gently and cook 5 minutes on low — don't boil after adding cream. Stir in kewra water off-heat.
Garnish with light hara dhania and julienned ginger.

variants.name: Desi Dhaba Handi
instructions: Warm oil in a wide pot or handi. Cook chopped pyaaz on high-medium heat — dhabas don't Cook slowly, they Cook fast and hot. 10 minutes to golden-brown at high heat.
Stir in adrak-lehsan paste, all dry spices. Bhuno 3 minutes. Stir in tamatar and cook down 8 minutes.
Stir in chicken and salt. Bhuno on high for 8 minutes. Stir in 3/4 cup water.
Cover tightly and cook on medium heat 25-30 minutes until chicken is cooked and very tender.
Stir in hari mirch and garam masala. Increase heat and cook uncovered 5-8 minutes until oil rises to surface — this 'oil on top' is the dhaba signal that the dish is done correctly.

variants.name: Karachi Chicken Handi
instructions: Warm oil in a handi or heavy pot. Cook sliced pyaaz until very dark brown — Karachi handi needs darker onions than white handi. Remove half for garnish, keep half in pot.
Stir in adrak-lehsan paste, all dry spices. Bhuno 3 minutes. Stir in pureed tamatar.
Stir in bone-in chicken pieces. Bhuno 8-10 minutes on high heat until well-coloured. Season with salt.
Reduce heat. Stir in whisked yogurt gradually. Once incorporated, cook on medium 5 minutes.
Stir in 1/2 cup water. Cover handi tightly — traditional handi cooking is sealed. Cook 25-30 minutes on medium-low until chicken is fully cooked and tender.
Uncover, Stir in slit hari mirch, garam masala, and half the hara dhania. Stir gently. Cook uncovered 5 minutes to desired consistency.

variants.name: Easy, Lemony Weeknight Chicken Kali Mirch (Pepper Chicken)

ingredients.text: 3/4 lb boneless chicken (cut into 3/4 inch cubes )

instructions: Mix the chicken marinade ingredients and set aside while you chop your ginger and onion. I usually just let it sit for 20 minutes, but you can do more.
Warm a pan on medium high heat and before you Stir in the oil Stir in your crushed pepper into it, dry roast it until it smells deeply aromatic.
Stir in 3-4 tbsp of oil and your diced onion, cooking on medium heat for 4-5 minutes or until the edges take on colour.
Stir in your ginger into the pan and cook until the edges of the ginger change colour (about a minute or two) - your onions will further caramelize and that's ok.
Stir in your marinated chicken and saute until the color changes.
Stir in your half cup water to the chicken ad simmer, covered, until tender - 25 minutes or so.
Once the chicken is cooked Stir in in your lemon segments and green chilies and taste and adjust seasoning to taste with salt/pepper/more bhunna zeera powder.
Garnish with chopped cilantro and serve with chapati.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Warm oil in a wok or karahi and Stir in crushed garlic. Cook on low heat for 30 seconds or until fragrant.
Increase heat to high, and Stir in chicken and salt.

Stir in crushed ginger, sliced onion and 1⁄2 cup of water. Bring to boil, and then lower to simmer. Cook uncovered until the chicken is tender and most of the water has evaporated, about 25-30 minutes.

Stir in yogurt, cumin powder, coriander powder and black pepper. Stir continuously on medium heat for about 5-7 minutes or until the chicken is well-coated in spices and the oil begins to separate from the dish.
Remove from heat. Garnish with julienned ginger, chili and a pinch of garam masala powder.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Warm oil in a wok or karahi and Stir in crushed garlic. Cook on low heat for 30 seconds or until fragrant.
Increase heat to high, and Stir in chicken and salt.

Stir in crushed ginger, sliced onion and 1⁄2 cup of water. Bring to boil, and then lower to simmer. Cook uncovered until the chicken is tender and most of the water has evaporated, about 25-30 minutes.

Stir in yogurt, cumin powder, coriander powder and black pepper. Stir continuously on medium heat for about 5-7 minutes or until the chicken is well-coated in spices and the oil begins to separate from the dish.
Remove from heat. Garnish with julienned ginger, chili and a pinch of garam masala powder.
