variants.name: Boneless Chicken Karahi Recipe

ingredients.text: 1 1/2 pound (~ 700 grams) boneless chicken (preferably chicken thighs, diced)

instructions: Warm oil in a large karahi or wok. When the oil begins to shimmer, Stir in cumin seeds. Cook until fragrant, roughly 30 seconds or less.
Lower heat and Stir in crushed garlic, ginger and diced green chilies. Cook until fragrant, roughly 30 seconds or less.
Turn the heat up to high, and Stir in chicken and salt. Sear until no longer pink, about 5-10 minutes.
Stir in chopped tomatoes and stir continuously on high heat until jammy, about 10 minutes.
Stir in red chili flakes, black pepper and garam masala powder, and mix well.
Let the chicken simmer on high heat until the gravy reduces, about 5 minutes.
Lower heat and Stir in cilantro and yogurt. Stir until well-mixed.
Remove from heat. Garnish with finely chopped cilantro, green chilies, and ginger.

variants.name: Chicken Karahi Keema - Stir-fried Minced Chicken in a Ginger and Tomato Sauce

ingredients.text: 2 tsp red chilli powder (or to taste)

instructions: Heat the cooking fat and brown the minced chicken over medium-high heat.
Stir in garlic, chunk ginger, red chilli powder, green chillis, followed by the tomatoes and red chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, green chillis, coriander.
Cook uncovered, stirring regularly, until the protein is cooked and the tomato masala reduces enough for the oil to separate.
Finish with chunk ginger, coriander powder, coriander and serve immediately.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Chicken Karahi Keema - Stir-fried Minced Chicken in a Ginger and Tomato Sauce
source_attributions.author: Fatima Cooks

variants.name: Karahi Chicken (boneless or bone in)
instructions: Mix the marinade ingredients with the chicken and set aside.
Put your pan on medium heat and Stir in the roasted masala to the pan and roast until aromatic and and then coarsely pound them in a grinder or mortar and pestle.
Stir in your oil, chicken, tomatoes, salt, chili flakes and HALF your roasted masala to the pan, simmer, covered, and on low till tender (20 minutes).
If for some reason you cannot and then Stir in a splash of water and simmer on low heat until it's to your liking.
Crank up the heat and dry up the masala until it starts to look glossy and stick to the pan.
Stir in the kasuri methi, half the garnishes, and water for consistency and taste. Here is where you can Stir in the rest of your roasted masala or save it for next time.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Warm oil in a medium karahi or heavy-bottomed pot on medium heat. Stir in onions and Cook for 6-8 minutes until golden.
Stir in ginger garlic paste and stir for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in all dry spices (chilli powder, turmeric, coriander powder, salt, black pepper) and stir for 1 minute.
Stir in chopped tomatoes and cook on medium-high, stirring occasionally, for 10-12 minutes until completely soft and the oil starts to separate to the sides.
Stir in chicken pieces and green chillies. Stir to coat in masala. Cover and cook on medium for 20 minutes until chicken is fully cooked.
Remove lid, increase heat to medium-high, and stir-Cook for 5 minutes to reduce excess liquid. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: - Heat oil in a wok and Stir in the nigella seeds.
- When they start to splutter and then Stir in the minced/ground ginger and garlic.
- Stir in the ground chicken and the spices and cook on high stirring frequently until the chicken is nicely browned (this is chicken though so it wont get dark like beef does).
- Stir in the tomatoes, mix well. For quicker cooking cover the dish for a few minutes, this will soften the tomatoes.
- Uncover the dish and cook on high until the 'masala' becomes dry and the oil starts to rise. If this is not happening at all you may need to Stir in more oil.
- Stir in the garam masala, stir, check for seasoning.
Garnish with the chillies, ginger, and cilantro.

variants.name: Malai Chicken Karahi - Creamy Stir-fried Chicken Curry

ingredients.text: 2.5 tsp red chilli powder (or to taste)

instructions: Heat the cooking fat and brown the boneless chicken chunks over medium-high heat.
Stir in garlic, ginger, red chilli powder, green chilli, followed by the tomatoes and red chilli powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric, pods green cardamom, Coriander for garnish.
Cook uncovered, stirring regularly, until the protein is cooked and the tomato masala reduces enough for the oil to separate.
Finish with ginger, coriander powder, Coriander for garnish and serve immediately.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Malai Chicken Karahi - Creamy Stir-fried Chicken Curry
source_attributions.author: Fatima Cooks

variants.name: Balochi Chicken Karahi

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp tel ya charbi (oil or fat)
4 whole sabut lal mirch (whole dried red chillies)

instructions: Warm oil (or sheep fat if using) in a heavy karahi on high flame. Stir in whole dried red chillies and cumin seeds — let them bloom for 30 seconds.
Stir in crushed garlic and grated ginger (not paste). Cook on medium-high for 2-3 minutes until lightly golden.
Increase heat to high. Stir in chicken pieces and sear on all sides for 5-6 minutes without stirring too much. Stir in salt and black pepper .
Stir in chopped tomatoes and cook on high heat for 8-10 minutes, letting them break down.
Stir-Cook continuously on medium-high for 20 minutes until chicken is cooked through and masala has dried significantly. Stir in green chillies after 10 minutes.
Increase heat to high for final 3-4 minutes to achieve a semi-dry, slightly charred finish. Garnish with ginger juliennes and coriander.

variants.name: Dhaba Chicken Karahi

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Get your karahi smoking hot on highest flame. Stir in oil and wait until it's shimmering and almost smoking. Dhabas cook on gas burners the size of your torso — we compensate with patience and maximum heat.
Stir in ginger garlic paste directly to hot oil and Cook aggressively for 2-3 minutes, scraping constantly.
Stir in tomatoes with all dry spices. Cook on high flame for 12-15 minutes, smashing tomatoes with a wooden spoon as they soften.
Stir in chicken pieces and stir vigorously to coat in the masala. Cook on high for 5 minutes without touching — let the chicken sear. and then stir and repeat.
Cook on medium-high for 20-25 minutes, stirring every 3-4 minutes. Stir in green chillies. The masala should reduce, the oil should separate, and the whole thing should smell incredible.
In the final 2 minutes, Stir in butter and garam masala.
Top with ginger juliennes, fresh coriander, and a drizzle of lemon juice.

variants.name: Lahori Chicken Karahi

ingredients.text: 0.5 cup Tel or Desi Ghee (Oil or Ghee)
1 tsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)

instructions: Put your karahi (wok) or a heavy, deep frying pan on the stove and crank the heat to HIGH. Stir in the tel or ghee (oil or ghee).

Immediately Stir in the roughly chopped lehsan (garlic) and HALF the julienned adrak (ginger) — keep the other half aside for raw garnish later. Stir constantly for 30 seconds. If it's colouring too fast, pull the karahi off the heat briefly.
Stir in all the murgi (chicken) pieces at once. Yes, all of them — the high heat can handle it. Using a large chamcha (ladle) or tongs, stir and turn the pieces constantly for 5 minutes.

Throw in the roughly chopped tamatar (tomatoes), namak (salt), lal mirch powder (red chilli), and dhania powder (ground coriander). Stir everything together well. Keep the heat HIGH — this is not a gentle simmer situation.

Once the tel has clearly separated from the masala, Stir in the slit hari mirch (green chillies) and crushed kali mirch (black pepper). Stir and cook for another 3-4 minutes. The hari mirch will blister slightly and their fresh heat will perfume the dish.
Turn off the heat. Scatter the remaining raw julienned adrak (ginger) over the top — DO NOT stir it in. The adrak sits on top, wilting slightly from the residual heat but staying sharp and pungent.

variants.name: Karachi Chicken Karahi

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
1.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Warm oil in a large karahi or heavy wok on HIGH flame until shimmering hot. This high heat is the soul of Karachi karahi — don't be shy.

Stir in sliced onions and Cook on high heat until golden brown, about 5-7 minutes, stirring constantly. Stir in ginger garlic paste and Cook for 2 minutes until the raw smell disappears and it turns slightly golden.
Throw in chopped tomatoes and cook on HIGH flame, stirring frequently, for 10-12 minutes until they completely break down and oil separates to the sides.
Stir in red chilli powder, coriander powder, black pepper, and salt. Stir well and cook spices in the masala for 2 minutes until fragrant and oil rises to the surface again.
Stir in chicken pieces and coat thoroughly in the masala. Cook on HIGH flame for 5 minutes, turning pieces to sear on all sides.
Reduce to medium-high and bhuno (stir-Cook) the chicken for 20-25 minutes, stirring every few minutes. Stir in green chillies halfway through.
Crank heat to high for the last 3-4 minutes to dry out excess moisture. Garnish with ginger juliennes and fresh coriander.

variants.name: Sindhi Chicken Karahi

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
8 whole sabut kali mirch (whole black peppercorns)
2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Warm oil in a karahi on medium-high. Stir in whole cumin seeds and peppercorns — let them sizzle and pop for 30 seconds.
Stir in diced onions to the tempered oil and Cook on medium-high for 8-10 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger garlic paste and Cook for 2 minutes, scraping the bottom of the pan. Stir in turmeric and stir — it blooms beautifully in the oil.
Stir in chopped tomatoes with all dry spices. Cook on medium-high for 12-15 minutes, mashing tomatoes with the back of your spoon, until masala is thick and oil separates.
Reduce heat to medium. Stir in whisked yoghurt one tablespoon at a time, stirring constantly after each addition to prevent curdling. Cook for 3-4 minutes until yoghurt is fully incorporated.
Stir in chicken pieces, increase heat to medium-high, and bhuno (stir-Cook) for 5 minutes. Stir in green chillies. Reduce heat, cover, and cook for 15 minutes in its own steam.
Remove lid, increase heat to high, and stir-Cook for 5-8 minutes to reduce excess moisture. Garnish lavishly with fresh coriander and serve immediately.

variants.name: Chicken Lollipop

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp Lal Mirch Paste (Red Chilli Paste)
1 tbsp Sirka (Chilli Vinegar) or White Vinegar
1 tsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)

instructions: FRENCH THE BONE — MAKE THE LOLLIPOP SHAPE: Hold a wingette with the larger bone in your non-dominant hand. Using a small sharp knife, cut around the cartilage at the narrow end of the bone — make a circular cut all the way around.

In a large bowl, Mix the ginger-garlic paste, red chilli paste, soy sauce, chilli vinegar, red chilli powder, salt, and red food colour (diluted in 1 tsp water). Mix well into a thick, even marinade. Stir in the Frenched chicken pieces and coat thoroughly — get the marinade.

In a bowl, mix 4 tablespoons cornflour and 2 tablespoons maida. Stir in the beaten egg. Stir in cold water, a tablespoon at a time, stirring constantly until you reach a thick, coating batter — it should cling to a spoon without dripping off immediately.

Remove the marinated chicken from the fridge. Working one piece at a time, dip the meaty end (not the bone handle) into the batter and coat all around the meat ball. If the batter is too thick and clumping, Stir in another tablespoon of cold water and mix.
In a karahi (wok) or deep pot, heat the frying oil to 170-180°C over medium-high heat. If the oil smokes, it's too hot — remove from heat for 1 minute.

Hold each piece by the exposed bone and lower gently into the oil — never drop pieces in as hot oil will splatter. Cook in batches of 5-6 pieces maximum — do not crowd the karahi. Cook for 8-10 minutes total, turning every 2-3 minutes for even colour.

Remove cooked lollipops with tongs and stand them bone-up in a colander or on a wire rack to drain — standing them upright allows oil to run down and off the meaty end rather than pooling. Arrange standing in a circle on a round plate with the bones.

variants.name: Chicken Malai Tikka
instructions: In a bari pyali (large mixing bowl), Stir in the malai (fresh cream), cream cheese, and dahi (yoghurt). Use a whisk or fork to beat them together until completely smooth — no lumps of cream cheese should remain.

Stir in the flavour builders: adrak-lehsan (ginger-garlic) paste, nimbu (lemon) juice, safed mirch (white pepper), chhoti elaichi (green cardamom) powder, javitri (mace) powder, corn flour, oil, namak (salt), and finely minced hari mirch (green chillies). Whisk everything into a smooth, creamy paste.
Cut your chicken breast into large cubes — about 2 inches each. Not too small, or they'll dry out on the grill.
Stir in the chicken pieces to the marinade. Cover the bowl with cling film and refrigerate for minimum 3 hours — overnight (6-8 hours) is ideal.

When you're ready to cook, take the chicken out of the fridge 20 minutes before grilling — this brings it to room temperature so it cooks evenly. Let excess marinade drip off — too much will cause flare-ups on the grill.

CHARCOAL GRILL METHOD (best results): Light your angeethi (charcoal grill) and let the coals turn ash-white — this means they're at the right temperature: hot but not raging. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, turning every few minutes. You're looking for gorgeous brown char spots — not blackened.
During the last 3-4 minutes of grilling, baste each piece with melted makkhan (salted butter) using a brush or the back of a chamcha (spoon).

OVEN METHOD (if you don't have a grill): Preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F). Cook for 18-20 minutes, turning once halfway. and then switch to the broil/grill setting and blast the top for 3-4 minutes to get those char spots.

variants.name: Chicken Malai Tikka Karachi

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)

instructions: Whisk cream, cream cheese, and yoghurt until perfectly smooth. Stir in all remaining ingredients.
Coat chicken thoroughly, pushing cream into the cuts. Marinate overnight minimum for bone-in pieces — the cream needs time to penetrate to the bone for full flavour.
Remove chicken from fridge 45 minutes before cooking. Cold bone-in pieces cook very unevenly — room temperature is essential.
Grill on medium heat (NOT high). Bone-in pieces take longer than boneless — 12-15 minutes per side. Baste with butter every 3 minutes.

variants.name: Chicken Manchurian

ingredients.text: 500 g Chicken Breast or Boneless Thigh

instructions: In a bowl, Mix the chicken pieces with 4 tbsp cornflour, 1 beaten egg, 1 tbsp light soy sauce, a pinch of black pepper, and 0.5 tsp salt. Mix well with your hands until every piece is evenly coated — the batter should be thick and clinging, not.

Warm 2 cups of oil in a karahi (wok) or deep pan over high heat. Cook the chicken in two batches — do not crowd the pan or the temperature drops and the chicken steams instead of frying. Cook for 4-5 minutes until golden and crispy.

In a small bowl, whisk together the ketchup, chilli garlic sauce, dark soy sauce, white vinegar, 1 tbsp cornflour, 1/4 cup water, a pinch of sugar, black pepper, and Ajinomoto (MSG). Stir until the cornflour is fully dissolved — no lumps. This pre-mixing step is crucial: once the.

Warm 2 tbsp oil in a clean wok or large karahi over highest heat. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and stir-Cook for 30 seconds — it should sizzle aggressively and turn fragrant but not brown. Stir in the onion squares and capsicum and toss on high heat for.

Pour the pre-mixed sauce into the wok. Stir continuously and let it come to a full boil — about 1 minute. If it looks too thick to coat the chicken (i.e., it is gloopy and stiff), Stir in 2-3 tbsp water and stir.
Stir in the fried chicken pieces into the gravy. Remove from heat immediately.

variants.name: Chicken Paratha Roll

ingredients.item: Store-bought parathas cooked per package instructions
ingredients.text: 6 Store-bought parathas cooked per package instructions

ingredients.item: Oil for cooking and/or soaked wooden skewers if barbecuing
ingredients.text: Oil for cooking and/or soaked wooden skewers if barbecuing

instructions: Cut the chicken into one inch pieces and Stir in in all the marinade ingredients and leave for a minimum of 2 hours and up to overnight.

Warm a saute pan and Stir in 2-3 tbsp of oil, cook the chicken sauteeing occasionally until cooked through. If grilling the chicken and then simply thread it onto presoaked wooden skewers and grill for a few minutes on each side until cooked through.

Warm a piece of coal until you can see hot red spots. and then Put the coal on a piece of oil (or an onion skin) inside your sauté pan, drizzle with a little oil and immediately cover the dish with an airtight lid until the smoke dissipates.
Mix 1/2 the yoghurt (1/2 a cup) and all the chutney ingredients in a mini blender and puree. Stir in the remaining yoghurt - this prevent your chutney from getting too watery.
Thinly slice your onion and soak in cold water for 30 minutes to get rid of any bitterness.
Drain and then mix in the mint.

Put your paratha on a clean surface, create a line of chicken pieces, layer on the onion mix, and and then the chutney. Roll up the paratha and wrap in foil/paper and serve with extra chutney on the side.
You can reheat a wrapped paratha roll in the oven to really yummy effect!

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Prepare the chicken marinade: In a large bowl, Mix 1⁄2 cup thick dahi (yogurt), 2 tbsp Shan Tikka Masala, 1 tbsp adrak lehsan paste, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tsp laal mirch powder, 1⁄2 tsp garam masala, and 1 tsp zeera powder. Whisk until smooth and well-blended. The.

Stir in 600g boneless chicken cubes to the marinade. The yogurt should cling to the chicken — if it looks too runny, Stir in 1 tsp of cornflour (cornstarch) to bind it. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, ideally 6–8 hours.

In a blender, Stir in 1 cup packed hara dhania (fresh coriander), 1⁄2 cup packed podina (mint leaves), 3–4 hari mirch (green chillies), 1 tsp whole zeera, 1⁄4 cup dahi, 1 tbsp lemon juice, and 1⁄2 tsp namak. Blend until smooth, scraping down the sides as needed. If.
Put in a bowl of ice water with 1⁄2 tsp salt for 15 minutes. Drain well and pat dry with a clean kitchen towel.

Cook the chicken: Heat 3 tbsp cooking oil in a large tawa or non-stick pan over high heat until it shimmers. Stir in the marinated chicken cubes in a single layer — do not overcrowd. Let them sear undisturbed for 3–4 minutes until deeply charred on the bottom.

Optional but traditional — Stir in charcoal smoke (dhungaar): Once the chicken is cooked, make a small well in the centre of the pan. Cover the entire pan tightly with a lid and let the smoke infuse for 2 minutes.

Cook the parathas: If using frozen lachha parathas, cook them according to package instructions on a preheated tawa over medium heat, using ghee for crisping. If making fresh parathas, roll them out thin, brush with melted ghee, fold into the characteristic lachha (layered) shape, and cook on the.

Assemble the roll: Put a hot paratha on a clean work surface or piece of butter paper. Stir in a generous line of the cooked chicken boti, a handful of soaked sliced pyaz, and a few strips of slit green chilli if desired.

Fold and roll: Fold the bottom edge of the paratha up over the filling. Fold the two sides in tightly toward the centre, and then roll away from you into a compact cylinder. Wrap the bottom third with butter paper or foil to hold the shape.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Chicken Paratha Roll — Lahori Street Style

alternate_names: Chicken Paratha Roll — Lahori Street Style

variants.name: Chicken Seekh Kabab - 20 Minute Prep!
instructions: Stir in the onion, chilies, cilantro/coriander, green chilies, ginger and garlic to the bowl of a food processor and blitz till roughly chopped.
Stir in the remaining ingredients to the food processor and blend on high until a cohesive paste forms.
Grease your hands and shape into kababs either on skewers or without.

Barbecue: Preheat your grill to high, Put kababs on the grill and cook covered for 4-5 minutes. Uncover, turn over and cook for another 2 minutes. Check one for doneness before removing the others from the grill!

Stovetop instructions: Preheat your pan, drizzle a little oil, put the kababs on top and cook on medium high heat on each side for 2-3 minutes or until evenly browned. If Aim for a "softer" exterior and then cook on lower heat, but don't go below medium!

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Mix all ingredients except butter in a large bowl. Work with your hands for 5 minutes until the mixture is uniform, slightly sticky, and holds a shape when pressed.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Wet hands well with cold water. Shape mixture onto flat skewers with gentle, even pressure.
Cook on medium-high heat (not maximum — chicken burns more easily than beef). Grill 3-4 minutes per side, basting with melted butter as you turn.
Let rest on skewers for 2 minutes before sliding off.

variants.name: Chicken Shawarma — Karachi Street Style

ingredients.text: 1 tsp Laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)
12 cloves Garlic cloves (for lahsun ki chutney)
1/4 cup Dahi (yogurt, for lahsun ki chutney)
1 tbsp Lemon juice (for lahsun ki chutney)

ingredients.preparation: white vinegar, for lahsun ki chutney
ingredients.text: 1 tsp Sirka (white vinegar, for lahsun ki chutney)
1/4 cup Neutral oil (for lahsun ki chutney)

instructions: Prepare the chicken marinade: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together 1⁄2 cup full-fat dahi (yogurt), 2 tbsp Shan Tandoori Masala, 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1 tbsp adrak lehsan paste, 1 tsp paprika powder, 1 tsp roasted crushed zeera, 1⁄2 tsp haldi, 1 tsp laal mirch powder.
Stir in 800g boneless chicken thighs to the bowl and rub the marinade into every surface. Cover the bowl with cling wrap and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.

Peel 12 fat garlic cloves and Stir in them to a blender with a pinch of salt. Stir in 1⁄2 cup mayonnaise, 1⁄4 cup dahi, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tsp sirka (vinegar), and 1⁄2 tsp namak. Blend until smooth.

Make the quick pickled vegetables: In a small bowl, Mix 1⁄4 cup julienned gajar (carrots) with 2 tbsp white vinegar, 1 tsp sugar, and 1⁄2 tsp salt. Toss and set aside for at least 30 minutes. Prepare the rest of the salad: finely shred 1 cup iceberg lettuce.
Warm a large tawa or flat griddle pan over medium-high heat. Stir in 2 tbsp cooking oil and swirl to coat the surface. cook in batches if needed.

Once the chicken is cooked through (internal temp 74°C/165°F), push it to one side of the tawa. In the empty space, Stir in the sliced pyaz (onions), tamatar (tomatoes), and chopped hari mirch. Sauté for 2–3 minutes until the onions soften and the tomatoes break down slightly.
Each side needs about 20–30 seconds — just until softened with light brown spots.
Stir in a handful of shredded lettuce, a few cucumber juliennes, a spoonful of pickled carrots, and optionally some French fries.
Roll tightly: Fold the bottom edge of the khubz up over the filling, and then fold the two sides in tightly, and roll away from you into a compact cylinder.

variants.name: Chicken Tikka

ingredients.preparation: thigh included - each leg weighed about 1/2 pound
ingredients.text: 6 chicken whole legs (thigh included - each leg weighed about 1/2 pound)

ingredients.item: red chili powder ((preferably Kashmiri red chili powder) )
ingredients.text: 3 tbsp red chili powder ((preferably Kashmiri red chili powder) )

instructions: Stir in the red chili powder, cumin seeds and Stir in juice of one lemon.
Coat chicken with oil, salt and pepper.
Stir in the chicken to the yogurt marinade. Refrigerate for 6 hours or overnight.
To begin grilling, turn up all burners (this grill had four burners) and bring heat up to 400°F.
Remove the chicken from marinade, and Put it on one side of the grill, preferably concentrated on top of only one burner. Cook each side for about 10 minutes (so 20 minutes total).
Shut the grill and keep it closed for 30 minutes. Let it cook for another 30 minutes with lid closed.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Blend cashews and almonds with 3-4 tablespoons of water until smooth.
Mix yoghurt, nut paste, grated ginger, minced garlic, and all remaining ingredients.
Cut deep slashes in chicken pieces. Coat with marinade, pushing into cuts. Marinate overnight.
Remove 45 minutes before cooking.

Cook on medium heat, 12-14 minutes per side for bone-in. Like malai tikka, Afghani tikka should not be cooked on high heat — the nut paste and yoghurt burn easily. Baste with oil or butter every 3-4 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Cut your chicken into small cubes (approximately 1in).
Stir in salt, haldi, chili, zeera powder, dhania powder, garlic, ginger and yogurt and mix well.
Allow the chicken to rest in the marinade for at least 1 hour, but preferably overnight.
When ready to prepare the chicken brochette, bring the chicken to room temperature and pre-heat your broiler.
Each side will take approximately 5-7 minutes to cook, depending on the intensity of your broiler.

variants.name: Lahori Chicken Tikka

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp Adrak Lehsan Paste (Ginger Garlic Paste)
2 tsp Lal Mirch (Kashmiri Red Chilli Powder)

instructions: In a large bartan (bowl), mix the salt, nimbu (lemon) juice, and adrak lehsan paste. Leave for 20 minutes at room temperature.

In the same bartan, Stir in the dahi (yoghurt), tikka masala, Kashmiri red chilli powder, haldi (turmeric), and oil. Mix well into a thick, smooth paste. Coat the chicken pieces thoroughly in this mixture, making sure it gets into all the cuts.
Remove the marinated chicken from the fridge 30 minutes before grilling.
Put chicken pieces on the hot grill, leaving space between each piece — don't crowd. Close any grill lid if you have one. Cook for 8-10 minutes without touching, and then turn with tongs.
Arrange the cooked tikka in a deep metal bowl or pot. Cover immediately with a lid and let the smoke work for 60-90 seconds.

Let the tikka rest for 3-4 minutes before serving — this allows the juices to redistribute through the meat. The tikka should smell smoky and spiced, the surface should have visible char, and the meat should be juicy when you cut into it. Anything less and the grill.

variants.name: Punjabi Chicken Tikka

ingredients.text: 1 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)
2 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)

instructions: Warm mustard oil in a small pan until it begins to smoke slightly. Remove from heat and let cool to room temperature.
Mix cooled mustard oil with yoghurt and all remaining ingredients. Mix thoroughly.
Slash chicken pieces deeply. Coat in marinade, pushing into cuts.
Remove from fridge 45 minutes before cooking. Pat off any excess marinade from the surface — too thick a layer can prevent proper charring.
Grill on charcoal or under broiler at maximum heat. 10-12 minutes per side for bone-in pieces.
In last 2 minutes, baste with a mixture of butter and a squeeze of lemon. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

variants.name: Karachi Chicken Tikka

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp kashmiri mirch (Kashmiri red chilli powder)
1 tsp lal mirch powder (regular red chilli powder)
2 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)

instructions: Mix yoghurt, Kashmiri mirch (this is the colour hero), regular chilli, ginger garlic paste, all dry spices, oil, and lemon juice. Mix well — the marinade should be thick, red, and aromatic.
Coat chicken thoroughly, pushing marinade into the cuts. Cover and refrigerate for minimum 4 hours — overnight is the Karachi restaurant standard.
Take chicken out 30 minutes before cooking.
Cook on charcoal grill or under maximum oven broiler. Coal grill: 8-10 minutes per side, turning once. Oven broil: 12-15 minutes per side.
Put lit coal piece in a small foil cup, drizzle few drops of oil to make it smoke, Put cup with chicken, cover tight for 3 minutes. This one step replicates the coal grill flavour at home.
Rest 5 minutes.

variants.name: Chickpea and Mango Salad (Chaat)
instructions: Wash, dry and cut the fresh ingredients to an even size.
Whisk or blend the dressing ingredients and measured spices until combined.
Fold everything together shortly before serving; adjust salt, chilli and acidity to taste.
Chill if appropriate and add crisp garnishes only at the end.

ingredients.item: the widest slurpiest noodles - a wide rice noodle or a tagliatelle etc

2 tbsp garlic, minced (8 cloves of garlic)

ingredients.item: additional soy sauce or salt for adjusting seasoning
ingredients.text: additional soy sauce or salt for adjusting seasoning

instructions: Boil the pasta in salted water as per package instructions and make sure to reserve half a cup of pasta water.
Warm the oil in a pan and when it starts to shimmer Stir in your garlic, ginger, ginger, chili flakes, scallions, and cilantro.
Let it sizzle on medium heat for just a minute and and then Stir in 2 tbsp of soy sauce.
Mix the pasta well, adding additional pasta water as needed to create a sauce and adjust seasoning with additional soy, salt, and pepper and dig in.

variants.name: Fudgy Chocolate Brownies
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.
instructions: Heat the oven to 175°C. Line a 23 cm square tin, leaving paper overhang for lifting.
Melt the chocolate and butter together gently, then cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk sugar and eggs for 2 minutes until slightly thickened. Whisk in the chocolate mixture and vanilla.
Sift in flour, cocoa and salt. Fold only until no dry pockets remain.
Spread in the tin and bake for 24–28 minutes. A skewer near the centre should carry moist crumbs, not liquid batter.
Cool completely in the tin before lifting out and cutting into 12 pieces for clean, fudgy squares.

variants.name: Walnut Chocolate Brownies
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.
instructions: Heat the oven to 175°C and line a 23 cm square tin.
Melt the chocolate and butter gently and leave to cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk sugar and eggs until combined and slightly thick. Whisk in vanilla and the melted chocolate mixture.
Sift in flour, cocoa and salt. Fold gently, then fold in three-quarters of the walnuts.
Spread the batter in the tin and scatter over the remaining walnuts. Bake for 26–30 minutes until the centre has moist crumbs.
Cool completely before slicing into 12 pieces.

variants.name: Chocolate Loaf Cake

ingredients.text: 3/4 cup milk (or buttermilk, either works here)

ingredients.preparation: start with 3 and milk works fine too
ingredients.text: 3-4 tbsp cream (start with 3 and milk works fine too)

instructions: Optional but recommended: Whisk your dry ingredients - flour, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda, salt together in a bowl and set aside.
Beat the butter and icing sugar well until fluffy and well combined - approx 2-3 minutes.
Stir in the instant coffee and then the eggs one by one mixing well between additions.
Mix in the 2 tsp of vanilla.
And then Stir in in your dry ingredients in two batches alternating with the milk - keep your mixer on low speed and mix until just combined.
Bake the cake in the prepared tin until a skewer inserted in the middle comes out clean, check on it at 40 minutes. Mine usually take 40-45 minutes.
Warm your glaze ingredients together in the microwave (or stove top) until just warm to touch and mix well. If it is too stiff to mix and then you can warm it a little further or Stir in more cream.

variants.name: Pakistani Chowmein (Desi Chinese Hakka Noodles)

ingredients.text: 300 g Hakka Noodles or Egg Noodles

instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a full rolling boil. Cook the noodles for 1 minute LESS than the package instructions say. Drain immediately and run cold water over them to stop cooking.
Mix the sauces together in a small bowl: dark soy, oyster sauce, chilli garlic sauce, white vinegar.
Warm 1.5 tbsp oil in your largest wok or frying pan on MAXIMUM heat. Let the oil smoke slightly before you Stir in anything. Stir in the sliced chicken strips and spread them out in one layer.

Stir in the remaining 1.5 tbsp oil to the same hot wok. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and green chillies immediately. Stir-Cook for 30-40 seconds, keeping them moving, until the paste turns from pale yellow to golden and smells nutty and fragrant rather than raw.

Throw in the carrot first (it takes longest to cook), stir-Cook for 60 seconds. Stir in the cabbage and capsicum, toss everything on maximum heat for another 90 seconds. You are looking for some charred edges on the cabbage, which means your heat is high enough.
Stir in the cooked, cooled noodles to the wok. Immediately pour the sauce mixture over the top. Cook on high heat, tossing continuously, for 2 full minutes.
Return the cooked chicken to the wok, toss for a final 30 seconds just to heat it through and integrate. Transfer to a large plate or bowl immediately.

Stir in the garlic and saute for a minute and turn the heat down. Stir in a little more oil if needed, but try to avoid it.
Stir in the chilli flakes, chilli powder/paprika, and salt.
Cook on low heat for 5 minutes or so watching carefully so that the garlic doesn't burn. Stir in a little water if needed.

instructions: Break the imli into smaller chunks and pour over hot water. Let sit for 5-10 minutes or until softened.
Strain the Imli into a pot, just use the back of a spoon to make sure you get maximum flavour in your pot.
Stir in remaining ingredients and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 15 minutes.

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp tamarind paste (or 50 grams of tamarind pulp in 1/2 cup water)

If making fresh tamarind paste, soak about 50 grams of tamarind pulp in hot water. Once the water has cooled down, about 15 minutes, squeeze the tamarind pulp well separating the paste from the fibers. Using a strainer or sieve, drain the paste into a bowl.

variants.name: Cilantro Lime Chicken Pasta

ingredients.text: 3/4-1 lb chicken breast (cut into bite sized pieces)

ingredients.item: shredded cheese - monterey jack, parmesan, mild cheddar or any combinationn
ingredients.text: 3/4-1 cup shredded cheese - monterey jack, parmesan, mild cheddar or any combinationn

ingredients.item: salt, freshly cracked pepper, red chilli flakes, red chilli powder
ingredients.text: salt, freshly cracked pepper, red chilli flakes, red chilli powder (for seasoning )

instructions: Bring a generous amount of water to boil and Stir in a few fat pinches of salt. Season the chicken pieces well with salt, pepper, and a tiny pinch of cayenne (red chilli powder).

Cook the chicken pieces in a hot skillet in the olive oil for about 2 minutes on each side on medium high heat - they should be golden brown and cooked through. Remove the chicken, turn down the temperature and and then Stir in the garlic and chilli flakes.
Sprinkle on the flour and cook for a minute to take away the raw smell. And then whisk in the chicken stock, the lime zest, cream (start with 1/4 cup) and some freshly ground pepper.
Bring to a boil and simmer till it thickens a little. Stir in the chicken pieces and 2 tbsp lime juice to the sauce.
Drain the pasta when it's cooked through making sure to reserve a cup of pasta water. Stir in the sauce to the cooked spaghetti, stir to coat.

Stir in the cheese, tossing the pasta frequently as you Stir in it. It should melt into the pasta fairly quickly, Stir in a splash of pasta water and additional cream to loosen the sauce if needed. Cook on medium heat stirring frequently until the sauce is a consistency you like. If it thickens too much and then Stir in more pasta.
Stir in the cilantro, mix lightly and and then taste the pasta - adjust seasoning with remaining lime juice, salt, pepper and chilli flakes.

variants.name: Classic Creamy Chocolate Mousse
instructions: Use a large bowl if possible or transfer to one once melted.
Let the mixture cool to room temp and then briskly stir the egg yolks into the chocolate mix to avoid lumps.
Whip the egg whites till foamy and then Stir in the cream of tartar.
Stir in the sugar in 1 tbsp at a time, mixing for a minute between additions to incorporate.
Beat the cream and sugar together till the cream is fluffy, a beater lifted out of the cream mix should see distinct peaks form.
When folding take care to gently swoop under and over to mix and not stir.

dish_families.name: Coconut Loaf Cake with Caramel Sauce

variants.name: Coconut Loaf Cake with Caramel Sauce
variants.dish_family: Coconut Loaf Cake with Caramel Sauce

ingredients.preparation: use caster if your granulated sugar is coarse
ingredients.text: 1 cup granulated sugar (use caster if your granulated sugar is coarse)

instructions: Beat the butter and sugar together while gradually adding in the coconut oil, continue beating for 2 minutes for a fluffy slightly airy mix.
Stir in in the eggs one by one, mixing for a minute after each addition - the batter will start looking even fluffier.
Mix in your vanilla extract.

With your mixer on low Stir in in half the flour, and then half the milk(s), and then the remaining half of the flour and the remaining half of milk. Mix until just combined, you are not trying to get a smooth batter, small lumps are fine.
Gently fold in your coconut and transfer the mix to your prepped pan.
Bake for 50-55 minutes or until a skewer inserted in the center comes out clean.
Mix the sauce ingredients, bring to a simmer, cook for three minutes and let cool for ten before pouring over the cake.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Coconut Loaf Cake with Caramel Sauce

variants.name: Coconut Macaroons w/ Unsweetened Coconut
instructions: Mix the remaining ingredients in a bowl and mix in the egg whites.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until they are a golden colour - mine were done at 23 minutes.

variants.name: Coffee Cake with Coffee Buttercream

ingredients.item: instant coffee dissolved in 1 tbsp hot water
ingredients.text: 2 tbsp instant coffee dissolved in 1 tbsp hot water

ingredients.item: hot water + 2 tsp instant coffee granules
ingredients.text: 1 tbsp hot water + 2 tsp instant coffee granules

instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees and butter/flour an 8 inch pan (for a slim cake) or a 6 inch pan for a higher cake.
Mix the flour, baking powder and salt and set aside.
Beat the butter till creamy, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in the sugars and beat for another 2-3 minutes until the sugars are fully incorporated and the mixture starts to look nice and fluffy.
Stir in the eggs one by one, beat 1 minute after each addition, and mix in your vanilla extract.
And then sift half your flour mix in, mix, scrape sides with a spatula, Stir in remaining liquid (coffee solution and milk) and and then sift in the other half of the flour mix, beat till combined.
Pour the batter into your prepared tin.

Start checking on it after the 30 minute mark, that’s around when the cake should be done ( a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean) if you are using an 8 inch pan. With a 6 inch, it takes 12-15 minutes longer.
Whip the butter till fluffy, and then Stir in the powdered sugar gradually and at low speed till incorporated and finally Stir in in your coffee mix, vanilla, and salt. Beat well.

variants.name: Coffee Biscuit Pudding
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.
instructions: Mix custard powder with 100 ml milk. Heat the remaining milk and sugar, whisk in the slurry and cook until thick. Cover the surface and cool fully.
Dissolve coffee in hot water and let it cool.
Briefly dip biscuits in the coffee and arrange a layer in a serving dish.
Spread over half the cold custard and half the grated chocolate. Repeat the biscuit, custard and chocolate layers.
Top with whipped cream, cover and chill for at least 5 hours.
Serve cold and keep refrigerated.

variants.name: Coffee Cream Delight
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.
instructions: Dissolve the coffee in hot water and cool completely.
Beat cream cheese and condensed milk until smooth. In a separate bowl whip the cold cream to medium peaks, then fold it into the cream-cheese mixture.
Dip each biscuit very briefly in the cold coffee; do not soak it until it falls apart.
Arrange a biscuit layer in a deep dish, spread over one-third of the cream and repeat to make three cream layers.
Sift cocoa over the top, cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Serve chilled and keep leftovers refrigerated.

variants.name: Cream Cheese Cucumber Rounds

ingredients.item: garlic, crushed or super finely minced
ingredients.text: 1 clove garlic, crushed or super finely minced

ingredients.item: minced chives or parsley for garnishing
ingredients.text: minced chives or parsley for garnishing

instructions: Stir in the cream and whip till the cream is well incorporated and the mixture looks fluffier - about 2 minutes.
Cut into one inch thick rounds.
Fill a piping bag with the cream cheese mixture - I used a large tip but you can also just cut a hole in the corner of a ziploc bag and pipe a pretty round.
When they are all filled and then garnish with parsley or chives.

variants.name: Crunchy Fried Chicken Balls

ingredients.item: egg whisked with a splash of water and salt
ingredients.text: 1 egg whisked with a splash of water and salt

instructions: Mix all the chicken ingredients in a bowl gently mixing to keep the mix soft.
Roll your chicken into 1.5 tbsp sized balls (I use a greased cookie scoop!).
Give each piece a whirl in the egg wash and and then the breadcrumbs to coat evenly.
Cook immediately or refrigerate for up to two days or freeze for up to 3 months.

dish_families.name: Cucumber and Strawberry Kachumar Salad with Lemon Balm

variants.dish_family: Cucumber and Strawberry Kachumar Salad with Lemon Balm

ingredients.item: leaves lemon balm (or mint, cut into thin ribbons (chiffonade) ⁣)

instructions: Warm oil in a heavy bottomed pot. Stir in the cumin seeds and whole black pepper.
When the cumin seeds start to sizzle and then Stir in the onions. Cook on medium heat stirring occasionally until the onions are mostly a rich brown.

Stir in the garlic paste, saute for a minute and then Stir in the red chili powder, turmeric, coriander powder and salt. If at any time during the process the spices or onions start to burn Stir in a splash of hot water.

Cook stirring frequently for about a minute and then Stir in the chicken pieces, stirring them at regular intervals until the look cooked/white from all sides. Pour 1.5-2 cups of hot water into the pot, bring to a boil and and then simmer covered for 30 minutes.

Increase the heat and dry up the masala, as you do so the onions will break down and form a beautiful cohesive paste. Once the masalas become a paste and the oil rises to the top (bhunn) and then Stir in hot water as per your preference along with the green chilies and bring the mixture to a boil.

instructions: Turn the heat to medium and Put a heavy-bottomed pan, (I use a 6 qt stockpot) on the stove. Stir in oil and allow pan to heat up for 2 minutes.
Stir in onions and saute till they start to turn golden. At this point, Stir in the fresh garlic and ginger and continue to sauté.

This will take a total of 15 minutes. Stir in tomatoes, salt, chili pepper and turmeric and turn the heat to medium or medium-high, start to "Cook" (bhuno) this mixture. Be careful, the tomato sauce may splatter, in that case, turn the heat down. It will take approximately 15-20 minutes.

Let the mixture cool a bit and transfer the chunky ingredients with a slotted spoon, to a blender. Blitz it all to a smooth paste, Stir in some water to the blender if Aim for to get all the sauce off the walls of the blender.
Transfer mixture back to the pan. Stir in chicken pieces and 1/2 cup of water and turn the heat to medium-high.

"Cook" (bhuno) the chicken till you start to see the oil separating from the sauce. This will take approximately 15-20 minutes and rigorous stirring. Stir in the remainder of the water- 1 1/2 cups and cardamom pods, turn the heat to low, cover with a lid and let it simmer for 20 minutes.
Serve with a garnish of fresh chopped coriander/cilantro, (both leaves and sweet stems), kachumbar and chapati or Basmati rice.

1 tsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)

instructions: Wash the masoor daal (and chana daal if using the blend) in 3 changes of water. If using the masoor-chana blend, note that chana daal needs longer to cook — either soak the chana for 1 hour first, or Stir in it to the water 10 minutes before.
PREPARE FOR TARKA — HEAT THE GHEE RIGHT: This step deserves full attention. Put a small, heavy-bottomed karai (wok) or tawa (griddle) on medium-high heat. Stir in the ghee.

BUILD THE TARKA — ZEERA FIRST: Stir in the zeera (cumin seeds) to the hot ghee. Stir in the sliced lehsan (garlic) and stir constantly for 30-45 seconds until pale golden — the moment it turns golden, the next ingredient must go in immediately. Stir in the sliced.

Stir in the chopped tamatar (tomatoes) to the golden onions and garlic. Stir and cook until the tomatoes completely dissolve into the ghee — about 5-6 minutes. Stir in the lal mirch powder (red chilli powder) and stir for 1 minute — it will Cook in the ghee.

With the tarka still sizzling on high heat, crack an egg directly into the pan. Let it cook for 30 seconds — the white will set slightly. Use the chamcha (ladle) to break the yolk and stir the egg into the tarka mixture — it won't scramble fully.

THE POUR — THE DEFINING MOMENT: Transfer the cooked daal to a serving bowl if needed, or keep in the cooking pot. pour the entire tarka over the daal in one confident move. Stir the tarka into the daal just once or twice.

variants.name: Dal Gosht Punjabi

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
1.5 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Warm ghee in a heavy pot. Stir in zeera and sizzle. Stir in sliced piyaz and cook until golden brown, about 12 minutes.
Stir in tamatar, laal mirch powder, dhania powder, haldi, and salt. Cook on medium-high, stirring until oil separates and masala coats the meat, about 10 minutes.
Stir in 400ml water. If using pressure cooker, cook on high pressure for 20-25 minutes (2-3 whistles). If using pot, simmer covered 45-60 minutes until meat is tender.
Open cooker/pot. Stir in drained soaked chana dal. Mix into the meat and masala.
Pressure cook another 10-15 minutes (1-2 whistles) or simmer covered 25-30 minutes until dal is tender and has absorbed the meat flavours.
Stir in garam masala and stir. Garnish with hara dhania and julienned adrak.

variants.name: Dal Saag Combined

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
0.75 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Rinse masoor dal and cook in 500ml water with haldi and a pinch of salt until completely soft and mushy, about 18-20 minutes.
Warm ghee in karahi. Stir in zeera and sizzle. Stir in chopped piyaz and cook until golden brown.
Stir in chopped paalak to the masala. Cook on medium-high heat for 4-5 minutes until wilted and bright green.
Stir in the cooked masoor dal to the spinach masala. Mix well. Simmer together 8-10 minutes until everything melds.

variants.name: Dhaba Dal Tadka

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
1.5 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)
3 whole sukhi laal mirch (dried red chillies)

instructions: Cook both dals together in 700ml water with haldi and salt until completely soft, about 35 minutes. Blend or mash half for creaminess.
FIRST TARKA — THE BASE: Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a large karahi. Stir in 1 tsp zeera. Stir in sliced piyaz and cook over medium-high heat until DEEP brown — caramelised, almost crispy edges.

Stir in adrak lahsun paste and cook 3 minutes. Stir in tamatar, laal mirch powder, dhania powder. Cook aggressively on high heat, stirring and mashing, until a thick masala forms and ghee pools at edges — about 10 minutes.
Stir in boiled dal to masala. Mix well. Simmer 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally.
SECOND TARKA — THE SECRET: Heat remaining 2 tbsp ghee in a small pan until smoking. Stir in remaining 1 tsp zeera, sliced lahsun, and sukhi laal mirch. Cook until lahsun is golden (30-40 seconds).
Top with hara dhania.

variants.name: Mixed Dal Tadka

ingredients.text: 75 g moong dal (split yellow mung beans)
1.5 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
1 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Mix all three washed dals in a pot. Stir in 800ml water, haldi, and a pinch of salt. Bring to boil, simmer covered 30-35 minutes until all dals are very soft.
Warm 2 tbsp ghee in a karahi. Stir in 1 tsp zeera and let splutter. Stir in chopped piyaz, cook until golden brown.
Stir in tamatar, laal mirch powder, and salt. Cook on medium-high heat until oil separates and masala is thick, about 8 minutes.
Stir in cooked dal mixture to masala. Stir well and simmer together 8-10 minutes. Stir in hari mirch.
In a small ladle or pan, heat remaining 1 tbsp ghee until smoking hot. Stir in remaining zeera and sliced lahsun. Cook until garlic turns light golden — about 30 seconds.
Immediately pour the sizzling tarka over the dal.

variants.name: Punjabi Maash Ki Dal

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
1 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Drain soaked maash and Stir in to a pot with 700ml water, haldi, and a pinch of salt. Bring to boil, and then simmer covered for 40-50 minutes until very soft.
In a karahi (wok), heat 2 tbsp ghee. Stir in sliced piyaz and cook on medium heat until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes. Stir in adrak lahsun paste and cook 2 minutes until raw smell disappears.
Stir in chopped tamatar, laal mirch powder, and namak. Cook on medium-high heat, mashing the tomatoes, until oil separates from the masala — about 8 minutes.
Stir in the boiled maash to the masala. Mix well and simmer together for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Stir in more water if it gets too thick.
In a small tawa or ladle, heat remaining 1 tbsp ghee until very hot. Stir in zeera — it should sizzle immediately. Stir in slit hari mirch and cook 30 seconds.
Pour the sizzling tarka directly onto the dal.

variants.name: Sindhi Moong Dal

ingredients.text: 200 g moong dal (split yellow mung beans)
0.5 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)
2 whole sukhi laal mirch (dried whole red chillies)

instructions: Put washed moong dal in a pot with 600ml water, haldi, and salt. Bring to boil and simmer 20-25 minutes until completely soft and mushy.
Warm oil in a small karahi. Stir in zeera and let it splutter. Stir in chopped piyaz and cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in adrak and cook 1 minute. Stir in tamatar and laal mirch powder. Cook until tomato breaks down and oil surfaces, about 5 minutes.
Stir in a tiny bit more oil if needed, and then Stir in kari patta and sukhi laal mirch.
Pour the tarka over the cooked dal and mix gently. Simmer together for 5 minutes. Adjust salt and consistency — Stir in water if too thick for your liking.
Top with fresh hara dhania.

variants.name: Dahi Baray Chaat

ingredients.text: 1 cup urad dal (white split lentils, skinned)
1/2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

ingredients.item: a generous handful papri or sev
ingredients.text: a generous handful papri or sev

instructions: Measure 1 cup of urad dal into a bowl and rinse it with cold water 3–4 times, swirling it with your fingers until the water runs mostly clear. Cover with plenty of cold water (at least 3 cups — the dal will expand) and leave it to soak.
Drain the soaked dal completely — shake off as much water as you can. Transfer to a blender or a mixer-grinder (mixie). Stir in the ginger piece, green chilli (if using), and 1 tsp salt.

Pour enough oil into a karahi (wok) or deep pateela (saucepan) to give you at least 3 inches of depth — you need the baray to float and Cook without touching the bottom. Heat the oil over medium-high heat. If it burns instantly, reduce the heat slightly.

Using a wet tablespoon or wet fingers (keep a small bowl of water nearby to dip your hand or spoon between each one), drop rounded spoonfuls of batter gently into the hot oil. Cook for 4–5 minutes, turning them with a slotted spoon so they colour evenly. They.
Fill a large bowl with warm (not hot, not cold) water and Stir in 1/2 tsp salt to it. Leave them to soak for 20–30 minutes.

After soaking, take each bara one at a time and gently squeeze it between your palms — gently, like you're squeezing a sponge, not wringing out a towel. Put the squeezed baray in a single layer on your serving platter or in individual serving bowls.
In a bowl, whisk the 2 cups of cold dahi with 1 tbsp sugar and 1/2 tsp salt until it is completely smooth, creamy, and pourable like a thick sauce.
Pour the cold whisked yoghurt generously over the baray — Aim for them completely covered.

The assembled platter will look like a beautiful festival of colour — pale white yoghurt, dark brown imli chutney, bright green hari chutney, and orange-red chilli powder scattered over fluffy white baray.

variants.name: Lahori Dahi Bhalla
instructions: Rinse the dhuli urad dal and moong dal together under cold water until the water runs clear — this removes excess starch. Put in a bartan (bowl), cover with cold water by at least 5cm, and soak for minimum 4 hours, ideally overnight in the fridge.

Drain the soaked dal. Transfer to a blender with the adrak (ginger), hari mirch (green chillies), namak (salt), and just 2-3 tablespoons of paani (water). Blend on high until completely smooth — no grainy texture at all.
Transfer the batter to a large bartan (bowl). beat it vigorously with a chamcha (ladle) or electric hand mixer for 3-4 minutes.
Warm tel (oil) in a karahi (wok) or deep degh (pot) on medium heat — test with a tiny drop of batter: it should rise to the surface within 2-3 seconds. Cook 4-5 at a time.

This is the most important step for Lahori Dahi Bhalla and the one most people skip. As soon as the bhalle come out of the oil, transfer them immediately to a large bartan of warm (not hot) paani (water) with a pinch of namak. Submerge completely and leave.

While the bhalle soak, whisk the dahi (yoghurt) until completely smooth. Stir in half a teaspoon of zeera powder, a pinch of namak, and optionally a teaspoon of chini (sugar) if Aim for the dahi slightly sweet in the Lahori style. Whisk again.
Pour the cold whisked dahi over them generously — enough to half-submerge each bhalla.
Stir in the remaining roasted zeera powder (cumin). Scatter a pinch of lal mirch (red chilli powder) for heat and colour. Stir in a handful of torn hara dhaniya (fresh coriander) leaves.

variants.name: Lahori Dahi Bhalla — Classic White Style

ingredients.text: 250 g dhuli urad dal (white split black lentils)

instructions: Wash urad dal and soak for 4-6 hours or overnight. Drain and grind in a blender or stone grinder to a smooth, thick batter using as little water as possible. The batter should be thick enough to hold a shape when dropped from a spoon.
Whip the batter vigorously with a spoon or electric beater for 5-8 minutes until it becomes fluffy and light.
Stir salt, grated ginger and green chilli into the whipped batter.
Warm oil to 170°C (medium heat). Cook in batches for 4-5 minutes until pale golden and cooked through. They should not be deeply brown — just golden.
Let the fried bhallas soak in warm water for 15-20 minutes.
Whisk yoghurt with sugar until completely smooth. Spread a thick layer in a deep serving dish. Arrange pressed bhallas on top.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Lahori Dahi Bhalla — Classic White Style

variants.name: Dal Pakwan

ingredients.text: 3-4 whole sabut lal mirch (whole dried red chillies)
1/2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Wash 1.5 cups of chana dal in several changes of water until the water is no longer cloudy. Soak in fresh water for 2 hours — this helps the dal cook evenly and stay firm, not mushy. After soaking, drain the dal and put it in a pateela.

Warm 3 tbsp of oil in a small tawa (flat pan) or a small karahi (wok) over medium-high heat until the oil is shimmering and hot. Stir in the whole zeera (cumin seeds) — they should sizzle and pop immediately.
Stir the tadka through the dal gently. Stir in amchoor (dry mango powder) and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt.

In a large bowl (patila), mix together 2 cups maida, 2 tbsp sooji, 2 tbsp til, 1 tsp ajwain, and 1/2 tsp namak. Mix these dry ingredients with your fingers. Stir in 2 tbsp of oil — rub it into the flour mixture using both hands, squeezing and.

Divide the dough into 10–12 equal balls. On a flat surface (no dry flour needed — the oil in the dough prevents sticking), roll each ball into a thin, flat circle about 5–6 inches in diameter, roughly the size of a side plate.

Warm oil in a karahi to medium heat — test it by dropping a tiny piece of dough in. If it shoots straight to the top and browns immediately, the oil is too hot — reduce the flame. Cook for about 2 minutes per side, pressing down gently.

Pour the hot dal into a serving bowl. Arrange the crispy pakwan on a large plate beside it. To eat: break a piece of pakwan, ladle some dal on top, Stir in a drizzle of each chutney and a pinch of sev, and eat it all together in.

variants.name: Balochi Dampukht

ingredients.text: 100 grams charbi (sheep or goat tail fat)

instructions: In a heavy-bottomed degh (pot) or large karahi (wok), heat 4 tbsp ghee or oil over medium heat. Stir in 2 of the sliced onions. Cook, stirring every minute, for 15-18 minutes until they are deep golden brown — the colour of dark honey — and some edges.

In a large bartan (bowl), Mix the mutton pieces with full-fat yoghurt, ginger matchsticks, whole garlic cloves, all the whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, peppercorns, cumin seeds, bay leaves), half the fried barista pyaz, and salt. Mix thoroughly so every piece of mutton is coated in the yoghurt.
Into the same degh that still has the ghee in it, scatter the third onion (raw, thinly sliced) in an even layer at the bottom.
Mix 2 cups of atta (whole wheat flour) with enough water to make a firm, non-sticky dough — about half a cup of water. Roll it into a long rope, about the thickness of your thumb.

THE FIRST PHASE — HIGH HEAT: Put the sealed degh on your stove over medium-high heat for the first 10 minutes. begin to hear a faint sizzling sound from inside the pot — this tells you the liquid has begun to boil and steam is building up inside.
THE LONG SLOW COOK — DO NOT OPEN: Cook on the lowest possible heat for 2 to 2.5 hours without opening the pot.
After 2-2.5 hours, turn off the heat. Let the pot rest for 10 minutes — this allows the steam pressure to reduce before you open it. The colour will be a warm, pale golden-brown.
No garnish is strictly necessary, but a scattering of fresh green coriander (dhania) and a few thin slices of raw onion alongside adds brightness.

variants.name: Balochi Dampukht Chicken

ingredients.item: Dumba charbi (fat-tail sheep fat) or ghee
ingredients.text: 4 tbsp Dumba charbi (fat-tail sheep fat) or ghee

instructions: Stir in sliced onions and sauté for 3-4 minutes until just beginning to soften. Don't brown — Aim for them to steam, not Cook.
Layer chicken pieces over the onions. Stir in tomato halves, salt, black peppercorns, garlic, ginger, and bay leaves.
Cover tightly with the lid.
Put over lowest heat for 90 minutes. The chicken will cook in its own steam plus the moisture from onions and tomatoes.
At 90 minutes, break the seal. If not quite done, reseal and cook 15-20 minutes more.

variants.name: Balochi Dampukht Mutton

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp dumba charbi ya ghee (sheep fat or ghee)

instructions: Rub mutton pieces generously with salt and black pepper. Let rest for 30 minutes minimum — 2 hours in the fridge if time allows.
In a heavy, thick-walled pot (clay is traditional, Dutch oven is excellent), layer: first the ghee, and then sliced onion, ginger, garlic, bay leaves, and black cardamom.
Roll into a rope and press firmly around the entire rim of the pot to create an airtight seal with the lid.

VERY LOW HEAT — HOURS OF PATIENCE: Put sealed pot on the absolute lowest heat possible. Optionally, Put a tawa (flat griddle) between the flame and the pot for even more gentle heat. Cook for 4-6 hours.
After 4 hours, carefully crack the seal slightly and insert a knife through to feel the meat. If there's any firmness, re-seal with fresh dough and cook another 60-90 minutes.
Garnish with hara dhania and serve with lemon wedges.

variants.name: KP Dampukht Beef

ingredients.text: 2 tsp sabut kali mirch (whole black pepper)

instructions: Rub beef pieces with salt and crushed black pepper. Allow to rest for at least 1 hour — beef benefits from longer salting than mutton.
In a heavy Dutch oven or clay pot, Stir in ghee. Layer onion, ginger, garlic, black cardamom (crushed), cinnamon, bay leaves.
Put over lowest heat possible, or in 150°C oven. Beef needs longer than mutton — 5 hours minimum, 6 hours for perfect tenderness.
Carefully crack seal and test beef with a knife — must meet zero resistance. Re-seal and cook if needed.
Garnish with hara dhania.

variants.name: KP Dampukht Lamb — Dum-Sealed Pot
instructions: Layer the sliced onions across the bottom.
Put the mutton pieces on top of the onions. Stir in salt, black peppercorns, black cardamom, cinnamon, whole garlic head, and ginger. Do NOT Stir in any water or oil.

Roll out the dough into a long snake and press it firmly around the join between pot and lid, sealing it completely. Alternatively, cover the pot tightly with two layers of aluminum foil, and then Put the lid on top and seal the foil around it.
Put the sealed pot over the lowest possible heat.
Do not open the pot — every time you open it, you lose the accumulated steam and pressure that is doing the cooking.
Once cooked, turn off heat and let rest, still sealed, for 15 minutes.

variants.name: Slow Dum Chicken

ingredients.text: pinch zarda rang ya kesar (saffron or food colour)

instructions: Cook sliced pyaaz in ghee to deep golden. Mix birista paste with yogurt, adrak-lehsan paste, all ground spices, and salt — this is the marinade. Coat chicken pieces thoroughly.
In a heavy pot, heat remaining ghee. Stir in whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves) and sizzle 30 seconds. Stir in marinated chicken with all the marinade.
Drizzle saffron-milk over the top. Stir in kewra water.
Cook on lowest heat for 75-90 minutes. Chicken dum is faster than gosht dum — 75 minutes is usually sufficient for medium pieces.

variants.name: Desi Pasta

ingredients.text: 400 g / 14oz pasta (I adore Garofalo spaghettini no. 4⁣)
A handful of fresh cilantro (coarsely chopped⁣)

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Put a large skillet on medium heat and Stir in olive oil. When oil is hot, Stir in garlic and sauté for 2 minutes, or till fragrant and golden along the edges (careful it doesn’t burn).
Stir in turmeric and Biryani Masala and give it a whirl. Tip in tomato sauce, and Stir in salt, and crushed red chillies.
Raise heat; Stir in pasta to skillet, mix to coat with the sauce and oil.
Stir in cooking water and cook over medium-high heat, till the water is absorbed.

variants.name: Karachi Parsi Dhansak

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp Tuvar Dal (Pigeon Pea / Arhar Dal)
2 tbsp Urad Dal (Split Black Gram, husked)
1 set Dhansak Masala (whole spices, freshly mixed)

instructions: Soak them together in cold water for 30 minutes while you prep everything else.

In a small, dry tawa (griddle) or frying pan over low heat, dry-roast 2 tsp coriander seeds, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1 cinnamon stick, 3 cardamom pods, 4 cloves, and 1 star anise. Stir constantly with a chamcha (spoon) for 2-3 minutes until you smell a warm, toasty.

In a large pateela (deep pot) or degh (heavy-bottomed pot), Stir in the drained soaked lentils, kaddu (pumpkin) chunks, chopped methi leaves, chopped tomatoes, and 1 roughly chopped onion. Stir in the mutton pieces on top. Pour in 1.5 litres of water.

Remove the mutton pieces carefully with tongs and set aside in a bartan (bowl). use a hand blender directly in the pateela to blend the dal and vegetable mixture until smooth, OR transfer in batches to a regular blender.

Into your blended dal-and-meat pot, stir in: 2 tbsp tamarind paste, 2 tbsp grated jaggery (gur), and your entire freshly ground Dhansak masala. Stir everything in thoroughly. Bring to a gentle simmer on medium heat.

In a separate small karahi (wok) or frying pan, heat 3 tbsp oil or ghee over medium-high heat. Stir in 1 finely sliced onion. Cook, stirring frequently, for 12-15 minutes until deep golden brown and crispy — what's called barista pyaz.

In a separate pateela, wash 2 cups of basmati rice and soak for 20 minutes. In a small pan, heat 2 tbsp sugar over medium heat without stirring until it melts and turns a deep amber caramel colour — 3-4 minutes. Stir in 2 cups of water carefully.

Give the Dhansak a final stir and taste for salt. The gravy should be thick — thicker than regular dal, almost like a loose stew — and should coat the back of a chamcha (spoon). If it's too thick, Stir in a splash of hot water and stir.

variants.name: Donna Hays Chocolate Meringue Cake

ingredients.text: 1/4 cup 25G Dutch Cocoa (sifted) + additional for dusting

instructions: Preheat oven to 325 degrees.
Whisk the eggs, extra egg yolks, brown sugar and vanilla for 3–4 minutes or until pale and thick. Stir in the chocolate mixture, flour, baking powder and almond meal and fold gently to Mix.
Pour the cake mix into the tin and bake for 35-40 minutes.
Beat the egg whites in a clean bowl on high speed until soft peaks form and and then gradually Stir in the sugar whisking till it dissolves.
Mix for another 2–3 minutes.
Bake for another 20–25 minutes or until the meringue is golden and crisp.
Let the cake cool at room temperature for 30 minutes and and then run a knife between the cake and pan to loosen the sides.

dish_families.name: Easy Boneless Chicken Shami Kabab - Instant Pot & Stove Top

variants.name: Easy Boneless Chicken Shami Kabab - Instant Pot & Stove Top
variants.dish_family: Easy Boneless Chicken Shami Kabab - Instant Pot & Stove Top

ingredients.preparation: close to exact please and after trimming any large chunks of fat
ingredients.text: 1 lb Boneless Chicken Thighs (close to exact please and after trimming any large chunks of fat)
1 lb Boneless Chicken Breast (close to exact!)
1 cup Chana Daal (200g) (Soaked 4-6 hours or overnight (preferred))
1/2 cup Diced Onion (half a medium-large onion) (50 to 60g)

ingredients.item: Green Cardamom Pods (just seeds or use 1 tsp cardamom powder)
ingredients.text: 4 Green Cardamom Pods (just seeds or use 1 tsp cardamom powder) (Optional)
Small Cinnamon Stick (2 cm or 3/4 inch)

ingredients.preparation: plus additional to adjust seasoning to taste
ingredients.text: 3 tsp Salt (plus additional to adjust seasoning to taste)

instructions: Mix all the ingredients except the Hara Masala ones in the Instant Pot along with half a cup water and give it a mix. Close the lid, set to seal and set to pressure for 25 Minutes and then natural release (that means turn the machine off and walk away till the pressure releases, and then open the valve.).

Put the Instant pot on saute mode and saute until the excess moisture dries out and the meat mix begins to stick to the bottom. Mix all the ingredients EXCEPT the green masala ones in a pot with 2 cups of water, bring to a boil and simmer on low for 45 minutes or until the daal is completely tender.

Crank up the heat, dry up excess water, your meat mixture should start to stick. Decision time: for a smooth kabab run the entire meat mix through a food processor (in batches or one go) OR run half of it through a food processor and mix it into the original kabab mix.
Stir in ALL the hara masala, feel free to sneak a taste! Wet your palms and shape the kababs to your preferred size.

Cook A TEST KABAB! Line a tray with parchment paper/plastic wrap and Put your kababs on it as you shape them. Put the tray in the freezer and once the kababs are frozen and then you can transfer them to a freezer safe container or bag.
To Cook: defrost on the counter or in the fridge or microwave and and then shallow Cook on medium high heat for about 1.5 minute per side.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Easy Boneless Chicken Shami Kabab - Instant Pot & Stove Top

variants.name: Easy Lemon Mousse

ingredients.text: 1/3-1/2 cup lemon juice (1/2 if you want it tart!)
2 cups biscuit crumbs (recommend: ginger), for layering

ingredients.item: a few drops of yellow food colour
ingredients.text: a few drops of yellow food colour

instructions: Let it sit until it absorbs into the water (a few minutes) and then heat it in the microwave for 30 seconds, if it doesn't dissolve into a liquid and then heat it some more.
Mix in the condensed milk on medium speed, and then the lemon juice, and finally the dissolved (cooled) gelatin.
Layer the crumbs (if using) at the bottom of a dish and then gently spoon the lemon mousse on top and smoothen it. Chill for a minimum of 2 hours and decorate as desired.

variants.name: Easy Marble Cake with Oil

ingredients.text: 1/2 cup neutral oil (such as corn oil) (112g)

instructions: Mix the first three ingredients in a bowl, set aside.
Stir in the vanilla, beat for 30 seconds to Mix.
Alternately Stir in the flour and milk to the bowl in two batches and mix until just combined.
Put a cup of the batter into a small bowl, Stir in the 3 tbsp cocoa and 1 tbsp milk and mix until just combined.
The batter for this cake is thin, so carefully Stir in it to the loaf pan, alternating between dollops of vanilla and chocolate batter.
Bake for an hour or until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean.
Warm the cream until simmering, pour over the chocolate and mix well.

dish_families.name: EASY Pasanday Recipe - Instant Pot & Stove Top

variants.name: EASY Pasanday Recipe - Instant Pot & Stove Top
variants.dish_family: EASY Pasanday Recipe - Instant Pot & Stove Top

ingredients.preparation: or 1 rounded tsp of ginger paste
ingredients.text: 3/4 inch piece of ginger - grated (or 1 rounded tsp of ginger paste)
6 cloves crushed/minced garlic (or 1 rounded tsp garlic paste)

instructions: Warm the oil in your Instant Pot on Saute, Normal heat.
When it shimmers Stir in the cinnamon, cloves, whole black pepper, and cardamom, saute for 30 seconds and when aromatic Stir in the onions.
Saute the onions stirring occasionally until the edges turn golden brown.
And then Stir in your ginger and garlic, saute for a minute.
Stir in the meat followed by the spices (salt, chili powder, chili flakes, garam masala, coriander powder, turmeric).
Stir in a cup and a half of hot water, stir and set the instant pot on manual for 8 minutes OR Stir in 2 cups of hot water and simmer on low for 30.
Quick release when done and check for tenderness, if your meat isn't as soft as you would like you can simmer it for a little longer otherwise turn on the saute mode to dry up the masala.
When the oil rises to the top and then turn the Instant Pot or stove off and gradually Stir in your yogurt.
The yogurt will cook in the residual heat, stir gently to Mix, taste, adjust seasoning and serve.

source_attributions.recipe_title: EASY Pasanday Recipe - Instant Pot & Stove Top

variants.name: Easy Velvety Mango Mousse
instructions: Sprinkle powdered gelatin over the water and let it sit for 4-5 minutes.
Warm the mixture for 20-30 seconds in the microwave and stir - the gelatin should dissolve entirely.
Whip 2 cups of cream in a large bowl on medium speed until soft peaks form - this can take anywhere from 4-8 minutes.
Stir in the sugar and whip until stiff peaks form.
Beat in your mango puree and cardamom powder, you may need to scrape the bowl from the bottom with a spatula to fold in your puree to evenly incorporate it. Do not stir!
Pour your gelatin in through a sieve and beat for 10 seconds.
Transfer the mango mousse into your serving dish or dishes and chill for at least two hours.

variants.name: Eclairs with Whipped Cream (Smaller Batch)

ingredients.preparation: Granulated where it's fine, Caster otherwise
ingredients.text: 1/4 cup Sugar (Granulated where it's fine, Caster otherwise)

instructions: Bring the first four ingredients to a boil in a small pot.
Remove from the heat and Stir in the flour all at once, stir well with a wooden spoon.
Transfer the dough to a mixing bowl, let it cool for a few minutes.
Stir in your eggs one by one beating well until the dough comes together to create something that is cohesive and shiny.
Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F.
Bake for 16-18 minutes for slim eclairs, 20 minutes for thicker ones.
Warm the cream to barely simmering, stir in chocolate chips to melt, set aside to cool (and thicken).
As it thickens and then Stir in the sugar gradually until stiff peaks form, turning it up to high.
Mix in the Vanilla, adjust for taste adding in more sugar if needed.

variants.name: Egg Bhurji (Khagina) Recipe

ingredients.text: 1/4 onion (roughly 2 ounce or 57 grams) ( roughly diced)
1 teaspoon red chili powder (preferably Kashmiri red chili powder )
1 small potato (roughly 4 ounce or 113 grams) (thinly sliced)
1 roma tomato (roughly 2 ounce or 57 grams) (roughly diced)

instructions: In a nonstick skillet, heat oil. Once it begins to shimmer, Stir in chopped onion and Cook on medium heat until translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in turmeric powder and red chili powder, and Cook on medium-low heat until fragrant.
Raise heat to medium-high. Stir in chopped potatoes, tomato and green chili, and begin to Cook until the mixture is well-coated in the masala, and potatoes are done, roughly 10 minutes.
Lower heat to medium, and Stir in eggs and cilantro. Remove from heat if necessary to prevent eggs from overcooking.
Remove from heat and serve immediately with roti or any bread of your choice.

variants.name: Lahori Egg Fried Rice

ingredients.text: 3 cups paka hua chawal (cooked cold rice)

instructions: Ensure your wok or karahi is properly heated — 3-4 minutes on maximum heat before adding oil.
Stir in oil to the screaming hot wok. Stir in garlic, ginger, and onion all at once. Cook aggressively on high heat for 1-2 minutes until the onion is translucent and the garlic is golden.
Stir in hari mirch, shimla mirch, and matar. Stir-Cook 2 minutes on high heat.
Stir in beaten eggs. Mix partially with the vegetables — Aim for egg pieces visible throughout.
Stir in cold rice and break up any clumps with the back of your spatula. Stir in soya sauce, chilli sauce, ketchup, and kali mirch. Toss everything on high heat for 3 minutes.
Lahori fried rice tends to be slightly wetter and more sauced than Karachi style — it should coat the rice generously.

variants.name: Vegetable Fried Rice Pakistani Style

ingredients.text: 3 cups paka hua chawal (cooked cold rice)

instructions: Get everything chopped, measured, and ready before you turn on the heat.
Warm wok on highest setting for 3 minutes. Stir in oil and let it shimmer.
Stir in garlic, ginger, and hari mirch. Stir constantly 30 seconds. Stir in spring onion whites.
Stir in gajar and shimla mirch — stir-Cook 2 minutes. Stir in band gobhi and matar — stir-Cook 1 more minute.
Stir in cold rice. Stir in soya sauce around the edges, sirka, and kali mirch. Toss everything together 2-3 minutes on high heat.

variants.name: Karachi Chicken Fried Rice

ingredients.text: 3 cups paka hua chawal (cooked cold rice)

instructions: Toss chicken cubes with 1 tsp soya sauce, a pinch of kali mirch, and salt. Let sit 10 minutes. Heat 2 tbsp oil in the wok on high heat and stir-Cook chicken cubes 3-4 minutes until just cooked through and slightly golden.
Stir in remaining oil to the wok. Let it heat on maximum for 2 minutes.
Stir in garlic, ginger, and spring onion whites. Stir 30 seconds. Stir in carrot and peas.
Stir in beaten eggs. Don't fully mix with vegetables yet.
Stir in RICE, CHICKEN, AND SAUCES: Stir in cold rice to the wok. Stir in pre-cooked chicken. Drizzle soya sauce around the edges, Stir in chilli sauce and kali mirch.
Taste and adjust salt, kali mirch, and soya sauce.

variants.name: Pakistani Egg Fried Rice
instructions: If using freshly cooked rice, spread it on a large tray or baking sheet and let it cool completely for at least 30 minutes, and then refrigerate for another 30 minutes if time allows.
Warm 1 tbsp oil in your wok over high heat until it shimmers. Pour in the beaten eggs.

Stir in the remaining 2 tbsp oil to the very hot wok. Stir in the minced garlic, white parts of the spring onions, and green chillies. Stir-Cook for 30-40 seconds — the garlic should turn golden and fragrant but not brown.
Stir in the cold day-old basmati rice to the wok in one go. and then stir and repeat.

Drizzle the dark soy sauce over the rice in a circular motion. Stir in the oyster sauce. Toss everything together vigorously until the colour is even — Aim for every grain to go from white to light golden-brown.
Stir-Cook for 30 more seconds to heat the eggs through. Remove from heat. Drizzle the sesame oil over the rice and fold through — do this off the heat so the oil does not burn.

variants.name: Pakistani Street-Style Egg Fried Rice

ingredients.text: 3 cups paka hua chawal (cooked and cooled rice)
1 tsp kali mirch powder (black pepper powder)

instructions: Put your karahi or wok over the highest heat your stove allows. Let it heat for 2-3 minutes until very hot. Stir in oil and swirl to coat.
Cook GARLIC, GINGER, CHILLI: Stir in minced garlic, ginger, and green chillies to the hot oil. Stir constantly for 30 seconds — they'll sizzle aggressively. Stir in spring onion whites.
Stir in diced carrot and peas. Stir-Cook on high heat for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in eggs to the cleared space.
Stir in cold rice to the wok. Stir in sirka and kali mirch. Toss everything together for 2-3 minutes on high heat.

dish_families.name: Eggplant Yogurt Dip: Baingan Ka Bharta

variants.name: Eggplant Yogurt Dip: Baingan Ka Bharta
variants.dish_family: Eggplant Yogurt Dip: Baingan Ka Bharta
instructions: Pre-heat your oven to 200C / 400F. Put large frying pan on medium-high heat and Stir in 3 tbsp oil.

Stir in minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds, (make sure the garlic does not turn brown). Stir in roasted cumin powder and stir for another 30 seconds, till fragrant. Stir in aubergine flesh, salt, 1⁄2 tsp turmeric and green chilies and turn heat to high.
Sauté rigorously for 5 minutes, till you see that all the excess liquid has been absorbed. Turn heat off and set aside.
