Transfer aubergine to a mixing bowl and stir in yoghurt till fully incorporated. Transfer to a serving dish and refrigerate for at least one hour.

Put a small frying pan on high heat and Stir in 2 tbsp of oil. When hot, Stir in a pinch of turmeric and red chilli powder and immediately remove from heat. Before serving, gently pour oil in a circular design over the yoghurt and aubergine mixture in the serving dish.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Eggplant Yogurt Dip: Baingan Ka Bharta

variants.name: Eid Sugar Cookies (Small batch)

ingredients.item: Store bought royal icing mix OR
ingredients.text: 200 g Store bought royal icing mix OR

ingredients.item: for an alternate decorating idea read notes
ingredients.text: for an alternate decorating idea read notes

instructions: Mix the butter, sugar and lemon zest until just smooth. Mix in the egg yolk, beat 30 seconds.
Stir in in the flour and salt and mix, the dough will look crumbly but come together when pressed together. If it is hot where you are and then chill the dough for 30 minutes.
Depending on where you are you may want to Stir in more flour. Roll out the dough about 1/4 inch thick and cut with cutters of choice.
Bake till the edges are golden - 10 minutes for medium sized cookies, adjust for smaller or larger ones. Knead dough again, roll and cut cookies until it is used up.

If using a royal icing mix follow package decorations for a stiff icing and then gradually (very gradullay, drops of water at a time) Stir in enough water that the consistency is toothpaste like. If making royal icing and then mix the icing sugar, milk, salt and vanilla on low speed until just combined, adjust the thickness by adding more icing sugar.

variants.name: Karachi Falooda

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp per glass Rooh Afza (Rose Syrup)
2 tbsp Tukmaria / Tukh Malanga (Basil Seeds / Sabja Seeds)

ingredients.item: scoop per glass Kulfi or Vanilla Ice Cream
ingredients.text: 1 scoop per glass Kulfi or Vanilla Ice Cream
1 tsp per glass Gulkand (Rose Petal Jam)
1 tbsp per glass Pista aur Badam (Pistachios and Almonds)

instructions: Put the tukmaria (basil seeds) in a bartan (bowl) with 1 cup cold water. Stir once and leave for 20-30 minutes.
Bring a pateela (saucepan) of water to a boil. Stir in the falooda seviyan and cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are soft but still have a slight chew.
If using instant mix or bought rabri, prepare as instructed and chill thoroughly. The rabri should be thick enough to pour slowly — not solid, not liquid.

BUILD THE GLASS — LAYER 1 (BOTTOM): Use a tall, wide glass — a milkshake glass or any 400-500ml glass. Start with gulkand (rose petal jam) if using: Stir in 1 teaspoon to the very bottom. and then Stir in the soaked tukmaria (basil seeds) — 2 tablespoons.

BUILD THE GLASS — LAYER 2 (NOODLES AND ROSE SYRUP): Stir in a generous pile of the cooled falooda seviyan (vermicelli) — about 3-4 tablespoons. and then pour 4 tablespoons of Rooh Afza rose syrup over the noodles. Stir in the crushed baraf (ice) — pack it in.

BUILD THE GLASS — LAYER 3 (MILK AND RABRI): Pour the cold doodh (milk) gently over the ice — about 3-4 tablespoons. and then spoon the rabri over in a thick layer — 3-4 tablespoons. Pour it slowly so it sits on top of the milk rather than.
Put one scoop of kulfi or vanilla ice cream on the very top of the glass — this is the crown. Stir in a pinch of dried rose petals if you have them.

The etiquette is to eat the ice cream first with the spoon, and then stir the whole glass gently (just enough to mix, not to fully homogenise) and drink through the straw. Do not let a falooda sit for more than 10 minutes before drinking — the ice.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Stir in basil seeds to 1 cup cold water. Stir and leave for 30 minutes — they expand dramatically into jelly-like pearls. Drain and refrigerate.

Boil water in a small saucepan. Stir in falooda sev and cook for 2-3 minutes until softened but still slightly firm (al dente — it will soften further in the milk). Drain, rinse under cold water immediately, and refrigerate in a small amount of cold water.
Every element must be cold before assembling. Make sure your glasses are chilled too — put them in the freezer for 10 minutes.
In a tall glass, Stir in 1 tbsp rose syrup. Stir in 2 tbsp soaked tukmaria seeds. Stir in 2-3 tbsp falooda sev.
Put a generous scoop of vanilla ice cream on top of the milk.
Stir lightly as you go to mix the layers — that first spoonful of everything together is peak Karachi.

variants.name: Ferrero Rocher Brownies
instructions: Melt the butter over low heat, and then pull the pan off the stove and stir in the chopped chocolate until it melts.
Beat the eggs, sugar, salt and vanilla on high for 4-5 minutes until the mix becomes pale and thick.
Pour the batter into the prepared dish and smooth the top.
Take a little batter and cover the top of the chocolate balls to protect the chocolate from burning.
Bake until the top looks slightly cracked 25-35 minutes (depending on pan).

variants.name: Fish Salan Recipe

ingredients.item: boneless white fish cut into 2.5-3 inch pieces
ingredients.text: 400 g boneless white fish cut into 2.5-3 inch pieces

ingredients.preparation: kashmiri chili powder is lovely here!
ingredients.text: 1/4-1/2 tsp chili powder (kashmiri chili powder is lovely here!)

ingredients.item: neutral oil (vegetable) or your preferred cooking oil
ingredients.text: 3-4 tbsp neutral oil (vegetable) or your preferred cooking oil

instructions: Warm your oil in a wide bottomed pan on medium high heat and Stir in the curry leaves.
Once thee curry leaves get nice and aromatic Stir in in your minced onions and saute until the edges get lightly golden.
Stir in in your spices, cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in in the tomato and turn the heat up to accelerate cooking the moisture out, in about 2-3 minutes see oil starting to rise above the surface.

Pour in about a cup of hot water. You have two options .1.) bring it to a boil and simmer for 10-15 minutes to soften the masala and bring it together2.) blend it all together (curry leaves are ok to be blended in) using an immersion blender or.
If you took approach (2) and then crank up the heat to dry out the masala a little and let it separate.
Gently Put your fish pieces in the dish, cook for a few minutes, flip.
Stir in your kasuri methi, half your chilies and cilantro, and cover and let the fish cook for 3-4 minutes.

Adjust the curries consistency to your liking with hot water, bring to a boil and turn the stove off (fish breaks easily so we don't want to manhandle it or boil for too long). Taste, adjust seasoning and garnish with remaining garnishes.

variants.name: Flavorful Achari Aloo

ingredients.preparation: I usually do slim 1/2 cm thick pieces for quicker cooking
ingredients.text: 4-5 Diced Potatoes (I usually do slim 1/2 cm thick pieces for quicker cooking)
1/2 tsp ginger garlic paste (or a 1/4 tsp each)

instructions: Mix all the ingredients in a small bowl and set aside.
Warm 1/4 cup of oil in a saucepan with a lid.
Saute the onions on medium heat until the edges are turning golden brown.
Stir in the ginger garlic paste, saute for 30 seconds.
Stir in in the achari masala ingredients and saute till aromatic.
Mix in the chopped potatoes and tomato, make sure you mix well.
Cover and cook on low flame for 20 minutes, Stir in a splash of water if the mix starts to stick.
After 20 minutes check for doneness, if the potatoes are tender you can adjust consistency by adding water or drying it up (your preference).
Stir in a squeeze of lemon juice and then taste and adjust seasoning.

variants.name: Fried Pumpkin Flower

ingredients.text: Pinch of salt or to taste

ingredients.item: canola (sunflower or vegetable oil (can be reused))
ingredients.text: 2 cups canola (sunflower or vegetable oil (can be reused))

instructions: Stir in 4 tbsp of water in a bowl. Stir in salt, red chili powder and rice flour. Mix well to make a paste.
Warm the oil in a small saucepan. Once hot, bring heat to medium-low.
Dip each blossom in the paste and and then with a slotted spoon, carefully Put in pan to Cook.
Cook each blossom till crispy brown, about 1 1⁄2 - 2 minutes per blossom.
Transfer blossoms to a paper towel to absorb excess oil.

variants.name: Frontier Style Fried Fish

ingredients.preparation: cleaned and sliced in 4 pieces lengthwise
ingredients.text: 1 1/2 pound fish fillet, preferably freshwater trout (cleaned and sliced in 4 pieces lengthwise)
3/4 cup oil or as needed (canola, vegetable or sunflower)

instructions: Generously season it with salt and red chili powder and set aside to marinade for 15 minutes.
In a deep saucepan or wok, heat oil. When hot, carefully Put the fish fillet in the wok with a slotted spoon and Cook each side for about two minutes or until golden brown.
Drain on paper towels or newspaper.

variants.name: Gajar Ka Halwa — Classic Pakistani Carrot Dessert
instructions: In a bhari degh (heavy-bottomed pot) or large pateela (saucepan), Stir in the grated gajar and pour in 1 litre of full-fat doodh (milk). Bring to a boil on high heat, stirring frequently with a chamcha (ladle) so the milk doesn't scorch on the bottom. Once boiling, reduce.
Begins the meditation. Cook the carrot-milk mixture on medium-low heat, stirring every 5-7 minutes, for 45-60 minutes.

Once the milk has fully evaporated and the mixture looks thick and jammy with no visible liquid, Stir in 2 tbsp of ghee (clarified butter) and stir it through. Stir in the cheeni (sugar) and the freshly ground elaichi (cardamom) powder. Stir well.

Once the sugar liquid has dried up and the halwa looks shiny and cohesive, crumble in the khoya (dried milk solids). Stir vigorously — the khoya will melt in and make the halwa incredibly rich and fudgy. Cook for another 5 minutes.
Turn off the heat. Stir in the remaining 2 tbsp ghee — this last addition gives the halwa a beautiful gloss and keeps it from drying out as it cools. you can Stir in more cheeni if needed.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Gajar Ka Halwa — Classic Pakistani Carrot Dessert

variants.name: Gajar Ka Halwa — Quick Stovetop Version
instructions: Peel and finely grate carrots using a box grater or food processor. Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a wide, heavy-bottomed karahi over high heat. Stir in grated carrots and cook on high for 8-10 minutes, stirring constantly, until most of the moisture evaporates and the carrots shrink significantly.
Pour the milk over the dried carrots and stir well. Cook on medium-high heat, stirring every 3-4 minutes, until all the milk is absorbed — about 20-25 minutes.
Stir in sugar and stir through. The sugar will initially release more moisture — keep stirring on medium heat for another 8-10 minutes until the liquid is reabsorbed and the halwa looks fudgy again.
Crumble in the khoya and Stir in the remaining 2 tbsp ghee. Stir vigorously for 3-4 minutes.
Stir in cardamom powder and fold in the fried raisins and half the almonds. The halwa is done when it holds its shape on a spoon and ghee starts to separate slightly at the edges.
Spoon into bowls or shape into a mound on a flat plate.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Gajar Ka Halwa — Quick Stovetop Version

dish_families.name: Garam Masala Recipe - Pakistani 10 Minute Recipe

variants.name: Garam Masala Recipe - Pakistani 10 Minute Recipe
variants.dish_family: Garam Masala Recipe - Pakistani 10 Minute Recipe
instructions: Put a pan on medium high heat and dry roast the peppercorns, cloves, black cardamom, and cinnamon bark until fragrant and toasty. This takes about 2-3 minutes.

Transfer the whole spices to a plate to cool and Stir in the cumin seeds to the same pan stirring frequently until evenly toasted - another 2 minutes or so. Stir in to the same plate as the other whole spices and let cool a little.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Garam Masala Recipe - Pakistani 10 Minute Recipe

variants.name: Garlic Naan

ingredients.text: 3/4 cup, approximately neem garam pani (lukewarm water)
1/2 cup, loosely packed hara dhania (fresh coriander/cilantro)

instructions: Activate the khameer (instant dry yeast) with cheeni (sugar) and 1/4 cup lukewarm pani (water) — wait 5-10 minutes until foamy. In a large bowl, Mix maida (refined white flour), namak (salt), dahi (yoghurt), tel (oil), and the foamy yeast. Stir in lukewarm water gradually, mixing to form.

In a small saucepan or small karahi (wok), melt the makhan (butter) over low heat. Stir in the finely minced lehsun (garlic). Cook for NO MORE than 60 seconds — Aim for the garlic to just begin to soften, still white or very pale yellow.
Stir the finely chopped hara dhania (fresh coriander) into the garlic butter.
Crank your oven to its maximum temperature — 250°C (480°F) or higher. Allow the oven and pan to preheat for at least 30 minutes.

Punch down the proofed dough. On a lightly floured surface, roll each ball into an oval about 25cm long, 12cm wide, and 5mm thick. The shape does not need to be precise — Garlic Naan is rustic by nature.
Carefully slide 1-2 shaped naans onto the screaming-hot cast-iron pan. Bake for 4-6 minutes, watching closely.

variants.name: Garlicky Spinach and Potato Croquettes
instructions: Stir in the garlic and and then saute for another 30 seconds before adding the remaining spices.
Give it a quick stir and then remove from the pan.
Mix in the spice mix and the spinach and taste.
Get a piping bag or a ziploc bag and cut a 3/4-1 inch hole in the tip. Fill your bag with the potato mix and pipe out 3 inch croquettes trimming with kitchen scissors as you go along.
Freeze for 30 minutes for easier handling.
Roll each cutlet in egg wash and and then breadcrumbs. Cook immediately for 2 minutes on each side till golden or freeze for another day.

variants.name: Gawar Sabzi Recipe

ingredients.text: 1 small yellow or red onion (thinly sliced in half rings)
1/2 teaspoon red chili powder (preferably Kashmiri red chili powder )

ingredients.item: gawar or any variety of green beans
ingredients.text: 12 ounce gawar or any variety of green beans (sliced crosswise, roughly 1-inch thick)

instructions: Warm oil in a saucepan and Stir in cumin seeds. Cook until aromatic.
Stir in onions and sauté on medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes until soft and translucent.
Lower heat and Stir in crushed ginger and garlic. Cook for 30 seconds or until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, salt and ground spices (turmeric and red chili powder). Increase heat to high and Cook until the tomatoes soften, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in chopped green beans and mix well.
Stir in the diced potatoes and continue to sauté on high heat for 5-7 minutes.
Lower heat to medium, cover the pan with a tight fitting lid and let the potatoes steam until ready.
Remove from heat.

variants.name: Ginger Paste

ingredients.text: 1/3 cup neutral oil - vegetable or olive

instructions: Mix your ginger slices and oil in a mini blender and puree till smooth, adding a little extra liquid if necessary.
If your blender is not very powerful and then Stir in half the ginger and all of the oil and puree. Once smooth and then Stir in remaining ginger.

variants.name: Gluten Free Corn Fritters (Sweetcorn Pakoras)

ingredients.text: 2 Tbsp corn flour (or more gram flour)
1/2 tsp sea salt (or more, to taste)
1 Thai bird's eye green chilli (finely chopped)

instructions: In a large mixing bowl Mix flours with corn, Thai bird's eye green chilli, red chilli flakes, dill, onions, garam masala, salt, baking powder, baking soda, and turmeric. Mix to Mix.
Warm three inches of oil in a heavy-bottomed pot on high heat, to 350F.
Cook, agitating and turning the pakoras, for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, until they turn golden-brown and are cooked through. Adjust heat up or down, as necessary, to maintain a temperature of 350-360F.
Remove cooked pakoras from the oil and transfer to a large platter lined with paper towels.

variants.name: Gobi Chicken

ingredients.item: Boneless Chicken cut into 1.5 inch cubes
ingredients.text: 3/4 lb Boneless Chicken cut into 1.5 inch cubes

ingredients.item: Cauliflower Florets - half a large cauliflower or one small one
ingredients.text: 2-2.5 cups Cauliflower Florets - half a large cauliflower or one small one

ingredients.item: piece of ginger, cut into matchsticks
ingredients.text: 2 inch piece of ginger, cut into matchsticks

ingredients.item: lemon juice, just a squeeze for seasoning
ingredients.text: lemon juice, just a squeeze for seasoning

instructions: Warm a pan and Stir in a generous lug of oil (about 1/4 cup). Stir in the cumin seeds to the pan and when they sizzle Stir in the diced onions.
Once the edges of the onion start to turn golden brown and then Stir in the ginger and garlic paste. Stir and and then Stir in all the dry spices and salt.
Saute for a minute and and then Stir in the chicken. Keep cooking the chicken on medium high heat, stirring to ensure that the colour changes and the chicken starts to look cooked.
Stir in the green chilies and a cup of water to the pan. Bring to a boil and and then simmer with a lid on for about 25 minutes.

Gently mix in your cauliflower florets, cover and cook for another 10-12 minutes or until they're just fork tender, not mushy. Stir in the remaining ingredients - the scallions, ginger, cilantro, a few grinds of pepper and a squeeze of lemon juice.

variants.name: Gobi Gosht - Beef & Cauliflower Stew

ingredients.item: A Head of Cauliflower approximately 2 1/2 cups chopped
ingredients.text: 1/2 A Head of Cauliflower approximately 2 1/2 cups chopped
1 lb Boneless Beef (cut into 1.5 inch chunks)

ingredients.preparation: add an extra 1/2 if you really want it spicy!!
ingredients.text: 1 tsp red chilli powder (add an extra 1/2 if you really want it spicy!!)

instructions: Mix everything from the boneless beef through to the cumin seeds in a pot or a pressure cooker. If using a pot and then Stir in two cups of hot water, mix, bring to a boil and then simmer for an hour. If using an Instant Pot cook.
Crank up the heat and dry up the masala until it starts to stick and then Stir in a lug of oil and cook till the oil seperates from the masala.
Stir in the chopped cauliflowers and mix well.
Cover and cook on low until the cauliflower is almost tender, 10 - 12 minutes, Stir in a splash of water if it starts to stick.
When the cauliflower is done sprinkle the ginger mix over and stir to disperse being careful not to mush the cauliflower.

variants.name: Gobi Gosht Recipe (Mutton with Cauliflower)

ingredients.text: 1 pound (~500 grams) goat/lamb meat (cut in small pieces)
3/4 cup neutral oil (canola, sunflower or vegetable )

ingredients.item: (~3-5 ounces/100-150 grams) yellow or red onions
ingredients.text: 2 small (~3-5 ounces/100-150 grams) yellow or red onions (thinly sliced)
1 pound (~500 grams) cauliflower (cut in small florets)

instructions: Warm heavy bottom pot and Stir in 1⁄2 cup oil. Once hot, Stir in sliced onion and sauté until evenly brown, roughly 7-10 minutes. Stir in crushed ginger and garlic, and bird’s eye chili (if using). Stir for roughly 30 seconds to 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in meat and stir on high heat until no longer pink for about 5-7 minutes.

Stir in tomatoes, red chili powder, 1⁄2 teaspoon of salt and whole garam masala (cumin seeds, cloves, peppercorn, green and black cardamom). Stir until well-mixed. Stir in 2 1⁄2 cups water and bring to boil. Lower to simmer and cover. Cook until the meat is tender about 2 – 2 1⁄2 hours. In a large wok or frying pan, heat remaining 1⁄4.

Once the meat is tender, carefully remove the lid and Stir in cauliflower. Increase heat to high, and stir until the cauliflower has absorbed the masala and the oil begins to separate from the spices. Remove from heat. Garnish with diced cilantro and chilies, and dust with garam masala powder. Once hot, Stir in 1⁄2 cup oil and sliced onion. Sauté until.

Stir in crushed ginger and garlic, and bird’s eye chili (if using). Stir for roughly 30 seconds to 1 minute until fragrant. Stir in meat and stir until no longer pink for about 5-7 minutes. Stir in tomatoes, red chili powder, salt and whole garam masala (cumin seeds, cloves, peppercorn, green and black cardamom). Stir until well-mixed.

Stir in 1⁄2 cup water or at least enough to cover 1/3rd of the meat mixture. Move the steam valve to sealing, and on manual setting, set the cooking time to 25 minutes at high pressure. In a large wok or frying pan, heat remaining 1⁄4 cup oil. Once hot, Stir in cauliflower, salt and pepper. Sauté until just slightly brown and.

Select ‘Sauté’ again and Stir in cooked cauliflower to the meat mixture. Cook until the cauliflower has absorbed the masala and the oil begins to separate from the spices. Garnish with diced cilantro and chilies, and dust with garam masala powder.

variants.name: Gobi Paratha

ingredients.text: 1/4 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Mix atta and 1⁄2 tsp salt in a wide paraat (mixing bowl). Stir in warm water gradually, mixing with your fingers until a dough forms. Knead for 5–6 minutes — push the dough away from you with the heel of your hand, fold it back, turn, and repeat.

GRATE AND DRY THE CAULIFLOWER (the most critical step): Break or cut the cauliflower into chunks and grate them on the fine or medium holes of a box grater into a bowl. Sprinkle 1 tsp salt over the grated gobhi, mix, and leave for 10 minutes.

In a clean bowl, Mix the squeezed gobhi, grated adrak, chopped hari mirch, ajwain, hara dhania, and lal mirch powder if using. Mix thoroughly. Taste a small pinch — it should be well-seasoned from the residual salt, fragrant from the ajwain, and have a little heat from the.
Take one ball, dust it in flour, and roll it on your chakla (rolling board) into a circle about 12 cm across using your belan (rolling pin).
Dust the filled ball lightly in flour and Put seal-side-down on the chakla. Roll from the centre outward in all directions, rotating the paratha a quarter turn after every few rolls.

Warm your tawa (flat griddle pan) over medium heat for 2 minutes. Cook for about 90 seconds until the surface changes from glossy to matte and you see small bubbles forming. Flip with a spatula — the cooked side should be pale gold with dry speckles, not brown.
Transfer to a plate or roti basket.

variants.name: Gol Gappay
instructions: START WITH THE PANI (make this first so it has time to chill). In a blender, Mix the podina (mint) leaves, hara dhaniya (coriander — stems and all), hari mirch (green chillies), and 1 cup of water. Blend on high until completely smooth — about 30-45 seconds.
Pour the green mixture through a chalni (fine sieve or muslin cloth) into a bari jug (large jug or pitcher).

To the strained green liquid, Stir in the remaining 3 cups of thanda pani (cold water), imli (tamarind) paste, chaat masala, bhuna zeera (roasted cumin powder), kala namak (black salt), regular namak (salt) to taste, and gur (jaggery). Stir well until the gur dissolves completely. Stir in more.
In a bari pyali (large bowl), mix the suji (semolina) and maida (all-purpose flour) with a pinch of namak (salt). Stir in water very gradually — about 1-2 tablespoons at a time — and mix as you go.
Knead the dough for a full 10 minutes. Yes, 10 minutes. This kneading develops the gluten that gives the puris structure to hold their hollow shape when fried.

Take one portion and roll it out on a lightly floured surface — VERY thin, about 1-2mm. Use a bottle cap or small round cookie cutter (about 4cm diameter) to cut out circles. Gather the scraps, re-knead briefly, and roll again.
Warm the tel (oil) in a karahi (wok) or deep pot to 180 degrees C (350 degrees F).
Cook the purian in small batches (4-5 at a time — do not crowd the karahi). Drain on paper towels or a wire rack.

In a pyali (bowl), Mix the ublay chanay (boiled chickpeas), diced ublay aloo (boiled potatoes), chaat masala, lal mirch (red chilli powder), a pinch of bhuna zeera (roasted cumin powder), and namak (salt) to taste.

variants.name: Karachi Gol Gappay with Imli Paani

ingredients.text: 1/2 tsp lal mirch for filling (red chilli)
4 pieces hari mirch for paani (green chilli)

instructions: Mix semolina, flour and salt. Stir in warm water gradually, mixing until a firm, stiff dough forms — firmer than roti dough. Knead for 5 minutes until smooth.
Divide dough into 3 portions. Roll each portion extremely thin — about 1-2mm. Cut into small circles using a round cutter or the rim of a glass (4-5cm diameter).
Warm oil in a karahi to 180°C. Once puffed, Cook for another minute until golden and crisp.
Mix mashed potato with boiled chickpeas, chaat masala, red chilli, salt and fresh coriander. Mix well.
Blend mint, green chilli, tamarind extract, roasted cumin, kala namak and regular salt with 600ml cold water. Strain through a sieve. Stir in more tamarind or chilli as needed.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Karachi Gol Gappay with Imli Paani

variants.name: Gola Kabab

ingredients.item: ground beef (keema) with 20% fat at least
ingredients.text: 1 lb ground beef (keema) with 20% fat at least

ingredients.item: a piece of coal for smoke
ingredients.text: a piece of coal for smoke

instructions: Mix all the ingredients listed above in a food processor and process till combined.

Check to see if you can easily shape it into a kabab, and if so Cook a test piece to check your flavors and adjust if needed. The kababs will get softer and more flavorful as they sit, If your mix is too soft: Stir in a tbsp.
Transfer the mix to a bowl with a lid or one you can cover with a plate.
Take a piece of coal and heat it stove top - directly for gas or on a rack for a ceramic cooktop. For a ceramic cooktop let it heat (without moving) until bright red.
While it's heating Put an onion peel or a piece of foil in the bowl with the meat mix, on top of the meat. Cover and let it sit for 15 minutes to let that smoke fully infuse.
Form a kabab into a 2 inch ball and run the dowel through it to form that iconic shape. Repeat until the meat mix is used up.
For freezing: Put them in a tray, flash freeze for an hour or two until solid and then transfer to a ziploc bag or box and keep for up to 3 months.
For frying: Cook the gola kabab on medium heat, not too high, for a few minutes on each side until cooked through.

variants.name: Lahori Gola Kebab

ingredients.text: 1.5 tsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)
1 tsp Kachri Powder (Dried Mango Powder / Tenderiser)

instructions: Warm a dry tawa (flat griddle) or frying pan on medium-low heat. Stir in the besan (gram flour) and stir constantly with a chamcha (spoon) for 3-4 minutes.

In a large bartan (bowl), Mix the beef mince and lamb mince. Stir in: raw papaya paste, roasted besan, ginger-garlic paste, green chillies, and red chilli powder. Mix with your hands — no spoon will do this properly.
Cover the bartan with cling film and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
Wet your hands with cold water.
Prepare your mangal (charcoal grill) with a good bed of hot coals.
Warm a piece of hardwood charcoal directly on your stove flame until it glows bright orange — 3-4 minutes. Wait 2-3 minutes.

variants.name: Punjabi Gola Kebab

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
1 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Very finely chop the mint — Punjabi gola kebab has mint throughout, not just as garnish.
Mix all ingredients. Mix for 6-8 minutes until mixture is very homogeneous.
Shape into round discs, slightly thicker than Karachi version (Punjabi gola kebab tends to be chunkier). Refrigerate 30-45 minutes.
Warm tawa with generous oil on medium-high. Stir in gola kebabs and cook 5 minutes first side until deep brown crust forms.
Flip once and cook another 4-5 minutes. Drain excess oil briefly.
Lahori gola kebab is typically spicier than Karachi version at serving — Stir in extra green chilli on the side.

variants.name: Gola Kebab Karachi

ingredients.text: 1.5 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
1.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Gola kebab must hold its shape when pressed — any moisture causes it to fall apart when cooking.
Mix all ingredients. Mix for 5-7 minutes until very homogeneous and sticky. The besan and egg white together give gola its distinctive binding that allows it to hold the round shape.
Wet hands and shape mixture into round, slightly flattened discs about 2 inches in diameter and 3/4 inch thick. Put on a plate and refrigerate 30 minutes to set the shape.
Warm a flat tawa (griddle) on medium-high with a generous pour of oil. Stir in gola kebabs and cook 4-5 minutes per side.

Once cooked on both sides, experienced Karachi tawa cooks spin the gola on its edge on the hot tawa to seal and cook the rim. Try it — hold the kebab with tongs and roll it on the edge of the griddle.
Squeeze lemon and Stir in chaat masala right before serving.

alternate_methods.label: grill
instructions: Stir in raw papaya paste, all dry spices, ginger-garlic paste, salt, green chilli, coriander and the fat. Knead for 8-10 minutes using your hands until completely homogenous.
Cover the seasoned mince and refrigerate for at least 1 hour — overnight is better.
Light natural hardwood charcoal and let it burn until covered in a white-grey ash — about 20-30 minutes. The grill should be very hot.
Take a handful of mince and mould it around a flat, wide seekh skewer.
Put seekh directly over hot coals. Cook for 4-5 minutes per side, rotating carefully every 2 minutes.
Slide the cooked gola kebab off the seekh onto a flat naan or roti using the bread itself to pull it off. Let rest 2 minutes.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Karachi Gola Kebab — Seekh on Charcoal

alternate_names: Karachi Gola Kebab — Seekh on Charcoal

variants.name: Gujrati Aloo Recipe

ingredients.text: 5 tablespoon full-fat yogurt (brought to room temperature)

instructions: Boil potatoes until soft. Peel them and cut each potato in equal parts.

In a large wok, heat oil. Stir in mustard seeds, cumin seeds, kadi patta, and dried chilies (in that order). On medium-low heat, briefly Cook until they change color, making sure they don’t burn, about 1 minute.
Stir in turmeric powder and cumin powder, and Cook until aromatic.
Gently Stir in the potatoes, coating them in the spices for a couple of minutes on medium heat.
Remove from heat, and gently mix in yogurt.

variants.name: Gulab Jamun — Soft Milk Dumplings in Rose Syrup
instructions: Mix cheeni (sugar) and pani (water) in a pateela (saucepan) over medium heat. Stir until sugar dissolves completely, and then stop stirring. Stir in crushed elaichi (cardamom) pods.

In a bartan (bowl), Mix grated or crumbled khoya, maida (flour), and baking powder. Mix with your fingertips until it looks like coarse breadcrumbs. Stir in doodh (milk) one tablespoon at a time, working the mixture gently until it comes together into a smooth, soft dough.
Divide the dough into 16-18 equal portions. Roll each one between your palms into a smooth ball with no cracks.
Warm oil or ghee in a karahi (wok) or deep pan to about 140°C (280°F) — low heat is critical.
Remove the fried gulab jamun with a slotted spoon and immediately slide them into the warm syrup.

Arrange gulab jamun in a serving bartan (bowl) and ladle plenty of syrup over them — they should be sitting in a pool of it. Garnish with chopped pista (pistachios) and a few strands of saffron if you're feeling fancy.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Gulab Jamun — Soft Milk Dumplings in Rose Syrup

variants.name: Soft Gulab Jamun — Perfect Every Time
instructions: Mix sugar and water in a wide pan. Bring to a boil, Stir in cardamom and saffron water. Simmer for 8-10 minutes until a light syrup forms (no thread test needed — just slightly thicker than water).
Stir in flour and baking soda. Mix together. Stir in milk a little at a time and knead gently until you have a very soft, smooth dough — it should feel as soft as an earlobe and not sticky.
Divide the dough into walnut-sized portions and roll gently between your palms into smooth balls. If they crack, Stir in a tiny drop of milk and re-roll.
Warm oil in a karahi for deep frying. The temperature must be very LOW — around 140-150°C. Stir in a few jamun at a time.
The jamun must be a deep, dark reddish-brown on the outside — not light golden. Once dark brown, remove with a slotted spoon and let cool for 2-3 minutes.

Put the cooled (not hot) jamun into warm (not cold) sugar syrup. Let them soak for at least 2 hours — they plump up dramatically as they absorb syrup. They continue improving for up to 24 hours in the syrup.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Soft Gulab Jamun — Perfect Every Time

variants.name: Hunza Gurgur Chai (Butter Tea)

ingredients.text: 2 tsp Kali Chai Patti (Strong Black Tea / Pu-erh)

instructions: Bring 2 cups of water to a rolling boil in a small pateela (pot) or kettle. Stir in the tea leaves (or tea bags). Reduce to medium heat and let the tea steep for a full 5 minutes — Aim for a deeply dark, almost mahogany-coloured liquid, much.
Remove the pot from heat. Strain the brewed tea through a fine mesh strainer or tea strainer into a heat-proof jug or directly into a blender.
Pour the hot tea into a blender. Stir in the butter cubes and salt. If adding milk, Stir in it .
Blend on high for 30-60 seconds. The mixture will turn from dark and oily-looking to a warm caramel-brown, creamy, and visibly frothy on top.

Pour a small amount into a cup or bowl and taste immediately while hot. If it tastes oily or the butter seems to be separating, blend for another 20-30 seconds. If too salty, Stir in a tiny splash more hot water.
Pour the Gurgur Chai into wide, shallow bowls — not mugs or cups. Since you're probably serving yourself, just make enough for several bowls and keep the rest warm in a covered jug.

variants.name: Gurgur Chai — Hunza Butter Tea

ingredients.item: Sabz chai patti or kali chai
ingredients.text: 2 tsp Sabz chai patti or kali chai (green or black tea leaves)

instructions: Bring water to a boil. Stir in tea leaves and simmer for 10-15 minutes — much longer than regular tea. Strain out tea leaves.
Stir in salt and butter to the hot tea.
Pour the tea mixture into a blender or use an immersion blender and blend for 30-60 seconds until the butter is fully emulsified and the tea is creamy and slightly frothy.
Stir in MILK (optional): If using milk, warm it separately and stir into the churned tea.
Pour into cups or bowls and drink while hot.
Pour gurgur chai into cups or bowls.

variants.name: Kashmiri Gushtaba
instructions: HAND-POUND THE MUTTON — THIS IS THE ENTIRE TECHNIQUE: Cut the mutton (with its fat) into rough chunks. Continue for 15-20 minutes, working in batches.

To the pounded mutton paste, Stir in half a teaspoon of salt, a pinch of ground cardamom, and a pinch of sonth (dry ginger powder). Mix by folding and pressing — not stirring — to incorporate the spices evenly.

In a wide, deep pateela (pot) or degh, bring 2 cups of water to a gentle boil. Stir in the black cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, cloves, and half a teaspoon of salt to the water. Reduce heat to medium-low and poach (not boil) the meatballs for 20 minutes.

In a separate heavy-bottomed karahi or the same pateela (remove the whole spices with a slotted spoon first), heat 3 tbsp ghee over medium heat. Stir in the fennel powder (saunf) and stir for 30 seconds — smell an immediate, beautiful aniseed fragrance rise from the pan. Stir.
Stir in THE YOGHURT — THE MOST CRITICAL STEP: The yoghurt must be at room temperature. Take it out of the fridge 30 minutes before this step. Whisk it smooth in a bartan before adding.

Once all the yoghurt is incorporated and the gravy is smooth and pale, pour in the reserved poaching liquid (the meatball cooking water with the whole spice flavour). Stir to Mix. Bring to a very gentle simmer — tiny bubbles at the edges only, not a full boil.
If it's too thick, Stir in a splash of hot water and stir gently.
Pour the gravy generously over the rice.

variants.name: Kashmiri Gushtaba — Yogurt Lamb Meatballs

ingredients.text: 500 g Raan gosht ka keema (leg of lamb mince)

instructions: Mix lamb mince and lamb fat. Either pound vigorously with a wooden mallet on a chopping board for 10-15 minutes (flipping and folding constantly) or blend in a food processor for 3-4 minutes until the mixture becomes very smooth and paste-like. Stir in 0.5 tsp salt during this.
Wet your hands and roll the mixture into 4 large meatballs (or 6-8 smaller ones if preferred).
Bring 3 cups salted water to a gentle simmer (not a boil). Poach for 20-25 minutes, turning occasionally.
In a wide pan, heat ghee over medium heat. Stir in cloves and sizzle 30 seconds. Stir in fennel powder, dried ginger, cardamom powder, and remaining salt.
Once simmering, cook the yogurt gravy on medium-low heat for 10 minutes, stirring frequently.
Gently slide the poached gushtaba into the yogurt gravy. Simmer on very low heat for 15 minutes — this final simmer integrates the flavors.

variants.name: Haleem

ingredients.text: 1 cup wheat kernels (rinsed and soaked overnight)
1/2 cup yellow split peas (rinsed and soaked overnight)

ingredients.preparation: rinsed and soaked for one hour
ingredients.text: 1/4 cup basmati rice (rinsed and soaked for one hour)

ingredients.preparation: rinsed and soaked for one hour
ingredients.text: 1/4 cup red lentils (rinsed and soaked for one hour)

ingredients.preparation: rinsed and soaked for one hour
ingredients.text: 1/4 cup moong daal (rinsed and soaked for one hour)
1 medium yellow onion (thinly sliced in half rings)
1/3 cup oil (canola, sunflower or vegetable oil)

ingredients.item: boneless beef chuck or lamb shoulder
ingredients.preparation: fat trimmed and roughly chopped in 1-inch pieces
ingredients.text: 2 lb boneless beef chuck or lamb shoulder (fat trimmed and roughly chopped in 1-inch pieces)

instructions: Bring 4 quarts of water to a simmer and Stir in grains. Stir in salt to taste, 1 tbsp red chili powder, turmeric powder, and 1⁄2 sliced onion. Dial heat to low and cover.
Once the grains are fall-apart soft, drain excess water and transfer to a food processor. Mince it well to soften the texture, and transfer grain mixture to a large pot.

Warm oil in a large pot. When the oil is sizzling hot, Stir in onions and Cook on medium heat till they are golden brown and crisp, about 7 minutes, more if necessary. Once onions are ready, transfer to a paper towel to drain excess oil.

Warm remaining oil again on low heat, Stir in ginger and garlic paste, and let it Cook for a few seconds. Stir in meat, salt to taste, and whole spices (black cardamom pods, cloves, peppercorns, cinnamon stick), and Cook on medium-high heat till the meat is evenly cooked.

Stir in coriander powder, garam masala, and remaining red chili powder into the yogurt. Stir in fried onions and the spiced yogurt to the meat. Continue to cook on medium-high heat for another 5-7 minutes till the oil begins to separate.
Lower heat. Stir in 5 cups of water and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook till meat is tender and falling apart, roughly 1 to 11⁄2 hours.
Transfer meat mixture to a food processor and mince till it has an even consistency. Once ready, transfer to the pot with the grains.
On low heat, begin to stir the grain and meat mixture together till it is well blended, about 5 minutes. Top with crispy, fried brown onion.

variants.name: Beef Haleem Lahori
instructions: The night before, soak gehu in a large bowl with plenty of cold water. In a separate bowl, soak chana dal. Come morning, soak masoor and moong for 1 hour before cooking.
In a heavy deg, heat 5 tbsp ghee. Cook 2 sliced pyaaz to deep brown. Stir in adrak-lehsan paste, lal mirch, half the haleem masala, and salt.

In another large pot, cook soaked wheat in 2 litres water for 1 hour. Stir in all dals and cook another hour until everything is completely broken down and mushy. Stir in 1 sliced raw onion and remaining haleem masala to the grains while they cook.
Remove beef, debone, shred finely. Stir in to grain pot along with all the meat cooking liquid. Stir well and bring to a gentle boil.
Taste haleem and adjust salt and masala. Stir in garam masala for fresh aroma. If too thin, cook uncovered on medium heat, stirring frequently, until it thickens.
In a separate pan, heat remaining 3 tbsp ghee until hot. Stir in the last sliced pyaaz and Cook on medium-high heat, stirring continuously, until golden brown and crispy. Drain on paper towel.
Warm 1 tbsp ghee until smoking hot. Stir in sliced ginger and Cook 30 seconds, pour over haleem as hot tarka.

variants.name: Punjabi Haleem

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)
1 bunch each Hara Dhaniya & Pudina (Fresh Coriander & Mint)

instructions: Put the beef in a large degh (heavy-bottomed pot) with 8 cups of pani (water), half the adrak lehsan paste (ginger-garlic paste), haldi (turmeric), and 1 tsp namak (salt). Bring to a boil on high heat — you'll see scum and foam rise to the surface. Once skimmed.

In the same stock (this is important — the stock has all the meaty flavour), Stir in the soaked and drained dalia (broken wheat), jau (barley), chana dal, masoor dal, and moong dal. Top up with hot water if needed — the liquid should cover the grains by.

Warm half the desi ghee in a separate pateela (pot). Slice 2 of the pyaz (onions) and Cook them on medium heat until deep golden brown — about 12-15 minutes, stirring regularly. Stir in the remaining adrak lehsan paste and Cook for 2 minutes until the raw smell.

In a separate small pan, heat 3 tbsp ghee or tel (oil). Slice the remaining 2 pyaz (onions) thinly and Cook on medium heat, stirring every minute, until they are deep mahogany brown and crispy — about 15-20 minutes. Remove with a slotted chamcha and drain on kitchen.

Stir in the spiced tarka and the shredded gosht (meat) back into the degh with the cooked grain mixture. Stir vigorously with a wooden chamcha (spoon) — really get in there and mix everything thoroughly. If it's too thick to stir, Stir in a splash of hot water.
The chamcha pounding method is traditional and therapeutic: press, stir, press, stir, for about 10 minutes.

Cook the pounded haleem on the lowest possible flame for another 30 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes to prevent sticking. The haleem should thicken to the point where it coats the back of a chamcha and holds its shape briefly when you push it aside.

Warm 3 tbsp desi ghee in a tiny pan until smoking. Stir in a pinch of lal mirch powder (red chilli) — it will sizzle and turn the ghee a gorgeous red-orange. It adds richness, colour, and a final hit of heat.
Ladle haleem into deep bowls.

variants.name: Karachi Haleem
instructions: The night before, wash gehu thoroughly and soak in plenty of cold water. Separately soak chana dal in cold water. In the morning, soak masoor and maash dal for 1 hour.
In a large, heavy deg, heat 3 tablespoons ghee. Cook 2 sliced pyaaz until deep golden. Stir in adrak-lehsan paste, haleem masala, haldi, and salt.

In another large pot, Stir in soaked gehu with 1.5 litres of water, bring to boil and cook on medium heat for 1 hour. Stir in all soaked dals to the wheat pot and continue cooking for 45 more minutes until everything is very soft and starting to.

Stir in shredded beef to the wheat-dal pot along with all the beef cooking liquid. Stir well and bring to a gentle boil. begin the traditional pounding: using a wooden laddle (karchi) or a potato masher, vigorously stir and mash the mixture in a circular motion for 15-20.
Haleem should be thick like porridge — thick enough to hold a spoon upright but pourable. Stir in hot water to loosen if needed, or cook uncovered to thicken. This is a large pot — season boldly.
Slice remaining pyaaz into thin rings. Cook in oil until golden and crispy — these birista (fried onions) are non-negotiable on haleem. Drain on paper towel.

variants.name: Beef Haleem South Punjab
instructions: Soak gehu overnight. Soak chana dal at least 2 hours before cooking. Morning: soak masoor and moong for 1 hour.

In a very large pot or pressure cooker, heat 6 tbsp ghee. Cook 3 sliced pyaaz to very dark brown — South Punjab goes darker than Lahore. Stir in adrak-lehsan paste, lal mirch powder, half the haleem masala, salt.
In a large second pot, cook soaked wheat in 2.5 litres water for 1 hour. Stir in all dals and 2 whole sliced onions (raw — the South Punjab trick). Stir in remaining haleem masala to the grains.
Debone beef, shred very finely. Stir in to grain pot with all beef cooking liquid. Bring to gentle boil.
This is the work — pound and stir continuously for 30 minutes. Stir in hot water if consistency becomes too thick.
Stir in garam masala. Heat remaining ghee in a separate pan until smoking. Cook a sliced pyaaz to make fresh birista, pour the entire pan including hot ghee over the haleem surface as a final tarka.

variants.name: Badam Halwa

ingredients.item: almond flour or skinless almonds ground at home
ingredients.text: 2/3 cup almond flour or skinless almonds ground at home

instructions: Prepare the grain, fruit or milk solids and measure the milk, sugar and aromatics.
Warm the ghee or milk as appropriate; toast the grain or simmer the dairy gently so it does not catch.
Add the sugar only after the main ingredient is tender, then cook until the mixture reaches the intended thick consistency.
Stir in the cardamom, saffron or floral water, garnish with nuts if used, and serve at the stated temperature.

variants.name: Egg Halwa (Anday Ka Halwa)

ingredients.preparation: Nido is fine - anything as long as it is pure whole milk powder
ingredients.text: 1 cup whole milk powder (Nido is fine - anything as long as it is pure whole milk powder)
1/8 tsp cardamom powder (optional, or adjust to taste)

instructions: Prepare the grain, fruit or milk solids and measure the milk, sugar and aromatics.
Warm the ghee or milk as appropriate; toast the grain or simmer the dairy gently so it does not catch.
Add the sugar only after the main ingredient is tender, then cook until the mixture reaches the intended thick consistency.
Stir in the cardamom, saffron or floral water, garnish with nuts if used, and serve at the stated temperature.

variants.name: Pumpkin Halwa
instructions: Prepare the grain, fruit or milk solids and measure the milk, sugar and aromatics.
Warm the ghee or milk as appropriate; toast the grain or simmer the dairy gently so it does not catch.
Add the sugar only after the main ingredient is tender, then cook until the mixture reaches the intended thick consistency.
Stir in the cardamom, saffron or floral water, garnish with nuts if used, and serve at the stated temperature.

variants.name: Peshawari Halwa Puri

ingredients.text: 1.5 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
1.5 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Knead until smooth, rest 30 minutes.
Roast sooji in ghee until deep golden, about 15 minutes — even darker than standard for this style. Stir in sugar dissolved in 500ml water carefully. Stir in saffron water, elaichi.
Cook piyaz golden, Stir in adrak lahsun paste (generous), tamatar, laal mirch powder. Stir in chana and simmer with water until thick and flavourful.
Roll dough to 5mm thickness (thicker than standard). Cook in hot oil — they won't puff as dramatically but will be crispier and more satisfying. Cook 2-3 minutes per side.
Top halwa with remaining slivered nuts.

variants.name: Lahori Halwa Puri with Channay
instructions: Rinse dried channay (chickpeas) and soak in cold water overnight — they double in size. Drain, Stir in to a pateela (saucepan) with fresh water and a pinch of namak (salt), bring to boil and simmer for 45-60 minutes until completely tender — they should crush easily between.

Mix maida (flour), 2 tablespoons of oil, a pinch of namak (salt), and enough lukewarm water (about 100-120ml) to make a firm but smooth dough. Knead for 5-6 minutes until the dough is elastic and not sticky.
Warm 3 tablespoons of oil in a karahi (wok) over medium-high heat. Stir in finely chopped pyaz (onion) and Cook for 10 minutes until deep golden. Stir in adrak lehsan paste and Cook 2 minutes.

Warm ghee in a degh or heavy-bottomed pan over medium-low heat. Stir in the suji (semolina) and stir constantly with a chamcha (ladle). After 8-10 minutes, the suji will turn golden-tan and emit a deeply nutty, almost popcorn-like smell.

In a separate pateela, bring together 1 cup water, half a cup of milk, the sugar, and crushed elaichi (cardamom) to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves. Very carefully Stir in this hot liquid to the toasted suji — it will spit and bubble violently. Stand back and.

Warm 500ml of tel (oil) in a deep karahi or degh to about 180°C — test by dropping a tiny ball of dough in; Roll each ball into a circle about 12-15cm wide and 3mm thick — not too thin or they tear, not too thick or they.
Work quickly — puri deflates within 2-3 minutes of frying and halwa firms up as it cools. Cook puri in batches while someone else portions the halwa and channay.

variants.name: Karachi Halwa Puri

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
for deep frying tel (oil for frying puris)

instructions: Mix maida with 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp oil. Stir in warm water gradually, kneading to a medium-soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest 30 minutes minimum.
Warm ghee in a heavy pan. Stir in sooji and roast on medium heat, stirring continuously, until light golden and nutty-smelling — about 10-12 minutes. Meanwhile boil 500ml water with sugar.
Warm oil, Cook piyaz until golden. Stir in adrak lahsun paste, cook 2 minutes. Stir in tamatar and chana masala powder, cook until oil separates.
Warm deep frying oil in a karahi (wok) to 180°C.
Divide dough into golf ball-sized portions. Roll each into a 4-inch circle — not too thin. Cook until golden on both sides, about 1-2 minutes.
Arrange with bowls of warm halwa and chana masala.

variants.name: Sindhi Halwa Puri

ingredients.text: for deep frying tel (oil for frying)

instructions: Mix atta with salt and 2 tbsp oil. Stir in warm water gradually to form a soft, pliable dough. Knead 8-10 minutes until smooth.

Roast sooji in ghee over medium heat until golden-brown and very fragrant, about 12-15 minutes — slightly darker than usual for Sindhi style. Boil sugar with 300ml water and milk. Stir in this carefully to roasted sooji.
Make a quick chana masala — Cook piyaz in oil until golden, Stir in tamatar and chana masala spices, cook until thick. Stir in boiled chana and simmer 10 minutes.
Roll atta puri slightly thicker than maida puris — about 3mm. Cook in hot oil (180°C). Cook until golden on both sides.

variants.name: Handi Kabab Masala

ingredients.preparation: optional, recommended only if you are not using charcoal
ingredients.text: 1 tsp garam masala (optional, recommended only if you are not using charcoal)

instructions: Stir in the rest of your kabab ingredients and blitz till well combined and smooth. With wet hands shape the kababs into your desired size. I made 11-12 kababs in the shape on the right.

Warm about 2 tbsp of oil in your pot/pan on medium high heat and cook the kababs for a few minutes on each side until cooked through. Remember to Cook a test piece first to check for seasoning. Warm 1/4 cup of oil in your pot on medium high heat and Stir in your cumin seeds, letting them sizzle for a minute.
Stir in your onions and one of the chilies and saute until the onions edges look caramelly. Stir in your ginger and garlic, sauté for a minute and and then Stir in your dry spices.

Stir in your tomatoes, cover for a few minutes to hasten the softening, and and then saute until the oil rises above the tomatoes. You can puree this mix if Aim for for a smoother curry or leave as is. If you puree it and then return it to the pot and cook on medium heat for 5-6 minutes or until the.

Put your cooked kababs in the pot, turning them so that all sides are coated with masala, Stir in a splash of water, and cover the dish and simmer for 6-8 minutes to meld it all together. Adjust consistency to your liking and and then you can either give smoke with a piece of charcoal OR Stir in garam masala, adjust seasoning.
Charcoal Smoke: To do this you heat a small piece of charcoal stovetop, you can Put it directly on a gas burner or on a metal rack for ceramic cooktop.

variants.name: Hanifia Sauce (Copycat Recipe)
instructions: Mix all the ingredients in a small pot, whisk well to break up lumps.
Bring to a boil, simmer till a thicker consistency - 5-10 minutes.

variants.name: Afghani Hareesa — Cross-Border Style

ingredients.text: 2 cups Gehu dana (cracked wheat / wheat berries)

instructions: In a large pot, heat 4 tbsp ghee. Cook 3 large onions until deep gold. Stir in ginger-garlic paste, cumin, 2 cinnamon sticks.
Stir in soaked drained wheat and 4 more cups water. Cook on low heat for 5-7 hours, stirring every 20-30 minutes.

In a small pan, heat remaining 4 tbsp ghee until shimmering. Stir in 1 sliced onion, the remaining cinnamon stick, and cloves. Cook until onion is deeply golden and cinnamon is fragrant — about 8-10 minutes.

variants.name: Hareesa — KP Slow-Cooked Wheat and Mutton Porridge

ingredients.text: 400 g sabut gehun / gehun ki giriyaan (whole wheat berries/grains)
600 g mutton (bone-in shoulder or neck pieces)
3 pods hari elaichi (green cardamom for tarka)

instructions: The night before cooking, Put the whole wheat berries in a large bowl and cover with at least 3x their volume of cold water. Leave to soak for 8-12 hours or overnight.

In a large, heavy degh (heavy-bottomed pot), Mix the mutton pieces, chopped onion, ginger-garlic paste, black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, black peppercorns, turmeric, and salt. Pour in 1.5 litres of cold water. Bring to a boil over high heat, skimming off any grey foam that rises to the surface.

Stir in the soaked and drained wheat grains directly to the pot with the mutton and broth. Stir everything together. If needed, Stir in more water to keep everything submerged — Aim for the level about 2 inches above the wheat and meat mixture.
After 3-4 hours, you'll notice the mixture becoming much thicker. use a heavy wooden spoon or a mathani (wooden masher) to vigorously stir and mash the mixture.

Continue cooking and stirring for another 30-60 minutes after the mashing stage. It should hold its shape for a second when you drop a spoonful onto the surface, and then slowly melt back in. If it's too thick, Stir in a splash of hot water.

Just before serving, heat Raha ghee in a small karahi (wok) or tarka pan over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Stir in the thinly sliced onions and Cook until they are deep golden brown, about 12-15 minutes. Stir in the green cardamom pods in the last minute of.
Immediately pour the hot tarka (ghee, fried onions, and cardamom) over the top — it will sizzle and bubble dramatically. Garnish with julienned fresh ginger and fresh coriander.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Hareesa — KP Slow-Cooked Wheat and Mutton Porridge

variants.name: KP Chicken Hareesa — Lighter Version

ingredients.text: 1.5 cups Gehu dana (cracked wheat / wheat berries)

instructions: In a pot, heat 3 tbsp ghee. Cook 1 sliced onion golden. Stir in ginger-garlic paste, cardamom, and cinnamon.
Stir in soaked drained wheat and 3 more cups water. Stir well. Bring to a boil, and then reduce to the lowest heat.
Cook for 2.5-3 hours on very low heat, stirring every 20-25 minutes. Stir in water if needed.
In a separate pan, heat remaining ghee and Cook the second sliced onion until deeply golden-brown. Pour hot tarka directly over the hareesa at the table.
Top with fresh coriander and slit green chilies.

variants.name: KP Hareesa Gosht

ingredients.text: 5 tbsp ghee or dumba charbi (sheep tail fat)
3 tbsp ghee for tarka (clarified butter for tempering)
1 tsp lal mirch for tarka (red chilli)

instructions: This is the most important step in making hareesa. Cover wheat kernels in at least three times their volume of cold water and soak for 12 hours minimum. Drain before cooking.

In a large, heavy-bottomed pot, Stir in soaked wheat with 2 litres of fresh cold water. Bring to a boil over high heat, and then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook for 2-3 hours, adding water as needed to keep wheat submerged.

In another pot, heat 2 tbsp ghee, Stir in sliced pyaaz and cook until golden. Stir in mutton pieces, salt, kali mirch, and zeera. Stir in 1 litre water and cook on medium heat for 2 hours until mutton is falling off the bone.

Stir in shredded mutton and all the meat cooking liquid to the wheat pot. Stir vigorously to Mix. begins the long pounding: using the back of a heavy spoon or a wooden pestle, continuously work the mixture in circular motions for 30-45 minutes.
After combining and initial pounding, cook on the lowest possible heat for another 2 hours, stirring every 10-15 minutes.
Taste hareesa and Stir in more salt and kali mirch as needed.
Warm 3 tbsp ghee in a small pan until it's smoking hot. Stir in lal mirch and immediately pour over the hareesa surface.

variants.name: Pashtun Hareesa — Wheat and Mutton Porridge

ingredients.text: 2 cups Gehu dana (whole cracked wheat / wheat berries)

instructions: Soak gehu dana in cold water overnight (8-12 hours). Drain before using.
In a large, heavy pot, heat 3 tbsp ghee. Stir in 2 sliced onions and Cook golden. Stir in ginger-garlic paste and Cook 2 minutes.
Stir in drained soaked wheat to the mutton broth. Stir in another 4 cups of water. Stir well.
Cook on low heat for 4-6 hours, stirring every 20-30 minutes with a wooden spoon.
When the wheat has completely broken down and the consistency is like thick porridge, use the back of a wooden spoon or a potato masher to mash any remaining wheat grains.
In a separate pan, heat remaining ghee until hot. Stir in 1 thinly sliced onion and Cook until deep golden-brown. Pour the hot tarka directly over the hareesa at the table for maximum drama.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Pashtun Hareesa — Wheat and Mutton Porridge

Cover, simmer till tender - 25 minutes.
Adjust consistency, check for seasoning, garnish with some fresh ginger or fresh chillies - or nothing at all - grab some roti or rice and dig in.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Stir in cilantro, green chilies, mint and yogurt to a food processor and pulse until well-mixed.
Warm oil over medium-low heat in a medium-sized saucepan or skillet. Stir in crushed garlic and Cook for roughly 30 seconds or until it stops smelling raw.
Stir in diced chicken, salt, crushed ginger and red chili flakes. Increase heat to medium-high, and sear until no longer pink, roughly 2 to 5 minutes.
Lower heat and stir in the yogurt mixture until the chicken is well-coated in the masala.
Let the masala come to a gentle simmer. Partially cover the saucepan with a lid, and let the hara masala bubble for roughly 10 minutes.

variants.name: Classic Chocolate Chip Cookies
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line two trays with baking paper.
Whisk flour, baking soda and salt together.
Beat butter and both sugars for 2–3 minutes until creamy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, followed by vanilla.
Fold in the dry ingredients only until no flour streaks remain, then fold in the chocolate chips.
Scoop 24 equal mounds onto the trays, leaving room to spread. Chill the trays for 15 minutes for thicker cookies.
Bake for 10–12 minutes until the edges are golden but the centres still look soft. Cool on the tray for 10 minutes.

variants.name: Double Chocolate Cookies
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line two baking trays.
Sift together flour, cocoa, baking soda and salt so no cocoa lumps remain.
Beat butter and sugars until creamy. Beat in the eggs one at a time and add vanilla.
Fold in the dry mixture just until combined, followed by the chocolate chips. Chill for 20 minutes.
Divide into 24 mounds and space them well apart on the trays.
Bake for 10–12 minutes. The centres should remain soft; let the cookies firm on the tray before moving them.

variants.name: Oatmeal Raisin Cookies
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line two trays.
Whisk flour, oats, baking soda, cinnamon and salt together.
Beat butter and both sugars until creamy. Beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Fold in the dry ingredients and raisins. Let the dough stand for 10 minutes so the oats hydrate.
Scoop 24 mounds onto the trays and flatten them slightly.
Bake for 11–13 minutes until golden at the edges. Cool for 10 minutes before transferring to a rack.

variants.name: Peanut Butter Cookies
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line two baking trays.
Whisk flour, baking soda and salt together.
Beat butter, peanut butter and both sugars until smooth. Beat in the eggs one at a time and add vanilla.
Fold in the flour mixture. Chill the dough for 20 minutes if it feels very soft.
Roll into 24 balls, place on the trays and flatten each with a fork in a crosshatch pattern.
Bake for 10–12 minutes until the edges are set. Cool on the trays because warm peanut cookies are fragile.

variants.name: Piped Butter Cookies
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.

ingredients.text: 225 g unsalted butter (very soft but not melted)

instructions: Heat the oven to 170°C and line two trays.
Beat the very soft butter and icing sugar for 3 minutes until pale. Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Sift in flour, cornflour and salt. Fold only until a soft, pipeable dough forms; do not overmix.
Transfer to a strong piping bag fitted with a large star nozzle. Pipe 24 rosettes or short fingers onto the trays.
Chill the piped cookies for 20 minutes so their ridges hold.
Bake for 12–14 minutes until pale gold at the edges. Cool fully before storing airtight.

variants.name: Banana Walnut Muffins
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Whisk flour, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon and salt together.
Whisk mashed bananas, sugar, eggs, oil and yogurt until combined.
Fold the wet mixture into the dry just until combined, then fold in three-quarters of the walnuts.
Divide among the cups and scatter over the remaining walnuts.
Bake for 20–24 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool for 5 minutes in the tin.

variants.name: Blueberry Muffins
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.

ingredients.text: 200 g blueberries (fresh or frozen, not thawed)

instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Whisk flour, baking powder, salt and sugar together. Toss the blueberries with 1 tablespoon of this flour mixture.
Whisk eggs, milk, oil and vanilla in another bowl.
Fold wet ingredients into dry just until combined, then gently fold in the blueberries.
Divide the batter evenly among the muffin cups.
Bake for 19–22 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Cool for 5 minutes before removing from the tin.

variants.name: Chocolate Chip Muffins
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Whisk flour, baking powder, salt and sugar in a large bowl. Stir through most of the chocolate chips.
In another bowl whisk eggs, milk, oil and vanilla.
Pour wet ingredients into dry and fold just until combined; a few small lumps are preferable to overmixing.
Divide among the cups and scatter over the remaining chips.
Bake for 18–22 minutes until risen and a skewer without melted chocolate comes out clean. Cool for 5 minutes in the tin.

variants.name: Double Chocolate Muffins
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C and line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Sift flour, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda and salt into a bowl. Whisk in sugar and most of the chocolate chips.
Whisk eggs, milk, oil and vanilla separately.
Fold the wet mixture into the dry only until no flour pockets remain.
Divide among the cups and top with the reserved chips.
Bake for 18–22 minutes until the tops spring back and a skewer avoids wet batter. Cool briefly before removing.

variants.name: Homestyle Chicken Salan (Chicken Curry)

ingredients.text: 1.5-2 lb bone in chicken (or 1.5 lb boneless)

instructions: Warm your oil in a large pot on medium high heat. When it shimmers and then Stir in the whole spices i.e cinnamon, cumin seeds, cloves, and whole black peppers.

After the cumin seeds start to sizzle and smell delicious and then Stir in the onions. When the edges of the onion turn golden and then Stir in the garlic paste and ginger paste and sauté for 30 seconds.

Stir in your tomatoes and spices. Cover the pot and turn the heat down a little to medium heat for 2-3 minutes - this speeds up the process of cooking the masala. Turn the heat back up, remove the lid and sauté the spice mix until the oil rises above the top.

Stir in your chicken pieces to your pot stirring periodically until all of the chicken turns white/opaque. Stir in 1/2 cup of water to your pot if the masala seems very bring to a boil and simmer on low until the chicken is cooked through, 15-20 minutes.
Adjust the consistency of the salan to your liking, Stir in the garam masala powder and cumin powder, and then adjust seasoning. Garnish with cilantro and green chilies and serve.

variants.name: Honey Chilli Chicken
instructions: Put the chicken cubes in a bowl. Season with 0.5 tsp salt and 0.25 tsp black pepper. Stir in the cornflour and toss until every piece is thoroughly coated — Aim for a dry, white powdery coat on each cube.

Warm 2 cups of oil in a karahi or deep pan over high heat. Test with a tiny piece of coated chicken — if it sizzles immediately and turns golden in 3-4 minutes, the oil is ready. Cook the chicken in two batches — do not crowd the.
In a small bowl, whisk together the red chilli paste, honey, tomato ketchup, dark soy sauce, and white vinegar. Stir until fully combined.

Warm 2 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and stir-Cook for 30 seconds until golden and fragrant. Stir in the onion and capsicum squares and toss for 60-90 seconds on high heat — Aim for them slightly charred at the edges.

Pour the glaze mixture directly into the wok over the vegetables. Stir and let it bubble for 60-90 seconds — as the liquid reduces and the honey heats, the sauce will become visibly glossy and thick. You are looking for the consistency of a thin syrup: it should.
TOSS THE CHICKEN — QUICKLY: Stir in the fried chicken cubes to the glaze. Remove from heat IMMEDIATELY.
Transfer to a serving plate immediately. Arrange sliced spring onion greens over the chicken. The three-condiment set on the table allows diners who want even more heat to help themselves.

variants.name: Easy Hot and Sour Soup (Hakka)

ingredients.text: 1/2 lb chicken (250 g, less works too)
1 1/2 cup coleslaw mix or shredded cabbages

ingredients.item: mushrooms quartered or cut into sixths
ingredients.text: 1/2-3/4 cup mushrooms quartered or cut into sixths
2-3 tbsp Asian Style Chili Sauce (I use Sriracha)

ingredients.item: soft or medium tofu cut into 1 cm pieces
ingredients.text: 1/2 cup soft or medium tofu cut into 1 cm pieces

instructions: Bring vinegar to a simmer in a small saucepan along with the sugar and salt. Snip your green chilies right into it with kitchen shears, simmer for 3-4 minutes and turn off the stove.
Warm the oil in a heavy bottomed soup pot on medium high heat. Stir in the ginger and garlic, let it cook for 30 seconds along with the green chili (if using).
Stir in the chicken and saute till it all changes color. Stir in your vegetables and saute for 4-6 minutes until tender crisp.
Meanwhile mix your broth together with the other ingredients under Flavored Broth Mix - you can also Stir in it all straight to the pot if that's easier. Simmer for another five minutes.

With the soup on a gentle boil whisk in the cornstarch slurry and turn the heat all the way down stirring while it thickens. Once it thickens you can turn off the stove and whisk the egg whites in and they'll cook in the residual heat.
Stir in your tofu and bamboo shoots if using and adjust seasoning - Aim for a spicy kick, sour notes, and that rich umami.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: In a large pot, heat 1 tbsp oil over medium-high heat. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and stir-Cook for 30-40 seconds until it smells fragrant and golden. Do not let it burn — reduce heat slightly if the paste is browning too fast.
Pour in the chicken stock and bring to a boil. Stir in the tomato ketchup, red chilli paste, dark soy sauce, and white vinegar. Stir well — the broth will turn from pale golden to a deep red-brown.

Stir in the julienned carrot to the simmering broth first — it needs slightly more time to soften. After 2 minutes, Stir in the shredded cabbage, capsicum, and shredded chicken. Simmer for another 3-4 minutes.
Mix 3 tbsp cornflour with 5 tbsp cold water until smooth. Pour slowly into the simmering soup while stirring continuously. If it is too thick, Stir in a splash of hot water.
Beat the eggs well. Reduce the soup to a gentle simmer. Pour the egg in a thin, steady stream from a height, stirring the soup slowly in wide circles as you pour.
Stir in salt and white pepper as needed. The three-condiment set belongs on the table — diners who want more heat or more sour can adjust their own bowl.

instructions: Season with the spices.
Stir in cream cheese (easier if you cut it up first) and sour cream.
Stir in the milk to loosen it up, and and then corn and adjust seasoning.
Bake for 5-6 minutes until hot and bubbly and irresistibly golden.

v small piece of cinnamon (a cm)

Stir in your tea leaves, bring to a boil.

variants.name: How to Make Garlic Paste

instructions: Stir in your garlic cloves to the blender with 1/4 cup water.
If the blender isn't pureeing it easily and then Stir in a little more water and puree again.

variants.name: Instant Pot Salan Masala
instructions: Warm a generous amount of oil in your IP on saute mode.
When it is hot Stir in the whole spices and saute for 30 seconds.

Stir in the onions, keep stirring and cook for about 10 minutes until the edges/tips of most of the onions are slightly golden. For a darker curry base keep cooking (and stirring) for 15-20 minutes - usually it is safer to go for a light golden.
Stir in your ginger and garlic pastes and saute for 2 minutes.

Once they pastes are incorporated Stir in the remaining dry masala and salt and saute until the mix starts to come together and form a cohesive paste. If it starts to burn Stir in a small splash of water.
Pour 2.5 cups of hot water into the Instant Pot, give it a stir and put it on manual (pressure) for 20 minutes.
Let it naturally release and saute to reduce the liquid for a more concentrated base.
When it is cool enough to handle and then drain the extra oil out of the masala.
This mix will keep in the coldest part of your fridge for 10 days or you can freeze it into roughly one cup servings for 3 months.

variants.name: Instant Pot Tandoori Roast Chicken

ingredients.item: baby potatoes, or regular potatoes in big chunks
ingredients.text: 1 lb baby potatoes, or regular potatoes in big chunks

ingredients.item: Shan Masala brand Tandoori Roast Chicken Masala
ingredients.text: 1/2 packet Shan Masala brand Tandoori Roast Chicken Masala

ingredients.item: Shan Masala brand Lahori Chargha Masala
ingredients.text: 1/2 packet Shan Masala brand Lahori Chargha Masala

instructions: Mix all the marinade ingredients in a small bowl.
Pour over the chicken and rub well, leave for at least an hour or overnight.
When almost ready to cook take the chicken out of the fridge.
Warm the oil in the instant pot on saute mode on high.
After 2-2.5 minutes Stir in the remaining marinade back into the pot and put the instant pot on manual (i.e. pressure) on high for 8 minutes.
When the timer beeps open the vent to release pressure and tip the potatoes in, mix a little to coat them in marinade.
Put the instant pot back on pressure for another 8-10 minutes (depending on the size of chicken you are using) and and then release the pressure.

The chicken is ready to eat but if Aim for a more caramelized look you can put it in an oven safe roasting dish and broil it or even turn the saute function on high until the potatoes and chicken take on a darker hue, about 5 minutes!

variants.name: Easy Instant Jalebi Recipe

ingredients.item: a few drops of lemon juice
ingredients.text: a few drops of lemon juice
baking soda - a small pinch (1/8 of a tsp)

ingredients.item: Neutral oil like corn plus a few tbsp of ghee
ingredients.text: Neutral oil like corn plus a few tbsp of ghee

instructions: Mix all the sugar syrup ingredients in a medium sized pot (and then you can use the same pot for dunking the jalebis) and bring to a boil.
Simmer for 5-6 minutes or until the syrup becomes slightly sicky and/or the last few drops of it fall of the spoon at a slower pace.
Warm oil in a large saucepan on medium heat. Stir in the ghee.
Mix all the jalebi ingredients in a bowl and whisk well. When it comes together and then you will see the batter fall off your whisk in smooth ribbons.
Transfer the batter into a piping bag, ziploc bag or a squeeze bottle (you may need to cut the tip).
Adjust your heat as needed to maintain that level.
Cook for approximately 1.5-2 minutes on each side. (set a timer if needed, 1.5 minutes feels like A LOT more when you're impatiently waiting to eat jalebi!).

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together flour, cornflour, baking powder and food colour. Stir in yoghurt and mix. Gradually Stir in water, whisking to form a smooth, lump-free batter.

Mix sugar and water in a wide, shallow pan. Stir in lemon juice, cardamom pods and saffron. Bring to a boil and cook for 5-7 minutes until a one-thread syrup forms (test between thumb and forefinger — a single thread pulls).
Transfer batter to a squeezy bottle or piping bag with a 3-4mm round tip, or use a zip-lock bag with a small corner snipped.
In a wide, flat karahi, heat oil to 180°C (medium-high).

Pipe batter in concentric spiral shapes directly into the hot oil, making 3-4 jalebis at a time. Cook for 1 minute on one side until they hold their shape, and then flip carefully with tongs. Cook another 1-2 minutes until crisp and golden-orange.
Immediately transfer hot jalebis from the oil directly into the warm sugar syrup. Let them soak for 30-45 seconds, turning once.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Instant Jalebi — Crispy Homemade in 30 Minutes

alternate_names: Instant Jalebi — Crispy Homemade in 30 Minutes

variants.name: Homemade Jalebi — Crispy Saffron Syrup Spirals
instructions: In a pateela (saucepan), dissolve cheeni (sugar) in pani (water) over medium heat, stirring until completely clear. Stir in crushed elaichi (cardamom). Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and cook for 8-10 minutes until you reach a one-string consistency.

Stir in dahi (yoghurt), haldi (turmeric), and instant khameer (yeast). Stir in warm pani (water) gradually, whisking constantly to eliminate lumps, until you have a smooth batter the consistency of thin pancake batter — it should flow freely from a spoon.
Transfer the batter to a piping bag with a small round nozzle (3-4mm opening), or make a DIY version: fill a zip-lock bag and snip a tiny hole in one corner, or use a clean squeeze bottle.
Warm oil in a wide, flat pan (not too deep — 3-4cm of oil) to 180°C (350°F).
Lift fried jalebi directly from the oil and immediately submerge in the warm syrup.
The crispy exterior will begin softening after 10-15 minutes as the syrup continues to soak through — which some people prefer, actually (the soft interior, crunchy edges stage is wonderful).

variants.dish_family: Juicy Shami Kabab - Instant Pot & Stovetop

Close the lid, set to seal and set to pressure for 30 Minutes and then natural release (that means turn the machine off and walk away till the pressure releases, and then open the valve.).

Mix all the ingredients EXCEPT the green masala ones in a pot with 2.5-3 cups of water, bring to a boil and simmer on low for 50-60 minutes or until the meat and daal are tender. Check halfway through, Stir in water if needed.
Crank up the heat, dry up excess water, your meat mixture should start to stick.
Stir in ALL the hara masala - it will seem like a lot but it works.

Cook A TEST KABAB!
