variants.name: Kaak

ingredients.text: 2 cups atta ya maida (whole wheat or plain flour)

instructions: In a large paraat (wide shallow kneading bowl) or any large bowl, Mix the atta (whole wheat flour) and namak (salt). Mix them together with your hand first, so the salt is evenly distributed through the flour.
Make a well in the centre of the flour. Do not Stir in all the water at once — you may not need the full cup.

Once the dough comes together, transfer it to your clean work surface (a flat counter or marble slab). Knead with the heel of your hand — push the dough away from you, fold it back, rotate, and repeat. Knead for 8-10 minutes.
Shape the dough into a ball, cover it with a damp cloth or invert a bowl over it, and let it rest for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Turn your oven on to 200°C (390°F).

Divide the rested dough into 4 equal portions. Roll each portion into a ball. On a lightly floured surface, use a rolling pin (belan) to roll each ball into a disc approximately 1cm thick and 15-18cm wide.

Carefully Put the discs on your preheated baking stone, cast-iron pan, or a regular baking tray lined with baking paper. Bake for 25-30 minutes. The Kaak is done when it looks pale golden-brown, feels completely dry and hard when you tap it, and sounds hollow when knocked.
Let them cool completely — at least 30 minutes.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Let stand 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour, salt, cumin, and ajwain (if using). Stir in activated yeast and enough remaining water to make a firm dough — firmer than regular bread dough. Knead 8-10 minutes.
Cover dough and let rise in a warm spot for 60-90 minutes until doubled.
Punch down dough. Shape into small rounds or ovals about 1cm thick and 8-10cm across.
Bake in a preheated 200°C oven for 20-25 minutes until golden and hollow-sounding when tapped.
Reduce oven to 120°C. Return the cooled kaak to the oven and bake for 60-70 minutes until completely dry, hard, and crunchy throughout.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Balochi Kaak — The Desert Dry Bread

alternate_names: Balochi Kaak — The Desert Dry Bread

variants.name: KP Kaak — Mountain Version

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp Tel ya ghee (oil or ghee)

instructions: Wait 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour and salt. Stir in oil and yeast mixture. Stir in remaining water gradually to form a firm (not soft) dough.
Cover and let rise 60-90 minutes until doubled.
Shape into small rounds or ovals 1cm thick.
Bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until golden.
Bake at 110°C for 70-80 minutes until completely bone dry.

dish_families.name: Kachay Qeemay ke Kabab or Galawat ke Kabab

variants.name: Kachay Qeemay ke Kabab or Galawat ke Kabab
variants.dish_family: Kachay Qeemay ke Kabab or Galawat ke Kabab

ingredients.text: 2 tsp cumin seeds, dry roasted and ground

ingredients.item: coriander seeds, dry roasted and ground

When ready to eat Cook them in oil on medium low heat, frying at a high heat will make the kababs hard, Aim for to cook the inside and char the outside a little.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Kachay Qeemay ke Kabab or Galawat ke Kabab

variants.name: Kadhi Pakora Recipe – Traditional Flavor, Made Quicker

ingredients.text: 1/2 cup besan (chickpea or chana daal flour)

ingredients.preparation: I use full fat, but 2% works
ingredients.text: 1 1/2 cup yogurt (I use full fat, but 2% works)
1/2 tsp methi dana or fenugreek seeds
1/4 tsp ajwain seeds or carom seeds
3/4 tsp red chilli powder or cayenne
3/4 tsp cumin powder or zeera powder
3/4 tsp coriander powder or dhania powder
1.5 cup besan or chickpea/chana daal flour

instructions: Warm your pot and then Stir in the besan to it and dry roast on medium heat until it smells aromatic. If the colour starts to change and then pull it off the heat immediately. I use an immersion blender because and then I can measure the yogurt in, Stir in the besan and blitz.

Stir in a little oil in the same pot and your curry leaves, methi dana (fenugreek seeds), and ajwain (carom) seeds and saute until fragrant. Immediately Stir in your garlic and dry spices, keep a little water handy in case you need to Stir in a splash to prevent the spices from burning.

Stir in your besan and mix well, it will start to clump up, but don't worry and just whisk the water in. Stir in the green chilies and bring it to a boil and then down to a simmer for 45 minutes., stirring intermittently and scraping the bottom.

Mix the pakora ingredients and start drizzling in the 3/4 cup water mixing well. If you Stir in it all at once it's harder to mix. Warm oil for deep frying (you can pan Cook as well, but and then they don't puff up as much).
Cook a test pakora and taste. The pakoras will expand as they Cook but they will also expand when added to the karhi. Cook for 3 minutes on each side or until deeply golden.

When the karhi is ready Stir in your pakoras, bring it to a boil and turn off. They will simmer in the residual heat. Warm your oil in a frying pan and Stir in the baghaar ingredients, when they are sizzly and aromatic and then pour the baghaar over your karhi.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: In a large bowl, Mix 2 cups sour dahi, 4 tablespoons besan, 1 teaspoon haldi, 1 teaspoon lal mirch, and 1 teaspoon namak. Whisk vigorously until completely smooth — no lumps allowed.
Pour the whisked mixture into a large degh (heavy-bottomed pot) or pateela (saucepan) and Put on medium heat. Stir continuously with a chamcha (ladle) as it heats up.

In a bowl, Mix 2 tablespoons besan, 0.5 teaspoon ajwain, a pinch of namak, and enough water (roughly 3-4 tablespoons) to make a thick batter — it should be thicker than pancake batter, more like a stiff paste that coats a spoon heavily. Stir in your sliced piyaz.
Pour enough tel into a separate karahi (wok) or deep pan to reach about 2 inches deep. Heat on medium-high. If it burns immediately, lower the heat.

Once your kadhi has simmered for 25-30 minutes and thickened slightly, gently Stir in the fried pakoras into the pot. Stir very gently — the pakoras are delicate and you don't want to break them apart. Let the kadhi simmer on low heat for another 10 minutes so.

Warm 4 tablespoons of tel in a small tawa (flat griddle pan) or a small pan on HIGH heat until you can see wisps of smoke. Stir in the methi dana first and let them sizzle for just 10-15 seconds — they burn fast and turn bitter if.
Uncover, give a gentle stir to distribute the tarka, and serve immediately over steamed chawal (rice). Garnish with a sprinkle of fresh hara dhania.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: To get started on the pakoras, mix in 1 1⁄2 cup besan (gram flour), 1⁄2 tsp red chili powder, salt, coriander seeds, and baking soda. Slowly Stir in roughly 2/3 cup water, gradually folding it in with the dry ingredients with a spoon. Let it sit for 10. If it's too watery, Stir in more flour.

Warm a small saucepan. Stir in 1⁄2 cup of oil. Make sure you don't overcrowd the pan - Cook in batches if needed. For the kadhi batter, Stir in the yogurt, 1⁄2 cup besan (gram flour), red chili powder, turmeric powder and 6 cups of water to a blender. Blend until smooth.
Warm 1⁄4 cup oil in a large pot. Stir in the fenugreek seeds. When they start popping, Stir in the chopped onion and Cook on medium heat till translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in crushed ginger and garlic, and Cook for 30 seconds. If using, Stir in diced tomato. Increase heat and continue to stir till the tomato softens.

Once the tomato breaks down and becomes paste-like, Stir in in the kadhi batter. While stirring constantly, bring the kadhi to a boil. Lower heat and let the kadhi simmer for roughly 20 minutes, uncovered. Stir in salt.

Stir in the pakoras to the kadhi, and let it simmer for another 10 minutes. Remove from heat. Warm 2 tablespoon oil in a non-stick pan. Stir in cumin seeds and Cook on medium heat until the color darkens slightly. Stir in the kadi pata, stir for a few seconds, and and then Stir in the chilies.
Pour the tadka with the oil on top of the kadhi, and serve with rice.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Kadhi Pakora Recipe – Traditional Flavor, Made Quicker

variants.name: Punjabi Kadhi Pakora

ingredients.text: 3-4 red or green chillies (fresh or dry)

instructions: Prepare and dry the vegetables or filling ingredients.
Mix the flour or besan with coriander powder, cumin powder, chilli flakes, turmeric, red chilli powder, coriander powder; add water gradually to make a coating batter or cohesive filling.
Heat the oil to medium-high. Fry in small batches until crisp and evenly golden, allowing the oil to recover between batches.
Drain well and serve hot with the listed chutney or garnish.

variants.name: Sindhi Kadhi Pakora

ingredients.text: 2 whole sukhi laal mirch (dried red chillies)
1 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Mix 2 tbsp roasted besan with sliced piyaz, ajwain, a pinch of laal mirch powder and salt. Stir in minimal water to form a thick, clingy batter. Cook in hot oil until golden.
Mix remaining 3 tbsp roasted besan with 300ml cold water. Whisk until completely smooth.
Warm oil in a deep pot. Stir in rai — wait to pop. Stir in methi dana, zeera, kari patta, and sukhi laal mirch.

Stir in besan slurry plus remaining water to the pot, stirring constantly. Stir in cubed aloo, tamarind paste, and salt. Bring to boil while stirring, and then simmer 20-25 minutes until aloo is tender and kadhi thickens slightly.
Slide in fried pakoras. Simmer 8-10 minutes.

variants.name: Green Tea Kahwah — Kashmiri Valley Style

ingredients.text: 2 tsp Kashmiri green tea leaves (kehwa patti)
0.25 tsp Sabz elaichi dana (green cardamom seeds, loose)

instructions: Crush the saffron threads between your fingers and steep in 2 tbsp warm water for 5 minutes.
In a small saucepan (or a samovar if you have one), bring 4 cups water to a simmer — not a full boil. Stir in crushed cardamom pods and cinnamon stick. Simmer 5 minutes to infuse.
Stir in green tea leaves. Simmer on very low heat for 3-4 minutes. Do not boil — boiling green tea makes it bitter.
Stir in the bloomed saffron with its soaking water. Stir gently.
Strain through a fine mesh strainer into small cups or bowls.
Pour into small khos (bowl-cups) or small ceramic cups. Float the almond and pistachio garnish on top.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Green Tea Kahwah — Kashmiri Valley Style

variants.name: Kahwah — Peshawari Saffron Green Tea

ingredients.text: 1.5 tsp hari chai patti (loose-leaf green tea
a generous pinch (about 10-12 strands) zafran (saffron strands)

instructions: WARM THE WATER — DON'T BOIL IT: Pour 500ml of fresh cold water into a small pateela (saucepan) or kettle. Heat it over medium heat until you see small bubbles beginning to form at the bottom and sides of the pan — this is around 80-85°C (175-185°F).
Stir in the cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves to the warm water. Reduce the heat to the lowest setting and let the spices infuse gently for 3-4 minutes. The water should remain hot but not simmer.
Stir in the loose-leaf green tea directly to the spiced water. Stir once with a chamcha (small ladle) or spoon. Let the tea steep for exactly 2-3 minutes on the lowest heat.
Pour the bloomed saffron (strands plus the tablespoon of warm water it was soaking in) into the tea. Stir gently.
Pour the kahwah through a fine mesh strainer into pre-warmed cups or small glass cups.

variants.name: Saffron Kahwah — Premium Celebration Blend

ingredients.text: 3 tsp Kashmiri green tea leaves (kehwa patti)

instructions: Steep all saffron in 3 tbsp warm water for 10 minutes.
Bring 6 cups water to a gentle simmer. Stir in cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves. Simmer 8 minutes — longer than everyday kahwah to extract maximum spice depth.
Stir in green tea leaves. Keep at a gentle simmer (never boil) for 4-5 minutes.
Stir in dried rose petals and bloomed saffron with liquid. Stir gently. Simmer 2 more minutes — the rose petals will soften and release their perfume.
Stir in honey while still warm.
Strain into a beautiful serving vessel (a copper pot is traditional).

variants.name: Kala Chana or Kalay Chanay

ingredients.text: 2 cups black chickpeas or kalay chanay

instructions: Soak your black chickpeas overnight, rinse the water off.
Warm oil in your IP/Pressure Cooker.
Saute cumin seeds till you can really smell them sizzling and and then Stir in the diced onions.
Cook stirring occasionally till slightly golden and then Stir in the ginger and garlic pastes and saute for a minute.
And then Stir in the Salt, Red Chilli Powder, Coriander Powder, Turmeric, and stir Cook for a minute.
Stir in the diced tomato and saute until it's cooked to a rich paste.
Stir in the black chickpeas, stir to cook and and then Stir in 2 1/2 cups of hot water to your Instant Pot and set it on Manual for 25 minutes .
Check the consistency, saute to reduce water or Stir in water and bring to a boil according to your personal preference.
And then Stir in the tamarind pulp and garam masala, let simmer for 2-3 minutes and then garnish with desired toppings.

variants.name: Kale Fritters (Pakora)

ingredients.item: Tuscan kale (chopped into thin ribbons (thick vein removed)⁣⁣)
ingredients.text: 1/2 cup Tuscan kale (chopped into thin ribbons (thick vein removed)⁣⁣)
1/2 cup red onion (thinly sliced into 1/2 moon shapes⁣⁣)

ingredients.preparation: grated on the large holes of a box grater ⁣⁣
ingredients.text: 1/2 cup potato (grated on the large holes of a box grater ⁣⁣)

ingredients.preparation: you can also use besan, which is roasted chickpea flour ⁣⁣
ingredients.text: 3/4 cup chickpea flour (you can also use besan, which is roasted chickpea flour ⁣⁣)

ingredients.item: Greek yoghurt (full-fat (you can also use sour cream of mayo)⁣⁣)
ingredients.text: 1 cup Greek yoghurt (full-fat (you can also use sour cream of mayo)⁣⁣)

instructions: Mix all ingredients, except for water, in a medium-sized mixing bowl. Mix well to Mix, ensuring that the chickpea flour has coated all the vegetables and herbs well.
Stir in 1⁄2 cup of cold water and stir till it transforms into a thick batter.
Warm 1⁄2-inch of oil in a large skillet, on medium-high heat, to 350F degrees.
Cook about 60-90 seconds per side, until the fritters turn golden-brown and are cooked through.
Remove the friters from the oil and transfer them to a large platter lined with paper towels.
Stir in salt, to taste.

variants.name: Karachi Halwa (Cornflour Halwa / Bombay Halwa)

ingredients.text: 1/2 tsp kewra essence or rose water
1 tbsp ghee ya tail (ghee or oil)

instructions: Have a strong wooden spoon or a heat-resistant silicone spatula ready for stirring.

In a large, heavy-bottomed karahi (wok) or a wide, deep pateela (saucepan) — heavy-bottomed is essential to prevent burning — pour 3 cups of cold water. Stir in 1 cup of cornflour to the cold water. Whisk vigorously with a wire whisk or a fork until the cornflour.

Stir in 2 cups of cheeni (sugar) to the karahi with the cornflour mixture and stir to Mix. Put the karahi over medium heat. and then around 5–7 minutes, it will start to thicken noticeably and look like a pale coloured gel.

When the mixture is thick and gel-like (around 8–10 minutes of cooking), begin adding the ghee. Don't Stir in it all at once. Stir in it in 3–4 additions, about 3 tablespoons at a time, stirring vigorously after each addition until each batch of ghee is fully incorporated.
Continue cooking and stirring on medium heat. This is the long part — it will take 20–30 minutes total from when you started. Watch for these stages: Stage 1 — pale, thick gel (10 minutes).

When the halwa is at Stage 3 (shiny, cohesive, pulling away from the sides), Stir in kewra essence or rose water if using, and stir through quickly. Remove from heat. Working quickly, pour and scrape the hot halwa into your pre-greased tray.

Leave the halwa to cool completely at room temperature — do NOT refrigerate it while it's hot or warm. This takes about 1–2 hours. Once completely cooled and set, use a sharp knife to cut it into diamond shapes: make parallel diagonal cuts in one direction, and then.
Arrange pieces in a single layer or separate layers with parchment paper.

variants.name: Fish Karahi

ingredients.item: crushed garlic - or 1 tbsp garlic paste
ingredients.text: 5-6 cloves crushed garlic - or 1 tbsp garlic paste

ingredients.item: heaped kasuri methi i.e dried fenugreek leaves
ingredients.text: 1 tbsp heaped kasuri methi i.e dried fenugreek leaves

instructions: Cut your fish into fairly large chunks – mine were about 2*2 inches.
Warm oil in your pan on medium high heat and roughly chop your tomatoes.
When the oil is hot Stir in the seeds i.e.
Stir in your garlic, let it cook for 30 seconds and and then Stir in your tomatoes, salt, chili powder, and chili flakes.
Mix well and cook the tomatoes on high heat, stirring constantly until they get dark red and caramelly looking. This takes me about 10 minutes in a large wok.
If you are up for it and then taste your spice mix, adjust seasoning if necessary, and then Put your fish pieces in the pan and cook for 3 minutes.
Carefully flip and let the fish cook through, another 2-4 minutes depending on the fish, a piece pressed will flake easily.
Drop the heat and Stir in the butter, kasuri methi, fresh pepper, give it a gentle stir, adjust seasoning.
Garnish with cilantro, ginger, chilies and dig in!

variants.name: Prawn Karahi Masala

ingredients.preparation: fresh or tinned, pureed in a blender
ingredients.text: 4 medium sized tomatoes (fresh or tinned, pureed in a blender)

ingredients.item: paprika or Kashmiri red chilli powder
ingredients.text: 3 tsp paprika or Kashmiri red chilli powder

ingredients.item: fresh ginger cut into matchstick slices
ingredients.text: fresh ginger cut into matchstick slices (as much as desired)

instructions: Heat the cooking fat and brown the heaped tbsp minced garlic over medium-high heat.

Stir in heaped tbsp minced garlic, heaped tbsp minced ginger, fresh green chillies, paprika or Kashmiri red chilli powder, followed by the tomatoes and fresh green chillies, paprika or Kashmiri red chilli powder, turmeric, cumin powder, coriander powder, red chilli powder.
Cook uncovered, stirring regularly, until the protein is cooked and the tomato masala reduces enough for the oil to separate.
Finish with heaped tbsp minced ginger, coriander powder, chopped coriander and serve immediately.

variants.name: Balochi Gosht Karahi — Desert Style

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp Dumba charbi (fat-tail fat) or ghee
1 tsp Sabut kali mirch (whole black peppercorns)
3 pieces Sabut laal mirch (whole dried red chilies)

instructions: Melt dumba fat or ghee in a large iron karahi over high heat. Stir in whole black peppercorns and dried red chilies.
Stir in mutton pieces. Sear on high heat, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes until browned all over.
Stir in halved tomatoes. Do not stir — cover the karahi and cook on medium for 35-40 minutes. The tomatoes and meat steam-cook together.
Uncover, Stir in ginger and green chilies. Stir everything together. Cook uncovered on medium-high for 20-25 minutes.
Increase heat and stir-Cook 5-8 minutes until sauce reduces and oil is clearly visible. Season with salt.
Right before serving, Stir in 4 tablespoons of cold plain yogurt directly into the hot karahi.

variants.name: Pashtun Beef Karahi — Tribal Belt Style

ingredients.text: 3 pieces Sukha sabut laal mirch (dried whole red chilies)
1 serving Kachi piyaz aur adrak (raw onion and ginger)

instructions: Warm oil in an iron karahi or heavy wok until very hot, almost smoking.
Stir in beef pieces and sear on high heat for 10-12 minutes — beef takes longer to color than lamb. Stir and turn to brown all sides.
Stir in SALT, PEPPER, AND TOMATOES: Stir in salt, black pepper, and halved tomatoes. Cover and cook on medium heat for 45 minutes — beef needs more time than lamb to become tender.
Uncover, Stir in ginger julienne and green chilies. Stir everything together. Cook uncovered on medium-high for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Increase heat and bhuno (stir-Cook vigorously) for 8-10 minutes until the sauce reduces and clings to the meat.
Scatter coriander, serve in the karahi.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Pashtun Beef Karahi — Tribal Belt Style

variants.name: Peshawari Karahi Gosht

ingredients.text: 1.5 tsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)
2 tbsp Adrak Julienne (Ginger Strips for Garnish)

instructions: Put your karahi (wok) or a heavy-bottomed frying pan on the highest flame your stove can produce. Stir in the tel (oil) or rendered fat and let it get smoking hot — see a faint haze rising from the surface.
Stir in the bone-in goat pieces in a single layer — do not crowd the pan. Sear on high heat for 3-4 minutes per side without moving the meat.

Push the meat to the sides of the karahi and drop the pounded lehsan (garlic) and julienned adrak (ginger) into the hot oil in the centre. Stir for 60-90 seconds until the raw smell of garlic disappears and it turns light golden — you'll smell the sweetness kick.
Stir in all the chopped tamatar (tomatoes) at once. Stir everything together, Stir in the lal mirch powder, dhania powder, kali mirch, and half the namak. Turn heat to medium-high.
Once the tomato masala has bhunned (caramelised), increase heat to maximum again. Toss the meat continuously in the masala for 5-7 minutes — this is the most important step.

Stir in the slit hari mirch (green chillies) and the ginger paste (the second half of the adrak you reserved). Toss on high heat for 2-3 minutes. The chillies will blister and soften slightly — they should still hold their shape but have a little give when you.
Take the karahi off heat. Cover loosely with a lid or plate and let it rest for 5 minutes — the residual heat will wilt the dhania and meld the flavours without turning everything mushy.

variants.name: Shinwari Karahi — Peshawari Mountain Karahi

ingredients.text: 5 tbsp Dumba charbi ya tel (sheep tail fat or oil)
1 tbsp Taza adrak strips (fresh ginger, raw)

instructions: In a large iron karahi or heavy wok, heat the dumba fat or oil until very hot — nearly smoking.
Stir in lamb pieces all at once. Do not stir for 2-3 minutes — let the meat sear and color on one side. and then stir and sear the other sides.
Stir in salt and black pepper. Stir to distribute.
Stir in halved tomatoes directly on top of the meat. Do not stir yet. Cover and cook on medium heat for 30 minutes — the tomatoes will collapse and steam the meat.

Uncover, Stir in ginger julienne and whole green chilies. stir everything together. Cook uncovered on medium-high heat for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the meat is completely tender and the tomato has broken down into a light, somewhat watery sauce.
Increase to maximum heat for 5 minutes, stirring constantly. The sauce should reduce to just coat the meat — Shinwari karahi is not thick.
Scatter fresh coriander over the top.

variants.name: Beef Karahi Karachi Style

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Warm oil in a large, heavy karahi on medium-high. Cook onions for 10-12 minutes until deep golden brown.
Stir in ginger garlic paste and Cook aggressively for 3 minutes until golden. Stir in turmeric and stir for 30 seconds.
Stir in chopped tomatoes with all dry spices. Cook on high heat for 15 minutes until tomatoes completely dissolve and oil separates clearly. Mash with a spoon as they cook.

Increase to highest heat. Stir in beef and stir-Cook for 8-10 minutes to brown the meat. This searing step builds the fond (caramelised layer) that makes Karachi karahi different from a regular curry.
Reduce to medium, Stir in 1/2 cup water, and cover. Cook for 30-40 minutes until beef is tender, checking every 10 minutes. Beef on the bone will take 40 minutes.
Remove lid, Stir in green chillies, and increase heat to high. Bhuno (stir-Cook) for 10-12 minutes, stirring constantly, until masala dries and coats the meat.
Stir for 1 minute. Garnish with ginger juliennes and coriander.

variants.name: Karela Gosht

ingredients.text: 600 grams mutton or lamb meat (bone in)
1 tsp red chilli powder (or to taste)

instructions: Prepare all ingredients before heating the pan.
Warm the cooking fat and cook onions, garlic, chunk ginger, red chilli powder until softened and aromatic.
Stir in cumin seeds, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric, red chilli powder, fresh coriander, then add the mutton or lamb meat and coat it thoroughly in the masala.
Add the listed liquid ingredients as needed, cover and simmer until the main ingredient is fully cooked.
Reduce the sauce to the intended consistency, adjust the seasoning and finish with chunk ginger, coriander powder, fresh coriander.

variants.name: Karela Sabzi

ingredients.item: yellow onions (thinly sliced in half rings (roughly 1 1/2 lb))
ingredients.text: 2 large yellow onions (thinly sliced in half rings (roughly 1 1/2 lb))

instructions: Generously salt sliced bitter melon and Put in colander for 2 hours.
In a large saucepan, heat oil and Cook bitter melon on low to medium heat for 20 – 30 minutes. Drain on paper towel and set aside.
In the same oil, Stir in onion and Cook for 10 minutes on low to medium heat till it browns evenly.
Stir in salt and spices and stir for 1 – 3 minutes. Stir in water to deglaze the pan if necessary.
Stir in diced tomatoes and Cook on high heat for 5- 7 minutes.
Stir in the fried bitter melon. Dial heat to lowest possible point and cover.
Stir in cilantro for garnish and serve with either roti or plain rice.

variants.name: Kashmiri Naan

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp tel ya makhan (oil or melted butter)

instructions: In a small katori (bowl), Mix the lukewarm water, 1 teaspoon of sugar (taken from the dough's 2 tablespoons), and the instant yeast. Stir once gently and leave it alone for 8–10 minutes.
In a large paraat (wide mixing bowl) or directly on a clean counter, Mix the maida, remaining sugar, and salt. Pour in the activated yeast mixture, dahi, and oil or melted butter.
Turn the dough onto a lightly floured surface and knead it with the heel of your hand — push forward, fold back, turn, repeat. Keep going for a full 8–10 minutes.
Shape the dough into a ball. Cover with a damp muslin (cheesecloth) or plastic wrap. Put in a warm spot — on top of the fridge, or inside an oven with just the light on — for 1 to 1.5 hours.

In a small bowl, Mix the crumbled or grated khoya, desiccated coconut, raisins, chopped almonds, sugar (for the filling), and cardamom powder. Mix well with a fork or your fingers until everything is evenly distributed.
Set your oven to its maximum temperature — ideally 250°C (480°F). Put a heavy baking tray or pizza stone on the top rack and let it heat for at least 20–30 minutes.

Divide it into 6 equal portions and roll each into a smooth ball. On a lightly floured chakla (rolling board), flatten one ball with your palm, and then use your belan (rolling pin) to roll it into a circle roughly 15cm (6 inches) in diameter.

Gently, very gently, use the belan to roll the sealed dough ball back out into an oval shape about 20–22cm long and roughly 1cm thick. Start from the centre and roll outward in one direction, rotate slightly, roll again.
Carefully pull the hot baking tray out of the oven using thick oven gloves. Bake for 4–6 minutes until the top is golden and has visible brown spots and blisters.

variants.name: Lahori Katakat — The Chopping Rhythm Street Food

ingredients.text: 800 g Mixed Offal OR Boneless Chicken

instructions: PREP THE OFFAL (if using): If using lamb brain (maghaz): remove the outer membrane carefully (it peels off like a thin skin), and then soak in salted cold water for 30 minutes to remove any blood. Soak kidneys in salted water for 20 minutes to reduce their strong.
Put it on the highest heat your stove allows and let it pre-heat for 3-4 minutes until it's smoking hot. Stir in oil.
Stir in whole cumin seeds to the smoking oil — they'll pop and hiss immediately. Stir in the meat in a single layer (or as close as possible in your pan).

While continuously chopping and stirring, Stir in the ingredients one by one directly to the pan: ginger-garlic paste first (it will splutter — stand back), and then the chopped tomatoes, and then the green chillies, and then the coriander powder, red chilli, turmeric, and salt.

Continue the chopping and stirring for 12-15 minutes on high heat. Everything becomes one cohesive mass — see: patches of caramelised brown char on the meat surfaces, the tomato moisture has evaporated, and the oil has separated and is visible as small shiny pools around the edges.

Reduce heat to medium. If it's too dry and sticking, Stir in 2-3 tablespoons of water and continue stirring — the water will immediately evaporate and help release any stuck bits from the pan (those stuck bits are flavour). A pinch more red chilli if Aim for more.
Turn off the heat.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Lahori Katakat — The Chopping Rhythm Street Food

variants.name: Mutton Katakat

ingredients.text: 2.5 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Unlike offal, mutton needs pre-cooking. Pressure cook the boneless mutton with a little salt and 1 cup water for 15-20 minutes until 70% tender.
Warm oil in a large flat tawa or heavy pan. Cook onions until golden. Stir in ginger garlic paste, Cook 2 minutes.
Stir in tomatoes and cook on high for 10-12 minutes until thick masala forms with oil separation.
Stir in par-cooked mutton pieces and green chillies to the masala on the tawa.
Cook on high heat for 15-20 minutes with continuous chopping and stirring.
Stir in butter and kasuri methi. The masala should coat every piece of mutton with a sticky, concentrated layer. Garnish with ginger juliennes and serve immediately.

variants.name: Karachi Katakat

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
2.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Soak kidneys in salted water 30 minutes.
Warm oil on maximum flame. Cook onions aggressively until deep golden. Stir in ginger garlic paste and Cook 3 minutes.
Stir in tomatoes and cook on high for 12-15 minutes until very thick.
Stir in kidneys to the masala. Cook on high, chopping and stirring continuously with a metal spatula for 5-6 minutes.
Stir in liver and green chillies.
Stir in brain last. Chop and stir for 3 minutes until integrated. Stir in amchur and garam masala.

variants.name: Ground Beef Kebabs Recipe
instructions: Stir in salt and ground spices (garam masala powder, red chili powder, black pepper, cumin powder) and mix well.
Stir in the onion-cilantro mixture, crushed ginger and garlic, lime juice and olive oil to the ground beef. Mix well.
Take fistfuls of the mixture, and begin to shape into little patties.

Grill Instructions: If you are using the grill, make sure you heat it up well. The time will depend on whether you are using a charcoal or gas grill. Once hot, Put kebabs on the grill and cook each side for 4-6 minutes.

Oven Instructions: If Aim for to prepare them in the oven, pre-heat it to 450°F. Set it to broil on high heat for 10 – 15 minutes depending on how well done you like them to be (I set them for 12 minutes).

variants.name: Kebab Curry

ingredients.item: can chopped tomatoes or tomato sauce (passata)
ingredients.preparation: or 4-6 large fresh tomatoes, chopped, skin removed
ingredients.text: 28 oz can chopped tomatoes or tomato sauce (passata) (or 4-6 large fresh tomatoes, chopped, skin removed)

instructions: Put a large pot (at least 8-in diameter) on medium heat. Stir in oil, onions and garlic.
Sauté till golden brown, and then Stir in tomatoes and cayenne pepper. Cover pot and turn heat to low. Allow to simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in salt to taste and set aside while you form the kebabs. Transfer into a mixing bowl.
To this, Stir in ground beef, gram flour, egg, cayenne pepper, salt, coriander and cumin powders. Mix to Mix well.
Put each kebab on parchment paper as you continue to shape them. Put pot with tomato sauce on medium heat, when it starts to bubble, Stir in 1 cup boiling water.

Replace the lid and turn the heat to low. Allow the kebabs to poach in the sauce for 30 minutes. When the time has elapsed, allow kebabs to rest for ten minutes before serving, otherwise they may crumble.
Garnish with green chillies, mint, coriander or any other fresh herb of your choice.

variants.name: Pakistani Beef Kebab

ingredients.text: 2 cups coarsely chopped fresh coriander, (stems and leaves)
1 cup coarsely chopped fresh mint leaves

ingredients.item: corn oil ((or any other neutral oil) for shallow frying)
ingredients.text: corn oil ((or any other neutral oil) for shallow frying)

instructions: Mix meat, onion, coriander, mint, chilies, cayenne pepper, green onions, coriander seeds, egg and salt in a food processor and process untill well combined and onions, green onions and coriander are finely chopped.
At this stage you have two options- either Cook the kebabs, or if you wish to employ healthy cooking techniques, broil them in the oven.

Warm 1/4 inch of oil in a pan over medium heat. Working in batches, Stir in patties to oil and Cook for 30-40 seconds per side or until golden brown and cooked through, adding more oil as needed (you may need to change the oil as it darkens).
Arrange patties on a cookie sheet and brush each patty with corn oil.
Put under a hot grill/broiler 30-40 seconds per side.

variants.name: Easy Keema Naan Recipe - In The Oven + Tawa

ingredients.preparation: you can use self-raising flour for a fluffier naan
ingredients.text: 5 2/3 cups flour (you can use self-raising flour for a fluffier naan)
1 2/3 lb mince meat of choice - lamb/chicken/beef
1 tsp ginger powder (or half tbsp fresh ginger)

instructions: Mix the flour, salt and listed dough ingredients; add water gradually and knead to a soft, smooth dough.
Cover and rest the dough while preparing any filling. Cook the filling until dry enough not to tear the bread, then cool it.
Divide and roll the dough. Add the filling if used, seal well and roll again without forcing it through the surface.
Cook on a hot tawa or heavy pan, turning and brushing with the measured fat, until both sides are spotted and cooked through.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Easy Keema Naan Recipe - In The Oven + Tawa
source_attributions.author: Fatima Cooks

variants.name: Keema Naan

ingredients.text: 3/4 cup approximately neem garam pani (lukewarm water)
1/2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Leave 5-10 minutes until foamy. In a large bowl, mix maida (refined white flour), 1 tsp namak (salt), dahi (yoghurt), tel (oil), and the yeast mixture. Stir in water gradually to form a soft, slightly tacky dough.
Warm the ghee (clarified butter) in a karahi (wok) or heavy frying pan over medium-high heat. When the ghee shimmers, Stir in the zeera (cumin seeds). Stir in the finely diced pyaz (onion).

Stir in the adrak-lehsun paste (ginger-garlic paste) and stir for 1 minute until the raw smell disappears and it turns light golden. Stir in the dhania powder (coriander powder) and lal mirch powder (red chilli powder). Stir continuously for 30 seconds — the spices will toast in the.
Stir in the minced beef or mutton keema to the pan. Keep breaking and stirring over high heat. Do not reduce heat.
This is the most important step. Continue cooking the keema over high heat, stirring and pressing, for 15-18 minutes total from the moment the meat hit the pan.

Stir in the hari mirch (green chilli), garam masala, remaining namak (salt), and hara dhania (fresh coriander). Stir to Mix. Transfer to a plate and spread out to cool to room temperature — do not stuff hot filling into the dough.

Put the sealed ball seam-side down on a lightly floured surface. Using a belan (rolling pin), VERY gently roll it out to an oval about 20cm long and 10cm wide. Roll slowly, with even pressure — no sudden heavy pressure that would push the filling through the surface.

Preheat your oven to 250°C (480°F) with a cast-iron tawa (flat griddle pan) or heavy baking tray on the top rack for at least 30 minutes. Bake for 5-7 minutes until the surface is golden with dark spots and the naan feels firm when tapped on the base.

variants.name: Keema Paratha

ingredients.text: 1/2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Mix atta and 1⁄2 tsp salt in a paraat (wide mixing bowl). Stir in warm water gradually, mixing until a soft dough forms. Knead for 5–6 minutes until smooth.

COOK THE KEEMA FILLING — DRY IS THE GOAL: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a small karahi (wok) or frying pan over medium-high heat. Stir in zeera (cumin seeds) — they should sizzle immediately. Stir in the finely chopped pyaaz and cook, stirring, for 5–7 minutes until the.
Stir in the adrak lehsun paste to the golden onion and stir for 1 minute — it will smell sharp and wonderful. Stir in dhania powder, lal mirch powder, and salt. Stir for 30 seconds.

Stir in the minced meat to the pan. Stir and break continuously for 2–3 minutes as the meat changes from pink to grey-brown. Keep cooking on medium-high heat, stirring regularly, until ALL the liquid has evaporated and the mixture looks dry and the meat starts to sizzle in.
Roll one ball into a 12 cm circle.

ROLL CAREFULLY — ONE SIDE ONLY: Dust the filled ball lightly in flour. Roll it out to about 18–20 cm, but here is the special technique for keema paratha: apply pressure from only one direction at a time. Roll outward from the centre, turn 90 degrees, roll outward.
COOK ON MEDIUM HEAT (slightly lower than other parathas): Heat the tawa (flat griddle pan) over medium to medium-low heat.
Transfer to a plate.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Mix atta with 0.5 tsp salt and 1 tbsp oil. Stir in warm water gradually to form a soft, smooth dough. Knead 5-7 minutes.
Warm 1 tsp oil in a pan. Stir in zeera, cook 30 seconds. Stir in minced piyaz and cook until translucent, 3-4 minutes.
Divide dough into 8 equal balls. Roll one ball into a 5-inch circle.
Flatten the stuffed ball gently with your hands, and then very carefully roll into a 7-inch circle.
Warm a tawa (flat griddle) on medium-high. Cook until bubbles appear (about 1 minute). Flip, Stir in 1 tbsp ghee around edges.
Keema paratha is at peak crispiness in the first 5 minutes.

variants.name: Khaddi Kabab

ingredients.item: bakra (young goat) or lamb, whole leg or large bone-in pieces
ingredients.text: 1.5 kg bakra (young goat) or lamb, whole leg or large bone-in pieces
1 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

ingredients.item: flour + enough water to make a thick dough atta (whole wheat flour) + pani
ingredients.text: 1 cup flour + enough water to make a thick dough atta (whole wheat flour) + pani (water)

instructions: In a large bowl, Mix the dahi (yoghurt), adrak-lehsun paste (ginger-garlic paste), namak (salt), lal mirch powder (red chilli powder), and sarson ka tel (mustard oil). Whisk until smooth and combined.
Score the meat deeply with a sharp knife — make cuts about 2-3cm deep all over the surface, especially near the bone.
Remove the marinated meat from the fridge 1 hour before cooking.
Mix 1 cup of atta (whole wheat flour) with just enough pani (water) to make a stiff, pliable dough — stiffer than bread dough, almost like clay. Roll it into a long rope about 1cm thick.
Transfer the marinated meat and all the marinade into your Dutch oven, clay matka (clay pot), or the heaviest, most oven-safe pot you own with a tight lid. Do not Stir in any water.
Put the sealed pot on your stovetop over medium heat for 15 minutes.
Preheat your oven to 150°C (300°F) while the pot is on the stove. After the 15-minute stovetop start, carefully transfer the sealed pot to the middle rack of the oven. Cook for 4 hours undisturbed.
After 4 hours, remove the pot from the oven. If it doesn't, re-seal with fresh dough and return to the oven for another 45 minutes.
Do not serve immediately. Let the Khaddi Kabab rest, uncovered, for 10 minutes.

variants.name: Chicken Khaddi — Home-Scale Pit-Style

ingredients.text: 1.5 tsp Laal mirch powder (red chili powder)

instructions: Mix all marinade ingredients (yogurt through lemon juice). Score the chicken deeply all over and stuff marinade into every cut and cavity. Marinate 4-8 hours minimum, overnight preferred.
Preheat your oven to 160°C.
Put in the oven for 2 hours at 160°C. Do not open the oven in the first 90 minutes. The chicken will cook in its own steam and marinade.
After 2 hours, remove the foil seal and lid. Increase oven to 230°C and roast uncovered for 15-20 minutes to char and crisp the skin.
Let rest 5 minutes.

variants.name: Khaddi Kabab — Underground Earth-Pit Kabab

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp Laal mirch powder (red chili powder)

instructions: Mix yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, all spice powders, salt, lemon juice, and mustard oil. Cover and refrigerate 8-12 hours.
Build a massive charcoal fire inside the pit and let it burn for 2 hours until the rocks are red-hot and the charcoal is glowing embers.
Cover the pit with a heavy metal sheet or wooden boards, and then seal completely with sand or soil.
Leave completely undisturbed for 4-5 hours. The sealed environment creates a convection oven effect — steam and heat circulate and cook the meat from all angles simultaneously.
At 4 hours, carefully open a corner of the seal. If not, reseal and cook 30-60 minutes more.
Transfer to a large thal (serving platter).

variants.name: Khageena
instructions: Warm a lug of oil in a saucepan.
Briskly whisk the eggs, a little chilli powder and a fat pinch of salt together.
When the oil shimmers (gets hot) Stir in your onions and green chillies and saute until the onion looks translucent.
Stir in your eggs and cook, breaking and folding in on over itself till required doneness.

variants.name: Khagina: Pakistani Scrambled Eggs
instructions: Break the eggs into a bowl, Stir in salt and whisk lightly together, just enough so that the yolks Mix with the whites.

Put pan over a fairly medium heat, Stir in the butter (or olive oil) and tilt the pan from side to side so the pan is coated evenly. As soon as the butter stops foaming and begins to turn a nutty brown, Stir in the onions and stir.
Stir in the cumin seeds and Cook for 2 minutes till aromatic.
To this, Stir in the tomatoes and stir till warmed over and slightly soft. Turn the heat to low.
Stir in cilantro, the egg mixture and chilies.
Continue to stir the eggs swiftly, for another 5-7 minutes, until they are at the point of setting and resemble a soft custard.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Break the eggs into a bowl, Stir in salt and chilli pepper and whisk lightly together, just enough so that the yolks Mix with the whites.
Warm a stainless steel frying pan for a minute or so on medium-heat, and then Stir in olive oil and butter, allowing it to melt.
Immediately Stir in onions and potatoes and sauté for 7-10 minutes till they are caramelised and look bronze.
Pour in the egg mixture and let it sit, without stirring, for 20 seconds. Stir till the eggs are at the point of setting and resemble a soft custard.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Zarreen's Khagina- Scrambled Eggs with Potatoes in the Pakistani Manner

alternate_names: Zarreen's Khagina- Scrambled Eggs with Potatoes in the Pakistani Manner

variants.name: Khameeri Roti

ingredients.text: 1 cup maida (refined white flour / all-purpose flour)
1 cup gehun ka atta (whole wheat flour)
1 tablespoon tail ya ghee (neutral oil or ghee)

instructions: In a small cup or bowl, Mix the warm water, sugar, and yeast. Stir gently and leave it undisturbed for 8–10 minutes.
In a large bowl (paraat), mix the maida and atta together. Stir in the salt and mix it in.
Pour the foamy yeast mixture into the well in the flour. Stir in the oil or ghee. Using your hand, bring the mixture together into a shaggy dough, and then knead for 8–10 full minutes.
FIRST PROOF — LET IT RISE: Shape the dough into a ball. Cover the bowl tightly with a damp cloth or cling wrap. Leave in a warm Put for 1 to 1.5 hours.
Let them rest uncovered for 10 minutes — this relaxes the gluten and makes rolling much easier.

If using an oven: Put a heavy baking tray or pizza stone on the top rack and preheat the oven to its maximum temperature (usually 250°C / 480°F) for at least 20 minutes. If using a tawa: heat it on high flame for 3–4 minutes until very hot.
On a lightly floured chakla (rolling board), roll each dough ball into a circle about 6–7 inches across and 5–6mm thick. Khameeri Roti is thicker than chapati — don't roll it thin.
On tawa: Put the roti on the hot tawa over high heat. Cook 60–90 seconds until the bottom has brown patches and the surface is bubbling. Flip and cook another 60 seconds.
Remove from heat and immediately brush with ghee.

variants.name: Kharay Masalay ka Gosht

ingredients.item: ginger grated or very very finely minced
ingredients.text: 1 1/2 inch ginger grated or very very finely minced

ingredients.item: yogurt - whipped and at room temp
ingredients.text: 1/2 cup yogurt - whipped and at room temp

instructions: Warm a very generous glug of oil in a pot or pressure cooker.
Stir in sliced onion.
Cook till the edges are golden.
Put the beef in the pot, saute and Stir in the ginger and garlic.
Stir in the whole spices, the red chilli powder, coriander powder, turmeric powder, and salt.

Cook till tender - for a pressure cooker Stir in about a cup of hot water and cook till the meat is tender. For a regular pot Stir in about a cup and a half, bring to a boil and simmer for 50 minutes to an hour until.
Turn the heat up and dry up the water, when the masala is at the "right" level the oil will rise above the spice paste.
At that point stir in the yogurt, the oil will quickly rise to the top.
Stir in diced chillies (according to taste), a handful of cilantro, black pepper and garam masala powder.

dish_families.name: Khatte Aloo | Khattay Aloo | Tangy Potatoes

variants.name: Khatte Aloo | Khattay Aloo | Tangy Potatoes
variants.dish_family: Khatte Aloo | Khattay Aloo | Tangy Potatoes

ingredients.preparation: can substitute with red chilli powder to taste
ingredients.text: 1 tbsp chilli flakes (can substitute with red chilli powder to taste)
1 tbsp desiccated coconut or coconut flakes (crushed)

ingredients.preparation: use 4 tbsp for a stronger tangy flavour
ingredients.text: 3 tbsp tamarind sauce/pulp/paste/puree (use 4 tbsp for a stronger tangy flavour)

ingredients.item: potatoes, boiled, peeled and cut into large chunks
ingredients.preparation: baby potatoes are GREAT for this, peeled and cut into large chunks
ingredients.text: 1 1/2 lb potatoes, boiled, peeled and cut into large chunks (baby potatoes are GREAT for this, peeled and cut into large chunks)
fresh coriander and green chilli (for garnishing)

instructions: Prepare all ingredients before heating the pan.
Warm the cooking fat and cook whole red chilli, chilli flakes, fresh coriander and green chilli until softened and aromatic.
Stir in whole red chilli, cumin seeds, chilli flakes, coriander powder, chaat masala, fresh coriander and green chilli, then add the oil and coat it thoroughly in the masala.
Add the listed liquid ingredients as needed, cover and simmer until the main ingredient is fully cooked.
Reduce the sauce to the intended consistency, adjust the seasoning and finish with coriander powder, fresh coriander and green chilli.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Khatte Aloo | Khattay Aloo | Tangy Potatoes
source_attributions.author: Fatima Cooks

variants.name: Karachi Khausa — The Memon Coconut Noodle Bowl

ingredients.text: 400 g Spaghetti or Thick Egg Noodles

ingredients.item: Crispy Sev or Fried Chow Mein Noodles
ingredients.text: 1 cup Crispy Sev or Fried Chow Mein Noodles

instructions: Warm a dry pan on medium heat. Stir in the besan (gram flour) and stir constantly for 3-4 minutes until it smells nutty and turns a shade darker. Spread it on a plate to cool for 5 minutes.
Warm oil in a large pateela (deep pot) on medium-high heat. Stir in 2 finely sliced onions. Cook, stirring regularly, for 12-15 minutes until deep golden-brown (barista).
To the remaining fried onions still in the pateela, Stir in ginger-garlic paste. Stir on medium heat for 2 minutes. Stir in turmeric and red chilli powder — they'll bloom immediately in the hot oil.

Open your coconut milk cans. The thick cream that has risen to the top — scoop that out first and Stir in it to the pot. Stir into the chicken for 2 minutes — the coconut cream will start to Cook slightly and smell intensely coconutty.

Stir in the dissolved besan paste to the simmering coconut curry in a slow stream, stirring constantly as you pour. Once all the besan is incorporated, bring to a full simmer on medium heat and cook for 10 minutes, stirring regularly. You'll see the curry visibly thickening —.
Reduce heat to medium-low, cover the pateela, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked through. Stir every 5 minutes.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a full boil. Cook spaghetti or noodles according to package instructions minus 1 minute (cook slightly less than stated — they'll continue cooking in the hot curry). Drain, drizzle with a teaspoon of oil, and toss to prevent sticking.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Karachi Khausa — The Memon Coconut Noodle Bowl

variants.name: Bread Kheer

ingredients.preparation: seeds removed and lightly crushed OR 1 tsp cardamom powder
ingredients.text: 6 cardamoms (seeds removed and lightly crushed OR 1 tsp cardamom powder)

instructions: Warm milk and half and half in a large heavy-bottomed pot on the stove (not nonstick).
Bring the mixture to a boil, tear the croissants and rusks into pieces and Stir in them in.
Simmer until both breads are soft, about 5-6 minutes.
Pour back in the pot (if using a regular blender). Stir in the cardamom, saffron, sugar and half the nuts.
Simmer on low heat, stirring frequently, the mixture will darken and thicken.
Cook it down by about 40 percent (nearly half) of what it was –this takes about 20-30 minutes depending on the pot you are using.

variants.name: Caramel Kheer
instructions: Soak basmati rice for one hour in cold water, allowing water to come 3-4cm (or 1-1.5in) above the rice (the rice will expand in water, so Aim for some extra water in the bowl to prevent the rice from drying out). After the rice has soaked for one hour, Put a large, heavy-bottomed pot on the stove on medium-high heat. When the.
Discard cold water from the rice and carefully transfer rice to boiling water with a pinch of salt. The rice will gently boil on medium-high heat. Check rice after 6 minutes.

Stir in milk, cream, and cardamom pods to the rice and starchy liquid. Stir and partially cover the pot with the lid (Aim for a little bit of steam to escape as it simmers, otherwise the milk will overflow). Set your timer to 20 minutes. Stir every 4-5 minutes to ensure that the pudding does not catch at the bottom of the.

At the 20-minute mark turn your stove off, remove the pudding from the burner and stir in the condensed milk (I added 200ml, but you may want to Stir in 250ml). Put in the fridge for 4-6 hours minimum, or overnight.

Put a frying pan on medium-high heat. When the pan is hot, Stir in butter and when it starts to sizzle and turn brown, Stir in breadcrumbs and a pinch of salt and gently stir. When the breadcrumbs have absorbed the butter, Stir in chopped walnuts and stir. Remove from heat and set aside while you prepare the caramel swirls.
Evenly sprinkle sugar in a saucepan and Put on medium-high heat. Remove the saucepan from the heat and allow the sugar to cool for five minutes.
Stir in a dusting of buttered breadcrumbs and walnuts and enjoy.

variants.name: Chawal ki Kheer - Pakistani Rice Pudding
instructions: Boil your rice until it is mushy - this is at least 10 minutes of active boiling.
While that happens use a wide bottomed steel pot (NOT NON STICK) to bring your milk to a simmer.
Lightly bruise the cardamom pods and Stir in them to the milk, keep the temperature low,.
Once the rice is mushy, drain most of the water and and then mash it up thoroughly on a plate with a fork.
Stir in to the milk mixture along with the sugar. Mix well.
Cook on low - a gentle simmer for an hour. Stir with a rubber spatula every and and then to check.
The kheer will cook down quite a bit in this time, Stir in 1/4 cup of the cream you are using and taste - Stir in more sugar or cream if desired.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Stir in milk and rice to a large pot. Bring to boil, about 3 minutes, and let it simmer on low heat for 40 minutes while stirring often.
Stir in sugar and keep stirring, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the remaining ingredients and let it simmer while stirring for another 8 – 10 minutes.
Put in serving bowl and top with slivered almonds for garnish.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Chawal ki Kheer - Pakistani Rice Pudding

variants.name: Leftover Rice Kheer
instructions: Prepare the grain, fruit or milk solids and measure the milk, sugar and aromatics.
Warm the ghee or milk as appropriate; toast the grain or simmer the dairy gently so it does not catch.
Add the sugar only after the main ingredient is tender, then cook until the mixture reaches the intended thick consistency.
Stir in the cardamom, saffron or floral water, garnish with nuts if used, and serve at the stated temperature.

variants.name: Quick & Extra-Creamy Instant Pot Kheer
instructions: Grind the rice before you soak it to a coarse grind. Pour over the water and set aside for 20 minutes (or longer).
Put your Instant Pot on sauté and Stir in in your three milks, cardamom seeds, saffron (if using), sugar and salt.
As soon as your sugar dissolves Stir in in your rice + soaking water, give it a quick mix, making sure nothing is stuck to the bottom.
Put your IP on LOW pressure for 18 minutes.
Natural release for 10-15 minutes (to manage the intense steam release), and and then release the remaining steam by turning the valve.
Whisk through to break any clumps, the kheer will thicken as it cools. Transfer to a bowl and garnish as you please.

variants.name: Strawberry Kheer (+ My First Published Article)

ingredients.text: 1/2 lb strawberries, (hulled and chopped into 1/2-inch pieces)

instructions: In a small saucepan, heat 11⁄2 cups of the milk over medium-low heat; do not bring to a boil, but keep warm while you prepare the kheer. In a large heavy-bottomed pan, Stir in the remaining 3 cups of milk, the rice, crushed cardamom seeds, sugar and slivered.

Every 7 to 10 minutes, remove the lid and stir gently, from the bottom up, to ensure that the rice is not sticking to the base of the pan. After about 40 minutes, the milk should be thickened but not entirely absorbed.

If it seems undercooked, Stir in some of the reserved warm milk, replace the lid and continue to cook for 7 to 10 minutes. Transfer the kheer to a container and allow it to come to room temperature before covering and refrigerating at least 5 hours, but preferably.
In a medium saucepan over medium heat, Stir in the rhubarb, cinnamon stick, water and sugar. Stir well.
Allow the mixture to bubble away until the rhubarb looks soft and has melted down into a sauce, about 20 minutes. Stir in the strawberries.
Continue to cook until the strawberries have softened and melted into the sauce, about 10 to 15 minutes.
Turn off the heat, discard the cinnamon stick, and allow the coulis to come to room temperature.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Strawberry Kheer (+ My First Published Article)

variants.name: Subdana Kheer: Pakistani Tapioca Pearl Pudding

ingredients.item: salted butter ((at room temperature) for brushing on apricots)
ingredients.text: salted butter ((at room temperature) for brushing on apricots)

instructions: Soak tapioca pearls in cold water for 2 hours till they swell. In a medium saucepan, heat milk on medium heat, till warm.
Stir in tapioca pearls, sugar and cardamom pods and stir. The pudding wil begin to thicken after around 15 minutes. Continue to stir for a full 35 minutes.
When the pudding looks thick like a rice pudding, take off the heat and allow to cool. Optional: Line your ramekins / glasses with a thin layer of slivered pistachios.
When cool, transfer pudding into ramekins / glasses and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, and ideally, overnight. Turn your broiler / grill on.
Brush apricot halves with butter and sprinkle with brown sugar. Put apricots under broiler for 2-3 minutes till slightly golden on top.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Subdana Kheer: Pakistani Tapioca Pearl Pudding

variants.name: Badam Kheer (Almond Milk Pudding)
instructions: The night before, soak almonds in enough water to cover. Reserve a handful of peeled almonds for garnish, and then proceed with the rest.
Stir in the peeled almonds to a blender with 1/2 cup of the milk. Blend on high for 2-3 minutes until completely smooth with no graininess.
Pour the remaining milk into a heavy-bottomed degchi (pot) and bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring occasionally. Once boiling, reduce to a simmer.

Pour the almond-milk paste into the simmering milk while stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Stir in the cardamom powder. Continue to cook on medium-low, stirring every few minutes, for 25-30 minutes until the mixture thickens.
Stir in sugar and stir until dissolved. Pour in the saffron milk — watch the beautiful golden swirls appear. Cook for another 5-8 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in rose water and kewra essence. Pour into serving bowls.

variants.name: Doodh Chawal Kheer — Pakistani Rice Pudding
instructions: Rinse 4 tbsp of chawal (rice) in cold water two or three times until the water runs mostly clear. Soak in fresh cold water for 30 minutes.
Pour 1.5 litres of full-fat doodh (milk) into a heavy bhari degh or pateela (saucepan). Heat on medium-high, stirring frequently.
Once the milk is boiling, Stir in the drained soaked rice. Stir well. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook at a steady simmer, stirring gently every 5 minutes.
This typically takes 45-60 minutes.

Stir in cheeni (sugar) and fresh-ground elaichi (cardamom) powder. Cook for another 5-8 minutes, stirring constantly — the sugar makes the milk slightly thinner momentarily. Stir in the saffron-soaked milk and any crumbled khoya (dried milk solids).
Pour kheer into a large serving bartan (bowl) or individual katoris (small bowls). Serve warm immediately, or cool to room temperature and refrigerate for 2-3 hours.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Doodh Chawal Kheer — Pakistani Rice Pudding

variants.name: Sewaiyan Kheer (Vermicelli Pudding) for Eid
instructions: Warm ghee in a heavy-bottomed karahi (wok) or pot over medium heat. Stir in the sewaiyan and stir continuously with a wooden spoon. Roast for 4-5 minutes until they turn a deep golden colour and smell nutty.

Pour the full-fat milk into the karahi carefully — it will sizzle. Stir in the lightly crushed cardamom pods. Stir everything together and bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring frequently so the milk doesn't catch on the bottom.
Once boiling, reduce heat to medium-low. Cook uncovered for 20-25 minutes, stirring every 3-4 minutes.
Stir in sugar and stir until fully dissolved. Stir in the saffron milk and raisins if using. Cook for another 5 minutes.
Turn off the heat. Stir in rose water and stir gently. The kheer will thicken more as it cools — if it looks too thick, stir in a splash of warm milk before serving.
Pour into a large serving bowl or individual bowls. Serve warm for a cosy Eid morning, or chill for 2-3 hours for a cold, creamy version.

variants.name: Chawal Ki Kheer — Sindhi Slow-Cooked Rice Pudding
instructions: Rinse basmati rice under cold water until clear. Soak in fresh water for 30 minutes minimum.
Pour the full-fat milk into a wide, heavy-bottomed degchi (pot). Stir in the bruised cardamom pods. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring occasionally.
Drain the soaked rice and Stir in it to the simmering milk. Stir well. Cook on low heat, uncovered, for 60-75 minutes.

After 50 minutes, the milk will have reduced significantly and the rice will be very soft and starting to break down. The kheer should coat the back of a spoon thickly. If it's too thick, Stir in a cup of warm milk and stir through.
Stir in sugar and saffron milk, stirring until fully dissolved. Cook for another 5 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in rose water and kewra water if using.
Pour into a serving bowl or individual clay pots (matke) for a traditional Sindhi presentation.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Chawal Ki Kheer — Sindhi Slow-Cooked Rice Pudding

dish_families.name: Kid Friendly Instant Pot Pulled Beef for EVERYTHING

variants.name: Kid Friendly Instant Pot Pulled Beef for EVERYTHING
variants.dish_family: Kid Friendly Instant Pot Pulled Beef for EVERYTHING
instructions: Stir in all the ingredients to the IP with 2 cups water, give it a good stir and put it on Manual (high pressure) for 20 minutes.
Saute and stir to dry up the liquid a little.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Kid Friendly Instant Pot Pulled Beef for EVERYTHING

variants.name: Koki with Onion and Chilli

ingredients.text: 0.75 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Mix atta, all chopped vegetables and herbs, all spices, and oil. Stir in water gradually — the extra onion releases moisture so Stir in less water than usual.
After resting, check the dough — if it feels too soft due to onion moisture, Stir in a tablespoon of atta to firm it up.
Divide into large portions.
Cook on a medium-low tawa for 5-6 minutes per side — the extra onion means this takes slightly longer than plain koki.
Apply ghee after flipping.

variants.name: Sindhi Koki Crispy

ingredients.text: 0.5 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: In a large bowl, mix atta, chopped piyaz, hara dhania, hari mirch, zeera, ajwain, laal mirch powder, and salt. Stir in oil and rub in. Stir in water gradually to form a medium-firm dough — slightly firmer than chapati dough.
Cover and rest the dough for 15 minutes.
Divide into large balls (larger than paratha — koki is thick).
Warm tawa on medium-low heat. Cook on very low heat for 4-5 minutes until the bottom looks set and is just beginning to colour.
Stir in a small amount of ghee around edges. Cook the second side 4-5 minutes.
Once both sides are golden-brown and cooked through (press the centre — it should feel firm), remove from tawa.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: In a large kunda (mixing bowl) or any wide bartan (vessel), Mix the atta, finely chopped pyaz, hari mirch, hara dhaniya, ajwain, salt, lal mirch, and 1 tbsp of ghee. Mix by hand to mix everything together, working the ghee into the flour — you're looking for a.
Knead the dough on a clean surface for 3-4 minutes until it is firm but not stiff.

Divide the dough into 3-4 equal balls — each about the size of a large lemon. Using a rolling pin, roll it into a circle about 6-7 inches in diameter and about 5-6mm thick (roughly 1⁄4 inch). This is significantly thicker than a roti or paratha — resist.
Warm a tawa (flat cast-iron or heavy pan) over medium-high heat until very hot. Stir in 1 tbsp of ghee and let it heat. Cook for 2-3 minutes.
Stir in another 1⁄2 tbsp of ghee, and then flip the koki.

variants.name: Chicken Korma Simplified
instructions: Crush your prefried onions by hand and mix into your yoghurt and set aside.
Warm 1/4 cup oil on medium hight heat and Stir in your dry whole spices - both cardamoms, cloves, black pepper, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf.
Once the spices have perfumed the oil and then Stir in in the ginger and garlic and give it a quick stir.
Stir in in your chicken pieces, turning them periodically until they have all changed colour.
Saute for about a minute and and then Stir in in your yoghurt and onion mix, stirring well to Mix.
Stir in in half a cup of water and bring it to a simmer, cook on low for 25 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through.
Uncover your pan and raise the heat to medium until you see the oil separate from the base for that rich korma taste.
Adjust consistency to your liking and Stir in kewra, garam masala powder, and pepper and adjust seasoning.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Warm ghee in a wide, heavy pot. Stir in sliced pyaaz and Cook on medium-high heat for 12-14 minutes until golden brown and starting to crisp at the edges. Remove half and set aside for garnish.
Stir in sabut garam masala to the pot with the remaining fried onions. Stir in adrak-lehsan paste and Cook 2 minutes. Stir in dhania powder, zeera powder, and lal mirch.
Stir in chicken pieces and salt. Turn heat to high and bhuno for 7-8 minutes until chicken has changed colour and is well-coated in masala.

Stir in YOGURT — THE CRUCIAL STEP: Reduce heat to medium-low. Stir in yogurt 2 tablespoons at a time, stirring constantly after each addition. Never Stir in cold yogurt straight from the fridge — room temperature is essential.
Once yogurt is incorporated, Stir in 1/2 cup warm water. Cover and cook on low-medium heat for 25-30 minutes until chicken is cooked through and tender. Stir gently every 10 minutes.
If using cashew/almond paste, stir it in along with kesar and crushed green cardamom. Cook uncovered for 8-10 minutes, stirring gently, until gravy is thick and coating the chicken pieces.
Transfer to a serving dish.

variants.name: Mutton Korma Recipe

ingredients.preparation: bone in, cut into curry pieces
ingredients.text: 1.1 lb mutton (bone in, cut into curry pieces)

ingredients.item: Kewra water (1tsp or more as per preference (optional))
ingredients.text: Kewra water (1tsp or more as per preference (optional))

instructions: Prepare all ingredients before heating the pan.
Warm the cooking fat and cook onion, sliced finely, cloved garlic, minced, minced ginger until softened and aromatic.
Stir in cloved garlic, minced, black cardamoms, green cardamoms, 7 cloves, bay leaf, black peppercorns, then add the mutton and coat it thoroughly in the masala.
Add the listed liquid ingredients as needed, cover and simmer until the main ingredient is fully cooked.
Reduce the sauce to the intended consistency, adjust the seasoning and finish with minced ginger, coriander powder.

variants.name: Safed Korma Mughal

ingredients.text: 1.5 tsp kali mirch (white or black pepper)

instructions: GOLDEN ONIONS — STOP BEFORE BROWN: Heat ghee in a wide, pale-coloured pot (so you can monitor colour accurately). Stir in sliced pyaaz and Cook on medium heat only — no high heat. Cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring constantly, until soft and just turning golden.
Transfer golden onions to a blender. Stir in 2 tablespoons water and blend to a completely smooth, creamy paste.
In the same pot with remaining ghee, Stir in cloves, cinnamon, and crushed green cardamom seeds. Stir in the blended onion paste. Cook gently for 5 minutes.
Stir in chicken pieces and kali mirch. Bhuno gently on medium heat — no high heat that causes browning — for 6-7 minutes.
This is the most delicate moment. Reduce heat to very low. Stir in yogurt 1 tablespoon at a time, stirring smoothly after each addition.
Once yogurt is in, Stir in 1/3 cup water, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 25-30 minutes. The chicken should cook through gently in the creamy yogurt environment.
Stir in cashew paste. Cook uncovered 8 minutes until gravy thickens. Stir in cream, stir gently, cook 3 minutes.

variants.name: Shahi Chicken Korma
instructions: Warm ghee in a deep degh (heavy-bottomed pot) over medium-high heat. Stir in sliced onions and Cook, stirring occasionally, for 20–25 minutes until they turn deep golden-brown — the colour of caramel, not gold.

Return the pot with the reserved ghee to medium heat. Stir in all the kharay masalay (whole spices). Cook for 60 seconds, stirring, until the elaichi (cardamom) puffs slightly and the laung (cloves) begin to uncurl.

Stir in the adrak-lehsan (ginger-garlic) paste to the spiced ghee. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the raw smell disappears and it turns light golden. Stir in the chicken pieces and salt.
Stir in this to the chicken along with the ground coriander and cumin. Stir everything together over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until the masala coats the chicken.
Reduce heat to low. Whisk the dahi (yoghurt) until completely smooth — no lumps. Stir in it to the pot one spoonful at a time, stirring continuously.

Stir in the badam (almond) paste — it will immediately thicken the sauce. Stir in 1/2 cup warm water, stir well. Cover the pot and cook on low heat for 20–25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has deepened to a beautiful golden colour.
Remove from heat. Stir in the gulab jal (rose water) and kewra water. Stir gently.

variants.name: Sindhi Mutton Korma

ingredients.text: 1.5 tsp kali mirch powder (black pepper powder)

instructions: Warm oil in a heavy pot. Cook sliced pyaaz on medium-high until very dark — darker than Punjab-style korma onions. Almost reddish-brown.

To remaining fried onions, Stir in sabut garam masala and sizzle. Stir in adrak-lehsan paste and bhuno 3 minutes. Stir in dhania powder, kali mirch, lal mirch, haldi — bhuno 5 minutes with a splash of water.
Stir in chopped tamatar to the masala and cook down completely — 10 minutes until they've dissolved into the oil.
Stir in gosht, salt, bhuno on high for 8 minutes until well-coated and coloured.
Reduce heat to low-medium. Stir in whisked yogurt slowly, 2 tablespoons at a time, stirring. Once incorporated, cook on medium 10 minutes.
Stir in 3/4 cup water, cover, cook on low for 60-70 minutes until mutton is very tender.
Uncover last 10 minutes to reduce gravy to coating consistency. Garnish with reserved birista and very generous hara dhania.

variants.name: Beef Korma Dawat
instructions: Warm ghee in a large, wide deg. Cook all sliced pyaaz on medium-high for 20-25 minutes, stirring constantly, until very deeply golden-brown. Do not drain — use the same ghee for everything.
Put half the fried onions into a blender with a splash of water and blend to a smooth paste. The other half is reserved for garnish.
In the same ghee, Stir in sabut garam masala, sizzle 1 minute. Stir in onion paste and Cook 5 minutes. Stir in adrak-lehsan paste, dhania powder, lal mirch powder.
Stir in beef pieces, turn heat to high. Bhuno aggressively for 10-12 minutes until well-coloured. Season with salt.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in whisked yogurt 3 tablespoons at a time, stirring constantly between additions. Take your time — 10-12 minutes total to Stir in all the yogurt.
Stir in 1 cup warm water. Cover tightly and cook on medium-low heat for 60-75 minutes until beef is very tender. Check and stir every 20 minutes.
Stir in cashew paste and saffron-milk. Cook uncovered 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until gravy is thick and glossy. Stir in kewra water and gulab jal.

variants.name: Kulcha
instructions: Mix lukewarm water, sugar, and yeast in a small bowl. Leave 8–10 minutes until frothy.
In a large paraat, Mix flour and salt. Stir in the yeast mixture, dahi, milk, and oil. Mix to form a soft dough — it should be softer and richer-feeling than naan dough.
Oil a bowl, Stir in the dough, cover with a damp cloth, and leave in a warm spot for 1–1.5 hours until doubled.

While the dough rises, Mix the mashed potatoes, chopped onion, fresh coriander, green chillies, carom seeds, salt, and red chilli powder in a bowl. Mix well with your hands until it comes together into a coherent mixture.
Warm for 30 minutes minimum. For a stovetop version, heat a heavy tawa (griddle pan) over high heat until a drop of water dances and evaporates in 2 seconds.

Punch down the dough and divide into 6 balls. On a floured chakla, roll one ball into a 15cm disc. gently roll the stuffed ball out into a thick oval or round about 18–20cm across and about 1–1.5cm thick.

Transfer to the hot baking tray and bake on the top rack for 5–7 minutes until the top is golden and blistered, and the underside is flat and cooked through. For the stovetop method: lay the kulcha on the hot tawa, cover with a lid, cook 3–4 minutes.
Stack them, butter-side up, and cover with a clean cloth to keep warm while you cook the rest.

variants.name: Malai Kulfi Recipe with Magic Crunch

ingredients.text: 1 1/4 cup whipping cream or heavy cream

instructions: Mix all the Kulfi ingredients in a heavy bottomed pot, mix well.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 45 minutes (or an hour, depends on the pot). Stir every few minutes to make sure it isn't burning/sticking. If it is turn the heat down.
Carefully cover with plastic wrap and freeze for 6 hours or till firm.
Put the pan on medium high heat and don't stir the sugar.
When the caramel reaches a deep amber quickly mix in the chopped nuts and spread on the baking sheet to harden.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Malai Kulfi Recipe with Magic Crunch

variants.name: Kulfi
instructions: REDUCE THE MILK — THE HEART OF KULFI: Pour all 1.5 litres of full-fat milk into a wide, heavy-bottomed degh (heavy-bottomed pot) or karahi (wok). Bring the milk to a boil on medium-high heat, stirring continuously with a chamcha to prevent it from boiling over.

During the reduction, stir every 4-5 minutes and scrape the malai (cream layer) that forms on the sides and bottom back into the milk. After about 45 minutes, stir more frequently (every 2-3 minutes) as the risk of scorching increases as the liquid reduces.

After 60-75 minutes, check whether the milk has reduced to approximately one-third of its original volume (1.5 litres should become roughly 500ml). Dip a spoon in: the milk should coat the spoon and flow slowly off it rather than running off like water.

Remove from heat briefly. If using cornflour, mix 1 tablespoon cornflour with 2 tablespoons cold milk until smooth, and then stir this into the hot reduced milk. Return to low heat and stir for 2-3 minutes — this helps bind the mixture and reduce ice crystal formation when.
Stir in the coarsely chopped pista and badam. Let the mixture cool completely to room temperature — about 30-45 minutes.

Once completely cooled, pour the kulfi mixture into kulfi moulds (conical metal or plastic kulfi moulds available at any kitchen shop or online). If using cups, cover tightly with plastic wrap, pressing it directly onto the surface of the liquid to prevent ice crystals.
Put the moulds in the freezer and freeze for a minimum of 6 hours. Overnight is ideal — 8 hours gives a firmer, better-set kulfi.
Garnish with sliced pista on top.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Blend until smooth .
Transfer to your container of choice and freeze till firm.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Put pan on medium heat on the stove. Pour in half-and-half. Separately mix cardamom powder with a tablespoon of the half and half and pour into pot.
Stir in almonds, pistachios and crushed cardamom seeds. As the temperature of the half-and-half rises, start to slowly Stir in condensed milk.
Once the mixture starts to steam and bubble, turn the heat to low. You will continue to stir for one hour every five minutes till the mixture thickens and reduces by half.
Allow to cool for 15-20 minutes. Pour slowly into popsicle moulds or shotglasses.
At the 30 minute mark when the kulfi has started to form, Put popsicle sticks in each mould/glass. Freeze overnight or for at least 8 hours.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Easy Pista Kulfi Recipe – No Cook, 6 Ingredients

alternate_names: Easy Pista Kulfi Recipe – No Cook, 6 Ingredients

variants.name: Kulfi Falooda — Classic Street Style
instructions: Pour 1.5 litres of milk into a wide karahi. Bring to a boil, and then reduce to medium heat. Cook, stirring frequently and collecting cream skins to the sides (like rabri-making), for 45-50 minutes until reduced to roughly 600ml.
Remove from heat. Stir in fresh cream, chopped almonds and most of the pistachios. Once cool, refrigerate for 30 minutes until cold.
Pour the cooled kulfi mixture into kulfi molds (conical metal or plastic molds) or into an ice cube tray covered with plastic wrap, or into small steel cups.
Freeze for a minimum of 6-8 hours — overnight is better.
Boil falooda sev for 2-3 minutes, rinse cold and refrigerate. Soak basil seeds in cold water for 30 minutes.
In a shallow plate or deep bowl, pour 50ml cold milk. Stir in a nest of falooda sev, and then a tablespoon of swollen tukmaria seeds.

variants.name: Mango Kulfi — Aam Wali Kulfi
instructions: Mix mango pulp, condensed milk, cream, milk, cardamom powder and saffron (if using) in a blender. Blend on high for 2 minutes until completely smooth and no fibre remains.
Pour the blended mixture into a bowl. Fold in chopped almonds and most of the pistachios, reserving a few for garnish. Stir gently to distribute.
Pour into kulfi molds, ice lolly molds, or small steel cups. If using cups, cover with foil and press a popsicle stick through the foil centre.
Put in the freezer for at least 6 hours — overnight is best.

variants.name: Kurkuri Bhindi - 3-Ingredient Crunchy Okra
instructions: - Heat oil in a wide bottomed pan or wok, Aim for a generous lug for stir frying.
- Stir Cook the okra on high heat moving periodically to make sure it cooks evenly and doesn't burn.
- Remove with a slotted spoon and put on paper towels to drain the extra grease.
- Season with Chaat Masala, toss to mix and serve immediately.

variants.name: Kurkuri Bhindi (Crispy Okra)

ingredients.text: 3/4 tsp coriander powder or to taste

instructions: Warm a non-stick wok, saucepan or skillet. Stir in oil until it’s 2-3 inches deep. Let it heat for a few seconds.
Bring heat to medium-low and Cook the okra in batches. Cook until it browns slightly and becomes a deeper forest green.
Drain on a paper towel. Season with salt and coriander powder, and gently mix well.

variants.name: Lachha Paratha

ingredients.preparation: whole wheat flour or all-purpose flour
ingredients.text: 2 cups atta ya maida (whole wheat flour or all-purpose flour)
5 tbsp ghee ya makhan (ghee or butter)

instructions: In a large paraat, Mix your flour of choice and salt. Stir in the oil and rub it in with your fingers until the flour looks like wet sand — this is called 'short-shortening' the flour and gives a slightly tender result. Stir in the lukewarm water gradually.
Shape the dough into a ball, cover with a damp cloth or bowl, and rest for 20–30 minutes at room temperature.

On a lightly floured chakla, roll one dough ball into as thin a circle as possible — ideally 2–3mm thick, roughly the size of a medium-large plate (28–30cm). The thinner you roll it, the more layers you will get in your final paratha.
Take the accordion-folded strip and coil it into a tight snail shell shape — starting from one end and winding the strip around itself.

Press the coiled disc flat with your palm — firmly but gently. and then use the belan to roll it out again into a round paratha about 18–20cm across and 5–6mm thick. be able to see the spiral of layers at the edges of the paratha as you.

Warm a tawa (flat griddle pan) or heavy frying pan over medium-high heat until a few drops of water flicked onto it evaporate in under 2 seconds — that is your cue that it is ready. Cook for about 2 minutes on the first side — you will.
