After flipping, Stir in about half a teaspoon of ghee to the tawa around the edges of the paratha and let it sizzle underneath. Cook 1–2 more minutes. Flip once more, Stir in another tiny amount of ghee to the other side.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Mix the atta and salt in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a dough attachment.
Slowly Stir in in 1 cup of water, letting it mix with the dough before adding more. If the dough seems dry, Stir in the additional 2 tbsp of water.
Continue to knead on medium speed until a smooth, dry, and flexible ball of dough forms.
(It is nice, but not necessary, to let the dough rest for 10-15 minutes to allow the gluten to develop.
Once you are ready to cook the parathas, Put spreadable butter, atta for dusting, and a rolling pin near your workstation.
Meanwhile, heat a tawa, heavy-bottomed (preferably cast iron) or flat griddle over medium heat.
While the tawa is heating, roll the paratha out to 5-6 inches in diameter and spread about 2 teaspoon of butter onto the flattened dough.

Starting from the top, roll down swiss-roll style until a long log is formed. Roll this log, especially from the middle, to make it thinner and as even as possible until it’s about 18 inches long. and then roll tightly into itself from one edge to another.

As the bottom of the paratha begins to cook, Stir in 1-2 tsp of butter to the top. Once the bottom is partly cooked (this will take about 10-15 seconds), use a spatula to flip over and Stir in butter on the other side. Cook on both sides.

variants.name: Lahori Chargha

ingredients.text: 1.5 tsp tatri (citric acid / lemon salt crystals)
1.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)
1 tbsp nimbu ka ras (fresh lemon juice)

instructions: Using a sharp knife, make deep cuts all over the chicken — every 1 inch, cut down to the bone.

In a large bowl, Mix the tatri (citric acid), salt, red chilli powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric, garam masala, ginger-garlic paste, yoghurt, and lemon juice. Mix everything together into a thick paste.

Rub the marinade all over the chicken — into every cut, under the loosened breast skin, inside the cavity, everywhere. Put the chicken in a large zip-lock bag or cover with cling film and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight (8-12 hours).
Pour 250ml water into the bottom of the steamer. Bring the water to a boil. Cover tightly with a lid, wrapping it in a kitchen towel if needed to trap all the steam.

After 35-40 minutes of steaming, check doneness. If there's any pink, steam for another 10 minutes. Let the steamed chicken rest on a rack for 10-15 minutes and pat the surface as dry as possible with kitchen paper.

Warm 1 litre of oil in a large, deep degh or wok to 180-190°C (355-375°F). Cook for 8-10 minutes, spooning hot oil over the top of the chicken continuously using a large chamcha. The chicken should turn deep mahogany-brown, almost the colour of dark chocolate.

Remove the chargha from the oil using a large slotted spoon or spider strainer and Put it on a wire rack or paper towels to drain for 2-3 minutes. The skin should be deep brown and very, very crispy — it should make a crackling sound when you.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Warm a cup full of water and mix the brown sugar and salt into it. Stir in enough water to cover the turkey. Cover and set aside for 12-24 hours. Take the brined turkey out of the fridge, drain the brine and pat the Turkey dry.
Put the turkey in a dish – you can use the roaster you will roast it in as well. Whisk the marinade ingredients except the butter in a bowl.
Stir in your softened butter. Shmear the rest over the back, legs, and wings of the turkey.

The day you are going to roast the turkey pull it out of the fridge a few hours before roasting to bring it to room temperature. Roast the Turkey till the top is a gorgeous brown colour, some of the masala will look charred and that is delicious. This will take about 30 minutes.

Drop the temperature to 350 F, tent the turkey with foil and roast until a meat thermometer inserted in the thigh reads 170 degrees F, this took me another 1 hour and 50 minutes over and above the initial bake time. Let the turkey meat rest for at least 20 minutes before carving.
Pour into a bowl and whisk in an additional cup of yogurt.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Desi Roast Turkey with Lahori Chargha Masala and Green Chutney

alternate_names: Desi Roast Turkey with Lahori Chargha Masala and Green Chutney

variants.name: Landhi

ingredients.item: mutton (goat or lamb), bone-in large pieces
ingredients.text: 1 kg mutton (goat or lamb), bone-in large pieces

ingredients.item: enough to submerge the meat pani (water) for soaking
ingredients.text: enough to submerge the meat pani (water) for soaking

instructions: Score the mutton pieces deeply with a sharp knife — cuts about 2cm deep all over. Rub the namak (salt) very generously over every surface and into every cut. Slide into your oven at 80°C (175°F).
After 3 hours, remove the meat from the oven.
Put the dried meat pieces in a large bowl and cover completely with cold pani (water). Cover the bowl and Put in the refrigerator overnight (at least 8 hours, ideally 10-12 hours).
Remove the meat from the soaking water and rinse each piece under cold running water. If it tastes extremely salty, soak for another 2 hours in fresh water and drain again.

Stir in 6 cups of fresh pani (water). Stir in all the whole spices: badi elaichi (black cardamom), laung (cloves), kali mirch (black peppercorns), darchini (cinnamon), tez patta (bay leaves), and zeera (cumin seeds). Do NOT Stir in salt yet — the meat still has salt inside it.
Put the pot over high heat and bring to a rolling boil. As the water heats up, a grey-brown foam will form on the surface — this is protein and impurities coming out of the meat.

Once the foam has been skimmed, reduce the heat to low. The liquid should be at a gentle simmer — small lazy bubbles rising, not a vigorous boil. Cover the pot partially (leave a small gap for steam to escape) and cook for 2 to 2.5 hours.
After 2 hours, test the meat by pressing a thick piece with a spoon. If the meat is still tough, continue cooking for another 30 minutes and test again.

variants.name: Landhi — Balochi Wind-Dried Mutton

ingredients.text: 2 kg Mutton legs or shoulder (bone-in, large cuts)
1 tbsp Laal mirch powder (red chili powder)

instructions: PREPARE THE CURE (for making landhi): Mix coarse salt, chili powder, and cumin.
Put on a rack over a tray and refrigerate uncovered for 24-48 hours.
Outdoors in winter (5-15°C, low humidity) is ideal.
Cut or hack the dried landhi into pieces. Soak in cold water for 6-12 hours, changing water once, to rehydrate and reduce the saltiness slightly.
In a pot, Cook onions in oil until golden. Stir in garlic and tomatoes, cook until masala forms. Stir in soaked landhi pieces (do not Stir in extra salt — landhi is already salty).
Cover and simmer 60-90 minutes until the landhi is tender and the curry is thick.
Stir in whole green chilies in the last 10 minutes.

variants.name: Landhi Karachi Style — Urban Revival

ingredients.text: 1 tsp Laal mirch powder (red chili powder)

instructions: Soak landhi in cold water for 4-6 hours, changing water once. Drain and pat dry before using.
Warm oil, Cook onions until deep golden. Stir in ginger-garlic paste, Cook 2 minutes. Stir in all dry spices (chili, coriander, cumin, turmeric).
Stir in tomatoes and cook until oil separates, 10-12 minutes.
Stir in soaked dried mutton pieces. Stir to coat in masala. Do not Stir in salt yet — taste at the end.
Stir in 2.5 cups water. Cover and simmer on low heat 60-75 minutes until the dried meat is tender and rehydrated, and the gravy is thick.
Stir in salt only if needed.
Stir in green chilies and fresh coriander. Simmer 5 more minutes uncovered to finish.

variants.name: Sweet Lassi Recipe
instructions: Stir in ice cubes and yogurt to a blender, and blend on low speed for 20 – 30 seconds until frothy.
Stir in water and sugar to the yogurt and ice cube mixture and blend on low speed until well-mixed.

variants.name: Mango Lassi — Summer Special
instructions: Taste a piece — if it's very sweet, reduce the added sugar. If it's slightly tart, Stir in the full sugar amount.
Stir in mango, yoghurt, milk, sugar, cardamom and ice cubes to the blender. Blend on high for 90 seconds until completely smooth, thick and frothy.
Pour a small amount and taste. Stir in more sugar if needed, or a splash of milk to thin if too thick to pour easily.
Pour into tall glasses. Garnish with a few saffron strands and a small sprig of mint.
Sprinkle a very light dusting of cardamom powder on the foam and Put a thin slice of fresh mango on the rim of the glass for a stunning presentation at dinner parties.

variants.name: Meethi Lassi — Sweet Punjabi Yoghurt Drink
instructions: For the best meethi lassi, your dahi (yoghurt) and bartan (bowl) should be cold before you start. Put the yoghurt in the freezer for 15 minutes if it's not fridge-cold.

Stir in dahi (yoghurt), cold pani (water) or ice cubes, cheeni (sugar), and freshly ground elaichi (cardamom) to a blender. Blend on high speed for 60-90 seconds until completely smooth, frothy, and slightly aerated.
If using gulab jal (rose water), stir it in by hand — do not blend it. A gentle stir keeps the aroma concentrated.
Pour the lassi into tall, chilled glasses — fill to about 2cm from the top.

Sprinkle crushed pista (pistachios) over the malai. If feeling extravagant, Stir in a tiny pinch of saffron strands. Serve immediately with a long spoon or a straw — the traditional way is to stir the malai into the lassi yourself at the table, getting a bit of cream.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Meethi Lassi — Sweet Punjabi Yoghurt Drink

variants.name: Namkeen Lassi — Lahori Salted Buttermilk
instructions: In a small dry tawa or frying pan, toast cumin seeds over medium heat for 1-2 minutes until they darken slightly and smell fragrant. This step takes 3 minutes but makes an enormous difference in flavour.
Stir in yoghurt, cold water, salt, kala namak, roasted cumin powder and fresh mint leaves to a blender. Blend on high speed for 2 full minutes.
Pour a small amount and taste. If too thick, Stir in a splash of water and blend briefly.
Pour the frothy lassi over the ice. Garnish with a pinch of roasted cumin and a mint leaf on the foam.

variants.name: Lobia Chawal (Red Beans with Rice)

ingredients.text: 1 cup red beans (rinsed and soaked overnight)
Salt to taste (I put in about 2 tbsp)

instructions: Bring a large pot of water, about 5 quarts, to a boil.
Stir in red beans, cover pot with lid, and let it simmer for roughly 2 hours or till beans are soft.
While beans are cooking, wash basmati rice well, and let them soak in water.
About an hour in, Stir in salt and cumin seeds to the beans. If you are running low, Stir in hot water as needed.
Once the beans are cooked through, check for salt, and Stir in more if needed. Again, check if you have enough water leftover to boil the rice. If you don't, Stir in hot water .
Remove from heat, and let it cool for about 20 minutes.
After it has cooled down, bring the water back to boil, and Stir in rice.
Cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid, and let rice and beans simmer on medium heat till the rice has absorbed the water, about 8-10 minutes.
Dial heat to the lowest point, and let rice steam undisturbed for 12 minutes. Remove from heat.

variants.name: Lobia Masala Recipe

ingredients.text: 1 small yellow or red onion (thinly sliced in half rings)

instructions: Warm oil in saucepan. Stir in chopped onion and Cook on medium-low heat until evenly brown, about 10 minutes.
Stir in crushed ginger and garlic and Cook for roughly one minute or until fragrant.
Stir in coriander powder and Cook for another minute until fragrant.
Increase heat to high, and Stir in chopped tomatoes, salt and red chili flakes. Cook until soft, about 7 - 10 minutes.
Stir in white beans and stir well. Bring down heat to medium, and let the beans simmer in the masala for another 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and Put in serving bowl. Top with lemon juice and diced cilantro for garnish.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Lobia Masala | Black Eyed Peas Curry
source_attributions.author: Fatima Cooks

alternate_names: Lobia Masala | Black Eyed Peas Curry

variants.name: Lotus Biscoff Ice Cream Cake
instructions: Whip the cream cheese until smooth and and then gradually beat in the cream, whipping until stiff peaks form.
Pour in the condensed milk and the vanilla extract and beat until combined.
Dollop in 200g (half of the 400g jar of biscoff) into the mix - dollops mix in faster and mix on low for 45 seconds or until most of it blends in.
Roughly break 8-10 biscuits and Stir in them in.
Pour your base into the pan (or box if you're eating it like ice cream!) and freeze for 4-6 hours.
Invert the ice cream cake onto your dish, drizzle over the biscoff and Stir in crushed biscuits.

variants.name: Makki Ki Roti

ingredients.text: 2 cups makki ka atta (stone-ground cornmeal / coarse corn flour)
3 tablespoons ghee ya makhan (ghee or white butter)

instructions: We shape it differently, and that's part of its charm.
In a large bowl, Mix the makki ka atta and salt. Stir in warm water a little at a time, mixing as you go. Aim for dough that holds its shape when pressed but doesn't crumble.

Put your tawa (flat griddle pan) on the stove over medium-low heat. Let it heat up while you shape the rotis. This bread cooks on lower heat than chapati — lower and slower gives it time to cook through without burning the outside.
SHAPE THE ROTI — METHOD 1 (WET HANDS): Divide the dough into 4–6 equal balls.
SHAPE THE ROTI — METHOD 2 (PLASTIC WRAP): Tear two pieces of cling film.
Carefully slide the shaped roti onto the warm tawa.
Cook on medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes.
Cook the second side for another 3–4 minutes until golden.
Transfer to a plate and apply another generous piece of white butter or a spoon of ghee on top.

variants.name: Malai Boti
instructions: Cut your chicken breast into even 3/4-1 inch pieces - I got roughly 22 pieces from my 2 medium sized chicken breasts.
Mix the marinade ingredients with the chicken cubes and set aside to rest for a minimum of four hours and up to two days.
If using wooden skewers soak them in water for 30-minutes.
Air Fryer: 6 minutes per side at 390F.
Oven: Cover the exposed ends of wooden skewers with foil (to be safe) and bake on a greased tray lined with foil for 18-20 minutes at 375F, flipping halfway.
Grill: 6-8 minutes per side, but please bear in mind timings vary with grilling so keep a close eye on it!

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Cut into even 2-inch cubes. Evenly sized pieces are important on the grill: smaller pieces overcook before larger ones are done.

In a bartan (bowl), Mix malai (cream), cream cheese, dahi (yoghurt), adrak lahsun paste, kali mirch (black pepper), elaichi powder, and nimboo juice (lemon juice). Whisk everything together until smooth with no lumps — the cream cheese needs to be fully blended in.

Stir in the salted meat to the marinade and Mix by hand to massage it in, making sure every surface and every score cut is coated. Cover the bartan with cling film or transfer to a zip-lock bag. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours — 4-6 hours is.

If using a charcoal BBQ, light the coals 45 minutes before you plan to grill — Aim for them glowing white-hot with no visible flame. For a gas grill, preheat on high for 10-15 minutes. For an oven grill (broiler), preheat on the highest setting and position the.

Thread the marinated pieces onto metal seekhs (skewers) — about 5-6 pieces per skewer, leaving a small gap between each piece so heat can circulate. Put on the hot grill. Grill for 4-5 minutes without moving, until the underside develops golden-brown marks.
Chicken is done when the juices run completely clear when you press a piece — there should be no pink at all, especially in the score cuts.

variants.name: Peshawari Mantu
instructions: In a large bartan (bowl), Mix 2 cups maida (plain flour) with half a teaspoon of salt. Make a well in the centre, Stir in 1 whisked egg, and begin adding warm water a little at a time — start with a quarter cup, mix, and then Stir.

In a bartan, Mix the minced qeema (beef or mutton) with 1 finely chopped onion, 1 tsp black pepper, half tsp cumin, and 1 tsp salt. Mix thoroughly with your hands — squeezing and pressing until everything is uniformly combined.
Divide the rested dough into two halves. On a lightly floured surface, roll one half as thin as you can — aim for about 2mm, roughly the thickness of a thin playing card.
Stir in a heaped teaspoon of filling in the centre — do not overfill.
In a bartan, Mix 1.5 cups of full-fat yoghurt with 4-5 cloves of raw garlic (crushed or very finely minced) and half a teaspoon of salt. Whisk until completely smooth.

In a small karahi, heat 2 tbsp oil over medium heat. Stir in 1 sliced onion and Cook until soft and slightly golden, about 8 minutes. Stir in 3 chopped tomatoes, 1-2 green chillies (slit), salt, and half tsp red chilli powder.
Fill a large pateela (pot) with about 3 cups of water and bring to a rolling boil.
ASSEMBLE AND SERVE — THIS IS THE MOMENT: Spread the cold garlic yoghurt in a thick, generous layer on a large flat serving bartan (plate or tray).

variants.name: Afghan Mantu — Steamed Dumplings
instructions: Mix flour, 0.5 tsp salt, and warm water. Knead 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover with a damp cloth and rest 30 minutes.
Mix minced beef with grated-and-squeezed onion, cumin, black pepper, and 0.5 tsp salt.
Boil masoor daal until completely soft. Drain and set aside.
Roll the dough thin (2mm). Cut into 8cm squares.
Arrange mantu with space between them. Steam for 20-25 minutes until dough is cooked through and glossy.
While mantu steam, heat oil in a pan. Cook the second onion until golden. Stir in tomatoes, chili powder, and remaining salt.
Arrange hot steamed mantu on top of the yogurt. Pour warm qurma sauce over the mantu.

variants.name: Beef Mantu — Hearty Filling Version
instructions: Mix flour, 0.5 tsp salt, warm water into a smooth dough. Knead 8 minutes. Rest covered for 30 minutes.
Mix beef, grated-squeezed onion, coriander, green chili, garam masala, and 0.5 tsp salt together.
Boil masoor daal until completely soft. Drain.
Roll dough thin. Cut 8cm squares.
Steam 20-25 minutes on an oiled steamer until cooked through.
Warm oil, Cook remaining onion golden, Stir in tomatoes, chili powder, coriander powder, and salt. Cook 12-15 minutes until thick and oil separates. Stir in lentils.

variants.name: Maple Pecan Cake

ingredients.text: 1/3 cup buttermilk (or regular full fat milk)

instructions: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F and prep a 9*5 loaf tin by greasing it, dusting with flour and tapping out the excess. Dry roast the pecans in a small saucepan on medium heat, moving them around until they darken and smell toasty.
Stir in the maple syrup and cook, stirring frequently until it is fully absorbed into the nuts. Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt together in a small bowl and set aside.
Beat the butter and sugar on medium speed till fluffy and well combined. Stir in the eggs one by one beating for about a minute after each addition.

With the mixer on low Stir in half the flour, and then the wet ingredients in your measuring cup and then the remaining flour and mix until just combined. DO NOT over mix! Pour the batter into your prepared cake tin, scatter the remaining pecans on top.

Bake for 35-45 minutes, mine was completely done at 35, a skewer inserted in the middle should come out clean. Let cool in the tin for 5 minutes and then invert on to a plate and drizzle with additional maple syrup if desired.

variants.name: Meethi Tikiyaan

ingredients.preparation: add more if you have prefer
ingredients.text: 3/4 cup + 1 tbsp sugar (add more if you have prefer)

ingredients.item: a scant 1/2 tsp baking powder, closer to 1/3 of a tsp
ingredients.text: a scant 1/2 tsp baking powder, closer to 1/3 of a tsp
1 tsp ground cardamom (coarsely pounded is best)

ingredients.item: a few drops of kewra or rosewater essence
ingredients.text: a few drops of kewra or rosewater essence

ingredients.item: warm milk to use as needed
ingredients.text: 2 tbsp warm milk to use as needed

instructions: Mix all the ingredients except the milk in a large bowl with clean hands.

Knead just until it all comes together to form a cohesive ball - the dough will not and should not be perfectly smooth, just hold together well and it will be on the harder side. If you cannot achieve this without the milk and then Stir in 1/2.
Set the dough aside and let it rest for at least two hours. If it hasn't and then Stir in a half tbsp of ghee and knead it in.

When you are ready to cook heat ghee on a low flame in a wide pot (at least 8 inches). A small ball of dough put into the ghee should sink to the bottom and instantly start slowly sizzling, gradually rising up and frying golden not brown. If.

Roll out the dough for the tikiyaan on a lightly floured surface (flour more if the dough is too sticky to handle) and roll out to about 1/8 of an inch or sugar cookie thickness. Use your cutter of choice - I used the top of a babyfood.
Cook just one first to make sure it is frying correctly, cook till the center looks slightly golden and the edges a little more so - about 2.5 minutes on one side and 2 on the other.
If you are happy with the outcome and then Cook 5 at a time, adding ghee as needed to the pot. Do remember that as the ghee level draws down the tikiyaan will brown faster, Stir in ghee as needed.

variants.name: Methi Chicken

ingredients.item: chicken, bone in, cut into curry-pieces
ingredients.text: 1/2 chicken, bone in, cut into curry-pieces (1 chicken weighs on average 1.7lb/800g)

ingredients.preparation: ideally ground into a paste, otherwise chopped
ingredients.text: 3 green chillies (ideally ground into a paste, otherwise chopped)
0.5 tsp red chilli powder (or to taste)
5 cups fresh fenugreek, chopped (known as Methi in Urdu)

instructions: Prepare all ingredients before heating the pan.
Warm the cooking fat and cook onion, finely diced, ginger garlic paste, green chillies, red chilli powder until softened and aromatic.
Stir in green chillies, coriander powder, cumin powder, turmeric, red chilli powder, then add the chicken, bone in, cut into curry-pieces and coat it thoroughly in the masala.
Add the listed liquid ingredients as needed, cover and simmer until the main ingredient is fully cooked.
Reduce the sauce to the intended consistency, adjust the seasoning and finish with ginger garlic paste, coriander powder.

variants.name: Methi Paratha

ingredients.text: 1/2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Sprinkle 1⁄4 tsp salt over the chopped methi and mix — this draws out a small amount of moisture and softens the bitterness slightly. Leave for 5 minutes.

In a wide paraat (mixing bowl), Mix the atta, remaining 3⁄4 tsp salt, lal mirch powder, and ajwain. Mix the dry ingredients together with a fork or your fingers. Stir in the chopped and salted methi leaves to the bowl and mix them into the flour with your.

Stir in warm water gradually — start with 1⁄2 cup and mix with your fingers. Stir in more water a tablespoon at a time until the dough comes together into one ball. Knead for 5–6 minutes — push away with the heel of your hand, fold, turn, and.

Divide the rested dough into 6 equal balls (loi). Roll with your belan (rolling pin) from the centre outward, rotating the paratha quarter-turns as you go, until you have a circle about 18–20 cm across. Because there is no filling, this is significantly easier than a stuffed paratha.

Warm your tawa (flat griddle pan) over medium heat for 2 minutes. Cook for about 60–90 seconds until the surface turns from glossy to matte and small bubbles appear. Cook the second side for 60–90 seconds.

variants.name: Mirch Pasanday (Pasanday with Stuffed Chilies)
instructions: Cut your beef fillet into wide strips - 2-3 inches wide. Put beef, onions, and salt in a heavy pot or a pressure cooker (follow manufacturer directions), Stir in 2.5 cups hot water, mix well and cook covered till tender.
Stir in more water if the meat starts to stick. Once the meat is tender and then crank up the heat to dry up the water.

While the meat is cooking Mix all the spices and dry roast them in a frying pan on medium heat till fragrant. Use a small knife to slit the side of the chillies and a small spoon to fill the chillies, reserve the leftover spice mix for later.

Warm 1/4 cup oil in a frying pan and cook the chillies stirring occasionally till they get tender and blistery. Remove the chillies with a slotted spoon, pour the hot oil over the pasandas and Stir in in half of what's left of your spice mix.
Cook on medium high heat for 5 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning with more spice mix if needed. Stir in the stuffed chillies and gently mix them in. Cook on low heat for 5 minutes.
If you have extra spice mix leftover you can save it to stuff chilies another time or use it for cooking any curry.

variants.name: Missi Roti

ingredients.text: 1 cup gehun ka atta (whole wheat flour)
1/2 teaspoon lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: In a large mixing bowl (paraat or any wide bowl), Mix the besan and atta. Stir in the ajwain, red chilli powder, and salt. Give it a quick mix with your fingers so everything is evenly distributed.
Stir in the finely chopped onion, green chilli, and fresh coriander to the flour mixture.
Stir in warm water a little at a time — start with 1/2 cup — and bring the dough together. Knead for 4–5 minutes until you have a smooth, firm dough. If it's sticky, Stir in a little dry atta.
Cover the dough with a damp cloth or an upturned bowl and let it rest for 15–20 minutes at room temperature.
Put your tawa (flat griddle pan) on the stove over medium heat. Let it heat for 2–3 minutes.

Divide the dough into 6 equal balls (about the size of a golf ball). Take one ball, flatten it slightly between your palms, and then use your belan (rolling pin) to roll it into a circle about 6–7 inches in diameter.
Carefully lift the rolled roti and Put it on the hot tawa. Cook on medium heat for about 90 seconds.
Using a chimta (tongs) or a flat spatula, carefully slide it under the roti and flip it.

Transfer the roti to a plate and immediately apply a generous knob of ghee while it's hot. That's the ajwain blooming in the heat, the onion caramelising at the edges, and the ghee doing what ghee does best.

variants.name: Mitho Lolo — Sindhi Sweet Jaggery Bread

ingredients.text: 2 cups gehun ka atta (whole wheat flour)
3-4 tablespoons ghee ya tail (extra ghee for cooking)

instructions: Pour the warm water over it and stir until the jaggery is completely dissolved. This may take 2–3 minutes of stirring. The liquid will be golden-brown, like a dark caramel.

In a large bowl, Mix the atta and saunf. Stir in the ghee (3 tablespoons) and rub it into the flour with your fingertips until the flour resembles breadcrumbs. and then pour in the dissolved jaggery water gradually, mixing and kneading as you go.
Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rest for 15–20 minutes. This relaxes the gluten and makes the dough easier to roll.
Put your tawa (flat griddle pan) on the stove over medium-low heat. This bread must be cooked on LOWER heat than a regular roti because the jaggery will burn quickly if the heat is too high.
Divide the dough into 6 portions. On a lightly floured chakla (rolling board), roll each portion into a circle about 5–6 inches in diameter and 5–6mm thick — notably thicker than a regular chapati.
Put the rolled lolo on the warm tawa. Stir in a teaspoon of ghee around the edges. Cook on medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes.
Stir in another teaspoon of ghee to the tawa. Cook the second side for another 3–4 minutes until it matches the first side in colour — deep golden-brown with slightly darker patches.
Transfer the lolo to a plate.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Mitho Lolo — Sindhi Sweet Jaggery Bread

variants.name: Mooli Paratha

ingredients.text: 1/2 tsp lal mirch flakes (red chilli flakes)

instructions: Make a well in the centre and Stir in warm water a little at a time, mixing with your fingers as you go.
Sprinkle 1 tsp salt over the grated mooli, mix, and leave it for 10 minutes.
Put the squeezed mooli into a clean bowl. Stir in the lal mirch flakes, ajwain, chopped hara dhania, and chopped hari mirch if using. Mix everything together with a fork or your fingers.
Divide the rested dough into 6 equal balls (loi). On your chakla (rolling board), use your belan (rolling pin) to roll it into a circle about 12 cm across — roughly the size of your palm.
Dust the sealed ball lightly in flour and Put on the chakla. Use the belan to roll it outward from the centre, applying light and even pressure.

Put your tawa (flat griddle pan) on the stove over medium heat. Let it heat up for 2 minutes — hold your palm a few centimetres above the surface; Cook for about 90 seconds until you see the top surface start to look drier and small pale bubbles.
Transfer the finished paratha to a plate or a roti basket lined with a cloth to keep warm.

variants.name: Murgh Cholay or Chana Chicken

ingredients.item: boneless chicken or 1.25-1.5 pounds chicken bone in
ingredients.text: 1 pound boneless chicken or 1.25-1.5 pounds chicken bone in

ingredients.item: 17-19 fl oz can chickpeas drained and rinsed through
ingredients.text: 1 17-19 fl oz can chickpeas drained and rinsed through

instructions: Take a stockpot sized pot and put it on medium high heat, wait a few minutes, and and then Stir in the oil. When the oil is hot and then Stir in in the onions and the cumin seeds & cook until the onions start to turn golden.

Stir in the garlic and ginger pastes and saute for 30 seconds, and then Stir in the tomatoes salt, chilli powder, turmeric powder, and coriander powder. Cover and keep it on medium high heat and and then uncover, the tomatoes should have broken down and become jammy.
Stir your chicken pieces in and saute until the colour changes.
In goes a cup of hot water, the chickpeas, and a pinch of baking soda (for touch chickpeas), bring it to a boil, and and then let it cook covered on low heat for another 25-30 minutes.

When the chicken is tender and then adjust consistency of your gravy by adding water and then Stir in the garam masala, the black pepper, the green chillies and cilantro. Cook for 2 minutes and then taste and adjust seasoning.

variants.name: Murgh Palak - Palak Chicken

ingredients.item: boneless chicken cut into big cubes
ingredients.text: 3/4-1 lb boneless chicken cut into big cubes (about 50% more for bone in)
1/2 teaspoon grated ginger or ginger paste
Heaped tbsp of Kasuri Methi (dried fenugreek - optional)

instructions: Warm a few tablespoons of oil in a pot and Stir in the diced onion, Cook on medium high heat till the edges start to take on a golden brown.
Optional: Stir in a diced green chilli (or two) for extra flavour.
Stir in the ginger and garlic and stir Cook for a minute.
Stir in the chicken and spices, saute on medium high heat until all the sides of the chicken pieces have changed colour.
Mix in the diced tomato, and 1/2-1 cup of hot water (more for stainless steel, less for non stick) and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until the chicken is tender.
Crank up the heat to dry up the excess water and Stir in your kasuri methi and saute for a minute.

Stir in your spinach - spinach is a naturally watery green so at this stage your goal is to cook the moisture out of the spinach and have the oil rise above your dish. This takes about 10-12 minutes on medium heat.
Adjust seasoning - a squeeze of lemon juice is lovely here, but you can also Stir in some garam masala, and/or extra chilies.

variants.name: Mutanjan - Meethe Chawal

ingredients.text: 3 cups white basmati rice (washed and soaked for 30 minutes)
1 tbsp ghee/unsalted butter (for cooking the rice with)
1/4 tsp red food colour (or as needed)
1/4 tsp orange food colour (or as needed)
1/4 tsp yellow food colour (or as needed)
1/4 tsp green food colour (or as needed)

instructions: Rinse and soak the rice, then boil it in plenty of water until almost tender and drain well.
Warm the ghee with the whole spices; add the sugar and listed liquid ingredients to make a light syrup.
Fold in the rice, food colour, fruit and nuts without crushing the grains.
Cover tightly and finish over very low heat until the syrup is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Rest for 10 minutes, fluff gently and add the reserved garnish.

variants.name: Mutton Handi

ingredients.preparation: Boiled and blended to a paste
ingredients.text: 1 Onion (Boiled and blended to a paste)
1/2 tsp Coriander Powder, roasted and ground
1 tsp Cumin Powder, roasted and ground

instructions: Marinade the meat in the marinade ingredients, overnight is best otherwise 2 hours. Remember to soak the nuts when your marinade the meat! In a frypan, heat 2 tablespoon of oil. Stir in marinated meat and Cook until mutton pieces are brown. This step is just to give meat a deep golden-brown color and lock the marinade flavors in the meat.

Blend onions with water in a smooth paste and give the paste a good boil. Once it boils, strain the water completely from the onion and a smooth onion paste is ready. Soak tomatoes in boiling water for 5 minutes, the skin will peel off easily. Blend the tomatoes into a fine puree.

Nuts will Stir in richness to the masala. In a handi (clay pot) or regular pot, Stir in a quarter cup of oil and Stir in all the whole spices (bay leaves, cloves, black cumin, black cardamom, cinnamon). Once they sizzle Stir in the onion puree.

Let the onions cook until they turn light brown. This step is important and would take 8 – 10 minutes. Stir in ginger-garlic paste, chopped green chili and sauté until the rawness of ginger garlic ends – say half a minute.

Stir in fried meat from before. Mix the meat into the onion’s masala, sautee for one minute. Stir in salt, red chili powder, turmeric, roasted cumin and coriander powder. Cook the masala on medium flame. Stir in a dash of water if needed.

Stir in the pureed tomato paste and let the meat and masala cook. Bhounfy the masala well (ek jan ho jaye masala) and cook until oil separates. Once, the masala is nicely cooked (bhoun jaye) Stir in water or stock (as required) to cook the meat. Let the meat simmer on medium flame until it is tender.

When the meat is fully cooked Stir in the nuts paste for richness. Lastly Stir in the freshly crushed black pepper and fenugreek leaves (slightly crushing with the hands) and cream. Mix and let it simmer for another 5 – 10 minutes on low flame.
Warm one tablespoon of butter or ghee. As the butter melts Stir in garam masala powder, when it sizzles pour it on the mutton handi. Slight mix and let it cook on dam for 5 minutes.

variants.name: Lamb / Mutton Karahi - An Easy, Traditional Recipe

ingredients.text: 1.1 lb lamb or mutton (bone in preferably)

ingredients.item: paprika or kashmiri red chilli powder
ingredients.text: 2 tsp paprika or kashmiri red chilli powder
ginger cut into matchsticks (as much as desired)

instructions: Heat the cooking fat and brown the lamb or mutton over medium-high heat.

Stir in bulb garlic, thumb sized chunk of ginger, paprika or kashmiri red chilli powder, chilli flakes, followed by the tomatoes and paprika or kashmiri red chilli powder, black pepper, chilli flakes, cumin powder, coriander powder, coriander.
Cook uncovered, stirring regularly, until the protein is cooked and the tomato masala reduces enough for the oil to separate.
Finish with thumb sized chunk of ginger, coriander powder, coriander and serve immediately.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Lamb / Mutton Karahi - An Easy, Traditional Recipe
source_attributions.author: Fatima Cooks

variants.name: Balochi Mutton Karahi

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp tel ya dumba charbi (oil or sheep tail fat)
5 whole sabut lal mirch (whole dried red chillies)

instructions: Warm oil (or Dumba fat) in a heavy karahi on high flame. Stir in cumin seeds and whole red chillies — let them sizzle for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in crushed garlic and sliced ginger. Cook on medium-high for 3-4 minutes until golden.
Increase to high heat. Stir in mutton pieces and black pepper. Sear for 8-10 minutes, turning to brown on all sides.
Stir in chopped tomatoes and cook on high for 8 minutes until they break down into the meat.
Reduce to medium-low, Stir in 3/4 cup water, cover, and cook for 45-55 minutes until mutton is completely tender. Check every 15 minutes.
Remove lid, Stir in green chillies, increase heat to high. Cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until masala is semi-dry and clings to the meat.
Garnish with fresh coriander and serve immediately.

variants.name: Dum Mutton Karahi

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Mix mutton with yoghurt, half the ginger garlic paste, half the chilli powder, turmeric, and 1 tsp salt. Marinate for at least 30 minutes (overnight in the fridge is better).
Warm oil in a heavy-lidded pot on medium-high. Cook two sliced onions until deep brown, 10-12 minutes.
Stir in ginger garlic paste and tomatoes to remaining onions. Stir in remaining dry spices. Cook on high 12 minutes until thick masala forms and oil separates.
Stir in marinated mutton and stir-Cook in the masala for 8 minutes on high heat. Stir in 1/2 cup water and green chillies.
Put lid on and seal the edge with dough (roll dough into a rope and press around the lid rim).
Put on very low flame (or use a tawa/griddle underneath the pot to diffuse heat). Cook on dum for 45-60 minutes.
Increase heat to high and bhuno for 8-10 minutes to dry and concentrate the masala. Garnish and serve.

variants.name: Lahori Mutton Karahi — Restaurant-Style Wok Curry

ingredients.text: 1 tsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)

instructions: Put a large, heavy karahi (wok) or wide heavy-bottomed pot on high heat. Stir in the tel (oil) and let it heat until shimmering — you can test by dropping a tiny piece of ginger in.
Stir in the mutton pieces to the hot oil. Do not stir for 2 minutes — let the meat develop a proper sear on one side.

Stir in the quartered tamatar (tomatoes), slit hari mirch (green chillies), lal mirch powder (red chilli powder), kali mirch (black pepper), and namak (salt). Stir everything together. The tomatoes will release a lot of liquid — keep the heat high.

This is the most important step. Once the tomatoes have broken down, continue cooking on high heat, stirring more frequently, until the masala thickens and the oil separates to the sides of the karahi — you'll see a pool of red-orange oil collecting around the edges. This process.

Once the masala is properly bhuno'd and oil-separated, Stir in 1⁄2 cup of hot water, stir, reduce heat to medium-low, and cover the karahi with a lid. Cook for 20-25 minutes until the mutton is tender — press a piece with a spoon.

Once the mutton is tender, increase heat back to high and bhuno (roast) the karahi again for 3-5 minutes, stirring constantly. Turn off the heat. Stir in malai (cream) and scatter julienned adrak (ginger strips) over the top.

A proper Lahori karahi is served in the karahi itself, placed directly on the table on a heat-proof stand. If you don't have a karahi, serve in a deep bowl but transfer immediately before the steam condenses and makes it watery.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Lahori Mutton Karahi — Restaurant-Style Wok Curry

variants.name: Mutton Karahi Karachi Style

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Warm oil in a large karahi on medium-high. Cook onions for 10-12 minutes until deep golden. Stir in ginger garlic paste and Cook 3 more minutes.
Stir in tomatoes and all dry spices. Cook on high for 15 minutes until tomatoes break down completely and masala is thick with oil separating. Mash tomatoes as they cook.
Reduce heat to medium. Stir in whisked yoghurt tablespoon by tablespoon, stirring between each addition. Cook for 4 minutes until yoghurt is fully absorbed into the masala.
Increase heat to high. Stir in mutton pieces and stir-Cook in the masala for 8-10 minutes to brown the meat on all sides.

Stir in 1 cup water, cover, and cook on medium-low for 45-60 minutes until mutton is very tender. Check every 15 minutes and Stir in water if needed (1/4 cup at a time). Mutton on bone needs the full 60 minutes.
Remove lid, Stir in green chillies and ginger julienne, and increase heat to high. Stir-Cook for 10-15 minutes until masala thickens and coats the meat.
Adjust salt, garnish with fresh coriander and extra ginger.

variants.name: Mutton Raan
instructions: Put your muton piece in your roaster and use a sharp knife to score deep cuts into your roast.
Mix your marinade ingredients together (if you are the masala tasting sort like me and then it should be a strong flavour).
If you can and then flip your roast over once and baste with the marinade.
Remove the raan from the fridge an hour before you will roast it to allow it to come to room temperature for more even cooking.
Preheat your oven to 350F and bake the raan covered with foil for 2 hours.
Scatter your potatoes along the sides and bake covered for another half an hour, and then remove the foil and allow it to bake until the potatoes are fork tender (usually 20 minutes or so more).

variants.name: Peshwari Naan Recipe | Coconut Naan

ingredients.item: plain flour OR self-raising flour for an extra fluffy naan
ingredients.text: 5 cups plain flour OR self-raising flour for an extra fluffy naan

ingredients.item: dried fruit (such as raisins or finely chopped prunes (optional))
ingredients.text: 2 tbsp dried fruit (such as raisins or finely chopped prunes (optional))

instructions: Mix the flour, salt and listed dough ingredients; add water gradually and knead to a soft, smooth dough.
Cover and rest the dough while preparing any filling. Cook the filling until dry enough not to tear the bread, then cool it.
Divide and roll the dough. Add the filling if used, seal well and roll again without forcing it through the surface.
Cook on a hot tawa or heavy pan, turning and brushing with the measured fat, until both sides are spotted and cooked through.

variants.name: Butter Naan (Home Tawa Method)
instructions: In a bartan (bowl), Mix the lukewarm water, sugar, and yeast. Stir gently and leave undisturbed for 10 minutes.
In a large bartan (bowl), Stir in the maida (flour) and salt. Pour in the activated yeast mixture, dahi (yoghurt), and oil. Mix with a chamcha (spoon) first, and then use your hands.
Turn the dough out onto a clean surface and knead for 8–10 minutes.

Grease the bartan (bowl) with a little oil, Put the dough in it, and turn once to coat. Cover tightly with a cloth or cling wrap. Leave in a warm Put for 1–1.5 hours, until the dough has doubled in size.
Punch the dough down (satisfying!). Cover with a damp cloth and rest for 10 minutes.
Put your cast-iron tawa (flat griddle) or heaviest frying pan on the highest heat for at least 3–4 minutes.

Wet one side of the rolled naan lightly with water using your fingers. Cook for 2 minutes — you'll see bubbles forming on the top surface and the underside should have dark spots when you peek. Cook the second side for 1–1.5 minutes.
If making garlic naan, mix minced lehsan (garlic) into the melted butter before brushing. Stack finished naans under a clean cloth to keep them soft and warm while you cook the rest.

variants.name: Balochi Namkeen Gosht

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp charbi ya ghee (animal fat or ghee)

instructions: In a heavy-bottomed pot with a tight-fitting lid, arrange meat pieces. Stir in ghee, salt, kali mirch, tez patta, ginger slices, and quartered onion. DO NOT Stir in water.
Put pot on the lowest possible heat. Cook for 90-120 minutes without opening the lid. The meat will release its own juices and cook in them.
After 90 minutes, open carefully (the steam is very hot). If still firm, re-seal and cook another 20-30 minutes.
Once meat is tender, remove lid and increase heat to high for 5-8 minutes until the liquid reduces to almost nothing and meat is sizzling in its own fat.
Transfer to a simple platter. Light garnish of hara dhania only.

variants.name: KP Namkeen Karahi

ingredients.text: 5 tbsp ghee or tel (ghee or oil)
1.5 tsp sabut kali mirch (whole black peppercorns)

instructions: Put a steel karahi or heavy-bottomed wide pan over high heat and heat the ghee until it's very hot — almost smoking.
Stir in zeera seeds to the hot ghee — they'll sizzle and pop immediately. Stir in roughly smashed lehsan cloves and thickly sliced adrak. Stir 30 seconds.

Once meat is well-coloured, Stir in 1 cup hot water to the karahi. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover loosely, and cook for 50-60 minutes until mutton is very tender. Check every 15 minutes and Stir in small amounts of hot water if the liquid evaporates completely before the.

Once meat is tender, turn heat to the maximum. Stir in the chopped tamatar and slit hari mirch to the karahi. Bhuno everything on high heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring and pressing the tomatoes against the hot karahi to break them down rapidly.
Remove from heat. Stir in julienned ginger strips. Stir once to mix some of the garnish into the meat — the residual heat will wilt the coriander slightly, releasing its fragrance.

SERVE IN THE KARAHI — NEVER TRANSFER: Bring the karahi directly to the table on a wooden board or cloth. Do not transfer to another serving dish. Put additional fresh coriander, slit green chillies, and lemon wedges around the karahi for guests to Stir in themselves.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: NO BROWNING, JUST COOK: Put the mutton pieces directly into a dry karahi (wok). Stir in salt and black pepper.
Stir in half cup of water. Cover and cook on medium heat for 45-60 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes, until the meat is almost tender and most of the water has cooked off.
Once water is mostly gone, Stir in the ginger julienne and slit green chilies. Increase heat to high. bhuno (stir-Cook vigorously) — scraping the bottom of the karahi constantly for 10-15 minutes.
Stir in fresh coriander at the very end, give one last stir, and serve immediately from the karahi.
Transfer to a serving dish or serve straight from the karahi. The raw ginger garnish is the Namak Mandi marker — it adds a sharp, fresh contrast to the deep cooked flavors.

variants.name: Peshawari Namkeen Gosht
instructions: Stir in the pani (water), namak (salt), and HALF the crushed kali mirch (black pepper). Bring to a boil over high heat.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to low. Cover the pateela with a tight lid and let the gosht simmer gently for 1.5 to 2 hours. Check every 30 minutes to make sure there's still some pani in the pot.

Increase the heat to medium-high. Turn the pieces every 2-3 minutes using tongs or a chamcha (ladle) so all sides get exposure to the hot fat. Cook for about 10-15 minutes total until the edges are golden and crispy, with dark caramelised spots.
Toss the pieces gently to coat.

Transfer the gosht to a communal platter — a large thaal (round metal plate) is traditional. Pour ALL the remaining charbi (fat) from the pateela over the meat. Arrange raw pyaz (onion) rings, whole hari mirch (green chillies), and nimbu (lemon) wedges around the meat.

variants.name: Swat Trout — Mountain River Fish

ingredients.text: 0.5 tsp Laal mirch powder (red chili powder)

instructions: Make 3-4 diagonal slashes on each side of the trout. Mix salt, chili, ginger-garlic paste, and lemon juice. Marinate 20-30 minutes — no longer, acid will start cooking the flesh.
Warm ghee in a heavy pan large enough to fit the trout.
Lay the trout in the pan carefully. Do not move it for 4-5 minutes — let the skin set and crisp.
Cook the other side 4-5 minutes. Total time for a 350g trout is about 8-10 minutes — it should be cooked through without being dry.
Transfer to a plate.

variants.name: Karachi Namkeen Gosht

ingredients.text: 2 inch piece adrak julienne (ginger for garnish)

instructions: Warm ghee in a heavy karahi or pot. Stir in zeera, let it pop. Stir in sliced ginger, whole garlic cloves, and sliced pyaaz.
Stir in mutton pieces, turn heat to high. Bhuno for 8-10 minutes, turning pieces to get colour on all sides.
SLOW COOK — THE KEY STEP: Stir in 1/2 cup water. Cover tightly and cook on medium-low heat for 70-80 minutes until meat is very tender.
In the last 10 minutes, uncover and cook on medium-high heat until all water has evaporated and the meat is sizzling in ghee.
Remove to a serving plate. The fresh garnish against the simple spiced meat is what makes namkeen gosht complete.

variants.name: Nankhatai
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). If you have a gas oven without a temperature gauge, medium heat is your target — most Pakistani ovens run slightly hot, so err on the lower side.

In a large mixing bowl, Stir in the semi-solid ghee and cheeni. Using a wooden spoon or your clean hand, beat them together vigorously for 3-4 minutes until the mixture becomes pale, fluffy, and somewhat light in texture.
In a separate bowl, Mix the maida, besan, suji, elaichi powder, and baking powder. Whisk them together with a fork for 30 seconds to distribute evenly.

Stir in the dry flour mixture to the creamed ghee-sugar in two additions, mixing gently with a spoon or your hand between each addition. The dough should come together into a soft, pliable ball that holds its shape when pressed — like Play-Doh.
Pinch off roughly equal portions of dough — about 1.5 tablespoons each, the size of a walnut. Roll each portion gently between your palms into a smooth ball.
Put the tray in the preheated oven on the middle rack. Bake for 15-18 minutes.

Remove from the oven and leave the nankhatai completely undisturbed on the tray for 15-20 minutes. After 15-20 minutes, they will have firmed up considerably. Gently transfer to a wire rack or plate to cool completely — another 20-30 minutes.

variants.name: KP Style Nihari
instructions: Warm ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Stir in sabut garam masala and tez patta.
Stir in sliced pyaaz to the fragrant oil and Cook to medium-golden (not as dark as Lahori style). Stir in adrak-lehsan paste, lal mirch, kali mirch, and salt. Bhuno for 3-4 minutes.
Stir in gosht to the pot over high heat. Bhuno with the masala for 6-8 minutes until meat is well-coated and has changed colour on the outside.
Stir in 1.5 litres of hot water. Bring to boil, skim foam, reduce to low heat, cover and cook for 3-3.5 hours. Check once an hour and Stir in hot water if needed.
Mix aata with water to make slurry, Stir in to pot as before, simmer 15 minutes.
Taste and Stir in more salt or kali mirch if needed.
Stir in hara dhania and squeeze over plenty of nimbu.

variants.name: Classic Lahori Nihari

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)

instructions: Put 2 tbsp gandum ka atta (wheat flour) in a small, dry pan — no oil, no ghee. Put on medium-low heat and stir constantly with a chamcha (spoon). The atta will slowly change colour from white to pale gold to a toasty brown — this takes about.
Warm the desi ghee in a heavy-bottomed degh (large pot) or Dutch oven on medium heat. Stir in the sliced pyaz (onions). Stir every minute or so for about 15-20 minutes.

Stir in adrak lehsan paste (ginger-garlic paste) to the remaining pyaz in the degh. Stir for 2 minutes until the raw smell disappears — you'll know because the sharp, nose-prickling garlic smell turns into something warm and fragrant. Don't let it burn — if it starts sticking, Stir.
Stir in the beef nalli (shank pieces) and extra nalli (marrow bones) to the degh. Turn the heat to high. Using a large chamcha (ladle), turn the meat to brown all sides — about 5-7 minutes total.

Sprinkle in the nihari masala, lal mirch powder (red chilli powder), haldi (turmeric), and namak (salt). Stir everything well to coat every piece of meat — the spices should sizzle and become fragrant within 30 seconds.

Stir in the hot pani (water) — pour it in slowly to avoid a steam explosion. Bring to a boil on high heat (this takes about 5 minutes). Once boiling, reduce to the absolute lowest flame your stove can manage.

After the long cook, the marrow should have mostly melted into the gravy. If there are still marrow bones with intact marrow, use a spoon to scoop the soft, fatty marrow out of the bones and stir it into the gravy. If it's still resisting, cook for another.

Take the roasted atta you prepared in Step 1 and mix it with about 4 tbsp warm water in a small bowl to make a smooth slurry — no lumps. Slowly stir this into the nihari, a little at a time. Cook on low heat for another 30.
Ladle the nihari into deep bowls — a generous amount of the dark, glistening gravy with chunks of gosht and any remaining bone pieces.

variants.name: Mutton Nihari Slow Cooked
instructions: If time allows, soak in cold water for 30 minutes — this draws out excess blood and gives you a cleaner-tasting nihari. Drain and pat dry.

Cook THE ONIONS — DEEP BROWN IS THE TARGET: Heat ghee in a large, heavy deg or kadai over medium-high heat. Stir in sliced pyaaz and Cook for 15-18 minutes, stirring every minute or so. Remove half the onions once golden-brown and set aside for garnish.
To the remaining onions in the pot, Stir in adrak-lehsan paste. Cook for 2 minutes. Stir in nihari masala, saunf, and lal mirch.
Stir in mutton to the masala and turn heat to high. Bhuno the meat with masala for 8 minutes until pieces are well-coated and have some colour. Stir in salt and stir.
Stir in 1.5-2 litres of hot water. Bring to a boil, skim foam. Reduce to lowest heat, cover tightly and cook for 3.5 to 4 hours.
Mix aata with 5 tablespoons of water into a smooth slurry. Ladle some hot gravy into a cup, whisk the slurry into it, and then Stir in back to the pot. Simmer 20-25 minutes stirring occasionally.
Top with reserved fried onions, julienned ginger, hara dhania, hari mirch, and lemon wedges.

variants.name: Beef Nihari Karachi Style

ingredients.text: 1.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: BROWN YOUR ONIONS — THIS IS NON-NEGOTIABLE: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed deg (pot) or pressure cooker over medium-high heat. Stir in sliced pyaaz and Cook, stirring frequently, for 12-15 minutes until they turn a deep mahogany brown. Not light golden — we're talking proper brown like strong.

Reduce heat to medium. Stir in adrak-lehsan paste and Cook for 2 minutes until the raw smell disappears — Continue until it smells nutty rather than sharp. Stir in nihari masala and lal mirch powder, stir everything together, and Stir in a splash of water to prevent burning.

Stir in the beef shank and nalli pieces to the pot. Increase heat to high and bhuno (stir-Cook) the meat with the masala for 5-7 minutes until every piece is coated and the meat has some colour on it.
Stir in 1.5 litres of hot water to the pot and bring to a vigorous boil. Once foam stops appearing (about 5 minutes), reduce heat to the lowest setting, cover tightly, and cook for 3 hours.

After 3 hours, the meat should be very tender — test by pressing a piece with a spoon. Mix aata with 4 tablespoons of water to make a smooth, lump-free paste. Fish out about a cup of hot gravy from the pot, whisk in the aata slurry, and.
In a small pan, heat 1 tablespoon of ghee until smoking hot, Stir in a pinch of red chilli powder and immediately pour this tarka over the nihari surface. Do not stir — let it sit on top.
Ladle nihari into deep bowls or a large serving dish.

variants.name: Bone Marrow Nihari

ingredients.text: 1 tsp lal mirch tarka (red chilli for tempering)

instructions: Put nalli pieces in a large pot, cover with cold water, Stir in 1 tsp salt, and bring to a hard boil. Boil for 5 minutes, and then drain completely and rinse bones under cold water. This blanching step removes impurities and blood from the bones — skipping.
In a heavy deg, heat ghee on medium-high. Stir in pyaaz and Cook for 18-20 minutes, stirring frequently, until they're a very deep mahogany.
To the fried onions, Stir in adrak-lehsan paste, crushed badi elaichi, nihari masala, kali mirch, and a splash of water. Bhuno for 5 minutes. Stir in blanched nalli and gosht.
LONG SLOW COOK — 4 TO 5 HOURS: Stir in 2 litres of hot water, bring to a boil, skim foam, and then reduce to the lowest possible heat. Cover tightly. Cook for 4-5 hours minimum.
After 4+ hours, the marrow should be loose in the bones. Stir it in thoroughly.
Mix aata with water into a smooth slurry. Stir in to a cup of hot nihari gravy, whisk smooth, pour back into pot. Simmer 25-30 minutes until gravy is thick enough to coat a spoon generously.
This nihari deserves a grand presentation. Cover the surface with julienned ginger strips, a mountain of fresh hara dhania, slit hari mirch, and lemon wedges around the edges.

alternate_methods.label: stovetop
instructions: Dry roast all the ingredients in a frying pan (no oil), grind to a powder. Warm oil in a large pot.

Thinly slice your onion, Cook till golden brown and then spread on paper towels to dry. Stir in all the remaining ingredients in the first list and stir Cook the meat until its browned and the masala is cooked - about 4-5 minutes.

And then Stir in your Nihari Masala Mix and 7 cups of water and stir well. Pressure cook for 45-50 minutes or slow cook for 4-5 hours undisturbed to get beautifully tender meat. For slow cooking stove top, bring the mixture to a boil and then let it simmer covered.
Crush the onions and mix in, bring the nihari to a boil. When ready to eat and then dissolve 1/3 cup atta in 1 cup water and whisk briskly as you Stir in it to the nihari.
The nihari will thicken as it cooks - 10 to 15 minutes. Adjust consistency per liking (more water or atta+water), just remember you need to simmer after adding it to lose the raw taste.

variants.name: Nimbu Soda (Pakistani Style Lime Soda)

ingredients.text: 1 teaspoon black salt or 1 teaspoon salt

instructions: Measure the liquid, sweetener and spices.
Simmer the spices in water long enough to release their aroma; add tea or other infusing ingredients as specified.
Add milk or the remaining liquid, heat gently, then strain or blend as appropriate.
Taste for sweetness and serve hot or well chilled according to the recipe.

instructions: Whisk butter and sugar in a large bowl with an electric beater or stand mixer on high speed until fluffy (about 5-7 minutes).
Stir in beaten egg and briefly whisk until well-mixed.
Pour in dry ingredients (cumin seeds, flour, baking powder and salt), and mix well with hand to form dough.
Rest in fridge for 40 minutes.
Pre-heat oven to 350°F.
With a rolling pin, roll out dough until about 1/5-inch thin.
Once flat, cut biscuits with a round cutter (I just used a jar lid) and move to baking sheet.
Put on center rack in oven and bake for 15 minutes.

Stir in the eggs one by one, beating well after each addition on medium high speed.
Stir in the dry ingredients to the bowl and put the mixer on low mixing JUST until the flour is 70% combined i.e.
Scatter the remaining hazelnuts over top and bake for 23-28 minutes or until the edges are puffy and a skewer inserted in the middle comes out only slightly moist.
Cool, cut, enjoy!

instructions: If Using Graham Cracker Crumbs: Tip out half the hazelnuts for the topping and Stir in the remaining ingredients into your food processor.

If Using Digestive Biscuits: Remove all the nuts from the food processor bowl, Stir in remaining crust ingredients and process till a crumbly mass forms. and then Stir in in the nuts and pulse once or twice.
Layer the plastic wrap length wise once, and then width wise, and then lengthwise.
Beat the cream cheese till smooth and creamy and then Stir in the sugar and mix well.
Beat in the Nutella for 2 minutes or till well combined.
Gradually Stir in the cream and beat until fluffy and well incorporated.
Mix in vanilla and salt.
Pour the cheesecake filling into your prepared tin, and then top with the crushed nuts from earlier and freeze for four hours or until firm.
Once the filling sets Put a layer of plastic wrap overtop until ready to serve.

ingredients.text: 1/2 cup canola oil or other neutral tasting oil

instructions: Preheat your oven to 350 degrees and grease a 6-inch (what I used) or a 9-inch pan and set aside.
Take out a large mixing bowl and briskly whisk the oil, sugar, and zest together till combined.
Stir in the eggs one by one whisking well after each addition.
Pour into your prepared pan and bake for 35-50 minutes depending on the pan you use.
Let it cool for ten minutes and then invert onto a cake plate and pour the glaze over while the cake is still warm.
While the cake is baking bring the glaze ingredients to a boil in a small non stick saucepan and simmer for 10-15 minutes until it is thickens and becomes syrupy.

variants.name: Oreo Cheesecake Jar

instructions: Whip the cream cheese until soft and and then Stir in the icing sugar, whipped cream, and vanilla - mix on low until combined and then turn up the speed and whip for another 1-2 minutes until fluffy.
Fold/Stir in half the oreo crumbs - you can do a little less if you like, there's no hard and fast rule here.
Warm your cream until just simmering, pour it over your chocolate chips and stir until just smooth.
From each section Put half the Oreo crumbs on the bottom of each jar, Stir in a layer of cheesecake filling (piping bag is easiest), the remaining crumbs, more cheesecake and top it with Ganache.
Refrigerate for 1-2 hours at least before serving, can be made a day ahead.

instructions: Warm oil in a saute pan and Stir in the cumin seeds, cook for 30 seconds.
Stir in your onions and cook on medium high heat till the edges start to turn golden.
Reduce the heat a little and Stir in the ginger and garlic.
Saute for a 30 seconds and Stir in the 3/4 tsp salt. If it starts to stick immediately Stir in a small splash of water.
In go your tomatoes and spice, mix them and cook on medium high heat stirring often until the excess water sautes out and you are left with a rich spice paste with oil rising above it (i..e bhunna).
Stir in your potatoes and and then Stir in the cauliflower on top. Mix gently and cook covered on low till both vegetables are tender - 20 to 25 minutes.
If at any point the veggies start to stick/burn Stir in a tiny splash of water but not too much.
When the vegetables are cooked through taste a piece of cauliflower and potato together and adjust seasoning (I always Stir in more salt at this stage).
Turn the stove off, top with the garnishes and cover for a minute or so to infuse aromas.
