When shimmering, Stir in onions. sauté the onions continuously for 10-15 minutes. They should be wilted and golden brown along the edges.
When onions are golden brown, Stir in garlic and ginger and continue to sauté for 2-3 minutes.
Stir in turmeric, ground coriander, ground cumin, and chili flakes. Mix to Mix, and then Stir in tomato sauce. Stir/sauté (bhuno) for 3-5 minutes.
Stir in potatoes, green chilies, 1 tsp salt, and 1 cup of water, and then turn heat to low and cover with a lid.
Allow to cook till potatoes are fork tender. Depending on the type of potatoes you are using, this should take 15-20 minutes.
Mix into the gravy.
Stir in second cup of water and allow to gently simmer, without lid.
Before serving, Stir in fresh cilantro, and enjoy with lemon wedges.

variants.name: Beef Keema Lasagna
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Heat the oil and cook the onions until golden at the edges. Add garlic and beef mince, breaking it up until fully browned and no pink remains.
Stir in cumin, chilli and oregano. Add tomatoes, tomato paste, half the salt and pepper; simmer for 20 minutes until thick but still spoonable.
Make a white sauce by cooking butter and flour for 90 seconds, then whisking in warm milk. Simmer until lightly thick and season.
Heat the oven to 190°C and prepare the sheets according to the packet if they are not oven-ready.
Layer keema sauce, lasagna sheets, white sauce and cheeses, finishing with white sauce and cheese.
Bake covered for 25 minutes and uncovered for 20 minutes. Rest for 15 minutes so the layers set before slicing.

variants.name: Chicken Lasagna
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Heat the oil and soften the onion. Add garlic and chicken mince; break it up and cook until no pink remains.
Add tomatoes, tomato paste, oregano, chilli flakes, half the salt and pepper. Simmer uncovered for 18–20 minutes until thick.
For the white sauce, melt butter, whisk in flour for 90 seconds, then gradually whisk in warm milk. Simmer until it coats a spoon and season.
Heat the oven to 190°C. If the lasagna sheets require pre-cooking, prepare them according to the packet.
Layer meat sauce, sheets, white sauce and cheeses in a baking dish, repeating and ending with white sauce and cheese.
Cover and bake for 25 minutes, uncover and bake for 15–20 minutes until browned. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting.

variants.name: Vegetable Lasagna
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Heat the oil and soften the onion. Add mushrooms and cook until their liquid evaporates, then add courgettes and peppers for 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic, tomatoes, tomato paste, oregano, salt and pepper. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, then fold in spinach until wilted.
Heat the oven to 190°C and prepare the lasagna sheets according to the packet if necessary.
Spread a little vegetable sauce in the dish. Layer sheets, vegetable sauce, spoonfuls of cottage cheese and grated cheeses.
Repeat the layers and finish with sauce and grated cheese. Cover and bake for 25 minutes.
Uncover and bake for 15–20 minutes until golden. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting.

variants.name: Chicken Tikka Pasta
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.

ingredients.text: 600 g boneless chicken (cut into 2 cm pieces)

instructions: Mix the chicken with yogurt, tikka masala, lemon juice and half the salt. Marinate for at least 20 minutes while preparing the other ingredients.
Boil the fusilli until al dente, reserving 1 cup of pasta water before draining.
Heat the oil in a wide pan. Cook the marinated chicken in a single layer for 8–10 minutes until lightly charred at the edges and 74°C inside. Remove from the pan.
In the same pan, cook the onion and peppers for 4 minutes. Add garlic, then tomato puree and simmer for 8 minutes.
Lower the heat, stir in the cream and return the chicken. Add the pasta and enough reserved water to make a silky sauce.
Taste for salt, finish with fresh coriander and serve hot.

variants.name: Chicken White Sauce Pasta
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.

ingredients.text: 500 g boneless chicken breast (cut into bite-size pieces)

instructions: Boil the pasta in well-salted water until just al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
Heat the oil in a wide pan. Season the chicken with half the salt and pepper, then cook for 6–8 minutes until browned and the centre reaches 74°C. Transfer to a plate.
In the same pan, cook the bell pepper and sweetcorn for 3 minutes. Add the garlic for the final 30 seconds, then transfer the vegetables to the chicken.
Melt the butter over medium-low heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 90 seconds without browning. Add the warm milk gradually, whisking until smooth.
Simmer the sauce for 4–5 minutes until it coats a spoon. Stir in the cheese, oregano, chilli flakes and remaining seasoning.
Fold in the pasta, chicken and vegetables. Loosen with a little reserved pasta water and serve while creamy.

variants.name: Creamy Chicken Alfredo Pasta
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Boil the fettuccine in salted water until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of cooking water before draining.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the oil with 1 tablespoon butter and cook the chicken for 6–8 minutes, turning until browned and 74°C at the thickest point. Set aside.
Lower the heat and melt the remaining butter in the same pan. Cook the garlic for 30 seconds without colouring it.
Add the cream and milk. Bring only to a gentle simmer, then stir in the parmesan a handful at a time until smooth.
Add the drained pasta and chicken. Toss over low heat, adding reserved pasta water little by little until the sauce is glossy rather than thick or clumpy.
Taste for seasoning, scatter over parsley and serve immediately.

variants.name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Boil the pasta until al dente. Save 1 cup of its cooking water, then drain.
Season the chicken. Heat the oil and 1 tablespoon butter, then cook the chicken until golden and 74°C inside. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining butter and mushrooms. Cook over medium-high heat for 6–7 minutes until their released liquid evaporates and the edges brown.
Add garlic and thyme for 30 seconds. Pour in milk and cream, then simmer gently for 4 minutes.
Stir in parmesan, return the chicken and add the pasta. Toss with enough reserved water to keep the sauce fluid.
Finish with black pepper, check the salt and serve immediately.

variants.name: Creamy Chicken Fajita Pasta
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Cook the penne until al dente. Reserve 1 cup pasta water and drain.
Combine paprika, cumin, chilli, oregano and salt. Coat the chicken with half the spice mix.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil and cook the chicken for 6–8 minutes until browned and 74°C inside. Remove it from the pan.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the onion and peppers over high heat for 4 minutes so they retain some bite. Add garlic and the remaining spice mix for 30 seconds.
Reduce the heat. Add milk and cream, simmer gently for 4 minutes, then melt in the cheese without boiling hard.
Return the chicken, add the pasta and toss until coated. Loosen with pasta water and finish with citrus juice.

variants.name: Spicy Chicken Red Sauce Pasta
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Cook the penne in salted water until one minute short of al dente. Reserve 1 cup cooking water and drain.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil. Season and sauté the chicken for 6–8 minutes until browned and cooked to 74°C, then remove.
Add the remaining oil and soften the onion and bell pepper for 5 minutes. Stir in garlic, chilli flakes, chilli powder and oregano for 30 seconds.
Add tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, sugar and salt. Simmer uncovered for 12–15 minutes until the raw tomato taste has gone.
Return the chicken and add the pasta. Toss for 2 minutes, loosening with reserved water so the sauce clings evenly.
Adjust chilli and seasoning before serving.

variants.name: Vegetable Red Sauce Pasta
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Cook the pasta in salted water until al dente. Reserve 1 cup cooking water and drain.
Heat the oil and soften the onion and carrot for 5 minutes. Add the peppers, courgette and mushrooms and cook for another 6 minutes.
Stir in garlic, oregano and chilli flakes for 30 seconds, followed by the tomato paste.
Add crushed tomatoes, sugar and salt. Simmer uncovered for 12–15 minutes until slightly reduced and the vegetables are tender.
Add the pasta and toss for 2 minutes, using reserved water as needed so the sauce coats every piece.
Taste for seasoning and serve hot.

variants.name: Spaghetti with Beef Meat Sauce
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Heat the oil and cook the onion and carrot over medium heat for 6–7 minutes until soft. Add garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the beef mince, breaking it into small pieces. Cook until well browned with no pink remaining.
Stir in tomato paste, oregano, thyme and chilli. Add crushed tomatoes, sugar, salt and pepper.
Simmer partially covered for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and rich. Add a splash of water if it catches.
Meanwhile boil the spaghetti until al dente, reserving 1 cup of its water before draining.
Toss the spaghetti with enough meat sauce to coat, loosening with pasta water. Spoon the remaining sauce over each serving.

variants.name: Pakistani Homestyle Chicken Jalfrezi (Boneless Chicken)

ingredients.text: 1/2 large onion, diced, approx half cup

instructions: Warm 3-4 tbsp of oil in a wok or saucepan with a lid.
Stir in the onions and saute on medium heat until the edges start to change colour.
Stir in the chicken, ginger paste, garlic paste, and spices and saute until the colour changes.
Mix in the tomatoes and simmer covered until the chicken is tender. This takes me roughly 20 minutes from previously frozen chicken, fresh is usually quicker.

Stir in the soy sauce, green peppers, black pepper, and one green chili and mix well and cook partially covered until the green pepper is cooked to your desired doneness. Tender-crisp takes 5 to 7 minutes.
Final steps: adjust consistency, and then seasoning, and Stir in the remaining green chilies slit lengthwise.

variants.name: Cheesy Baked Macaroni
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C. Boil the macaroni for 2 minutes less than the packet recommends, then drain.
Melt 3 tablespoons butter. Whisk in flour and cook for 90 seconds. Gradually whisk in warm milk and simmer until lightly thickened.
Remove from the heat. Stir in mustard, pepper, half the cheddar and half the mozzarella until smooth, then season to taste.
Combine the sauce with the macaroni and transfer to a greased baking dish.
Mix the breadcrumbs with the remaining melted butter. Scatter the remaining cheeses and buttered crumbs over the macaroni.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until bubbling and golden. Rest for 8 minutes before serving.

variants.name: Creamy Chicken Macaroni Salad
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Poach or pan-cook the chicken until it reaches 74°C. Cool completely, then cut into small cubes.
Boil the macaroni until just tender. Drain, rinse under cold water and leave until completely cool and dry.
Blanch the peas for 2 minutes and cool them. Place the macaroni, chicken, peas, corn, carrot and pepper in a large bowl.
Whisk mayonnaise, yogurt, mustard, lemon juice, sugar, pepper and salt until smooth.
Fold the dressing through the salad. Chill, covered, for at least 1 hour.
Stir before serving and keep refrigerated; do not leave the salad at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

variants.name: Pakistani Chicken Macaroni
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Boil the macaroni until al dente, rinse briefly with cool water and drain well.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok or wide pan. Season and stir-fry the chicken for 6–8 minutes until browned and 74°C inside, then remove.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry onion, carrots and cabbage over high heat for 3 minutes. Add peppers and garlic for another 2 minutes.
Mix ketchup, chilli garlic sauce, soy sauce, vinegar and black pepper. Pour the mixture into the pan and let it bubble for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken and add the macaroni. Toss over high heat for 2–3 minutes until evenly coated and hot.
Taste before adding more salt because soy sauce is already salty.

variants.name: Pakistani Keema Macaroni
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Boil the macaroni until just al dente, drain and set aside.
Heat the oil and cook the onions until light golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and stir for 1 minute.
Add the beef mince. Break it up thoroughly and cook over medium-high heat until no pink remains and its moisture has evaporated.
Add chilli, cumin, coriander, salt, tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook for 10–12 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes collapse and oil begins to separate.
Add the pepper and peas with 0.5 cup water. Cover and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in garam masala.
Fold in the macaroni and cook together for 3 minutes. Finish with coriander and adjust seasoning.

variants.name: Pakistani Vegetable Macaroni
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Boil the macaroni until al dente, rinse briefly and drain thoroughly.
Heat the oil in a wok. Stir-fry onion and carrots over high heat for 2 minutes.
Add cabbage, peppers, peas, corn and garlic. Continue stir-frying for 4–5 minutes so the vegetables cook but retain some bite.
Mix ketchup, chilli garlic sauce, soy sauce, vinegar, pepper and salt, then add to the wok.
Fold in the macaroni and toss over high heat for 2–3 minutes until evenly coated and steaming.
Taste and balance with a little extra vinegar or chilli sauce if needed.

variants.name: Pakistani Masala Omelette

ingredients.item: ghee (or 1 tbsp neutral oil (sunflower or corn))
ingredients.text: 1 tbsp ghee (or 1 tbsp neutral oil (sunflower or corn))

instructions: Pre-heat your grill/broiler.
Beat two eggs in a small bowl and Stir in onion, coriander, green chili, haldi, cayenne and salt. Whisk well.
Put a small frying pan on medium heat and Stir in ghee/oil.
Pour egg mixture into frying pan and keep swirling till the egg mixture is well distributed.
After 2-3 minutes, you will see the edges begin to crisp up. At this point, you can either flip the omelette over, or if Aim for to be cautious, Put it under the grill till golden, about 2 minutes.

dish_families.name: Pakistani Palak Paneer - Richly flavored, Dhaba Style

variants.name: Pakistani Palak Paneer - Richly flavored, Dhaba Style
variants.dish_family: Pakistani Palak Paneer - Richly flavored, Dhaba Style

ingredients.preparation: recommended: south asian, more in post
ingredients.text: 340 g frozen spinach (recommended: south asian, more in post)
1 tbsp crushed garlic or garlic paste
1/2 tbsp grated ginger or ginger paste

instructions: If you are using prefried paneer or don't want fried paneer you can skip this step, but otherwise cut your paneer into small cubes and pan Cook in a little oil until golden on each side. Soak the paneer briefly in salted water and drain - this will. Warm 3-4 tbsp of oil in a saute pan or wok on medium high.

Stir in your diced onions, green chilies, and cumin seeds to the pan and cook till the onions take on an amber hue. Stir in in your ginger and garlic, give it a stir and cook for a minute to cook the rawness out.
Stir in in your tomatoes, salt, chili flakes, and turmeric. Cover your saute pan with a lid and cook for 2 minutes.

Continue to cook the tomato mixture for another 3-5 minutes or until the oil starts to rise above the tomato mix. You can put your frozen spinach in, turn the heat down to medium, and cook covered for 5 minutes.

Remove the lid, mix well, and cook uncovered on medium high heat for another 5-7 minutes, the mix will look cohesive and rich. Run your mix (and 2 ice cubes if you are in a rush) through a chopper, mini food processor or blender along with 1-2 tbsp of cream (or yoghurt).

Put your mix back in the pan along with 1 tbsp more of oil and your kasuri methi. the extra oil is because your blended mix will burn quickly otherwise. Cook on low heat, covered for about 5-7 minutes or until the mix starts to separate a little.
Stir in your paneer cubes, cook for low, covered for 5 minutes and serve!

source_attributions.recipe_title: Pakistani Palak Paneer - Richly flavored, Dhaba Style

variants.name: Pakistani Pickled Red Onions

ingredients.text: 2 small red onions (cut in half rings)

instructions: Wash and dry the vegetables thoroughly, then slice them to the stated size.
Warm or mix the vinegar, salt, sugar and measured spices until the salt and sugar dissolve.
Pack the vegetables into a clean jar and cover completely with the pickling liquid.
Cool, seal and refrigerate for the stated resting time before serving.

variants.name: Pakistani Saffron Milk

ingredients.preparation: crushed in a pestle and mortar
ingredients.text: 1 tsp saffron strands, (crushed in a pestle and mortar)
6 green cardamom pods, (shells removed, seeds extracted)

instructions: Crush saffron threads in a pestle and mortar and transfer to a bowl. Stir in 3 tbsp milk.
Beat the cream in a chilled bowl with a whisk or an electric mixer just until it holds a loose peak.
Put milk in a medium-sized sauce pan on medium-low heat. Stir in cardamom seeds and bring to a simmer.
While milk is still warm (it should not be hot), Stir in saffron water, honey and cardamom powder. Stir well to incorporate.
Transfer to serving glasses and Stir in dollop of cream and sprinkle with crushed pistachios before serving.

variants.name: Pakistani Soya Aloo ki Sabzi
instructions: Peel the potatoes, cut into large wedges and and then dice those into 1/2 cm thick slices. If you prefer to cut them another way that is fine too.
Warm oil in a pan on medium heat.
Stir in the cumin seeds and whole red chillies. When the cumin seeds crackle turn down the heat a little and Stir in the chilli flakes.
In go the potatoes and salt, give it all a little whirl and let the potatoes cook for 20 minutes on low heat. Do not Stir in water.
When the potatoes are done taste, adjust seasoning and and then Stir in the chopped dill. Gently stir and cover the pot.

variants.name: Pakistani Style Deep-fried Shrimp Recipe

ingredients.text: 1 pound ~500 grams jumbo shrimp or prawn (peeled, deveined and thawed)
1 cup neutral oil (canola, sunflower or vegetable )

instructions: In a large bowl, Stir in the beaten egg and all marinade ingredients (cilantro, chili, ginger, garlic, salt, red chili powder and lemon juice). Mix until well-blended.
Stir in shrimp/prawn to the marinade, and coat well.
Stir in 1 cup flour, baking soda, white pepper and salt. Mix well. Stir in water gradually, mixing it with a fork until well-blended.
Drain the egg marinade into the batter mixture, leaving the shrimp/prawn behind.
Beat the egg marinade into the flour batter with a fork until smooth.
In a separate plate or bowl, pour 1⁄2 all purpose flour to coat the shrimp/prawn, and Put it right besides the stove. In a small saucepan, heat oil.
Dip the shrimp/prawn into the batter, and and then coat it really well with the dry flour. Spoon the flour over it if you have to, and Stir in more as needed.

Once the oil is hot, gradually lower the battered shrimp into saucepan, and Cook each side for roughly 1 1⁄2 minute until crispy. Once the oil is piping hot, you can gradually lower the heat as you make your way to the rest of the shrimp/prawn.
Once done, Put the prepared shrimp/prawn on it to drain.

variants.name: Pakistani Tomato Omelette

ingredients.item: chopped fresh coriander/cilantro leaves and stems
ingredients.text: 2 tbsp chopped fresh coriander/cilantro leaves and stems (1 tbsp + 1 tbsp)

instructions: Put a saucepan on medium-high heat and Stir in oil.

After the oil has heated up for two minutes, Stir in the garlic, haldi and zeera powder. Sauté till the garlic is golden around the edges (make sure it does not turn brown, as it will taste bitter and rancid).

Stir in chopped tomatoes, chili flakes and salt and stir (careful, tomatoes may splatter). Cover the saucepan with a lid and turn heat to medium. Leave to simmer for twenty minutes till tomato sauce has thickened.
Remove from heat and set aside.
Whisk eggs and set aside.

Put frying pan on medium-high heat and Stir in oil, onions, salt, dhania powder, haldi and sauté till onions are golden and caramelised around the edges. This requires constant stirring and will take about 10-15 minutes.
When onions are caramelised (bronze), Stir in red chili flakes and pour the whisked eggs in. Gently stir, mixing onions with the whisked eggs. Turn heat down to medium.

Working quickly (because you don't want the egg mixture to overcook), Stir in tomato sauce into the egg mixture a teaspoon at a time, creating a dotted pattern across the omelette. Allow egg mixture to cook for 3-4 more minutes, keeping a keen eye on the pan. As.
For a soft-centred omelette, keep it under the grill for 3 minutes.

variants.name: Chocolate Trifle
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.

ingredients.text: 400 ml whipping cream (whipped to soft peaks)

instructions: Mix custard powder with 150 ml milk. Heat the remaining milk and sugar, whisk in the slurry and cook until thick.
Remove from the heat and stir in 100 g chopped chocolate until smooth. Cover the surface and cool completely.
Layer half the cake in a serving bowl, followed by half the chocolate custard and half the biscuit crumbs.
Repeat the cake, custard and biscuit layers.
Top with whipped cream and the remaining 50 g chopped chocolate.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours before serving.

variants.name: Mango Trifle
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.

ingredients.text: 400 g plain sponge cake (cut into cubes)
300 ml whipping cream (whipped to soft peaks)

instructions: Mix the custard powder with 100 ml milk. Heat the remaining milk and sugar, whisk in the slurry and cook until thick. Cover the surface and cool fully.
Set aside one-quarter of the best mango pieces for the top.
Arrange half the sponge in a bowl and drizzle with half the mango juice. Add half the mango and half the cooled custard.
Repeat the sponge, juice, mango and custard layers.
Spread whipped cream over the top and decorate with reserved mango and pistachios.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours. Keep refrigerated until serving.

variants.name: Pakistani Fruit Custard Trifle
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.

ingredients.text: 400 g plain sponge cake (cut into cubes)

ingredients.item: halal-certified jelly crystals or agar jelly
ingredients.text: 85 g halal-certified jelly crystals or agar jelly (prepared and set)
400 ml whipping cream (whipped to soft peaks)

instructions: Prepare the halal-certified or agar-based jelly according to its packet, chill until firmly set, then cut into cubes.
Mix custard powder with 150 ml of the milk until smooth. Heat the remaining milk with sugar, whisk in the slurry and cook until thick. Cover the surface and cool completely.
Place half the sponge in a deep serving bowl. Add half the drained fruit, apple, banana and jelly.
Spoon over half the cold custard. Repeat the sponge, fruit, jelly and custard layers.
Top with whipped cream, cover and chill for at least 4 hours so the layers settle.
Keep refrigerated and serve within 24 hours because the fresh banana softens quickly.

variants.name: Aloo (Potato) Pakoras

ingredients.text: 1 teaspoon sea salt (or more, to taste)
1 lb 450g yellow potatoes, approx 3 medium potatoes

instructions: This ensures they cook through while staying tender inside.

In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the chickpea flour, baking powder, chili flakes, cumin, and salt. Gradually Stir in the ice water, whisking until the batter is smooth and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon—similar to pancake batter. Stir in the sliced potatoes and.
Warm oil in a large pot over medium-high heat until it reaches 350°F (175°C).

Cook for 60-90 seconds, or until golden brown and crisp. Adjust the heat as needed to maintain 350°F-360°F (175°C-182°C)—if the oil is too hot, the pakoras will brown too quickly without cooking through.
Remove the pakoras with a slotted spoon and transfer to a large platter lined with paper towels.

variants.name: Chicken Pakoray - Crunchy & Chatpatay

ingredients.text: 3/4 lb chicken (roughly two smaller chicken breasts) (cut into 1 inch pieces)
1 minced green chili (use half if they're spicy)

instructions: Mix your marinade ingredients into the chicken and set aside for 20 minutes.
Stir in your dry mix and mix well, and slowly Stir in in water 1 tbsp at a time (I usually use 3) until you have a coating like in the image.
Warm about an inch of oil in a pan and Cook for a 3 minutes on each side or until deeply golden.
For optimal crunch drain them on a wire rack.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Prepare and dry the vegetables or filling ingredients.

Mix the flour or besan with red chilli powder, chilli flakes, cumin powder, coriander powder, turmeric, freshly chopped coriander leaf; add water gradually to make a coating batter or cohesive filling.
Heat the oil to medium-high. Fry in small batches until crisp and evenly golden, allowing the oil to recover between batches.
Drain well and serve hot with the listed chutney or garnish.

variants.name: Crispy Onion Pakoda Recipe | How to Make Onion Pakoras

ingredients.text: 2 Tbsp corn flour (or more gram flour)
1/2 tsp sea salt (or more, to taste)

ingredients.item: fresh cilantro ((25g), coarsely chopped (leaves and stalks))
ingredients.text: 1 cup fresh cilantro ((25g), coarsely chopped (leaves and stalks))

ingredients.item: red or yellow onion ((175g), thinly sliced into 1/2 moon shapes)
ingredients.text: 1 cup red or yellow onion ((175g), thinly sliced into 1/2 moon shapes)

ingredients.item: Thai bird’s eye green chili (chopped finely with kitchen shears (use 1 if you prefer it less spicy))
ingredients.text: 2 Thai bird’s eye green chili (chopped finely with kitchen shears (use 1 if you prefer it less spicy))

instructions: Put the sliced onions in a bowl of ice water and let them soak.
In a large mixing bowl, Mix gram and corn flour with cumin, red chili flakes, salt, baking powder, baking soda, turmeric, fresh cilantro, and green chilies. Stir to Mix.
Squeeze excess water from the onions and Stir in them to the bowl. Gradually Stir in the ice water, a little at a time, stirring after each addition.
Warm 3 inches (7.5cm) of oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat until it reaches 350°F (175°C).
Cook, agitating and turning the pakoras, for 11⁄2 to 2 minutes, until golden brown and fully cooked through. Adjust the heat as needed to maintain 350°F-360°F (175°C-182°C).
Remove the cooked pakoras with a slotted spoon and transfer to a platter lined with paper towels.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: You will have to deep-Cook the pakoras.
Put oil (2-3 inches of it) in wok on medium-high heat.
Roast some zeera (whole cumin seeds and set aside).
In a mixing bowl, Mix besan (gram flour) with salt, baking powder (a tsp should do), roasted zeera (cumin seeds) and red pepper flakes.
Slowly Stir in in water, a few drops at a time, and stir till it becomes a thick mixture, a bit like cake batter.
If it burns, turn the heat a tad bit lower-you don't want a crisp crust with raw vegetables inside.
They should take about 1 minute per side, to become a golden brown.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Crispy Onion Pakoda Recipe | How to Make Onion Pakoras

variants.name: Pakora Mix & How to Make Pakoras
instructions: Mix all the dry ingredients in a clean air tight jar, they will easily last two weeks or more.

To make pakoras - take out some of the dry mix.For plain pakoras put 3/4 the amount of water to the dry mix and Cook on medium heat till golden and for vegetable ones start with half a cup water to 1 cup mix and adjust if needed.

variants.name: Ramp (Wild Garlic) Pakora

ingredients.text: 1 cup gram flour (I used @bobsredmill garbanzo bean flour⁣)

instructions: Trim white bulbs off of ramps and set aside for use in another dish (stir fries, tarka on dal, etc.).
In a medium bowl, whisk gram flour, spices, and salt. Slowly Stir in ice water, starting with a 1/4 cup. Whisk till smooth and thick.
Meanwhile, heat 3 inches of oil in a medium heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat (a candy thermometer will register 350F).
To dredge the ramps in the batter, transfer batter (in increments) to a large platter with a rim. Working in batches, Stir in battered ramp to oil, and Cook 15-20 seconds.
Drizzle chili oil on yogurt (season w salt) and dunk those pakoras into this cooling dip!

variants.name: Vegetable Pakora Recipe

ingredients.preparation: peeled and sliced into thick strips
ingredients.text: 1 medium potato (peeled and sliced into thick strips)

instructions: Prepare and dry the vegetables or filling ingredients.
Mix the flour or besan with fresh coriander, green chillies, chilli flakes, cumin seeds, coriander powder; add water gradually to make a coating batter or cohesive filling.
Heat the oil to medium-high. Fry in small batches until crisp and evenly golden, allowing the oil to recover between batches.
Drain well and serve hot with the listed chutney or garnish.

variants.name: Daal Pakora — Crispy Split Pea Fritters
instructions: Drain soaked chana dal thoroughly. Stir in to a food processor or blender. Blend to a coarse paste — not smooth, not whole lentils, but somewhere in between with visible texture.

Transfer ground dal to a bowl. Stir in onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander, red chilli powder, cumin seeds, ajwain and salt. Mix together thoroughly with your hands until everything is evenly distributed.
It should hold its shape and sizzle actively.
Warm oil in a karahi to 180°C (a small drop of batter should sizzle immediately and float up). Cook for 4-5 minutes until deep golden and very crispy, turning occasionally.
For extra crispiness, Cook the pakoras, remove, let them cool for 2 minutes, and then Cook again for 1-2 minutes. Drain on paper towels.
Daal pakoras lose their crunch within 15-20 minutes.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Daal Pakora — Crispy Split Pea Fritters

variants.name: Palak Pakora — Spinach Fritters
instructions: Stir in red chilli, ajwain, cumin, salt, chaat masala and grated ginger. Gradually Stir in water while whisking to form a smooth, medium-thick batter — it should coat the back of a spoon but drip off slowly.

It should sizzle, float and hold its shape. If it spreads too thinly, the batter is too runny — Stir in a spoonful more besan. If it forms a thick blob, the batter is too thick — Stir in a splash of water.
Warm oil in a karahi to 180°C. Hold a spinach leaf by its stem, dip into the batter, coat completely (both sides), and gently lower into the hot oil. Cook in batches of 4-5 leaves — don't crowd.
Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain briefly on paper towels — don't leave them too long or they steam and go soft. Serve within 5 minutes of frying.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Stir in salt, ground coriander seeds, chile flakes and baking soda, and mix until evenly distributed. Gradually pour in the water, mixing the batter as you pour, and whisk well.
In a frying pan or skillet, Stir in roughly 1 1⁄2 to 2-inches of oil. Heat oil until it is very hot.

Cover each spinach leaf with the batter, and carefully lower into the pan. Bring heat down to low, and Cook each side until it is an even golden brown, roughly 2 minutes each side. Adjust heat and time as necessary.

variants.name: Pyaz Pakora (Onion Fritters)

ingredients.text: 1 tsp Lal mirch powder (Red chilli powder)

instructions: Mix the sliced pyaz (onions) in a large bartan (bowl) with 1/2 teaspoon salt. Toss well and leave for 15 minutes.

In a large bartan (bowl), Mix besan (chickpea flour), chawal ka atta (rice flour), remaining salt, lal mirch (red chilli), dhaniya powder (ground coriander), zeera (cumin seeds), and ajwain (carom seeds). Mix the dry ingredients thoroughly. Stir in the egg (if using).
Stir in the chopped hari mirch (green chillies) and hara dhaniya (fresh coriander) to the batter. Stir in the squeezed, drained onions.
Pour oil into a deep karahi (wok) or degh and heat over medium-high heat.

Using a tablespoon or your hand, drop rough mounds of the onion-batter mixture into the hot oil — about 2 tablespoons per pakora. Don't shape them into neat balls — a rough, jagged, irregular shape creates more surface area, which means more crunch. Cook in batches of 6–8.

Remove pakoras with a slotted spoon and drain on a plate lined with paper towels. They should look deeply golden, feel firm, and emit that characteristic sizzling, crackling sound as they drain. Immediately sprinkle with a pinch of chaat masala (spice blend) or a tiny extra pinch of.
While the pakoras Cook, put the chai on. Let it simmer for 3 minutes, strain into mugs.

variants.name: Palak Gosht (Mutton Curry with Spinach)

ingredients.text: 1 lb. mutton with bone (chopped in small pieces)
1 medium-sized yellow onion (sliced in half rings)

instructions: Warm oil in a stockpot. When hot, Stir in chopped onions, and Cook on medium heat until soft and translucent, about 7-10 minutes.
Stir in crushed ginger and garlic, and Cook for roughly 30 seconds.
Stir in green chili (if using) and ground spices, and Cook for roughly 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, and the remainder of the salt. Cook tomatoes on high heat until soft, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in chopped mutton, and continue to Cook on high heat for 15-20 minutes.
Stir in roughly 3 cups water (just enough for the meat to be completely submerged) and cover with a tight fitting lid. Bring to simmer, and let the curry cook on medium-low heat for 1 1⁄2 hour.
Lift cover and fold in diced spinach. Partially cover the stockpot, and let it simmer for another 30 minutes.
If there is still excess liquid, remove lid and increase heat to high to boil out some of the water.

variants.name: Pallo Fish Curry Sindhi

ingredients.text: 1.5 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
1.5 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Rub fish pieces with salt, a pinch of haldi, and ajwain. Set aside 15 minutes.
Warm oil in a flat-bottomed pan. Stir in kari patta and let sizzle. Stir in chopped piyaz and cook until golden brown.
Stir in 200ml water to masala. Stir and bring to a gentle simmer.
Lower fish steaks into the simmering masala very carefully. Don't stir — pallo is delicate and will break apart.
Cover and cook on low heat for 12-15 minutes until fish is cooked through.
Garnish with hara dhania.

variants.name: Pallo Machli (Stuffed Sindhi River Fish)

ingredients.text: 1 large (about 1-1.2 kg) rohu ya catla machli (rohu or catla fish, whole)
2 tbsp lemon ya imli (lemon juice or tamarind paste)

ingredients.item: sheets kela ka patta ya foil
ingredients.text: 2 large sheets kela ka patta ya foil (banana leaf or aluminium foil)

instructions: If the fishmonger hasn't already done it, rinse the whole fish thoroughly under cold running water inside and out.
In a small bowl, mix lemon juice (or tamarind paste), 1/2 tsp haldi, and 1/2 tsp salt into a paste. Leave to marinate for at least 20–30 minutes. If you have time, marinate for an hour in the fridge.
Blend into a coarse, thick paste — Stir in 1–2 tablespoons of water only if needed to get the blender moving.

CHOOSE YOUR COOKING METHOD — OPTION A (BAKING, PREFERRED): Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F). Put on a baking tray and bake for 30–35 minutes. and then open the top of the parcel and bake for another 10–15 minutes to brown and crisp the skin.

CHOOSE YOUR COOKING METHOD — OPTION B (PAN-FRIED): Heat 3 tbsp of oil in a large, heavy tawa (flat griddle) or a wide karahi over medium heat. Cook undisturbed for 6–8 minutes. Cook the other side for 6–8 minutes.
Garnish with lemon wedges and fresh coriander.

variants.name: Sindhi Fried Pallo Fish

ingredients.text: 1.5 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)
1 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)

instructions: Mix ajwain, haldi, laal mirch powder, dhania powder, adrak lahsun paste, lemon juice, and salt into a paste. Marinate minimum 20 minutes.
Warm oil in a flat-bottomed karahi or tawa to 180°C. Stir in fish pieces without crowding. Cook on medium-high heat for 3-4 minutes per side until golden-brown and crispy.
Drain on a wire rack (not kitchen paper, which steams the fish).

variants.name: Paneer Jalfrezi

ingredients.item: oil, for the onion and tomato base
ingredients.preparation: and additional oil to fry the paneer
ingredients.text: 1/2 cup oil, for the onion and tomato base (and additional oil to fry the paneer)

ingredients.preparation: bell peppers, cubed. I prefer using a variety of colours
ingredients.text: 2 capsicums (bell peppers, cubed. I prefer using a variety of colours)

instructions: Prepare all ingredients before heating the pan.
Warm the cooking fat and cook oil, for the onion and tomato base, onions, diced, garlic, ginger until softened and aromatic.
Stir in chilli flakes, coriander powder, cumin seeds, paprika, turmeric, Fresh coriander, then add the oil, for the onion and tomato base and coat it thoroughly in the masala.
Add the listed liquid ingredients as needed, cover and simmer until the main ingredient is fully cooked.
Reduce the sauce to the intended consistency, adjust the seasoning and finish with ginger, coriander powder, Fresh coriander.

variants.name: Paneer Reshmi Handi

ingredients.item: boneless chicken, cut into small strips
ingredients.text: 750 g boneless chicken, cut into small strips (2 small chicken breasts)

ingredients.item: green pepper or 1/2 a large one thinly sliced into strips
ingredients.text: 1 small green pepper or 1/2 a large one thinly sliced into strips
1/3 cup yoghurt (whipped and at room temp)

ingredients.preparation: as much as you can handle!
ingredients.text: sliced green chilies (as much as you can handle!)

instructions: Whisk your yoghurt well and keep near where you are cooking. Warm a few tbsp of oil in a wok (with a lid) or saute pan.
Stir in your onions and cook on medium heat until they start to change color. Stir in your ginger and garlic paste and let it cook for a minute.

Stir in your chicken to that base and saute, moving frequently until the chicken pieces have all changed colour. Go in with your spices and give it a quick cook, about a minute or so before adding in your yoghurt and a splash of water.

Let the chicken simmer, covered, until tender - this takes about 10 minutes tops. Warm your charcoal and Stir in your green peppers, butter, and cream into the chicken mix, cooking the peppers until just tender crisp.

If the handi is warm and then just stir in the cheese, and if not and then turn the heat on just enough to warm it and melt the cheese in. Turn off immediately (cheese burns!), Stir in your finishing touches of freshly cracked black pepper and green chilies and serve.

variants.name: Panjeeri | Panjiri

ingredients.preparation: can be adjusted to personal preference
ingredients.text: 1/2-1/4 cup raisins (can be adjusted to personal preference)

instructions: Measure and chop the nuts, seeds and dried fruit before heating the pan.
Warm the ghee and toast the flour or semolina slowly, stirring continuously, until nutty and evenly golden.
Toast the nuts and seeds as needed, then combine them with the roasted flour mixture.
Cool slightly before mixing in the sugar and remaining aromatics; break up any lumps.
Cool completely and store airtight.

variants.name: Pappa Roti Recipe

ingredients.preparation: cut into equal pieces, freeze after cutting
ingredients.text: 5 tbsp butter (cut into equal pieces, freeze after cutting)
2 tsp coffee (dissolved in 2 tsp hot water)

instructions: Mix the dough ingredients in the bowl of your stand mixer, and use the dough hook to stir on low till combined and then turn the speed up to 6 and knead for 5 minutes. If the dough feels sticky Stir in another tbsp of flour and knead for another 3-4 minutes at which point if you pick up a piece of.

The dough should stretch in a very thin film around the butter - a too thick dough won't bake through or give you a doughy center. Flatten each piece out into a circular shape, Put the pat of frozen butter inside and form a circle making sure the bottom is well sealed.

Leave them to rise on a lined baking tray for 45 minutes. Gently cover the top with a kitchen towel or a piece of plastic wrap. Beat the icing sugar and butter together, first on low for the icing sugar to incorporate and then on higher speed. Best to do this with a hand mixer or a whisk.

Stir in the egg and whip and then the vanilla and coffee. The mix may look curdled and that's fine. Mix in the flour until just combined and then put your coffee topping in an icing bag or use a ziploc instead of one.

Snip a 1 cm piece off the end of the icing bag and pipe the coffee topping on in swirls over the coffee buns, making sure to cover the surface. Bake for 17 minutes - the coffee buns should be a medium brown and well domed.

variants.name: Cheats Aloo Paratha - Probably The Easiest Aloo Paratha You'll Make

ingredients.text: 1.5 tsp red chilli powder (or to taste)
2 tbsp chopped mint (optional but highly recommended)

instructions: Mix the flour, salt and listed dough ingredients; add water gradually and knead to a soft, smooth dough.
Cover and rest the dough while preparing any filling. Cook the filling until dry enough not to tear the bread, then cool it.
Divide and roll the dough. Add the filling if used, seal well and roll again without forcing it through the surface.
Cook on a hot tawa or heavy pan, turning and brushing with the measured fat, until both sides are spotted and cooked through.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Cheats Aloo Paratha - Probably The Easiest Aloo Paratha You'll Make
source_attributions.author: Fatima Cooks

variants.name: Peshawari Stuffed Chapati

ingredients.text: 0.75 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Mix atta with salt and 1 tbsp oil. Stir in water to make a slightly firmer dough than usual — this handles the thick stuffed chapati better. Knead 5 minutes.
Mix with chopped piyaz, grated adrak, hari mirch, hara dhania, zeera, ajwain, and laal mirch. Season well.
Roll one ball flat.
Roll out to a medium-thick chapati — thicker than a regular chapati, thinner than a South Punjab paratha.
Cook on a medium-hot tawa without any fat first — about 1 minute each side. and then Stir in a small amount of ghee (about half tsp per side) and cook until golden patches appear.

variants.name: Aloo Paratha — Spiced Potato Stuffed Flatbread

ingredients.text: 4-6 tbsp Makhan ya Ghee (Butter or Ghee)

instructions: In a large bartan (bowl), Mix the atta (flour), salt, and one tablespoon of oil or ghee. Gradually Stir in lukewarm water, mixing with your hand as you go. Knead the dough for 7-8 full minutes — it should be smooth, soft, and slightly tacky but not sticky.

Boil the potatoes whole and unpeeled in salted water until completely tender — a knife should slide in with zero resistance, 20-25 minutes. Drain, peel while still hot (use a cloth to hold them), and mash immediately.

Mix the cooled mashed aloo with hara dhania (coriander), hari mirch (green chillies), lal mirch, ajwain (carom seeds), zeera (cumin), nimbu (lemon) juice, and namak (salt) to taste. Mix thoroughly. Roll into balls approximately 40g each (about the size of a walnut).

Divide the rested dough into the same number of balls as filling portions. On a lightly floured surface, roll a dough ball into a circle about 15cm in diameter. roll this stuffed ball out again, slowly and gently, into a circle 20-22cm in diameter.

Warm a tawa (flat griddle) or heavy flat pan over medium-high heat until hot — a few drops of water flicked on it should evaporate within 2 seconds. Cook for 60-90 seconds — you'll see the surface start to look drier and small bubbles will form. Stir in.

The paratha is done when both sides have golden-brown patches and the bread has cooked through — no doughy-white patches should remain. Press the edges down firmly during cooking — the edges cook last and need direct contact with the tawa. Stir in a small knob of cold.
Aloo paratha is a serve-immediately dish — unlike naan which holds reasonably well, paratha loses its crisp-outside-soft-inside texture after 10 minutes.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Aloo Paratha — Spiced Potato Stuffed Flatbread

variants.name: Aloo Paratha South Punjab

ingredients.text: 0.75 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Mix atta, 0.5 tsp salt, and 1 tbsp ghee. Stir in warm water to form a soft dough. Knead 5 minutes, cover, and rest 20 minutes.
Mix in chopped piyaz, hari mirch, grated adrak, hara dhania, ajwain, laal mirch powder, zeera powder, amchur, and remaining salt.
Divide dough into 8 balls. Dust with atta and roll to a rough 7-inch circle.
Warm tawa on medium-high. Cook each paratha dry first until bubbles form, about 1 minute per side. and then apply ghee on each side and cook until golden-brown with crispy spots.

variants.name: Parsi Custard Recipe (Lagan Nu)
instructions: Pre-heat oven to 300°F (150°C).
Bring milk to boil in a stockpot. Lower heat and stir in condensed milk and sugar. Keep stirring on low heat for 15 minutes until the mixture thickens.
In the meantime, in a large bowl whisk the eggs, vanilla extract, nutmeg and ground cardamom till foamy.
Once the milk is lukewarm, slowly stir in the egg mixture. Pour the custard into the baking dish and bake in the oven for roughly 1 hour until the custard is set.
Allow to cool and Put in the fridge for at least 2 hours.

variants.name: Patta Gobi (Fried Cabbage)

ingredients.item: mustard oil or a neutral cooking oil
ingredients.text: 1/3 cup mustard oil or a neutral cooking oil

instructions: Warm large wok for a few seconds and Stir in oil. When oil becomes to shimmer, after a few seconds, Stir in mustard seeds.
When mustard seeds begin to pop, Stir in green chilies, crushed ginger, turmeric powder, and Cook on medium heat for roughly 30 seconds.
Stir in shredded cabbage, salt and sugar. Cook on high heat for 5 minutes, coating it with the oil and spices till it begins to soften and acquire a pale yellow hue.
Remove from heat and serve with main of choice.

variants.name: Lahori Paya — Slow-Cooked Trotters

ingredients.text: 1 kg (4-6 pieces) Paya (Goat or Beef Trotters)
1.5 tsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)

ingredients.item: for garnish Hara Dhania aur Adrak
ingredients.text: for garnish Hara Dhania aur Adrak (Fresh Coriander and Ginger)

instructions: Put the paya (trotters) in a large degh (heavy-bottomed pot) with enough cold water to cover by 3 inches. Stir in the whole onion, ginger slices, a teaspoon of salt, and half the whole spices. Bring to a full, rolling boil over high heat.

SLOW BRAISE — THE LONG COOK: Return the cleaned paya to the degh with 2 litres of fresh cold water, the remaining whole spices, and half a teaspoon of salt. Bring to a boil, and then reduce heat to the lowest possible setting. Cover with the lid slightly.

About 30 minutes before the paya are done, heat ghee in a separate karahi (wok) over medium-high heat. Stir in the finely chopped pyaz (onion) and Cook for 12-15 minutes until deep golden-brown — deeper than you'd go for most dishes.

Use a chamcha (ladle) to transfer the cooked paya into the masala karahi along with 2-3 ladlefuls of the broth. Stir well to coat the trotters in the spiced masala. Cook together for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally — the masala should be absorbed by the trotters.

Let everything simmer together on low heat for 20-25 minutes, partially covered. The broth should thicken slightly — it won't be as thick as a regular curry, but it should coat the back of a spoon. The finished paya should look like a deep brown, glossy gravy with.

Garnish generously with fresh julienned adrak (ginger) — not chopped, julienned, which is traditional and important for the texture contrast. Stir in chopped hara dhania (coriander), sliced hari mirch (green chilli), and a squeeze of nimbu (lemon).

variants.name: Peanut Butter Blondies

ingredients.preparation: can use additional chocolate chips instead
ingredients.text: 1/4 cup peanut butter chips (can use additional chocolate chips instead)

instructions: Preheat your oven to 350 degrees and prep a square baking tin with parchment paper or buttered foil. Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt together in a bowl and set aside.
Beat the peanut butter and butter together till luxuriously smooth. Stir in sugars and beat well for about 1-2 minutes.
In go the eggs one by one, beat 30 seconds between additions and then Stir in the vanilla extract. Gradually Stir in the flour and beat until just combined.
Stir in the peanuts + chocolate/peanut butter chunks/chips and mix just enough to disperse, i.e. Bake for 35-45 minutes, just until a toothpick comes out mostly clean.
Give it 5 minutes and then remove the parchment/ foil from the pan and set the blondies aside on a rack to cool down. Cut into squares and serve.

variants.name: Peshawari Naan
instructions: In a small katori (bowl), mix the lukewarm water, sugar, and yeast. Stir once and leave for 8–10 minutes until foamy and fragrant.
In a large paraat or on a clean counter, Mix flour and salt. Stir in the yeast mixture, dahi, and oil. Mix together into a dough.
Oil a large bowl, Put the dough inside, cover tightly with a damp cloth, and leave in a warm Put for 1–2 hours until doubled.
Set your oven to its absolute maximum — 250–260°C if possible. Heat it for at least 30 minutes.

Punch down the risen dough and divide into 4 large portions — remember, Peshawari Naan is big. Roll each portion into a smooth ball. On a lightly floured chakla (rolling board), use your hands and belan (rolling pin) to stretch and roll each ball into a large oval.

Using a flat board or a pizza peel dusted with flour, slide one naan onto the screaming hot pan in the oven. Bake for 3–5 minutes on the top rack. Watch through the oven glass — see the naan puff dramatically into large bubbles within the first 2.
The heat of the bread will melt the butter instantly and it will soak into all those little crags and bubbles.

variants.name: Peshawari Siri Paye

ingredients.text: 500 g siri (beef or goat head pieces)

instructions: Cover with cold water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Let it boil for 10 minutes.

Stir in 3 litres of fresh cold water. Stir in the halved onions, ginger, garlic, black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, black peppercorns, bay leaves, fennel seeds, and turmeric (if using). Bring everything to a boil over high heat.

Cover the degh and cook on the lowest heat for 6 to 8 hours. Check every 1-2 hours and give it a gentle stir with a chamcha (ladle). If the water level drops below the meat, Stir in hot water to keep everything submerged.
After 6 hours, test the paye (trotters). If not done, continue cooking for another 1-2 hours.
In the last hour of cooking, Stir in the salt to the broth. Stir and taste — it should be deeply savoury and fragrant.
The broth should be thick enough to coat the back of your spoon.

Top each bowl with julienned fresh ginger, a few whole green chillies, and a generous handful of fresh coriander. The garnishes are not optional — they cut through the richness of the broth and Stir in brightness.

variants.name: Phirni
instructions: Put the rice in a bowl and cover with cold water. Let it soak for 30 minutes minimum — the grains will absorb water and become soft enough to grind. Drain the water completely.
Stir in the zafran to this warm milk and let it sit for 10-15 minutes.

Pour the remaining milk into a heavy-bottomed pateela (saucepan) or degh. Put on medium heat and bring to a gentle boil, stirring frequently with a chamcha. Once it reaches a boil, reduce the heat to medium-low.

Stir in 2-3 tablespoons of the hot milk from the pot into your ground rice and mix it to form a smooth slurry — this prevents lumps when you Stir in it to the pot. pour this rice slurry slowly into the simmering milk while stirring constantly with.
Keep stirring continuously on medium-low heat for 20-25 minutes. It should coat the back of a spoon thickly.
Stir in the cheeni and stir until fully dissolved — about 2 minutes.
Fill each one about 3/4 full as the phirni won't expand but you need room for garnish. Let them cool at room temperature for 15-20 minutes, and then carefully transfer to the refrigerator.
Just before serving, arrange the sliced pista, badam, and gulab ki pattian on top of each phirni.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Soak basmati rice for 30 minutes. Drain and Stir in to a blender with 1/4 cup of the milk. Blend to a coarse paste — not smooth powder, Aim for visible rice granules.
Pour remaining milk into a heavy-bottomed karahi. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring to prevent scorching. Reduce to medium-low.
Stir the rice paste once more (it settles) and then pour it into the hot milk in a thin stream while stirring constantly. Continue stirring on medium heat.
Cook, stirring frequently, for 15-20 minutes until the phirni is thick enough to coat a spoon — it should leave a clear trail when you draw a line through it on the back of a spoon.
Stir in sugar and stir to dissolve. Stir in saffron milk and cardamom powder. Cook for another 3-4 minutes.
Pour warm phirni into individual clay matke (pots). Let cool to room temperature for 30 minutes, and then refrigerate uncovered for at least 4 hours — overnight is perfect.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Phirni for Eid — Saffron Rice Pudding in Clay Pots

alternate_names: Phirni for Eid — Saffron Rice Pudding in Clay Pots

variants.name: Phitti Hui Coffee - a Pakistani Latte

ingredients.item: Additional Milk and Water for making the coffee
ingredients.text: Additional Milk and Water for making the coffee

instructions: Put the coffee, sugar and 2 tbsp of the hot water in a medium bowl and beat on medium for a full two minutes.

Stir in a tbsp more of water, whip on medium high for another minute, and then Stir in the water in 1 tbsp increments, whipping for 30 seconds after each until your water is used up/ The mixture will look like a luxurious coffee mousse.
Beat for another minute for additional volume.
To make the coffee Stir in a generous dollop into a mug, Stir in boiling water and milk as per taste. Mix a little and enjoy.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Phitti Hui Coffee - a Pakistani Latte

variants.name: Phitti — Hunza Buckwheat Breakfast

ingredients.text: 1 cup kuttu ka atta / phitti (buckwheat flour)

ingredients.item: khoobani ka tail ya saada tail
ingredients.preparation: apricot kernel oil or neutral vegetable oil
ingredients.text: 2 tablespoons khoobani ka tail ya saada tail (apricot kernel oil or neutral vegetable oil)

instructions: Put a heavy pan (a karahi or any thick-bottomed pan) on medium-low heat. Once warm, Stir in the buckwheat flour directly to the dry pan — no oil yet. Stir continuously with a wooden spoon for 4–6 minutes.

Remove the pan from heat briefly. Stir in the apricot kernel oil (or neutral oil) to the toasted flour and stir quickly to Mix — it will smell extraordinary. Return to low heat and stir for another 30 seconds.
Stir in the salt. and then, with the pan on low heat, Stir in warm water slowly — a few tablespoons at a time — stirring constantly. If you prefer a looser porridge consistency, Stir in more water.
Stir in more salt if needed.
Arrange the dried apricots and walnuts alongside or on top. The walnuts Stir in crunch and richness.

variants.name: Pineapple Upside Down Cake

ingredients.preparation: about 2-2.5 cups cubed or half a cored pineapple
ingredients.text: 200 g pineapple slices (about 2-2.5 cups cubed or half a cored pineapple)

ingredients.preparation: half a cup at room temperature
ingredients.text: 1 stick butter (half a cup at room temperature)

ingredients.item: vanilla extract or a few drops lemon or orange extract
ingredients.text: 1 tsp vanilla extract or a few drops lemon or orange extract

instructions: Sprinkle the brown sugar over the butter.
Arrange pineapple chunks or slices. I cut my slices about 1/4 inch thick.
Stir in the eggs one by one, beat for about a minute after each addition.
Pour in the extract you are using and beat for another 30 seconds.
Alternately mix in your dry ingredients and milk in 2-3 batches just until the ingredients are used up and a cohesive batter is formed.
Bake for 40-45 minutes depending or until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean.
Cool for 10-15 minutes before inverting on to your serving plate.

variants.name: Pinni

ingredients.text: 0.75 cup pisi cheeni (powdered sugar / icing sugar)

instructions: OPTIONAL — Cook THE GOND: If using gond (edible gum crystals), prepare it first. Heat 2 tablespoons of extra ghee in a small pan until very hot. Stir in the gond crystals — they will puff up dramatically within seconds, expanding to 4-5 times their original size and.

Put a heavy karahi (wok) or thick-bottomed degh on medium-low heat. Stir in 0.75 cup ghee and let it melt and heat through. Stir in all 2 cups of atta to the hot ghee and start stirring immediately with a chamcha.

First 10 minutes: Pale tan, raw wheat smell — like uncooked dough. Minutes 10-20: Colour deepens to a warm light brown; Minutes 20-35: The flour turns a golden-brown colour (think the colour of cardboard boxes — a warm, even tan) and the smell becomes deeply fragrant, like freshly.

Once the atta is perfectly golden and fragrant, remove the karahi from the heat immediately — residual heat will continue cooking the flour, so don't delay. Transfer to a large mixing bowl or leave in the karahi if it's wide enough. Let it cool for 10-15 minutes —.

To the warm roasted atta, Stir in: pisi cheeni, sonth, elaichi powder. Mix thoroughly with a chamcha or clean hands until completely combined — the sugar will melt slightly into the warm atta and disappear, and the spices will distribute evenly.
Stir in the chopped pista, badam, giri (coconut), chironji, and chopped kharaak if using. Stir in the crushed gond if you prepared it. Mix everything together until evenly distributed.

While the mixture is still warm (work quickly — it becomes harder to shape as it cools), take 2 heaped tablespoons of mixture (roughly the size of a large walnut) and press firmly together in your palm. Roll between your palms with firm pressure in circular motions until.
Put the finished pinni balls on a plate and let them cool completely — about 30 minutes at room temperature.

variants.name: Pomegranate and Chickpea Salad

ingredients.item: lemon (juiced and zested⁣ (keep juice and zest separate)⁣)
ingredients.text: 1 lemon (juiced and zested⁣ (keep juice and zest separate)⁣)

ingredients.item: cilantro stems (finely chopped (reserve leaves for other use)⁣⁣)
ingredients.text: 1/4 cup cilantro stems (finely chopped (reserve leaves for other use)⁣⁣)
2 tsp. pul biber or Aleppo pepper (you can sub with paprika⁣⁣)
1 tsp sea salt (or more, to taste⁣⁣)

instructions: Put all ingredients in a large bowl, reserving 1⁄2 of the lemon zest, and toss gently to blend all ingredients well.
Transfer to a serving bowl and adorn with remaining lemon zest.

variants.name: Poori Aloo - Nashtay Walay Aloo

ingredients.preparation: if using paste then use 1 tsp
ingredients.text: 3/4 tsp crushed garlic (if using paste then use 1 tsp)

ingredients.item: grated ginger or 3/4 tsp ginger paste
ingredients.text: 1/2 tsp grated ginger or 3/4 tsp ginger paste

ingredients.item: yellow fleshed potatoes roughly chopped into 1/2 inch pieces
ingredients.text: 4 yellow fleshed potatoes roughly chopped into 1/2 inch pieces (3.5 cups or 400-420g peeled)
1-2 tbsp of Achar Oil or Achar

instructions: Saute the onion in a little oil on medium heat until the edges are lightly golden.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and saute for 30 seconds.
Stir in the spices, saute for another 30 seconds.
Stir in the potatoes into the pot along with 3 cups of water and stir well.
Bring the potatoes to a boil and simmer on low heat until tender.
Mix well pressing gently to break up the potatoes a little, and then stir in the achar/oil and adjust seasoning.

dish_families.name: Prairie Girl Classic Vanilla Bean Buttercream

variants.name: Prairie Girl Classic Vanilla Bean Buttercream
variants.dish_family: Prairie Girl Classic Vanilla Bean Buttercream

ingredients.text: 1 1/2 cup salted butter at room temp
6 oz cream cheese at room temp

ingredients.item: vanilla bean paste or seeds from one pod or 2tsp VE
ingredients.text: 1 tbsp vanilla bean paste or seeds from one pod or 2tsp VE

instructions: Beat the butter, cream cheese, cream, vanilla of choice, and 3 cups of icing sugar till smooth, about 3 minutes.
With the mixer on medium Stir in the remaining icing sugar, a cup at a time for 4 minutes.
Crank up the speed and beat to luxurious fluffiness for about 3-4 minutes.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Prairie Girl Classic Vanilla Bean Buttercream

variants.name: Praline Cake
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees, grease and flour a 9 inch cake pan.
Mix the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a bowl and set aside.
Stir in eggs, beat for 1-2 minutes.
Stir in the vanilla and mix to Mix.
Alternatingly Stir in the buttermilk and dry ingredients in 2 batches each until just mixed.
Pour into prepared pan and bake for 28-30 minutes or until a skewer inserted in the middle emerges clean.
Put a frying pan on medium high heat, Stir in your notes, toast the nuts, swirling every thirty seconds or so for about 2 minutes.
Bring the brown sugar, butter and cream to boil in a small saucepan, simmer for 3 minutes and and then Stir in the vanilla and salt.
Stir in the nuts and pour over the cake.

variants.name: Prawn Masala

ingredients.text: 500 g raw prawns, (de-veined, shells and tails removed)

ingredients.item: sized tomatoes, (de-seeded and diced (1cm)- try to find tomatoes which are a bit firm)
ingredients.text: 2 medium-sized tomatoes, (de-seeded and diced (1cm)- try to find tomatoes which are a bit firm)

ingredients.item: chopped fresh coriander leaves and stalks
ingredients.text: 2 tbsp chopped fresh coriander leaves and stalks

instructions: Put a medium-size wok, or a 25cm (approximately 10 in) frying pan on medium heat.
Stir in oil and garlic and sauté for two minutes, till fragrant.
Stir in prawns, haldi, zeera powder, sukha dhania powder, salt and red chili powder and continue to sauté for three more minutes till the prawns turn opaque.
Turn heat to medium-high and Stir in tomatoes. Give the prawns a whirl with your spatula, and after one minute, turn the heat off.

variants.name: Punjabi Prawn Masala Curry

ingredients.item: green chilli. lemon slices and chopped coriander
ingredients.text: green chilli. lemon slices and chopped coriander

instructions: Prepare all ingredients before heating the pan.
Warm the cooking fat and cook onion, diced, minced garlic, minced ginger, red chilli powder until softened and aromatic.
Stir in cumin powder, coriander powder, garam masala, red chilli powder, cumin seeds, turmeric, then add the minced garlic and coat it thoroughly in the masala.
Add the listed liquid ingredients as needed, cover and simmer until the main ingredient is fully cooked.
Reduce the sauce to the intended consistency, adjust the seasoning and finish with minced ginger, coriander powder, green chilli. lemon slices and chopped coriander.

variants.name: Chana Pulao
instructions: Wash and soak your rice and set aside. Drain the can of chickpeas into a sieve or a colander and run water over it to wash off the liquid from the can.
Warm oil in a pot on medium high heat, Aim for an even thin layer of oil. Stir in your whole spices and stir Cook for a minute.

Stir in your sliced onion and cook on medium heat until the onion gets a light caramel colour. Stir in in the minced ginger and continue to cook allowing the ginger to develop golden edges and the onions to darken.

Once the onions are looking good Stir in your chickpeas, 1 tsp salt, coriander powder, and saute for 2 minutes. Stir in half a cup of hot water to the pot and simmer the chickpeas on low for 15 minutes or until tender. Taste the chickpeas - Aim for depth and assertive flavour so Stir in more salt if needed.

Drain and Stir in your rice and Stir in to the pot with 1 tsp salt and green chilies. Cook on medium high for 2 minutes. Use the same measuring cup you used for rice and Stir in 2.5 cups water (1/2 cup went in with the chickpeas).

Bring the rice to a boil and cook on medium till most of the water dries. Cover the pot and cook on low heat till the water is absorbed and the rice is cooked through. This last step takes 8-10 minutes.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Cook half the sliced onions in 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy degh (pot) on medium-high heat, stirring frequently, until they turn deep golden-amber — 10-12 minutes. These will be used as garnish and they'll crisp up as they cool.

With the ghee still hot, Stir in the remaining sliced pyaz (onion) to the pot. Cook until translucent — just 4-5 minutes, not deep golden this time. Stir in the adrak lehsan paste (ginger-garlic paste) and stir for 2 minutes until the raw smell cooks off.

Stir in the boiled kabuli chana (chickpeas) to the pot and stir to coat them in the spiced ghee. Stir in the dahi (yoghurt) and stir until it's absorbed — about 1 minute. Stir in half the chopped hara dhaniya (coriander) and the slit hari mirch (green chillies).
Pour in the 3 cups of water or stock. The liquid should just cover the rice. Bring to a boil on high heat.
Cook on the lowest possible heat for 15 minutes.
Mound onto a large platter, scatter the crispy barista pyaz (fried onions) over the top, and garnish with the remaining fresh hara dhaniya (coriander).

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Warm a heavy-bottom pot over medium-low heat. Stir in oil. Once it begins to shimmer, Stir in cloves, peppercorns, black cardamom and cumin seeds.
Cook for 7 to 10 minutes on medium-low heat until an even golden brown.
Stir in crushed ginger, garlic, and slit chiles, and Cook on low heat for one minute or until the ginger and garlic stop smelling raw.
Stir in turmeric powder, and stir until well-mixed.
Stir in chickpeas, and season with salt.
Fold in rice, and stir until well combined. Stir in water, cover with a tight-fitting lid, and bring to a boil.
Remove lid, lower to a simmer on medium heat, and let the water boil out, about 7 to 8 minutes.
Once the water has boiled out, bring the heat down to the lowest possible point. Wrap tight fitting lid with a cotton cloth, cover pot with it, and let the rice steam for 8 to 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and Put on serving platter.

variants.name: Matar Pulao Recipe (Pakistani Pea Pilaf)

ingredients.text: 1 medium yellow onion (halved and thinly sliced)

ingredients.preparation: rinsed in several changes of water
ingredients.text: 2 cups basmati rice (rinsed in several changes of water)

instructions: Warm oil over medium-low heat in a heavy-bottom pot. Cook until aromatic, about 30 seconds.
Fold in onion, and sauté on medium-low heat until it is an even golden brown, about 10 to 12 minutes.
Stir in crushed ginger and garlic, and Cook for 30 seconds to 1 minute or until it no longer smells raw.
Stir in peas, and salt. Stir until well-mixed.
Gently fold in rice, and Stir in 4 cups of water. Cover, and bring to a boil.
Remove lid, lower to a simmer, and let the water boil out, about 10 minutes.
Once the water has boiled out, remove from heat. Bring the heat to the lowest point, and let the rice steam for 10 to 12 minutes.
Remove from heat, Put in large serving dish, and gently fluff the rice with a fork.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Warm ghee in a medium pot over medium heat. Stir in zeera and sabut garam masala — let them sizzle 30 seconds. Stir in sliced onion and cook until golden, about 10 minutes.
Stir in peas to the tarka and stir 1 minute. Stir in 600ml water and salt. Bring to a boil and taste the water — it should be well-seasoned.
Stir in soaked, drained basmati to the boiling seasoned water. Stir once. Bring back to boil, and then reduce to absolute lowest heat, cover tightly, and cook 18 minutes.
The peas should be perfectly cooked — tender but still bright green and holding their shape.
After the 8-minute rest, open the pot carefully. If you see any unabsorbed water at the edges, cover for 5 more minutes on very low heat.
FLUFF, GARNISH, AND SERVE: Use a fork to gently fluff the rice, lifting from the bottom.

variants.name: Moti Pulao

ingredients.text: 2.5 cups basmati rice (washed and soaked for 30 minutes)

ingredients.preparation: first for onion masala, second for when you add rice
ingredients.text: 1 + 1 3/4 tsp salt (first for onion masala, second for when you add rice)

ingredients.item: hot water for cooking the rice
ingredients.text: 3.5 cups hot water for cooking the rice

instructions: Mix everything in the kofta section to make a smooth mix. If your mix is too wet Stir in a tbsp of breadcrumbs, otherwise shape a little piece and test Cook so you can adjust seasoning to preference.
Shape the mini koftay with lightly greased hands for easy shaping.
Warm oil in your pot and Stir in the whole spices (pepper, cloves, cinnamon, cardamom, cumin) and let them sizzle for a minute.
Stir in in the pre fried onions, garlic, ginger, chili powder, coriander powder, garam masala and 1 tsp of salt, give it a quick stir.
Pour in about 1/3 cup of hot water. Cover the pot and let it simmer on medium low for 2-3 minutes.
Maintain the heat level and Stir in your mini meatballs to the pot and cover cooked for 5-6 minutes.
Stir in in the peas and green chilies, the rice, nutmeg, mace, remaining salt and water.
Bring it all to a boil on medium high heat and cook until the water level drops below the rice. (this takes roughly 8-10 minutes).
Cover and let it steam through for 6-8 minutes and and then fluff and serve.

variants.name: Mutton Pulao Recipe

ingredients.preparation: washed, trimmed, and cut in small pieces
ingredients.text: 3 pounds (~ 1 1/2 kilogram) mutton (washed, trimmed, and cut in small pieces)
4 medium-sized yellow or red onions (thinly sliced in half rings)

ingredients.preparation: washed in several changes of water and preferably soaked overnight
ingredients.text: 3 cups basmati rice (washed in several changes of water and preferably soaked overnight)

instructions: Stir in meat in a large pot of salted water (I Stir in 1 tablespoon of salt at this stage) with black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon stick, cumin seeds, 2 sliced onions, and 1 tablespoon of crushed garlic. Bring to boil, cover pot and simmer on low heat until.
Strain the bone broth, and set aside.
In a large pot, heat oil. Once the oil begins to shimmer, Stir in the remaining sliced onion, and Cook for about 15 minutes on medium-low heat or until a deep golden brown.
Stir in crushed garlic, and Cook for roughly 30 seconds or until fragrant.
Stir in the mutton, salt, and Cook for 8-10 minutes on medium-high heat.
Stir in 6 cups of the strained mutton broth to the pot. Check for salt, and bring to a boil.
Stir in rice, and let the water boil out, about 10 minutes.
Let rice steam on very low heat for 10 minutes.

variants.name: Mutton Yakhni Pulao

ingredients.item: onions, sliced into fine and even slivers
ingredients.text: 2.5 medium onions, sliced into fine and even slivers

ingredients.item: long grain basmati rice (I recommend Veetee Premium Long Grain Basmati Rice) washed and soaked for up to 90 minutes
ingredients.text: 4 cups long grain basmati rice (I recommend Veetee Premium Long Grain Basmati Rice) washed and soaked for up to 90 minutes

instructions: Rinse and soak the rice. Prepare the mutton, bone in and measure the whole spices.

Brown the onions in the cooking fat, then cook the fresh green chillies, whole, garlic, whole, onions, sliced into fine and even slivers and black cardamoms, whole, green cardamoms, whole, coriander seeds, whole, black pepper corns, whole, cumin seeds, whole, cinnamon stick until fragrant.
Stir in the mutton, bone in; cook until lightly browned, then add water and simmer until the protein is nearly tender.
Add the drained rice and enough cooking liquid for absorption. Cover and cook gently until the rice is tender.
Rest off the heat for 10 minutes, fluff carefully and finish with the reserved garnish.

ingredients.text: 2.5 cups white basmati rice (washed and soaked for a minimum of 30 minutes)

instructions: Rinse and soak the rice. Prepare the lamb, bone in and measure the whole spices.

Brown the onions in the cooking fat, then cook the onions, finely sliced, garlic, freshly grated ginger and whole cumin seeds, finger-sized piece whole cinnamon, whole coriander seeds, black peppercorns, bay leaf, green cardamoms until fragrant.
Stir in the lamb, bone in; cook until lightly browned, then add water and simmer until the protein is nearly tender.
Add the drained rice and enough cooking liquid for absorption. Cover and cook gently until the rice is tender.

variants.name: The BEST One-Pot Chicken Pulao

ingredients.text: 2.5 cups Basmati Rice, washed and soaked

ingredients.item: of nutmeg, break/chop into a rough quarters
ingredients.text: 1 piece of nutmeg, break/chop into a rough quarters (optional)

instructions: Wash your rice in a few changes of water until it runs clear and then soak while you start your pulao. Warm a very generous lug of oil in a pot big enough to cook your pulao in.
Stir in the onions and cook on medium heat till amber. Stir in the chicken and saute until the pieces are all white.
Stir in all the remaining pulao masala ingredients except the green chillies. Mix well, saute on medium high heat for two minutes.

Let the masala come to a boil, and then simmer on low until the chicken is done. The chicken releases it's own liquid so you shouldn't need to Stir in any unless the masala seems like it will stick/burn. This can take anywhere between 25-30 minutes depending on your chicken.
Once the chicken is done Stir in the rice, green chillies, and 3.5 cups of water to the pot along with 1.5 tsp salt. Mix well and taste, it should be just a little salty.

Bring the pulao to a boil and cook partially covered until almost all the water has evaporated and then close the lid completely for 5-8 minutes until the remaining moisture has absorbed and the rice is done.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Wash your rice, soak it in cold water and set it aside.
Warm oil in a large pot (preferably non stick) and Stir in your whole spices - the cloves, black pepper, cardamom, and cinnamon. Cook for two minutes till fragrant.
In go the onions - these will take 6-10 minutes to caramelize. Aim for a dark brown colour - Stir in a splash of water immediately to stop the browning from turning into burning.
And then Stir in your ginger and garlic, stir Cook for two minutes till fragrant.
Stir in salt, coriander powder and red chilli powder. Cook for another 2 minutes.
And then Stir in the chicken and stir Cook it well till all of it turns white. The intent isn't to fully cook them, but to give the chicken a head start.
And then Stir in the rice, 3 1/4 cup water and 1 1/4 tsp salt. Stir to Mix and bring it to a boil.
Cover and simmer on medium heat for 10-15 minutes - essentially until the water is mostly absorbed.
Cook on low heat for another 10 minutes and then check for doneness.
