variants.name: Balochi Beef Pulao
instructions: In a large pot, Stir in beef with 1.5 litres water, halved onion, ginger, garlic cloves, kali mirch, badi elaichi, bay leaves, and generous salt. Bring to boil, and then simmer covered for 75-80 minutes until beef is very tender.
Remove beef and set aside. Strain stock through a fine sieve.
In the heavy pot, heat ghee. Stir in zeera and remaining sabut garam masala — let them sizzle. Stir in sliced onions and Cook until deep golden, 15 minutes.
Stir in strained yakhni to the tarka pot. Stir in beef pieces. Bring to boil.
The pulao should be fragrant with black cardamom and visually simple — no colours, no garnish.

After 10 minutes rest, open the pot and fold gently. Transfer to a large communal platter or serve directly from the deg. The rice should be fragrant with black cardamom and black pepper, with a clean, honest appearance — no food colours, no elaborate garnish.

variants.name: Kabuli Pulao (Afghan-Peshawari Rice)
instructions: Warm 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy degh (pot) on medium-high. Stir in the sliced pyaz (onion) and cook, stirring, for 12-15 minutes until deep golden-brown. Stir in the mutton/lamb pieces and sear on all sides until browned — about 5-7 minutes.

Remove the meat pieces from the stock and set aside — they'll be placed back on top of the finished rice. Strain the stock through a fine sieve into a measuring jug. You need exactly 3 cups of stock for 2 cups of rice — Stir in water.

Warm 2 tbsp ghee in a separate karai (wok) on medium heat. Stir in the julienned gaajar (carrots) and stir for 3-4 minutes until they begin to soften. Stir in the cheeni (sugar) and stir continuously — the sugar will melt, coat the carrots, and slowly caramelise.

In the same karai with remaining ghee, Cook the slivered badam (almonds) on medium heat for 60-90 seconds, stirring constantly, until pale golden. If using pista (pistachios), Stir in for the last 30 seconds.
Bring the 3 cups of strained stock to a boil in the cleaned degh. Stir in the soaked, drained basmati chawal (rice). Stir once, and then reduce heat to medium.

Once the stock is absorbed, reduce heat to the absolute lowest setting. Spread the caramelised carrots and kishmish (raisins) over the rice in a beautiful layer. Cover the degh tightly with foil first, and then the lid — the foil seals in the steam better than the lid.
Arrange the meat pieces on top.

variants.name: Kashmiri Sweet Pulao
instructions: Stir in saffron threads to warm (not boiling) milk and let sit for 20 minutes.
In a small pan, heat 1 tbsp ghee. Stir in blanched badam slices and toast 2 minutes until golden. Stir in pistachios and toast 1 minute.
In a heavy pot, heat remaining ghee over medium heat. Stir in elaichi powder and let it sizzle for 15 seconds. Stir in drained basmati and toast in the ghee for 2-3 minutes, stirring gently.
Stir in water (550ml), the bloomed saffron milk, sugar, and salt. Stir once and bring to a boil. Reduce to lowest heat, cover tightly, and cook 18 minutes.
Open the pot and gently fluff the rice with a fork — it should be a glorious golden colour from the saffron. Transfer to a serving platter and scatter the toasted dry fruits all over the top.

Transfer to a wide, shallow serving platter. Arrange the toasted dry fruits — golden badam slices, plump kishmish, green pistachios, golden coconut flakes — generously and artfully across the golden saffron rice.

variants.name: KP Chicken Pulao
instructions: In a pot, Stir in chicken pieces with 1.2 litres water, quartered onion, ginger slices, garlic cloves, badi elaichi, kali mirch, a bay leaf, and salt. Bring to boil and simmer 25-30 minutes until chicken is just cooked through. Strain and measure 750ml yakhni for 500g rice.
Warm ghee in a heavy pot. Stir in zeera and remaining sabut garam masala. Stir in sliced pyaz and cook until golden — about 12 minutes.
Stir in strained yakhni to the tarka. Bring to boil. Stir in soaked basmati.
After 18-20 minutes, turn off heat and rest for 10 minutes with lid still on. Do not open during this rest — the trapped steam finishes the cooking evenly.

variants.name: KP Rice with Gosht (Chawal Gosht)
instructions: In a heavy pot, Stir in mutton with quartered onion, ginger, garlic, badi elaichi, half the remaining whole spices, dahi, salt, and 1.5 litres water. Bring to boil, and then simmer covered for 60 minutes until mutton is very tender.
Remove mutton. Strain stock. Taste and season.
Warm ghee in a large pot. Stir in zeera and remaining whole spices. Stir in sliced onions and cook until golden, about 12 minutes.
Stir in yakhni and mutton to the tarka. Bring to boil. Stir in soaked basmati.
KP chawal gosht is served simply and directly — no garnish needed, no elaborate plating.
Open the pot after 10-minute rest. Transfer to a large serving platter or serve directly from the pot KP-style.

variants.name: Aloo Gosht Pulao

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
1.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Make a proper aloo gosht first. Heat oil in a heavy pot. Stir in whole spices, and then sliced onions — cook until golden.
Stir in water or simmer uncovered to reach the right amount.
Bring the aloo gosht and its gravy to a boil. Gently Stir in soaked basmati over the top. Carefully stir just once to distribute rice without breaking the potatoes.
After 20 minutes, turn off heat and rest 10 minutes with lid on.

variants.name: Degi Mutton Pulao

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)

instructions: In a large pot, Stir in mutton with 2 litres water, quartered onion, adrak lehsan paste, dahi, half the whole spices, and generous salt. Bring to boil, and then simmer covered for 75-80 minutes until mutton is very tender.
Remove mutton pieces. Strain the stock. If you have more, simmer uncovered for 10-15 minutes to reduce and concentrate.

In the large deg or heaviest pot you own, heat all the ghee. Stir in kali zeera, zeera, dhania seeds, and remaining sabut garam masala. Stir in sliced onions and cook slowly, stirring every few minutes, until deep golden — about 18-20 minutes.
Stir in yakhni to the tarka. Bring to a rolling boil. Stir in soaked and drained basmati.
Reduce to absolute lowest heat. Cover tightly (a kitchen towel under the lid helps seal it). Cook 22-25 minutes.

variants.name: Home-Style Chicken Pulao

ingredients.text: 1.5 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
1 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Warm ghee in a heavy pot. Stir in zeera and sabut garam masala — they'll sizzle and release fragrance within 30 seconds. Stir in sliced pyaz and cook on medium-high heat until deep golden, about 12-15 minutes.
Stir in adrak lehsan paste and Cook 1 minute. Stir in chicken pieces and Cook on high heat for 5 minutes until sealed on all sides. Stir in dahi (if using), lal mirch, salt, and 1 litre water.
Stir in or remove water as needed.
Taste the stock and adjust salt — it should be well-seasoned. Bring to a boil. Stir in soaked and drained basmati.
After 20 minutes, turn off heat and let rest, still covered, for 10 minutes.
CHECK, FLUFF, AND GARNISH: After the 10-minute rest, open the pot. Use a fork or large spoon to fluff from the bottom upward in gentle strokes — do not stir vigorously.

variants.name: Lahori Mutton Pulao

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
1 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: In a large pot, Stir in mutton with whole spices, roughly chopped onion, adrak lehsan paste, hari mirch, dahi, salt, and 1.5 litres of water. Bring to a boil, and then simmer covered for 50-60 minutes until mutton is completely tender.
Remove mutton pieces and set aside. Strain the stock through a fine sieve — have about 1 litre of beautifully fragrant yakhni.
In the same pot (cleaned), heat ghee. Stir in zeera and remaining sabut garam masala. Stir in sliced onions and Cook until deep golden, about 15 minutes.
Return the strained yakhni to the pot with the fried onion tarka. Stir in mutton pieces back. Bring to a boil.
COOK, COVER, AND REST: Bring back to boil, and then reduce to lowest heat, cover tightly, and cook 20 minutes. Turn off and rest 10 minutes.
TASTE, GARNISH, AND SERVE: After the 10-minute rest, open the pot.

variants.name: Moong Dal Pulao

ingredients.text: 150 g dhuli moong dal (split green lentils)
1 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
0.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Warm ghee in a pot. Stir in zeera and garam masala — let them sizzle 30 seconds. Stir in sliced onions and Cook until golden, about 12 minutes.
Stir in washed moong dal to the tarka and stir for 2 minutes.
Stir in 700ml water to the pot. Bring to boil and cook moong dal 8-10 minutes until just beginning to soften but not cooked through.
Stir in soaked and drained basmati to the partially cooked dal water. Stir gently once. Bring back to boil, and then cover tightly and cook on lowest heat for 18-20 minutes.

REST, FLUFF, AND SERVE WARMLY: After the 8-minute rest, open and fluff gently with a fork. The moong dal will be soft and integrated throughout the rice — some lentils will hold their shape, others will have softened into the rice slightly, creating a subtle natural creaminess.

variants.name: Wedding Pilau (Dawat Wala Pulao)

ingredients.text: 5 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)

instructions: In the largest pot you have, Stir in mutton with 3 litres water, quartered onion, 2 tbsp adrak lehsan paste, yogurt (250g), half the whole spices, and generous salt. Bring to boil, and then simmer covered for 80-90 minutes until mutton is completely tender and falling off the.
Remove mutton. Strain the stock carefully. Simmer to reduce if needed or top up with water.
Warm all the ghee in the largest heavy pot. Stir in zeera, kali zeera, and remaining whole spices. Let them bloom for 1 minute — the fragrance should fill the room.
Stir in all the yakhni to the tarka pot. Bring to a rolling boil. Taste and adjust salt — season boldly.
Transfer to large serving platters — one won't be enough.
After the 15-minute rest, open the pot ceremonially — this is the moment guests have been waiting for. Transfer to the largest serving platter you have.

variants.name: Yakhni Pulao

ingredients.text: 1 set Kharay masalay barray (Large whole spices for yakhni)
1 set Kharay masalay chhotay (Small whole spices for frying)

instructions: In a large degh (pot), Stir in the gosht (meat), 1 whole pyaz (onion, halved), adrak (ginger), lehsan (garlic), and all the large kharay masalay (whole spices for yakhni). Stir in 5 cups of water and 1 teaspoon salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, skimming off.
Remove the cooked gosht pieces and set aside. Strain the broth through a fine sieve or muslin cloth, discarding all the boiled spices, onion, and aromatics. If you have more, reduce by boiling.
Warm ghee in a wide, heavy degh over medium-high heat. Stir in the 2 sliced onions. Cook for 15–18 minutes, stirring frequently, until deep golden brown — darker than you might think is right.

Stir in the small kharay masalay (green cardamom, cinnamon, cloves) to the onion-oil in the pot. Stir in the cooked gosht pieces back in. Cook the meat with the onions and spices for 3–4 minutes, turning occasionally, until the meat has picked up some colour.
Pour the measured yakhni (stock) into the pot. Bring to a full rolling boil over high heat. Stir in the drained soaked chawal (rice).

Once the yakhni has been mostly absorbed and the rice surface looks like a cratered moon (small steam holes forming), reduce heat to the absolute lowest setting. Cover the pot with a tight lid — seal the edges with a chapati dough rope or Put a damp cloth.
Turn off the heat. Leave the pot sealed for another 5 minutes off the heat — the residual steam finishes the rice.

alternate_methods.label: instant-pot
instructions: Mix all the yakhni ingredients along with 3.5 cups of water in your Instant Pot or pressure cooker. Stir and set on Manual for 15-18 minutes, naturally release. While the meat is cooking soak your rice.
When the pressure releases strain the stock to remove the whole spices. Warm a lug of oil in a pot.

Stir in the whole spices - cumin seeds, cloves, black pepper, cinnamon sticks and Cook until they crackle and you can smell the aroma. Put the chopped onions into the pot and saute until they caramelize (8 minutes or so).

Stir in the garlic and ginger paste, saute for another minute. Stir in the chopped or ground green chillies if using. Stir in the coriander powder, red chilli powder, and 1 tsp of salt. Cook for another 30 (Stir in a splash of water if it starts to burn).
In go the beef chunks, stir for a minute so they can absorb the spices and flavors. Stir in the rice and the strained stock.

Put in 2.5 tsp of salt, bring to a boil and cook partially covered until the water is more or less dry and the pulao is done. If the rice is still not cooked shut the lid and turn the heat down, keeping it on low till cooked.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: In a large pot, (I use a 6 qt stockpot), Stir in goat meat, black and green cardamom pods, cloves, black cumin, coriander seeds, cinnamon stick, bay leaf, black pepper berries, salt, whole onion marked with an 'X', ginger, garlic and water. Put stockpot on low-medium heat and let it simmer till the meat is tender. Keep checking the meat every 20.
To tenderise, the meat will take approximately 1-1 1/2 hour. The meat I use takes 1 hour and 20 minutes to tenderise. The garlic cloves will soften up as they cook.

When the meat is tender, in a fine sieve, drain the stock. The rest of the spices will stick to the meat, do not worry about that and please don't wash it off, or you'll lose the flavour of the meat. In a heavy-bottomed pan, Stir in oil, and sliced onions. On medium heat, Cook the onions till caramelised, this will take.
Turn the heat to low. Stir in three and a half cups of stock, the soaked rice and the reserved meat.
Cover pot with a teacloth (or kitchen paper towel) and Put lid on top. Allow rice to cook for 20 minutes. Turn the heat off and allow the rice to settle and rest for 15-20 minutes.

variants.name: Zafrani Pulao (Saffron Rice)
instructions: Stir in the saffron strands to 3 tbsp of warm doodh (milk). Stir gently and let sit for at least 20 minutes.
Warm 2 tbsp ghee in a small karai (wok) on medium heat. Stir in the kaaju (cashews) first — they take longest. Stir for 60-90 seconds until pale golden.

In a heavy degh (pot), heat the remaining 2 tbsp fresh ghee plus the fruit-flavoured ghee from step 2 on medium heat. Stir in the whole spices — elaichi (cardamom), dalchini (cinnamon), laung (cloves).
Stir in 3 cups of water to the pot. Stir in cheeni (sugar) and namak (salt). Bring to a boil.
Cover the degh with foil pressed tight around the edges, and then the lid. Cook on lowest heat for 15-18 minutes.

variants.name: Qeema Pulao

ingredients.text: 1.5 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
1 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Warm oil in a wide, flat-bottomed pot. Stir in zeera, and then sliced and chopped pyaz — cook until golden. Stir in adrak lehsan paste and Cook 1 minute.
Stir in chopped tomatoes, hari mirch, lal mirch, dhania powder, and salt to the cooked qeema. Cook on medium heat until tomatoes break down and oil separates, about 10 minutes.
The qeema masala acts as your flavour base. Stir in 600ml water to the pot (the qeema masala + water = flavoured cooking liquid for the rice). Bring to boil.
Stir in soaked basmati to the boiling qeema water. Stir once. Reduce to lowest heat, cover tightly, cook 18-20 minutes.
Open, fluff gently, and scatter fresh dhania (coriander) over the top. Stir in garam masala powder as a finishing touch.
After 8 minutes rest, open the pot.

variants.name: Sindhi Peas and Carrot Pulao

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
0.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Warm oil/ghee in a pot. Stir in zeera and garam masala — let them splutter. Stir in onions and cook until golden.
Stir in gajar batons to the masala and stir well to coat. Cook 3 minutes. Stir in matar and stir.
Stir in 600ml water to the pot with vegetables. Bring to a rolling boil.
Stir in soaked basmati. Stir once. Return to boil, and then cover and cook on lowest heat for 18-20 minutes.
After the rest period, open the pot and fluff with a fork.

variants.name: Sindhi Pulao

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
1.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: In a pressure cooker or large pot, cook gosht with 1 litre water, half the whole spices, a few peppercorns, salt, and adrak lehsan paste. Pressure cook 20 minutes (after first whistle) or simmer 60 minutes until very tender. Drain and reserve 900ml stock.
Warm ghee in a heavy pot. Stir in remaining whole spices and zeera. Stir in onions and cook until deep golden, about 15 minutes.
Stir in cooked gosht pieces to the masala and stir to coat. Stir in the reserved 900ml yakhni. Bring to a boil.
Stir in soaked basmati to the boiling yakhni. Stir once gently. Bring back to boil, and then reduce to lowest heat, cover tightly, and cook 20 minutes.
Open the pot and fluff gently.
Open the pot after 10-minute rest. Cook the remaining sliced onion (reserved from ingredients list) in a small amount of oil until crispy golden.

variants.name: Sindhi Rice Khichdi

ingredients.text: 150 g masoor ya moong dal (red or yellow lentils)
1 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
0.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)
4 pieces sukhi lal mirch (dried whole red chillies)

instructions: Warm 3 tbsp ghee in a heavy pot. Stir in half the zeera and Cook 30 seconds. Stir in chopped onion and cook until translucent.
Stir in washed dal to the pot and stir with the masala for 2 minutes. Stir in washed rice and stir. Stir in 850ml water and salt.

Reduce heat to medium-low, cover partially, and cook 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rice and dal are both completely soft and the khichdi has a slightly mushy, cohesive consistency. Stir in more hot water if it seems too thick during cooking.
In a separate small pan, heat 2 tbsp ghee until very hot. Stir in thinly sliced garlic and Cook until golden, about 90 seconds. Stir in remaining zeera and dried whole red chillies.
Pour the hot tarka directly over the khichdi in the serving bowl at the table.
The sizzling tarka pour should happen at the table, not in the kitchen. Bring the pot of khichdi and the sizzling tarka separately to the table and pour the tarka over in front of your guests.

variants.name: Punjabi Style Chole
instructions: Warm oil in a saucepan and brown crushed onion on low heat for about 10 minutes. Warm oil in a heavy, non-stick saucepan. On low heat, Cook garlic for about 30 seconds.

When it changes color slightly, Stir in coriander, cumin, and red chili powder. Stir for a few seconds. Stir in splash of water to deglaze the pan. Stir in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer, and stir till the sauce thickens, roughly 3 minutes.

Stir in chickpeas, salt and black pepper. Stir and coat with the spicy tomato mixture for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, Stir in tamarind to 5 cups of warm water. Remove seed, and Stir in tamarind-infused water to the saucepan.

Bring the masala to a simmer, cover with lid, and lower heat. Let chickpeas cook for 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring occasionally to make sure the chickpeas don't stick to the pan. Stir in water as needed. After 1 hour, remove cover.
Stir in crushed onions and green chili. Stir for 5-7 minutes. Stir in yogurt and garam masala powder. Stir and remove from heat.

variants.name: Puri Chole in Under 30 Minutes

ingredients.preparation: unless your chickpeas are salty, then adjust at the end
ingredients.text: 1 tsp salt (unless your chickpeas are salty, then adjust at the end)

instructions: Saute the onion in a little oil on medium heat until it's lightly golden.
Stir in, ginger and garlic and saute for 30 seconds.
Stir in all the remaining ingredients except the teabag and mix well.
Pour a cup and a half of hot water into the pot, bring to boil and simmer for 15 minutes.
Put the teabag into the pot, mix, and simmer until the chickpeas are tender - varies by brand, but this takes another 10 minutes for me.
Lightly mash some of the chickpeas with a spoon and stir, Stir in water to preferred consistency and adjust seasoning to preference.

Stir in ground coriander, ground cumin, red chilli powder, garam masala, paprika, pepper, then add the garlic, minced and coat it thoroughly in the masala.

Reduce the sauce to the intended consistency, adjust the seasoning and finish with ginger, minced, ground coriander, a handful of freshly chopped coriander.

instructions: In a heavy-bottomed pot, Stir in meat, ginger, garlic, onion, tomato sauce, salt, chili pepper, turmeric, black cardamom pod and 250ml (1 cup) water. Stir, cover and leave to cook on a low-medium flame for one hour.
Stir/check every 20 minutes to make sure the meat is not sticking to the bottom of the pot.

Turn the heat to medium-high / high. Stir the meat rigorously for 10 minutes (in Urdu, this procedure is called 'bhun-na') till the liquid has completely evaporated and the meat turns darker. Be careful not to let the mince meat stick to the bottom of the pan, if.
After ten minutes of stirring, Stir in 250ml (approx 1 cup) of water and potatoes and reduce heat to medium.

Cover and allow potatoes to cook for 15-20 minutes. Check potatoes for doneness after 10 minutes by inserting a knife. When potatoes are done, remove lid, turn heat to medium-high and allow liquid to evaporate.
Mix in fresh chopped coriander or desired herb.
Spoon approximately 2tbsp of mince meat onto bun, Stir in your favourite condiment and eat immediately.

Stir in your diced onion and cook until the edges are golden brown. Stir in your ginger and garlic paste, saute for a minute.
Turn the heat up and Stir in your keema, stirring it frequently to evenly brown the meat. Stir in all your spices except the garam masala and mix well.
Saute your Keema on medium high heat until it becomes nicely browned - this takes a good 7-8 minutes. Stir in your chopped tomatoes and potatoes, and a cup of water and bring to a boil.

Simmer until your potatoes are almost tender (varies across potatoes but usually 10 minutes is enough here) - I leave a tiny bit of a bite so that they don't overcook and fall apart as I dry mine out. Stir in your garam masala, a squeeze of lemon, half the diced chilies, half the cilantro, and additional ginger (if using). Give it.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Warm oil in a wide, flat karahi or pan. Cook chopped pyaaz on medium-high until golden — about 8 minutes. Fine-chopped onions cook faster than sliced.
Stir in adrak-lehsan paste, dhania powder, lal mirch, zeera powder, haldi. Stir well. Stir in tamatar and cook down 6-7 minutes until tomatoes are fully incorporated and oil separates.
Stir in minced beef. Bhuno on high heat, stirring frequently, for 8-10 minutes until mince is fully browned and any liquid has evaporated. Season with salt.
Stir in diced aloo. Stir to coat with the spiced mince. Stir in 1/3 cup water, cover and cook on medium-low heat for 15-18 minutes until potatoes are cooked through.
Uncover and cook on high heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring, until most liquid has evaporated.
Sprinkle garam masala and stir through. Stir in chopped hari mirch and most of the hara dhania — stir in. Transfer to a serving dish, garnish with remaining hara dhania.

ingredients.text: 1 cup full-fat yogurt (whisked and brought to room temperature)

Stir in onions and sauté until evenly brown for 7 to 12 minutes.

Increase heat to medium-high, and Stir in ground beef and salt. Crumble with wooden spatula and Cook until no longer pink, about 5 minutes.
Stir in 1⁄2 cup room temperature water and bring to a simmer. Lower heat, cover and let the beef cook for 30 minutes. Stir occasionally to make sure it doesn't stick to the bottom of the pan.
Fold in yogurt and stir continuously on medium-low heat for about 5 to 8 minutes until the oil begins to separate from the keema and you get the desired texture.

instructions: Warm oil in a karahi (wok) or deep frying pan over medium-high heat. Stir in the diced onions. Cook, stirring frequently, for 8–10 minutes until they're light golden brown — the colour of pale caramel.

Stir in the adrak-lehsan (ginger-garlic) paste to the onions. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the raw garlic smell cooks off. Stir in the lal mirch (red chilli), dhaniya (coriander), and haldi (turmeric).

Tip in the chopped tamatar (tomatoes). Stir well to Mix with the masala. Cook on medium heat for 6–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have completely broken down and the oil starts to separate around the edges.
Stir in the minced meat and hari mirch (green chillies) to the pan. Turn the heat to high. Cook, stirring constantly, for 5–6 minutes until the meat is no longer pink anywhere.

Once the liquid has evaporated (about 10 minutes of cooking), reduce to medium heat. Keep stirring and cooking — you're looking for the oil to separate and the qeema to Cook in its own fat. This takes another 5–7 minutes.
Stir in the matar (peas) and salt. Stir through. Stir in 1/4 cup water, cover the pan, and cook on low heat for 5 minutes — the peas will steam and the flavours will meld.

3 inch ginger, halved, cleaned and julienned

instructions: Thinly slice the onions and Cook till golden brown, set aside to drain and roughly crush by hand. Dry roast the besan, Stir in the cumin seeds, coriander powder, cloves, black pepper, black cardamom, green cardamom to the mix and toast for another minute or two.

Stir in poppy seeds if using and grind your spices. Mix the ground spices and the remaining marinade ingredients (ginger paste, garlic paste, chilli flakes, yogurt, chilli powder, lemon juice, papaya paste and salt) together. Stir in crushed onions to this mix.

Thoroughly mix the above into the meat, best to do this by hand, wearing gloves if you have them. Marinate overnight for best results. Stir in a lug of oil to a heavy bottomed pan and begin to cook the meat mixture.

The mixture will release a great deal of liquid as it cooks, keep stirring and cooking on medium high heat for 10-15 minutes, the mixture will start to look cooked, Stir in a splash of water if it sticks or more oil if needed. Turn the heat down and cook covered for another 20 minutes on low heat, stirring frequently, the meat.

Stir in most of the ginger, the slit green chillies, and a tsp of garam masala, cook for another few minutes, adjust seasoning with additional salt and lemon juice. Warm a piece of coal on your stove top (you can do this on a ceramic top as well, just takes longer) till it gets seriously ashy.

Pan Cook: Heat an even film of oil up to half an inch high in a pan on medium high. Once the oil is hot Cook for 2-3 minutes per side or until golden. Deep Cook: Heat a generous amount of oil in a wok and once the oil is sizzling hot Stir in your samosas and Cook until golden.
Remember to drain on a wired rack!

Stir in CHICKEN MINCE — HIGH HEAT, NO COVER: Stir in chicken qeema to the masala. Immediately turn heat to HIGH. Do not cover, do not reduce heat.

Warm oil over medium heat in a heavy-bottomed pot until it begins to shimmer. Stir in the sliced onion and Cook until translucent, about 5 to 7 minutes. Stir in the crushed garlic and ginger, bird’s eye chiles and Cook until it stops smelling raw, about 1 minute.

instructions: WHOLE SPICE BASE — THE BALOCHI WAY: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Stir in sabut garam masala (the whole cloves, cinnamon, cardamom) and let them sizzle for 45 seconds until fragrant — you'll hear them pop and the room will smell immediately warm and.
Stir in sliced pyaaz along with roughly chopped lehsan and thickly sliced adrak to the spiced fat. Cook on medium heat for 10-12 minutes until the onions turn golden.

Stir in qeema to the spiced onion mixture. Turn heat to high and immediately break up any clumps. Bhuno on high heat, stirring continuously, for 8-10 minutes until mince is completely browned and dry.
Stir in POTATOES — BALOCHI STYLE: Stir in medium-diced aloo to the cooked mince. Stir gently to Mix. Stir in 1/2 cup water.
DRY FINISH — BALOCHI RESTRAINT: Remove the lid and cook on medium heat for 5-6 minutes until any remaining liquid has evaporated.
Balochi presentation is restrained — a small handful of hara dhania scattered over the top is sufficient. This is not the dish for elaborate garnish.

variants.name: Karahi Qeema
instructions: Warm oil in a wide steel karahi or heavy frying pan until very hot — almost smoking. Stir in chopped pyaaz and Cook on high heat for 5-6 minutes until golden. The high heat is essential — we want fast, intense cooking, not slow simmering.
Stir in adrak-lehsan paste, lal mirch, dhania powder, salt. Bhuno 2 minutes on high. Stir in chopped tamatar and slit hari mirch simultaneously.
Stir in minced beef directly to the hot tomato masala. Do not reduce heat. Break up lumps immediately and stir vigorously on high heat for 8-10 minutes until fully browned and dry.
Once mince is cooked and dry, Stir in kali mirch and continue bhunai for 2-3 more minutes.
Stir in half the hara dhania. Serve directly in the karahi — don't transfer to another dish, the presentation is part of the experience.

variants.name: Keema Bhurji
instructions: Warm oil in a tawa (flat griddle) or wide frying pan on high heat until very hot. Stir in chopped pyaaz and Cook 3-4 minutes — just until softened and slightly golden.
Stir in minced ginger, garlic, and green chillies. Stir 1 minute. Stir in qeema.
Stir in finely chopped tomato, stir on high 3 minutes until just softened — don't fully cook out.

Reduce heat to medium. Make space in the pan and Stir in beaten eggs. Let them set slightly for 10 seconds and then begin folding them into the mince — continuously scramble and fold for 2-3 minutes until eggs are just set but still slightly soft.
Off heat, stir in fresh hara dhania generously.

variants.name: Beef Qeema South Punjab
instructions: See a mix of rough pieces and some released powder.
Warm oil in a wide pot or karahi on medium-high heat. Stir in finely chopped pyaaz and Cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring regularly, until they turn deep golden-brown.
Stir in adrak-lehsan paste to the dark onions and Cook 2 minutes. Stir in the rough-ground spices, dhania powder, lal mirch powder, and garam masala (half , half at end). Stir well.
Stir in minced beef to the cooked masala. Turn heat to high. Stir in salt.
Stir in chopped hari mirch and half the hara dhania. Stir on high heat for 2-3 more minutes.
Stir in remaining garam masala, stir through off-heat.

Add the listed liquid ingredients as needed, cover and simmer until the main ingredient is fully cooked.

variants.name: Quick Whole Wheat Chocolate Muffins

instructions: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F.
Whisk the dry ingredients in a medium to large bowl.
Measure the oil and milk into a measuring cup, Stir in the remaining wet ingredients to it and whisk well.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry ones until well combined, small lumps are ok.
Stir in the chocolate chips if using.
Bake for 16 to 20 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean.

variants.name: Creamy Rabri — Lahori Style
instructions: Pour milk into a wide, heavy-bottomed karahi (wider = more surface area = faster reduction and more cream skins). Stir in cardamom pods. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring to prevent scorching.
As the milk simmers, a cream skin (malai) will form on the surface every 8-10 minutes. Do NOT stir it back into the milk.
Continue on medium-low heat for 60-75 minutes, collecting skins every 8-10 minutes and letting the milk reduce. Stir the bottom gently each time you collect a skin.
After 60-75 minutes, the milk will have reduced to about 1/3 of its original volume and will be thick, creamy, and pale golden. Stir gently to incorporate.
Stir in sugar and stir to dissolve. Stir in saffron milk. Cook for another 5 minutes, and then remove from heat.

Pour into a wide, flat serving dish (thaal) or individual clay pots. Let cool to room temperature, and then refrigerate for at least 2 hours. Garnish with slivered almonds, pistachios, and a few saffron strands before serving.

variants.name: Traditional Rabri
instructions: Stir in the zafran (saffron) threads and stir once. Let it sit for at least 15 minutes — the milk will turn a deep golden orange and smell extraordinary.

REDUCE THE MILK — PHASE 1: Pour all 2 litres of doodh (full-fat milk) into a wide, heavy-bottomed degh (pot) or pateela (saucepan). Bring to a rolling boil over high heat, stirring constantly to prevent a skin from sticking to the bottom. Once boiling, reduce to medium heat.
DO NOT stir it back in yet.

Once the milk has reduced to roughly half its original volume (about 45-60 minutes in), Stir in the cheeni (sugar) and the bloomed saffron along with its soaking liquid. Stir well to dissolve the sugar.
Continue simmering and folding malai layers for another 30-40 minutes.
Take the pot off heat. Stir in elaichi powder (cardamom) and kewra water (if using).
Transfer the rabri into a wide serving bartan (bowl) or individual cups. Let it cool to room temperature, and then refrigerate for at least 2 hours — ideally overnight.

variants.name: Baingan ka Raita or Dahi Baingan
instructions: Warm oil in a frying pan and Cook on medium heat until one side turns golden (about 2 minutes), and then flip and cook the other side (closer to 1 minute). Cook in batches & drain on paper towels.
Sprinkle lightly w salt (or chaat masala if you wish!) and put a layer down in the dish you are using.
Gently pour over your sliced eggplant.
Either way put 1 1/2 tbsp of oil in a small pan and heat.
Slice the garlic into thin rounds and Stir in to the pan along with the rest of the ingredients.
Cook the garlic so that it is golden on each side and and then gently pour the baghaar/tadka on top of the raita.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Warm a non-stick frying pan. Stir in oil. Once it begins to shimmer, Stir in slices of eggplant in batches.
Cook each side on medium-low heat until it's golden brown. I was using a non-stick pan, and each side was taking about 2 minutes.
Stir in salt to taste.

Stir in boondi, salt, whole cumin and ground cayenne⁣⁣.

variants.name: Cucumber Raita

ingredients.text: Salt and black pepper to taste

instructions: Wash, dry and cut the fresh ingredients to an even size.
Whisk or blend the dressing ingredients and measured spices until combined.
Fold everything together shortly before serving; adjust salt, chilli and acidity to taste.
Chill if appropriate and add crisp garnishes only at the end.

variants.name: The Ultimate Palak (Spinach) Raita
instructions: Warm a pan with 2 teaspoons or so of oil, Stir in your garlic clove and chili flakes, saute for 30 seconds.
Stir in your spinach/green chilies and cook for 4-5 minutes on medium high heat until the spinach wilts and the excess water evaporates. Transfer it to a bowl.
Wait 2-3 minutes for the mix to cool and and then Stir in in your yoghurt, mix it well to smooth out lumps, and and then adjust consistency and seasoning.
Warm oil for the baghaar, Stir in the curry leaves, cumin seeds, garlic, and chilies and saute on medium heat until the garlic is golden and pour over the raita.

variants.name: Vegetable Raita - Yogurt w Veggies

Season with salt when they are all done and set aside to cool to room temperature.
Stir in the garlic paste, salt, and red chilli powder to the yogurt, mix well until smooth.
Pour over the cooled veggies and stir.

variants.name: Rice Flour Pancakes

Warm 1 tbsp of oil in a non-stick frying pan on medium heat. Once hot, spoon a ladle of the batter on to the pan and cook each side for 2-3 minutes till light brown and cooked through. Remove from heat.

variants.name: Kashmiri Rogan Josh

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp Kashmiri Lal Mirch (Kashmiri Red Chilli)

instructions: Let them soak for 10 full minutes — you'll see the ghee turn a stunning deep burgundy red. Strain out the bark pieces and set aside this crimson ghee.

In a large karahi (wok) or heavy-bottomed pateela (pot), heat the remaining 1 tbsp ghee plus your ratan jot-infused ghee over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Stir in the badi elaichi (black cardamom), elaichi (green cardamom), laung (cloves), and dalchini (cinnamon).
Turn heat to high. Stir in the lamb pieces in a single layer — don't crowd them.

Reduce heat to medium. Stir in the Kashmiri lal mirch, saunf (fennel powder), and sonth (dry ginger powder) directly to the oil in the centre of the karahi. Cook these dry spices for 60-90 seconds, stirring constantly.
Here is the most important moment. Remove the pan from heat for 30 seconds to let it cool slightly. Whisk your room-temperature dahi (yoghurt) vigorously in its bowl until completely smooth.
Stir in the browned lamb back into the masala and stir to coat every piece. Stir in 1 cup of warm water. Season with salt.
After 50 minutes, lift the lid.
Turn off the heat and let the Rogan Josh sit uncovered for 5 minutes before serving.

variants.name: Kashmiri Rogan Josh — The Real Red Curry

ingredients.text: 6 whole Kashmiri laal mirch (Kashmiri dried red chilies)
2 tsp Badiyan ka phool powder (fennel seed powder)

instructions: Soak dried Kashmiri chilies in warm water for 20 minutes. Blend to a smooth, vibrant red paste. This is your color and mild heat base.
Warm ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot until smoking. Stir in black cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon.
Stir in sliced onions and Cook on medium-high heat until deeply golden — 15-20 minutes.

Stir in fresh ginger and garlic. Stir-Cook 2 minutes. Stir in the Kashmiri chili paste and cook, stirring, for 5 minutes until the oil separates from the paste — you'll see the ghee coming out at the edges.
Stir in fennel powder, dried ginger powder, and salt. Stir well and cook 2 more minutes.
Stir in the meat and stir vigorously to coat every piece. Cook on high heat 8-10 minutes, stirring constantly, until the meat is seared and coated in the red masala.
Stir in 2 cups water. Bring to a boil, and then cover and simmer on low heat 60-90 minutes until the mutton is tender.
Remove lid and cook on medium-high heat for 5-10 minutes, stirring, until excess water evaporates and the gravy clings to the meat.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Kashmiri Rogan Josh — The Real Red Curry

variants.name: Lamb Rogan Josh — Home Cook Version

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp Kashmiri laal mirch paste (Kashmiri chili paste)
1.5 tsp Badiyan ka phool powder (fennel seed powder)

instructions: Warm ghee in a heavy pot. Stir in black cardamom and cinnamon, let sizzle 1 minute.
Stir in onions and Cook until deep golden, 15-20 minutes.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste. Cook 2 minutes.
Stir in Kashmiri chili paste and cook until oil separates, 5 minutes. Stir in fennel powder, dried ginger, and salt. Stir well.
Reduce heat. Stir in whisked yogurt one spoon at a time, stirring constantly so it doesn't curdle. Once all yogurt is incorporated, cook on medium until it dries down, 8-10 minutes.
Stir in lamb pieces and stir to coat. Sear on high heat 5-7 minutes.
Stir in 1.5 cups water, cover, and simmer on low 60-75 minutes until tender.

variants.name: Roghni Naan

ingredients.text: 3/4 cup, approximately neem garam pani (lukewarm water)

instructions: In a small bowl, Mix the khameer (instant dry yeast), cheeni (sugar), and 1/4 cup of the neem garam pani (lukewarm water). Stir briefly and leave for 5-10 minutes.

In a large bowl or paraat (wide kneading bowl), Mix the maida (refined white flour), namak (salt). Stir in 1 egg, tel (oil), dahi (yoghurt), and the foamy yeast mixture. Stir in the remaining lukewarm water, a little at a time, until the dough comes together in a.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly oiled surface (use a few drops of oil, not flour). Knead for 8-10 minutes using the heel of your hand — push, fold, turn, repeat.
Cover the bowl with a damp kitchen cloth or plastic wrap. Leave for 1 to 1.5 hours, until the dough has doubled in size.
In a small bowl, beat the remaining egg with 1 tablespoon of tel (oil) until combined.
Turn your oven to its absolute maximum heat — 250°C (480°F) or as high as it goes. Let the oven preheat for at least 30 minutes with the pan inside.

Punch the risen dough down gently with your fist to release the gas. On a lightly floured surface, roll each portion into an oval shape about 25cm long and 12cm wide and about 5mm thick — think a rounded teardrop or tongue shape.

Very carefully slide 1-2 naans at a time (however many fit without touching) onto your preheated cast-iron pan or baking stone. Bake for 4-6 minutes. Watch carefully — at this high heat things happen fast.
Naan is at its absolute best in the first 10 minutes.

variants.name: Round Tres Leches Cake
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350 degrees F. Mix the ingredients for the flour mix in a bowl and set aside.

Whip the egg whites in a medium bowl on medium high heat until soft peaks form (3-4 minutes) and then gradually Stir in the 1/4 cup sugar and whip till stiff peaks form. Stir in in the vanilla extract.

Kepe the mixer on low and Stir in the flour and the 1/3 cup milk in two increments each so: half of the flour, half of the milk, remaining flour, remaining milk. Mix until JUST combined, do not over mix! Pour mixture into prepared pan and bake for 35-45 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean.
Mix the milk mix, whisk well and set aside. Whip the cream with the sugar until nice and fluffy, Stir in the vanilla and mix to incorporate.

Gently pour MOST of the milk mix onto the cake, reserving 1/3-1/2 cup for serving. Once the milk is absorbed, cover with cream, top with your fruit and chill for at least 2-4 hours before serving for the flavours to meld. When ready to serve, cut a slice, pour a little extra milk mix on to the plate and enjoy.

variants.name: Rumali Roti

ingredients.text: 1 cup maida (refined white flour / all-purpose flour)
1 cup gehun ka atta (whole wheat flour)
3/4 cup garam doodh ya pani (warm milk or warm water)

instructions: In a large bowl, Mix maida, atta, and salt. Stir in the oil and rub it into the flour with your fingertips until the flour looks like damp sand — this coats the flour proteins and makes the dough extensible rather than elastic. and then Stir in warm.
REST THE DOUGH — PROPERLY: This is non-negotiable. Divide the dough into 4 balls, brush with a tiny bit of oil, cover with a damp cloth, and rest for AT LEAST 30 minutes. 45–60 minutes is better.

Put a heavy karahi (wok) or large tawa upside down on the stove over medium-high heat. Let it heat for 3–4 minutes until very hot. The roti will be draped over the convex underside of the karahi to cook.
On a very lightly floured chakla (rolling board), take one rested dough ball and begin rolling with your belan (rolling pin). Roll, rotate, roll, rotate — working from the centre outward.
This is the nerve-wracking part. Loosely roll the thin roti around your belan (like a scroll), and then carry it over to the inverted karahi and unroll it over the convex surface.
The roti cooks fast — 30 to 45 seconds per side on a properly preheated surface. Cook another 20–30 seconds on this side.
