ingredients.preparation: mustard leaves, spinach, spring greens, arugula etc
ingredients.text: 2 lb mixed leafy greens, chopped - either fresh, frozen or tinned (mustard leaves, spinach, spring greens, arugula etc)

ingredients.preparation: known as heavy whipped cream in the US
ingredients.text: 5 tbsp double cream (known as heavy whipped cream in the US)

instructions: Prepare all ingredients before heating the pan.
Warm the cooking fat and cook onion, garlic, ginger, chili flakes until softened and aromatic.
Stir in cumin seeds, coriander powder, turmeric, then add the oil and coat it thoroughly in the masala.
Add the listed liquid ingredients as needed, cover and simmer until the main ingredient is fully cooked.
Reduce the sauce to the intended consistency, adjust the seasoning and finish with ginger, coriander powder.

variants.name: Balochi Saag Gosht

ingredients.text: 1.5 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
8 whole sabut kali mirch (whole black peppercorns)
1 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Warm ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot until very hot. Stir in whole spices (badi elaichi, laung, kali mirch) and sizzle 30 seconds. Stir in gosht and cook on very high heat until deeply browned on all sides — about 10 minutes.
Stir in roughly sliced piyaz and cook until golden. Stir in adrak lahsun paste and cook 2 minutes. Stir in tamatar, laal mirch powder, haldi, and salt.

This is the Balochi technique — cover tightly and cook on low heat for 30-35 minutes, allowing meat to cook in its own steam and juices. Check every 10 minutes. Stir in just a splash of water only if it's sticking.
Once meat is nearly tender, Stir in paalak leaves. Mix into the concentrated masala and meat. Cover and cook 10-12 minutes on low heat.
Remove lid and cook on medium-high heat for 5 minutes to concentrate the flavours and evaporate excess moisture.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

variants.name: KP Sabzi Gosht
instructions: Warm oil in a heavy, deep pot. Stir in sliced onions and cook until golden. Stir in gosht pieces and brown on all sides on high heat, about 8 minutes.
Stir in quartered tamatar, haldi, and salt. Stir and cook 5 minutes. Stir in 300ml water.
Bring to boil, and then reduce to a low simmer. Cover and cook for 45-60 minutes until meat is tender and falling from the bone. Check and Stir in water as needed.
Stir in paalak and hari methi leaves to the tender gosht. Mix gently. Cook uncovered on medium heat for 10-12 minutes until greens are wilted and integrated.

variants.name: Bathua Saag

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
0.75 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Rinse bathua leaves three to four times in a tub of water, swishing vigorously to dislodge grit.
Cover and cook on medium heat 5-7 minutes until completely wilted. Drain excess water and roughly chop.
Warm ghee in a karahi. Stir in zeera and sizzle. Stir in chopped piyaz and cook until golden brown, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in adrak lahsun paste and cook 2 minutes. Stir in tamatar, laal mirch powder, haldi, and salt. Cook until oil surfaces and masala is thick, about 7-8 minutes.
Stir in chopped bathua to the masala. Mix well and cook uncovered on medium heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until everything melds together and excess moisture evaporates.
Stir in slit hari mirch and cook 2 minutes.

variants.name: Chicken Saag

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
1 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Mix chicken with yoghurt, 1 tbsp adrak lahsun paste, haldi, and a pinch of salt. Set aside 20 minutes minimum.
Boil spinach in salted water for 2 minutes, drain, and immediately put in cold water. Blend to a rough paste.
Warm ghee. Brown sliced piyaz until golden, Stir in remaining adrak lahsun paste, cook 2 minutes. Stir in tamatar, laal mirch powder, dhania powder, and salt.
Stir in marinated chicken to masala. Cook on high heat, turning pieces, for 5 minutes to seal. and then reduce heat, cover, and cook 20-25 minutes until chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the spinach paste and mix thoroughly. Cook on medium heat for 8-10 minutes — just enough to meld flavours.
Stir in garam masala and stir.

variants.name: Methi Gosht

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
1 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Sprinkle 1 tsp salt over methi leaves. Mix and set aside 15 minutes.
Warm oil in heavy pot. Stir in chopped piyaz and cook until golden brown, about 10 minutes. Stir in adrak lahsun paste, cook 2 minutes.
Stir in tamatar, laal mirch powder, dhania powder, haldi, and remaining salt. Cook until oil separates and masala is fragrant, about 10 minutes.
Stir in 250ml water. Pressure cook 20-25 minutes or simmer covered 50-60 minutes until meat is tender. Check occasionally and Stir in water as needed.
Squeeze the salted methi leaves one more time, and then Stir in to the tender gosht. Mix well and cook uncovered on medium heat for 10-12 minutes.
Stir in garam masala, slit hari mirch. Cook 2 more minutes. Garnish with julienned adrak.

variants.name: Paalak Gosht

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
1 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Warm ghee in a heavy pot. Stir in finely sliced piyaz and cook until golden brown. Stir in adrak lahsun paste, cook 2 minutes.
Stir in tamatar, laal mirch powder, dhania powder, haldi, and salt. Cook on medium-high until oil separates and masala clings to meat, about 10 minutes.
Stir in 200ml water. Pressure cook for 20-25 minutes until meat is tender. Or simmer covered in a pot for 45-60 minutes.
Separately, boil 500ml water. Stir in paalak leaves and blanch for just 2 minutes. Drain and immediately transfer to cold water (this preserves the green colour).
Open the pressure cooker. Stir in spinach paste to the meat. Stir well and simmer together on medium heat for 8-10 minutes.
Stir in garam masala and stir. Drizzle malai over the top and Stir in julienned adrak.

variants.name: Sarson Ka Saag

ingredients.text: 1 set Namak aur Masalay (Salt and Spices)

instructions: Roughly chop everything, removing any thick stems from the sarson (stems take too long to cook).

In a large degh (heavy-bottomed pot), Stir in all the washed greens, one chopped onion, the tomatoes, green chillies, adrak-lehsan paste, lal mirch powder, haldi (turmeric), and namak (salt). Stir in 1 cup of water and stir everything together. Bring to a boil over high heat, and then.
Once the greens have cooked down and the mixture smells deep and earthy (not raw), use a hand blender directly in the pot or a potato masher to partially blend the saag.

In a separate karahi (wok), heat 2 tablespoons of ghee over medium-high heat. Stir in the remaining finely chopped onion and Cook for 10-12 minutes until deep golden brown — not pale yellow, not black, but a rich amber. Stir in 1 tbsp adrak-lehsan paste and Cook for.

Warm the remaining 2 tablespoons of ghee in a small pan until shimmering hot. Stir in the thinly sliced lehsan (garlic) — they will sizzle and turn golden in about 60-90 seconds. The moment they turn faintly golden (not brown), Stir in the whole lal mirch (dried red.

variants.name: Sarson Saag South Punjab

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
1.5 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Roughly chop all greens (sarson, paalak, bathua). Bring to boil, reduce heat to low, and cook covered for 60-90 minutes.
Mix makkai atta with 4 tbsp water to make a smooth paste. Stir in to the mashed saag, stirring continuously. Cook 15 minutes more on low heat.
In a separate karahi, heat 4 tbsp ghee on high heat. Stir in 2 sliced piyaz and cook until very deeply caramelised — almost crunchy at edges. Stir in adrak lahsun paste, cook 3 minutes.
Stir in the tarka to the saag and mix vigorously. Cook together on medium heat for 15 minutes.
Warm remaining 1 tbsp ghee in a small pan, Cook the remaining sliced piyaz until crispy.

variants.name: White Mutton Karahi (Safed Karahi)

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp tel ya makhan (oil or butter)

instructions: Warm butter or oil in a heavy karahi on medium. Stir in all whole spices and let them sizzle for 1 minute until aromatic.
Stir in minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook on medium for 3 minutes until cooked through but not browned.
Stir in mutton pieces, salt, and black pepper. Increase heat to medium-high and cook for 8 minutes, stirring often, until mutton is sealed on all sides.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in whisked yoghurt slowly, 2 tablespoons at a time, stirring continuously. Stir in green chillies .
Stir in 1/2 cup water, cover, and cook on very low heat for 45-55 minutes until mutton is fork-tender. Check every 15 minutes and Stir in small amounts of water if drying out too fast.
Once mutton is tender and most liquid has reduced, pour in the cream. Stir gently to incorporate. Cook uncovered for 5-8 minutes on medium until sauce is thick and coats the back of a spoon.
Garnish with ginger juliennes and a light sprinkle of coriander.

variants.name: Safed Karahi — The Creamy White Karahi

ingredients.text: 2 medium onions blended Pyaz Paste (Onion Paste)

instructions: Soak 50g raw cashews in warm water for 20 minutes — this softens them for easier blending. Drain and blend with 4 tablespoons fresh water until completely smooth. Separately, blend 2 medium onions with 2 tablespoons water until completely smooth.

Warm oil in a heavy karahi on medium-high heat. Stir in the raw blended onion paste. Cook the onion paste, stirring frequently, for 8-10 minutes until the raw smell disappears and it turns a pale golden colour.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste to the cooked onion and stir for 2 minutes until the raw garlic smell is gone — your nose will tell you. and then Stir in the chicken pieces. Turn heat to high.
Stir in the cashew paste to the karahi and stir it through the chicken and onion mixture. Cook for 3-4 minutes on medium heat, stirring constantly.
Stir in the heavy cream to the karahi. Turn heat to medium-high. Stir constantly as the cream heats up.

Reduce heat to medium. Stir in whisked yoghurt slowly — one tablespoon at a time, stirring after each addition. Once all yoghurt is incorporated, Stir in white pepper, cracked black pepper, slit green chillies, and salt.
Turn heat to high for the final 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly. This final high-heat bhunna evaporates excess water and concentrates the sauce so it coats the back of a spoon.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Safed Karahi — The Creamy White Karahi

variants.name: Sindhi Safed Karahi

ingredients.text: 1 kg murgh ya gosht (chicken or mutton)
2 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)

instructions: Stir in whole spices and onions simultaneously and cook very gently for 8-10 minutes — soft and translucent, not browned.
Stir in ginger garlic paste and cook on low for 3 minutes. Stir in nutmeg and mace — just a whisper. These Sindhi signature spices Stir in an exotic, almost floral note.
Stir in meat pieces and black pepper. Increase to medium heat. Cook for 6-8 minutes, turning to seal on all sides.
Reduce heat to lowest setting. Beat yoghurt well and Stir in one tablespoon at a time, stirring constantly. Take 5-6 minutes for this step — patient yoghurt addition prevents splitting.
Stir in green chillies and 1/2 cup water. Cover and cook on low for 35-45 minutes (chicken) or 55-65 minutes (mutton) until meat is completely tender.
Uncover, Stir in cream in a slow pour, stirring gently. Cook on medium for 6-8 minutes until sauce is silky and coats the meat.
Garnish with sliced blanched almonds, a sprinkle of coriander, and ginger juliennes. The almond garnish is specifically Sindhi and adds wonderful texture.

variants.name: Sai Bhaji Karachi

ingredients.text: 1 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: In a pressure cooker, Stir in all greens (paalak, methi, soa), soaked chana dal, aloo, chopped piyaz, tamatar, minced garlic, grated adrak, haldi, laal mirch, and salt. Stir in 400ml water. Pressure cook for 15-18 minutes (2-3 whistles).
If it's very dry, Stir in a splash of water.
Simmer the mashed mixture on medium heat for 10-15 minutes, stirring frequently, until it thickens and darkens.
Warm remaining ghee in a small pan until shimmering hot. Stir in thinly sliced lahsun. Cook until golden — about 45 seconds.
Pour the sizzling garlic tarka over the sai bhaji.

variants.name: Sindhi Sai Bhaji

ingredients.text: 1 tsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)

instructions: In a large, heavy-bottomed pateela (pot), Stir in the soaked chana daal, chopped spinach, diced aloo, tomatoes, pyaz, methi patta (fenugreek leaves), half the zeera (cumin), haldi, lal mirch, and 1 tbsp oil. Stir in 1.5 cups of water and the salt. Give everything a single stir to.
Bring the pot to a boil over high heat, and then reduce to medium-low. Cover tightly with a lid. Cook for 35-40 minutes, checking every 10 minutes and stirring once or twice.
Once the chana daal is completely soft (it should squish easily between your fingers), Stir in the hara dhaniya (fresh coriander). Stir it in and cook for another 5 minutes uncovered.
In a small separate tawa (flat pan) or a small karahi, heat the remaining 2 tbsp of oil over high heat until it is smoking hot.
Pour the sizzling tarka (oil, cumin, and garlic) directly over the mashed Sai Bhaji and stir it through.

variants.name: Balochi Sajji — Whole Roasted Chicken
instructions: Using sharp kitchen scissors or a heavy knife, cut along both sides of the backbone and remove it.

In a small bartan (bowl), mix the salt, coarsely ground zeera (cumin), lal mirch (red chilli), kali mirch (black pepper), juice of one nimbu (lemon), and kachri powder into a dry rub — it should be just barely moist from the lemon.

Aim for indirect heat — charcoal on one or two sides of the grill, with the centre clear. The target temperature is around 200-220°C, which is medium-high for a home charcoal grill. Stir in a few pieces of wood (fruit wood like apple or cherry is excellent.

Thread a long, thick skewer through the chicken lengthwise from tail to neck, or Put the butterflied bird skin-side up on the indirect heat side of the grill. Close the grill lid. Cook for 30 minutes without opening.

After 30 minutes, open the lid and baste the chicken generously with melted ghee using a brush or a folded piece of cloth on a stick (the traditional method). Close the lid and cook for another 20-25 minutes. The skin should be turning deep golden-brown and the fat.
For absolute certainty, a meat thermometer should read 74°C (165°F) at the thickest point. The skin should be crackly and deep mahogany-brown.
Move the cooked sajji to a large flat platter and rest for 8-10 minutes under a loose foil tent.

variants.name: Chicken Sajji — Quetta Style

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp Kacha papaya paste (raw green papaya paste)
1 piece Seekh or skewer (long iron rod)

instructions: Mix kacha papaya paste with rock salt and lemon juice. Rub aggressively into every cut and cavity. Put the chicken in a covered container and refrigerate for at least 8 hours, ideally 12-14 hours.
Balance the skewer horizontally over the fire using bricks or a grill stand. Rotate every 8-10 minutes. Total cook time is 75-90 minutes for a 1.5kg chicken.
Put a tray under the chicken to catch drippings — these gold juices are used to cook the sajji rice.
In a heavy-bottomed deg (pot), heat the collected drippings plus ghee. Stir in cumin seeds and soaked rice. Stir in 3.5 cups water, salt to taste.
Let the chicken rest 5 minutes before serving.

variants.name: Fish Sajji — Makran Coast Style

ingredients.text: 1.5 kg Surmai or Rohu (kingfish or large carp)

instructions: Mix salt, dried lime powder, red chili, ginger-garlic paste, and mustard oil into a paste. Rest for 30 minutes at room temperature — fish doesn't need the overnight marinade that chicken does.
Fish cooks faster than meat — you need intense, consistent heat, not a long slow fire.
Secure with wire if needed so the fish holds its shape.
Hold or prop the skewer 15-20cm above the coals. Rotate every 5-6 minutes. Total time: 35-45 minutes depending on thickness.
Let rest 3 minutes. Scatter fresh coriander on top and arrange lemon wedges and whole green chilies around it.

variants.name: Sajji with Yogurt Chutney Sauce

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp Kacha papaya paste (raw papaya paste)

instructions: Score the leg of lamb deeply all over. Mix papaya paste and salt, rub into every cut. Cover and refrigerate 12-16 hours.
Push a heavy seekh through the leg bone lengthwise. Roast over the embers, rotating every 10 minutes. Total time: 100-120 minutes for 2kg.
While the sajji roasts, blend dahi, pudina, hara dhania, lehsun, hari mirch, salt, zeera powder, and lemon juice until smooth.
Internal temperature target: 75°C (165°F).
Rest the lamb for 10 minutes before carving.

variants.name: Salt and Pepper Chicken
instructions: Sprinkle 1 teaspoon of the cracked black pepper and 1 teaspoon of salt directly over the chicken and toss to coat. Let it sit for 10 minutes while you prep everything else.

MISE EN Put — GET EVERYTHING READY: Chop all your vegetables before you turn on the heat. Have the garlic, ginger, green chillies, onion, capsicum, and spring onion all cut and sitting in separate piles.

Put your karahi (wok) or a large heavy-bottomed frying pan on the highest heat your stove can produce. Leave it empty and let it heat for 2 full minutes until it begins to smoke slightly. Stir in the 3 tablespoons of cooking oil and swirl to coat.
Stir in the chicken pieces in a single layer. Do NOT stir immediately — let them sear undisturbed for 2-3 minutes per side.

In the same smoking-hot karahi with whatever oil remains, Stir in the minced garlic and julienned ginger. Stir constantly for 30 seconds — they will colour quickly. Stir in the white parts of the spring onion and the slit green chillies.

Stir in the thick-sliced onion and diced capsicum. Stir-Cook for 1-2 minutes — the onion should soften slightly at the edges but still have crunch in the centre. Stir in the seared chicken pieces back into the karahi.

Drizzle the tablespoon of soy sauce around the edges of the hot karahi (not directly on the chicken) — it will sizzle and smoke and Stir in colour without making things wet. Stir in the remaining 1 teaspoon cracked black pepper and 0.5 teaspoon salt. Toss everything vigorously.
Salt and Pepper Chicken must be eaten the moment it comes off the heat.

variants.name: Salty-Sweet Butterscotch Chip Cookies Recipe

ingredients.item: espresso powder or 3/4 tsp instant coffee
ingredients.text: 1/2 teaspoon espresso powder or 3/4 tsp instant coffee

ingredients.item: granulated sugar mixed with 1 to 1 1/4 teaspoons salt
ingredients.text: 1/3 cup granulated sugar mixed with 1 to 1 1/4 teaspoons salt (for topping**)

instructions: Toast your pecans in a clean dry frying pan on medium heat, moving occasionally until they darken and smell toasted.
Stir in the egg, beat till well combined.
With your mixer on low gradually Stir in the flour.
Stir in the chips and toasted nuts.
Refrigerate the dough for 2 hours to overnight unless you are in a rush.
When it is time to bake line your baking sheet (or two sheets) with parchment paper and preheat to 375 degrees F.

Mix the sugar and salt and put in a bowl. Make the size of cookie you prefer and roll into a ball, let the cookie take a little sugar shower and then transfer to the baking sheet and leave 2 inches between cookies.

Bake the cookies for 9-12 minutes depending on the size of the cookie and the kind of cookie you like. A longer bake time will give you a delightfully crunchy cookie, a shorter bake time where the edges are golden and the cookie is just cooked in the.

variants.name: Easy Cheese Samosa

ingredients.item: minced chilies, for jalapeno use one
ingredients.text: 1-2 minced chilies, for jalapeno use one

ingredients.item: crushed garlic clove or 1/2 tsp garlic powder
ingredients.text: 1 small crushed garlic clove or 1/2 tsp garlic powder

ingredients.item: flour and water for a thick slurry
ingredients.text: flour and water for a thick slurry

instructions: Stir in shredded cheese.
Mix together 2 tbsp flour and just enough water to make a paste.
Put a teaspoon full of the cheesy mix and form a samosa.
Shallow Cook 1-2 minutes on each side until golden. You can also air Cook these - just remember to lightly brush with oil!

variants.name: Samosa Chaat Recipe with Chole

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp kashmiri laal mirch (kashmiri chilli powder)

ingredients.preparation: himalayan black salt, looks pink ground up
ingredients.text: 1/2 tsp kala namak (himalayan black salt, looks pink ground up)

ingredients.item: batch Imli chutney or 2/3 cup your favorite storebought imli chutney
ingredients.text: 1/2 batch Imli chutney or 2/3 cup your favorite storebought imli chutney

instructions: Warm your samosas right before assembly.
Mix all the ingredients except the ketchup in a small saucepan, bring to a simmer and cook for 5-6 minutes until thickened.
Stir in ketchup and adjust seasoning to liking.
Mix all the chole/cholay ingredients except chaat masala in a small saucepan, bring to a boil, simmer till the chickpeas are tender, approximately 10 minutes.
Stir in chaat masala, and adjust seasoning.
Whisk together yoghurt, sugar, and cold water.

variants.name: Sweet Coconut Samosas - Khopra / Nariyal Ka Samosa

ingredients.preparation: as much as needed to form a dough
ingredients.text: water (as much as needed to form a dough)

instructions: Prepare and dry the vegetables or filling ingredients.
Mix the flour or besan with the measured spices; add water gradually to make a coating batter or cohesive filling.
Heat the oil to medium-high. Fry in small batches until crisp and evenly golden, allowing the oil to recover between batches.
Drain well and serve hot with the listed chutney or garnish.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Sweet Coconut Samosas - Khopra / Nariyal Ka Samosa
source_attributions.author: Fatima Cooks

variants.name: Aloo Samosa (Crispy Potato-Filled Pastry)
instructions: In a large bartan (bowl), Mix maida (flour), salt, ajwain (carom seeds), and oil. Rub the oil into the flour with your fingertips until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs and holds its shape when you squeeze a handful — this is the 'moyan' technique.

Warm 2 tbsp oil in a karahi (pan) over medium heat. Stir in zeera (cumin seeds) — they should pop and sizzle immediately. Stir in the finely diced pyaz (onion) and Cook for 4–5 minutes until lightly golden.

Divide the rested dough into balls — about 10 equal portions. On a lightly floured surface, roll each ball into a thin oval — about 15 cm long and 8 cm wide, similar in thickness to a thin roti (1–2mm). Cut each oval in half across the middle.

Fold it into a cone shape by overlapping the two corners of the straight edge — one corner folds over the other by about 1 cm. Seal the overlapping edges with a dab of water or a flour-water paste (mix 1 tbsp flour + 2 tbsp water).
Warm oil in a deep karahi (wok) or degh to 160–170°C — lower than you'd think.

Samosas are best served within 10 minutes of frying — they lose their shattering crispness as they cool. Arrange on a plate and serve immediately with hari chutney (green coriander-mint chutney) and imli ki chutney (tamarind chutney).

variants.name: Keema Samosa — Lahori Street Style

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp ghee or vanaspati (clarified butter or shortening)

instructions: Mix sifted flour, salt and cold ghee in a bowl. Gradually Stir in cold water, mixing with a fork, until the dough just comes together. Knead briefly, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Warm 2 tbsp oil in a karahi. Stir in cumin seeds. When they splutter, Stir in onions and cook until golden (8-10 minutes).
Stir in peas to the dry mince and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in garam masala.
Once completely cool, stir in fresh coriander and green chilli.
Roll dough into small balls and roll each into an oval. Cut in half. Take one half and form a cone shape, sealing the straight edge with water.
Warm oil in a karahi to 160-170°C — medium, not high. Stir in samosas and Cook for 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden and flaky.

variants.name: Aloo Samosa — Sindhi Style
instructions: Rub cold ghee into sifted flour and salt until resembling breadcrumbs. Stir in cold water gradually to form a firm dough. Knead for 3-4 minutes.
Warm 2 tbsp oil in a karahi. Stir in cumin seeds and crushed coriander seeds — let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Stir in half the onion (chopped finely) and cook until translucent.
Stir in roughly mashed potatoes. Mix well with the spiced oil. Cook for 3-4 minutes, mixing and mashing further as you go.
To the cooled filling, Stir in the raw half of the onion (finely chopped), fresh coriander and green chilli. Mix well.
Roll dough thin and cut into semi-circles.
Deep Cook in medium-temperature oil (160-170°C) for 8-10 minutes until crispy and golden.

variants.name: Schezwan Chicken
instructions: Soak dried red chillies in boiling water for 20 minutes until completely softened. Drain and blend into a smooth paste with 2 tablespoons of water. In a small bowl, Mix the blended chilli paste with soy sauce, white vinegar, ketchup, and sugar.
Pat the chicken pieces completely dry. Season with a pinch of salt and a pinch of black pepper. Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a karahi (wok) over maximum heat until smoking.

In the same karahi with remaining oil (Stir in 1 more tablespoon if needed), Stir in the star anise. Cook for 30 seconds until it begins to release its fragrance. Stir in the minced garlic and ginger.
Stir in the chunky onion and capsicum pieces. Stir-Cook for 2 minutes over high heat. If you prefer softer vegetables, Stir in 30 seconds more cooking time.
Pour the Schezwan sauce base into the karahi. Stir to coat the vegetables. Let the sauce cook for 1 minute — this 'cooks out' the raw chilli paste flavour and develops the sauce's depth.
Return the seared chicken to the karahi. Pour in 4 tablespoons of water or chicken stock. Toss to coat everything in the sauce.

The sauce should coat each piece of chicken and cling to the vegetables in a thick gloss — not watery, not gluey, but somewhere perfectly in between. Taste one final time: if it tastes sharp and flat, Stir in a pinch more sugar. If it tastes dull, Stir.

variants.name: Mutton Seekh Kebab

ingredients.text: very large handful hara dhania (fresh coriander)

instructions: Stir in minced fat to the qeema.
Mix all ingredients with your hands for 6-8 minutes.
Refrigerate for 2 hours minimum. Mutton fat needs to solidify for the mixture to hold its shape on hot skewers.
Grill over real charcoal if at all possible — mutton seekh specifically benefits from the coal flavour. Cook 5-6 minutes per side on medium-high heat, rotating for even colour.
Rest 3 minutes and then serve.

variants.name: Beef Seekh Kebab Lahori

ingredients.text: 1 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Mix minced beef with all ingredients in a large bowl. Mix with your hands for 5-7 minutes, almost kneading the mixture.
Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes minimum (2 hours is better).
Take a fist-sized portion of the mixture and press it around a flat metal skewer in a cylinder shape, about 6-8 inches long.

Cook on a charcoal grill or griddle on high heat for 4-5 minutes each side, turning carefully until charred and cooked through. For oven: broil at maximum heat for 8-10 minutes, turning once. Internal temperature should reach 75°C.
Cover tray tightly for 2 minutes.

variants.name: Lahori Seekh Kebab

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp Adrak Lehsan Paste (Ginger Garlic Paste)

instructions: In a large bartan (bowl), Mix the beef keema, lamb keema, squeezed onion, adrak lehsan paste, chopped hara dhania (coriander), podina (mint), lal mirch (red chilli), garam masala, toasted cumin, and namak (salt). knead — yes, actually knead — the mixture with your hands for 3-4 full minutes.
Cover the bartan with cling film and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, ideally 2-3 hours or overnight.
Use wet hands to smooth the surface as you shape it into a sausage roughly 15cm long and 3cm thick.

Light your charcoal grill and wait until the coals are white-grey with no orange flame — this takes 15-20 minutes and is important. Lay the skewers across the grill. You'll hear a satisfying sizzle (sss-sss) immediately — if you don't, the grill isn't hot enough.
Cover immediately with a lid for 60 seconds and then remove the coal.
Let the kebabs rest for 2 minutes before sliding off the skewer — they firm up slightly and the juices redistribute.

variants.name: Malai Seekh Kebab

ingredients.text: 500 g raan ka qeema (minced chicken thigh)
3 tbsp cream cheese ya labneh (cream cheese)
1 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)

instructions: Mix cream, cream cheese, yoghurt, ginger garlic paste, and all spices in a bowl until smooth.
Stir in minced chicken, coriander, besan, and salt to the marinade. Mix with your hands for 5 minutes until fully combined.
Refrigerate for minimum 2 hours, ideally 4-6 hours. The longer chill also firms the cream, making skewering easier.
Work with very cold hands (rinse under cold water).
Cook on medium heat — not high. High heat burns the cream and produces bitter char. Baste liberally with butter every 2 minutes.
Malai seekh should be light golden — resist the urge to cook it darker. Rest 2 minutes, and then serve.

variants.name: Sindhi Seekh Kebab

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
1.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Mix all ingredients including amchur (mango powder). The amchur will smell quite strong in the raw mix — it mellows beautifully during cooking. Mix for 6-8 minutes until sticky.
Refrigerate 1-2 hours.
Sindhi seekh is grilled on high heat to develop good char. 5-6 minutes per side, turning once. The amchur caramelises beautifully on the grill.

variants.name: Sesame Fried Chicken

ingredients.item: boneless chicken cut into small 1.5 inch strips
ingredients.text: 1.5 lb boneless chicken cut into small 1.5 inch strips

ingredients.item: cornstarch for super crispy or fill 1/3 cup halfway with flour and halfway with cornstarch
ingredients.text: 1/3 cup cornstarch for super crispy or fill 1/3 cup halfway with flour and halfway with cornstarch

instructions: Mix the marinade up in a bowl, Stir in the chicken pieces, stir to coat well and set aside for 20 minutes or longer.
Whisk an egg and Stir in it into the bowl, mix well.
Stir in remaining batter ingredients and mix, if the mixture becomes too sticky Stir in a small splash of water.
Warm oil in a saucepan, at least one inch of oil is ideal.
When it starts to shimmer Stir in the chicken pieces in one by one, making sure to shake any excess batter off into the bowl.
Cook two minutes on each side until golden brown.

variants.name: Doodh Seviyan (Quick Sheer Khurma) – Easy Eid Vermicelli Dessert
instructions: Stir in the cloves and cardamom, Cook for a minute.
And then Stir in the sivaiyan, Cook for 2 minutes until darker in color.
Stir in milk, bring to a boil (watch carefully) and and then Stir in the salt, nuts and saffron if using.
Simmer for 10-15 minutes until thickened and the vermicelli has softened.

Stir in most of your can of condensed milk, and qalaqand (if using) and stir well before tasting. Sheer Khurma becomes sweeter tasting as it cools, but if you feel it is under sweet and then Stir in more condensed milk.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Melt ghee over medium heat in a large heavy-bottomed pot. Once it begins to shimmer, Stir in cracked cardamom pods, and Cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Brown it over medium heat, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Slowly pour milk into the pot. Cover, and bring to a boil.
Remove the lid, and lower to a simmer. Stir in sugar and stir until it dissolves.
Let the seviyan simmer on medium to medium-low heat for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally. Once the mixture begins to thicken, and you are close to the desired consistency, remove from heat.
Pour seviyan into serving bowl, and let it set at room temperature. Garnish with slivered almonds or your choice of nuts or dried fruit.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Doodh Seviyan (Quick Sheer Khurma) – Easy Eid Vermicelli Dessert
Doodh Seviyan (Quick Sheer Khurma) – Easy Eid Vermicelli Dessert
Easy Seviyan Recipe (Pakistani Sweet Vermicelli with Milk)

alternate_names: Easy Seviyan Recipe (Pakistani Sweet Vermicelli with Milk)

variants.name: Nani Ami's Seviyan

ingredients.preparation: or vermicelli bought in a Pakistani or Indian grocery store
ingredients.text: 120 g (1 packet) sawayyan (or vermicelli bought in a Pakistani or Indian grocery store)

ingredients.preparation: warm or cold- suited to your taste
ingredients.text: milk, (warm or cold- suited to your taste)

ingredients.item: dried, unsalted nuts of your choice
ingredients.text: dried, unsalted nuts of your choice

instructions: Put a large pot of water on the stove and when it comes to a boil, Stir in vermicelli (don't Stir in in stages, it must all cook together).
Remove after 20 seconds (test for doneness first) and strain immediately.
Transfer to a dish.

variants.name: Seyal Maani (Sindhi Leftover Roti in Spiced Gravy)

ingredients.text: 6-8 medium rotis purani roti (day-old rotis or chapatis)
1 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

ingredients.item: to garnish hara dhania aur hari mirch
ingredients.text: to garnish hara dhania aur hari mirch (fresh coriander and green chillies)

instructions: The rough torn edges help the roti absorb the gravy better than clean-cut edges.

Warm 4 tbsp of oil in a wide karahi (wok) or handi (pot) over medium-high heat. Stir in the zeera (cumin seeds) — they should crackle immediately. Stir in the thinly sliced pyaz (onions) and spread them out in the pan.

Stir in the crushed lehsun (garlic) and adrak (ginger) to the golden onions. Stir-Cook for 1–2 minutes until the raw garlic smell disappears and you can smell a toasty, sweet aroma. Stir in the chopped tamatar (tomatoes) and slit hari mirch (green chillies).
Pour 1 to 1.5 cups of water into the masala (use 1 cup for crispier maani, 1.5 cups for softer maani). Stir and bring to a boil.
Stir in all the torn roti pieces to the bubbling gravy. Don't stir too aggressively or the roti will completely disintegrate. Reduce heat to medium-low.

If Aim for crispy edges (highly recommended), increase the heat to medium-high, spread the maani in an even layer in the pan, and let it cook undisturbed for 3–4 minutes. The bottom layer will develop crispy, slightly charred edges — these are the best bites.
Scatter fresh hara dhania (coriander) generously over the top and Stir in a few slit green chillies for colour.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Warm oil in a wide flat pan. Stir in zeera and sizzle. Stir in sliced piyaz and cook on medium-high heat until caramelised and deep golden — about 12-15 minutes.

Stir in adrak lahsun paste and cook 2 minutes. Stir in tamatar, laal mirch powder, dhania powder, haldi, and salt. Cook on high heat until tomatoes completely break down and oil separates — about 10 minutes.
Stir in 200-250ml water to the masala. Stir and bring to a simmer. Stir in slit hari mirch.
Stir in torn roti pieces to the masala. Cook covered on low heat for 5-7 minutes.
Push the bread to the sides. Scramble gently and mix through the bread as they cook. This takes about 2 minutes.
Stir in hara dhania and fold in gently.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Seyal Maani (Sindhi Leftover Roti in Spiced Gravy)

variants.name: Bread Shahi Tukda — Easy Punjabi Home Style
instructions: In a non-stick saucepan, bring milk to a boil. Reduce to medium and cook for 15 minutes, stirring frequently, until reduced by about a third. Stir in condensed milk and saffron milk.
Dissolve sugar in water in a small saucepan over medium heat. Stir in cardamom seeds and boil for 5 minutes. Remove from heat and Stir in rose water.
Trim crusts from bread and cut diagonally into triangles. Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a flat tawa (griddle) over medium heat. Toast each triangle for 1-2 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Immediately dip each hot toasted triangle into the warm syrup for 20-30 seconds per side.
Arrange syrup-soaked triangles on a serving plate.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Bread Shahi Tukda — Easy Punjabi Home Style

variants.name: Shahi Tukda

ingredients.text: 8 slices purana dauble roti (day-old white sandwich bread)
1 cup tel (cooking oil) or ghee (clarified butter)
1 tablespoon gulab ki pattian (dried rose petals)

instructions: MAKE THE RABRI FIRST (this takes longest): Pour 1.5 litres of full-fat milk into a wide, heavy-bottomed degh (heavy-bottomed pot) or karahi (wok) — a wide pan speeds things up by allowing more evaporation. Bring to a boil on medium-high heat, stirring frequently to prevent a skin forming.

Once the milk has reduced significantly, Stir in 0.5 cup cheeni and stir until dissolved. Stir in the bloomed saffron milk, elaichi powder, and Olper's cream if using. Stir and cook for another 5 minutes.

In a small pateela (saucepan), Mix 1 cup cheeni, 0.75 cup water, and crushed elaichi pods. Bring to a boil on medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves completely. Let it boil for 3-4 minutes until it thickens slightly — it should reach a one-string consistency (dip a.

Cut each slice diagonally into two triangles, or keep them as rectangles — either works. If the bread is very fresh, lay the slices on a baking tray and leave them uncovered for 1-2 hours to dry out slightly.

Warm tel or ghee in a karahi to medium-high heat — you need about 1-1.5 inches of depth. Cook the bread slices 2-3 at a time (don't overcrowd — they need space). Cook for 1-2 minutes per side, turning with a chimta (tongs), until both sides are deep.

While the fried bread is still warm (this is important — warm bread absorbs syrup better), dip each piece into the warm sugar syrup for 10-15 seconds per side. Arrange the soaked bread in a single layer on a serving platter.
Pour the warm rabri generously over the arranged bread — don't be shy, shahi tukda is not the time for restraint.

variants.name: Shahi Tukda — Karachi Double Ka Meetha Style

ingredients.text: 1 cup ghee or tel (ghee or oil)

instructions: Pour milk into a wide karahi and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium and cook, stirring frequently, for 20-25 minutes until the milk reduces to roughly half its volume. Stir in condensed milk and stir through.
In a small saucepan, Mix sugar and water. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolves. Stir in saffron milk and cardamom powder.

Cut the crusts off each bread slice and cut diagonally into triangles (or leave as rectangles — your call). Heat ghee in a wide karahi over medium heat. Cook bread triangles in batches for 1-2 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp.

As soon as the bread comes out of the ghee, transfer directly to the warm saffron syrup. Let each piece soak for 30-45 seconds per side, turning once. The bread should absorb syrup but still hold its shape.
Arrange the syrup-soaked bread pieces on a large flat serving dish or tray, overlapping slightly.
Scatter sliced pistachios over the rabri. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour for the flavours to meld, or serve slightly warm for an indulgent hot dessert experience.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Shahi Tukda — Karachi Double Ka Meetha Style

variants.name: Shahi Tukray Recipe

ingredients.text: 1 tsp ground cardamom (freshly ground is optimal)
1 tsp saffron, coarsely crushed by hand

instructions: Mix all the milk mix ingredients except the condensed milk in a wide bottomed pot and for 5-7 minutes until slightly thickened.
Stir in your condensed milk.
Cook your breads pieces in oil (my preference) or ghee in batches until golden brown.
Stir in your bread slices into the milky base and let it simmer for a few minutes to help the bread absorb the flavour.

For easier plating don't leave your bread in too long because it becomes hard to transfer. If you are making it in advance and then you can also Put the fried bread in your dish and gently pour over the milk. The bread will absorb the milk mix.
Garnish with nuts and saffron.

alternate_methods.label: oven
instructions: Pre-heat oven to 350° F.
Warm oil in a non-stick frying pan. Cook bread in batches, about 1-2 minutes each side until golden brown. Stir in extra oil as needed.
Arrange bread in layers in buttered baking dish.
Put milk in saucepan and bring to boil. Lower heat. Stir in ground saffron and cardamom, and let it simmer for 10 minutes.
While the milk simmers on low heat, beat eggs and sugar with a whisk in a large bowl until well-mixed.
Pour milk into the egg and sugar mixture, and beat again until well-mixed.
Pour custard over bread, and bake uncovered for 25 minutes.

alternate_methods.label: oven
instructions: Pre-heat oven to 350F. Cut off edges from the bread, slice in half on the diagonal.

Put pan on medium high heat and smear with some butter, and then Stir in a few drops of oil (approximately 2 tsps). Cook bread till lightly brown on both sides. You will have to keep adding more butter and oil as you Cook the batches of bread.
Transfer fried bread into baking dish. Do not double layer the bread. Slowly begin to pour half-and-half on bread. As the bread absorbs the liquid, pour more.

In the meantime Put a saucepan on the stove on high heat and Stir in sugar,water and cardamom pods. Once it comes to a boil, turn the heat to low, Stir in saffron powder and allow it to simmer for 10 minutes.
Pour half of heavy cream over the bread. Pour hot syrup on top of bread, and then pour the remainder of the whipped cream and bake in the oven for 30 minutes.
Garnish with almonds and pistachios.

variants.name: Shallots with Coconut and Tamarind

ingredients.item: optional garnish: minced cilantro, sliced mild chillies
ingredients.text: optional garnish: minced cilantro, sliced mild chillies

instructions: Toast the coconut and coriander seeds on medium high heat in dry saucepan, the coconut will get beautifully golden, 2-3 minutes. Stir to avoid burning.
Blend the first three ingredients to a paste using a little water.
Put a lug of cooking oil in a 10 inch saucepan and heat.
In with the shallots, cook for 3-4 minutes on medium high heat until browned on the outside and slightly softened.
Stir in salt (start w 3/4 tsp), 1/4 cup water (may need more if it starts to burn), and turmeric. Cook for another 5 minutes.
Pour in your coconut paste and 1 tbsp of the tamarind pulp. Mix well and adjust seasoning by adding more salt or another 1/2 tbsp of tamarind pulp.
Transfer the shallots to the serving dish.
Warm a tbsp and a half of oil n a small saucepan and Stir in the nigella seeds (kalonji), curry leaves, and dried red chilli. Cook for about 20 seconds and then pour over the shallots.

variants.name: Shami Kebab

ingredients.text: 1 lb boneless beef chuck (trimmed and roughly diced)
1 inch ginger knob (peeled and finely diced)

ingredients.preparation: roughly chopped, plus 1/2 red onion, finely diced
ingredients.text: 1 red onion (roughly chopped, plus 1/2 red onion, finely diced)
5 dried round whole red peppers (available at Indian/Pakistani specialty stores)

ingredients.preparation: wet lightly under a splash of water
ingredients.text: 1 slice white bread (wet lightly under a splash of water)

instructions: In a large stock pot, Stir in all ingredients up until the white bread (with the exception of 1⁄2 finely diced red onion) and 4 cups of water, and bring to a boil. Drop heat to a simmer and cook until the water disappears and the lentils are.
Stir in garam masala powder, diced cilantro, chili, and red onion.
Stir in minced meat to the bread-egg mixture. Mix well until an even consistency is achieved.
Warm oil in a shallow nonstick frying pan. Put patties in pan and Cook each side till it's a deep brown. Transfer to a plate lined with a paper towel to absorb excess oil.

variants.name: Shami Kebab (Chicken, Lamb, Mutton & Beef)

ingredients.text: 1 cup raw split yellow lentils (chana daal)
1 bulb garlic, peeled (doesn't need to minced)

ingredients.preparation: depending on your taste - please check before frying!
ingredients.text: 2-3 tsp of salt (depending on your taste - please check before frying!)

instructions: Combine the minced ginger with the yogurt, bulb garlic, peeled, minced ginger, chilli flakes, onion and cumin seeds, coriander powder, coarse black pepper, chilli flakes, chat masala, piece cinnamon stick; marinate for the time available.
Shape or skewer the mixture as appropriate, keeping portions even so they cook at the same rate.
Grill, roast or pan-cook until browned outside and safely cooked through at the centre.
Rest briefly and finish with minced ginger, coriander powder, fresh coriander.

variants.name: Chicken Shami Kebab
instructions: In a pot, Mix chicken mince, soaked dal, onion, ginger-garlic paste, whole cardamom, cloves, green chilli, red chilli, black pepper and salt. Stir in 1/2 cup water. Cook on medium heat, stirring occasionally, for 25-30 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the water is absorbed.
Once the water is absorbed, increase heat and stir constantly for 3-5 minutes to completely dry out any remaining moisture.
Cool the mixture for 10 minutes.
Transfer to a bowl. Mix in coriander and mint. Refrigerate the mixture for 20-30 minutes — chicken mixture is softer than beef and needs chilling to hold shape when frying.
With wet hands, shape into round flat patties. Put on a plate and refrigerate again for 10 minutes before frying.
Warm oil in a tawa over medium heat. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and crisp. Drain and serve.

variants.name: Lahori Shami Kebab

ingredients.text: 1 set Kharay masalay (Whole spices for boiling)
1 tsp Lal mirch powder (Red chilli powder)

instructions: In a degh (heavy pot), Mix the gosht (beef), soaked chana dal, half the pyaz (onion), adrak (ginger), lehsan (garlic), 2 hari mirch (green chillies), all the kharay masalay (whole spices), lal mirch powder (red chilli), and salt. Stir in just enough water to cover — about 2.5.
Once the meat is completely tender, remove the lid and cook on medium heat, stirring constantly, until all remaining liquid has evaporated.
Transfer the cooled mixture to a food processor.

Transfer the ground mixture to a large bartan (bowl). Stir in the beaten anda (egg), finely diced raw pyaz (onion), 2 finely chopped raw hari mirch (green chillies), and the hara dhaniya (fresh coriander). Mix thoroughly with your hands — really work the egg through the mixture.
Wet your hands slightly to prevent sticking. Roll into a smooth ball between your palms.

Warm oil in a flat tawa (griddle) or wide frying pan over medium heat. Cook for 3–4 minutes on the first side without moving. The underside should develop a deep golden-brown crust — this crust is what holds the kebab together.
Remove finished kebabs onto a plate lined with paper towels. They should be deep golden-brown on both sides, firm to the touch, and smell incredible — like spiced, roasted meat.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: In a heavy pot, Mix mince, soaked chana dal, quartered onion, ginger-garlic paste, whole spices, red chilli and salt. Stir in just enough water to cover (about 1 cup). Bring to a boil, reduce heat, cover and simmer for 40-45 minutes until the meat and dal are very.
After water is absorbed, spread the mixture on the pan and cook uncovered on medium heat for 5 minutes, stirring constantly, until completely dry.
Transfer to a bowl. Mix in finely chopped coriander and mint. Mix well with your hands.
With wet or lightly oiled hands, take a golf-ball sized portion and flatten into a round patty about 1cm thick.
Warm oil in a flat-bottomed karahi or frying pan over medium heat. Cook kebabs for 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden-brown and crisp. Drain on paper towels.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Lahori Shami Kebab — A Classic Variation

alternate_names: Lahori Shami Kebab — A Classic Variation

variants.name: Sindhi Shami Kebab — with Potato
instructions: In a pressure cooker or heavy pot, Mix mince, soaked dal, half the onion (quartered), ginger-garlic paste, toasted cumin and coriander powder, red chilli and salt. Stir in 3/4 cup water. Pressure cook for 20 minutes or simmer in a regular pot for 40 minutes until completely dry.
Cook in 1 tbsp oil over medium heat until deep golden-brown.
Mix with mashed potato and caramelised onion. Mix together thoroughly.
Mix in fresh coriander and chopped green chilli. Shape into round patties with lightly oiled hands.
Warm oil in a tawa or karahi over medium heat. Cook kebabs for 2-3 minutes per side until crispy and golden. Drain on paper towels.

variants.name: Sheer Khurma: Pakistani Vermicelli Pudding
instructions: Put pan on medium-high heat and Stir in cardamom seeds and vermicelli. Sauté for 3-5 minutes, stirring constantly till the cardamom is fragrant and the vermicelli begins to change colour slightly.
Stir in milk, full cream, sugar, almonds, raisins and stir.
Turn heat to low and let it cook, uncovered, for 1 -11⁄2 hour.
The pudding will need to be monitored and stirred every 10-15 minutes. Be sure to stir all the way into the bottom of the pan so the base of the pudding doesn't burn.
When it reaches the desired consistency, turn the heat off, allow to cool at room temperature for 1 hour, and then refrigerate overnight.

variants.name: Sheer Khurma
instructions: First, prepare your garnish ingredients: soak the zafran (saffron) strands in 1 tablespoon of warm doodh (milk) and set aside — it needs at least 10 minutes to release its colour and flavour.
Put a bhari pateela (heavy-bottomed pot) on medium-low heat and Stir in the desi ghee.
Aim for every strand uniformly golden brown — like the colour of chai. This takes 5-7 minutes on low heat.

With the toasted sevaiyan still in the pot, Stir in the slivered badaam (almonds), pista (pistachios), chironji, and kishmish (raisins). Toss everything in the ghee for about 2 minutes until the nuts are lightly golden and the raisins have puffed up. use a chamcha (spoon) to remove roughly.

Pour in all 2 litres of doodh (milk). Be careful — the ghee will spit when the cold milk hits it, so pour slowly and stand back slightly. Increase the heat to medium-high and bring the milk to a boil, stirring frequently.

Once the milk comes to a rolling boil (big bubbles breaking the surface), reduce the heat to low. Stir in the cheeni (sugar), lightly crushed elaichi (cardamom) pods, sliced khajoor (dates), and the zafran (saffron) milk you soaked earlier. Stir everything together gently.
Let the sheer khurma simmer on low heat (dum — gentle steam) for 15-20 minutes. Stir every 3-4 minutes to prevent the bottom from catching.
Turn off the heat. Stir in the arq-e-gulab (rose water) if using, and stir gently. Adding it off the heat preserves its delicate floral fragrance — boiling destroys it.
Ladle the sheer khurma into small katorian (bowls), garnish with the reserved toasted nuts and a few strands of zafran (saffron).

source_attributions.recipe_title: 27+ Eid Recipes | Special Eid Dishes | Eid Food Ideas + Sheer Khurma Recipe
source_attributions.author: Fatima Cooks

alternate_names: 27+ Eid Recipes | Special Eid Dishes | Eid Food Ideas + Sheer Khurma Recipe

variants.name: Sheermal
instructions: Stir in all the saffron strands. Leave to steep for at least 15 minutes — ideally 30.
In a small katori, mix 2 tablespoons of the warm milk (not the saffron milk — keep that separate), 1 teaspoon of the sugar, and the yeast. Leave 8 minutes until foamy.

In a large paraat, mix the flour, remaining sugar, salt, and cardamom powder (if using). Stir in the activated yeast mixture, the remaining warm milk (not the saffron milk), and half the saffron milk. Stir in the ghee.
Shape into a ball, Put in an oiled bowl, cover with a damp cloth, and leave 1–1.5 hours in a warm Put until doubled.
Set your oven to 200°C (390°F) — note this is slightly lower than for naan because sheermal's sugar content means it colours faster. Put a baking tray in the oven to preheat for 20 minutes.
Punch down the risen dough. On a lightly floured chakla, roll each ball out into a thick oval or round about 18–20cm across and 8mm thick.

Slide the sheermal onto the hot baking tray. Bake at 200°C for 8–12 minutes until golden and cooked through. Remove from the oven — if Aim for more colour on top, turn the grill on for 1–2 minutes, watching carefully.

variants.name: Shinwari Karahi Balochi Style

ingredients.text: 6 tbsp dumba charbi ya tel (tail fat or oil)
4 whole sabut lal mirch (whole dried red chillies)

instructions: Warm oil (or melt and render Dumba tail fat) in a large, heavy iron karahi on high heat. Stir in cumin seeds and whole red chillies — bloom for 30 seconds.
Stir in whole garlic cloves and sliced ginger to the fat. Let them Cook for 2-3 minutes until golden and fragrant.
Stir in mutton, salt, and crushed black pepper. Sear on maximum heat for 10-12 minutes, turning regularly, until meat is browned all over.
Reduce to medium. Stir in yoghurt and stir immediately to coat the meat. Cook for 3-4 minutes until yoghurt dries into the meat.
Stir in 3/4 cup water, Stir in green chillies, cover with a lid or foil, and cook on medium-low for 30-40 minutes until mutton is completely tender.
Remove lid, increase to maximum heat, and bhuno hard for 8-10 minutes until all moisture evaporates and masala is almost dry.
Let rest for 5 minutes in the karahi. Garnish with ginger juliennes and coriander.

variants.name: Shinwari Karahi — The Tribal Lamb Fat Karahi

ingredients.text: 150 g Dumbe Ki Charbi (Lamb Tail Fat)
1 tbsp Kali Mirch Sabut (Whole Black Peppercorns)
1 tsp Kali Mirch Kuti (Cracked Black Pepper)

instructions: The iron holds and distributes heat in a way that creates the characteristic slightly-charred exterior on the meat while keeping the interior tender.
Put your empty iron karahi on the highest heat your stove can produce. Stir in the cubed dumbe ki charbi (lamb tail fat) directly to the dry karahi.
Stir in the bone-in mutton pieces directly to the hot fat in the karahi. Leave undisturbed for 3-4 minutes per side. Aim for a deep brown, almost crusty sear on each surface.
Once the meat is well-seared on all sides, Stir in the whole black peppercorns directly into the fat and meat. Stir in the whole green chillies. Stir to distribute.

This is not a slow-cooked dish — Shinwari karahi is high-heat, high-drama. Cover the karahi with a lid or plate and cook for 20-25 minutes on high heat, removing the lid every 5 minutes to stir and check.
After 20 minutes, pierce the thickest piece of mutton with a thin knife or skewer. The colour should be deep golden-brown, almost caramel on the outside.
Turn off the heat. Immediately Stir in the coarsely cracked kali mirch (black pepper) directly over the meat. Stir once.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Shinwari Karahi — The Tribal Lamb Fat Karahi

variants.name: Hyderabadi Kadhi

ingredients.text: 2 whole sukhi laal mirch (dried red chillies)
0.75 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Toast besan in a dry karahi until nutty and golden, 3-4 minutes. Mix with 250ml cold water to a smooth, lump-free paste.
Warm oil in a large pot. Stir in rai and wait for popping. Stir in methi dana — just 0.5 tsp, they're intensely bitter.
Stir in haldi and laal mirch powder. Stir 30 seconds and then immediately Stir in the besan paste mixed with remaining water. Stir constantly as it heats.
Bring to gentle boil while stirring constantly. Reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes. The Hyderabadi version is thicker — let it reduce slightly more than you think .
Stir in cubed aloo, baingan, salt, and tamarind paste. Simmer 20-25 minutes until vegetables are completely tender. Stir occasionally.
This kadhi should coat the rice, not flood it.

variants.name: Karachi Sindhi Kadhi

ingredients.text: 3 whole sukhi laal mirch (dried whole red chillies)
1 tsp laal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: In a dry pan, toast besan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly, until it turns one shade darker and smells nutty.
Mix roasted besan with 300ml cold water to make a smooth paste. Whisk out all lumps — this is critical for a smooth kadhi. Stir in more water to make it pourable.
Warm oil in a large pot. Stir in rai — wait for it to pop. Stir in zeera, kari patta, and sukhi laal mirch.
Stir in the besan slurry to the pot along with remaining water. Stir continuously on medium heat as it comes to a boil — if you stop stirring, it will lump. Cook 15 minutes, stirring frequently.
Stir in aloo, gajar, phali, and baingan. Stir in tamarind paste and salt. Simmer on low heat 20-25 minutes until vegetables are tender.
Taste and balance — Stir in more imli for tang, more salt if needed.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Soak your imli (tamarind) ball in 1 cup of warm water for 20 minutes. Strain through a sieve, pressing the pulp through with the back of a chamcha (spoon).
Warm the oil in a large, deep karahi (wok) or heavy-bottomed pateela (pot) over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Stir in the rai (mustard seeds) first — stand back slightly, they pop and splatter.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Stir in the besan (gram flour) to the spiced oil and stir continuously with the chamcha.

Pour the tamarind water into the roasted besan mixture and stir vigorously — the besan will absorb it quickly. and then Stir in the remaining 4 cups of water, a cup at a time, stirring between each addition to prevent lumps.

Once the kadhi is boiling, Stir in the aloo (potato) cubes and gawar phalli (cluster beans) first — they take longest to cook. Stir in the sahjan ki phalli (drumstick pieces) at the same time. Season with salt.
After 15 minutes, Stir in the bhindi (okra) to the pot.

variants.name: Sindhi Style Prawn Fry Recipe

ingredients.text: 1/2 pound shrimp or prawn (pre-cooked and thawed)
1/2 yellow onion (thinly sliced in half rings)

instructions: Warm 1⁄4 cup of neutral oil in a saucepan. Stir in shrimp or prawn, salt, and Cook for 5-7 minutes until cooked through.
Remove from saucepan and drain on paper towel.
Reheat remaining oil and Stir in cumin seeds. Cook for 30 seconds or until aromatic.
Stir in chopped onion and Cook for 5-7 minutes until limp and translucent.
Stir in crushed ginger and garlic, and Cook for 30 seconds to 1 minutes.
Stir in ground spices and Cook for 1 minute, until they stop smelling raw. Stir in a splash water to deglaze the pan if needed.
Stir in diced chilies, cilantro, and cooked shrimp/prawns. Cook and coat in the masala for a couple of minutes.

variants.name: Singaporean Rice

ingredients.item: mixed vegetables - I use 1 cup shredded coleslaw mix and 1 cup mixed sliced peppers
ingredients.text: 2 cups mixed vegetables - I use 1 cup shredded coleslaw mix and 1 cup mixed sliced peppers

ingredients.item: chicken, sliced into slim 1-1.5 inch pieces
ingredients.text: 2 lb chicken, sliced into slim 1-1.5 inch pieces

ingredients.item: additional cayenne if your hot sauce isn't spicy enough
ingredients.text: additional cayenne if your hot sauce isn't spicy enough

ingredients.item: a handful of chopped scallions for garnish
ingredients.text: a handful of chopped scallions for garnish (optional)

instructions: Boil the rice, drain excess water and stir in soy, pepper, and vinegar. Boil noodles per package directions.

While they are boiling heat 2 tbsp of oil in a pan on medium high heat and Stir in the ginger garlic paste. After sauteing the ginger garlic paste for 30 seconds Stir in your vegetables and remaining seasonings (including crumbled boullion cube) and saute till tender crisp.
Stir in the drained noodles to the vegetable mix. Saute the ginger garlic in hot oil and then Stir in the sliced chicken.
Keep the heat on medium high and saute until all the chicken changes colours. Stir in the soy sauce, vinegar, pepper, chili powder, cook for another two minutes.
Stir in the ketchup, hot sauce and water, cook on low for 4-5 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning - I usually Stir in 1/2 tsp of salt.

Whisk all the ingredients together and set aside. Take a large platter/rice dish and then spoon out a layer of rice followed by the noodles and then the chicken and a drizzle of your sauce (you'll have extra leftover).
Warm 3 tbsp of oil in a small pan and Stir in garlic cooking on medium heat till golden. Stir in your green chilies, they may sputter so be careful as you saute them for 30 seconds.
Carefully spoon your garlic chips and chilies over the dish - you don't need to pour the oil over!

dish_families.name: Slow Cooker Dum Kay Pasanday (Masala-Rubbed Roast Beef)

variants.name: Slow Cooker Dum Kay Pasanday (Masala-Rubbed Roast Beef)
variants.dish_family: Slow Cooker Dum Kay Pasanday (Masala-Rubbed Roast Beef)

ingredients.text: 1 inch cinnamon stick (broken into small pieces)

ingredients.preparation: trimmed and chopped into thin 2-inch slices
ingredients.text: 2.2 lbs beef tenderloin (trimmed and chopped into thin 2-inch slices)

instructions: Toast spices in a dry skillet on medium-low heat for 3 - 5 minutes, stirring occasionally until mustard seeds begin to pop.
In a large platter, mix the beef, salt, yogurt, lemon juice, ginger and garlic paste and spice mix. Marinate for 2 hours, or more.
Warm oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat. Stir in chopped onion and Cook until caramelized, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the marinated beef and cook on high heat till the meat is no longer pink, 5-7 minutes.
Put in Crock-Pot or any slow cooker, Stir in 1 cup water. Cook on low heat for 6 hours or high heat for 3 hours.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Slow Cooker Dum Kay Pasanday (Masala-Rubbed Roast Beef)

variants.name: Soft 20 Minute Rasmalai - Milk Powder
instructions: Mix the first four ingredients in a wide bottomed pan and bring to a boil.
Turn the heat down, and mix well, ensuring the sugar is dissolved.
Once the sugar dissolves turn the heat low to maintain the gentlest simmer.
Stir in the slivered pistachios and keep the milk at a very gentle simmer.
Mix the milk powder, flour, and baking powder well, followed by the oil and and then the egg.

QUICKLY shape into 10-12 balls, they'll be about an inch or so big. If you wait too long and then the dough dries out, forms cracks, and becomes too hard in the middle to cook through (lots on this in the post). My preferred technique for shaping is.
Once all your dough balls are made and in the pan on that gentlest of gentle simmers, cover the pan and let them cook undisturbed for 5-7 minutes.

After 5 minutes, carefully flip each ras malai, and and then continue cooking for another 5 minutes and and then turn the stove off and let them cool before transferring them to a box/dish. Cooling them in the warm milk ensures that they cook through.
Leave in the fridge for at least 2 hours or overnight for best results, garnish with additional pistachios and serve.

variants.name: Soft Dahi Baray

ingredients.item: Yogurt 2 pounds or about 1 1/2 times a 750g yogurt carton
ingredients.text: Yogurt 2 pounds or about 1 1/2 times a 750g yogurt carton

ingredients.item: ma’ash/urad daal - the white kind covered with water and soaked overnight
ingredients.text: 1 cup ma’ash/urad daal - the white kind covered with water and soaked overnight

instructions: Mix the yogurt, sugar and spices along with 1⁄2 cup of water and whisk. Drain the maash ki Daal making sure to reserve about 1/3 cup of soaking liquid.
Only Stir in more if absolutely necessary. Transfer the mixture to a bowl.

For softer Dahi Baray: Whisk energetically to create volume in the batter, about 4-5 minutes with a large whisk. 2 minutes with an electric mixer works. Warm a skillet and Stir in 2 inches of oil and put on medium-high heat for the oil to heat through.
Stir in a pinch of salt in the water. Get a tray or platter and line it with paper towels to help drain the grease from the dumplings.
After a minute and a half the dumpling will turn a lovely golden color at which point turn them over and cook for another minute and a half. Remove from the oil and drain on paper towels.

Pour a layer of yogurt mix into your dish of choice. Remove the dumplings from the water one by one, gently squeezing them beneath your palms to drain the excess water and and then lay them out in rows on top of the yogurt until your dish is filled.
Top with enough of the yogurt to adequately cover the dumplings and refrigerate. Leave it for atleast an hour so the flavours soak through the dumplings.

variants.name: Multani Sohan Halwa — Gift Box Style

ingredients.text: 1 cup meda (refined wheat flour or cornflour)

instructions: Stir in lemon juice. Bring to a boil, stirring until dissolved. Cook to a firm-ball stage (120°C / 248°F on a candy thermometer).
Once at firm-ball stage, slowly pour in the cornflour-water paste while stirring vigorously with a wooden spoon. Keep stirring on medium heat.
This is the marathon stage. Stir continuously for 30-40 minutes over medium heat. Stir in saffron water and cardamom powder during this phase.
Begin adding ghee, 2 tablespoons at a time, stirring it in fully before adding the next addition. This takes 20-25 minutes as you gradually Stir in all the ghee.

Grease a flat tray or thali with ghee. Pour the hot halwa onto it and quickly spread to about 1cm thickness using the back of a greased spoon. Let cool completely (1-2 hours) until solid and glass-like.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Multani Sohan Halwa — Gift Box Style

variants.name: Multani Sohan Halwa
instructions: In a small bowl, whisk together the corn starch and 1⁄4 cup of cold water until completely smooth — no lumps.

In a heavy-bottomed pateela (pot) — ideally stainless steel or copper, not non-stick — Mix the sugar, 3⁄4 cup water, and lemon juice. Stir until the sugar dissolves, and then stop stirring completely.
Bring the syrup to a boil over medium-high heat. The stages: Soft ball (115°C) — too early, won't set hard. Firm ball (120°C) — still too soft.

The moment your thermometer reads 150°C, reduce heat to the lowest setting. Give your starch slurry a quick stir (it will have settled), and then pour it into the syrup in a slow, steady stream while stirring vigorously with a chamcha (spatula).
Stir in the ghee in 3-4 additions, stirring each addition fully into the mixture before adding the next.

Stir in the elaichi powder (cardamom) and kewra water (if using) to the mixture and stir through. Working very quickly — the mixture will begin to set as it cools — pour it onto your pre-greased baking tray and spread it out with the back of a greased.

Allow the Sohan Halwa to cool at room temperature — do not put it in the fridge, which can cause condensation and make the surface sticky. After 20-25 minutes it will be firm to the touch. After 45 minutes it will have set fully.

variants.name: Southwest Rolls

ingredients.item: jalapeno deseeded or 1 small thai chili seeds scraped out
ingredients.text: 1/2 jalapeno deseeded or 1 small thai chili seeds scraped out (minced)

ingredients.item: olive oil for cooking and spraying/brushing on the rolls
ingredients.text: olive oil for cooking and spraying/brushing on the rolls

instructions: Sauté the jalapenos and peppers in a tbsp of oil, and then Stir in the black beans and corn followed by the spices and and then the cream cheese.
Mix well to make sure the cream cheese melts and stir in the chicken.
Stir in milk to adjust consistency - mixture will be thick.
Stir in scallions and let it come to room temperature.
Spray the rolls with oil and air Cook at 390F for 4 minutes on each side.

variants.name: Spiced Glazed Carrots

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp corn oil (or any other neutral oil)
1 1/2 tsp black mustard seeds; (known as rai in Urdu)

ingredients.item: chili powder (depending on the amount of heat you prefer. (Start with 1/2 tsp))
ingredients.text: 1/2-1 tsp chili powder (depending on the amount of heat you prefer. (Start with 1/2 tsp))

instructions: Put a wok or a frying pan on medium heat.
Stir in oil and allow to heat for 2 minutes.
Stir in mustard seeds and as soon as they start to sputter, remove from the flame (don’t turn the flame off) and Stir in the julienned carrots.
Stir-Cook for a minute and Put back on heat.
Stir in turmeric, salt and chili powder and give it a whirl.
Cover with a lid for 3-5 minutes- you don’t want to overcook the carrots, they should be semi-crisp by the end of this process.
Remove lid, turn off the flame and serve with chapati (a Pakistani wholewheat flatbread) and some raita or have as a side with a whole roast chicken.

variants.name: Spicy Baked Eggs

ingredients.text: 1 lb medium-sized tomatoes, (blanched, skins peeled, and diced)

ingredients.item: salted butter for smearing on baking dish
ingredients.text: salted butter for smearing on baking dish

instructions: Put 8-inch frying pan on medium heat.
Stir in 2 tbsp oil and chopped onions, saute till translucent and slightly golden.
Stir in chopped tomatoes.
Stir in salt, haldi, red chili pepper and paprika.
Stir for 7-10 minutes over a medium-high heat. The tomatoes should keep their shape somewhat.
Transfer the chopped tomato sauce to the dish.
Put in oven for 15-20 minutes for a soft yolk and 20-25 for a more cooked yolk.

dish_families.name: Spicy Chicken Enchiladas with Our Favourite Enchilada Sauce

variants.name: Spicy Chicken Enchiladas with Our Favourite Enchilada Sauce
variants.dish_family: Spicy Chicken Enchiladas with Our Favourite Enchilada Sauce

ingredients.text: 1 1/4 cup tomato puree or 1 cup passata

ingredients.item: sized white onion or half a large one
ingredients.text: 1 medium sized white onion or half a large one
1-2 diced jalapenos, seeded or otherwise (upto you)
1/2 cup Monterey Jack or Cheddar (or a combo)

instructions: Warm oil in a pot, when it shimmers Stir in the flour and cook for 1-2 minutes on medium, stirring frequently. Stir in red chilli powder and saute (turn your stoves exhaust on for this!) for 30 seconds.
Stir in the rest of the ingredients. Bring to a boil and simmer for 20 minutes, until the sauce has thickened and almost halved. Stir in salt if needed.
Mix the remaining filling ingredients, season. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees.

Warm Corn Tortillas in a little oil in a pan for 30-45 seconds if needed, I usually skip this step since mine are quite soft! Put a few tbsp of filling down the middle of each tortilla, roll and Put in the baking sheet seam side down.
Pour half of the enchilada sauce over the dish making sure to evenly distribute it. You may Stir in more if it is needed. Top with shredded cheese and bake for 25-30 minutes until deliciously bubbly.
Garnish with scallions and dollops of sour cream & serve with the extra Enchilada Sauce on the side.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Spicy Chicken Enchiladas with Our Favourite Enchilada Sauce

Roast at 425 for 45 minutes, insert a skewer to check doneness, it should go through fairly easily.
Sprinkle the ginger mix over the cauliflower at the 45 minute mark (assuming it is fairly tender) and roast for another ten minutes.

variants.name: Vegetable Noodle Spring Rolls
instructions: In a pan heat some oil and saute the minced garlic. On high heat, Cook the carrot and bell pepper. Don't cook for more than 2 mins.
Stir in the cabbage. And then put in all your spices and sauces, keeping the heat on high.

Stir in the spring onions and continue to stir. Dry any moisture and turn off heat. Take a sheet of spring roll. Put it in a shape of a diamond on your working surface. At one end Stir in around 2 tbsp of the filling.
Repeat for the rest of the filling. At this stage, you can freeze them in a single layer and when frozen transfer to a ziplock bag.
For frying, heat oil in your pot. and then Cook these rolls on medium heat till golden on all sides. Take out on a paper towel to drain excess oil.

variants.name: Pakistani Spring Rolls
instructions: Warm 2 tablespoons of oil in a karahi (wok) over high heat. Stir in minced garlic and Cook for 30 seconds until light golden. Stir in the julienned cabbage and carrot.
Leave it to cool at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, or speed it up in the fridge for 15 minutes. A weak wrapper tears when you roll it and definitely tears in the hot oil.

Mix 3 tablespoons of maida with just enough water to make a thick, smooth paste — aim for the consistency of school glue or thick cream. Even 3 minutes of exposure to air will dry them out and make them crack.

Lay one wrapper on a clean dry surface in a diamond position (one corner pointing towards you). Put 2 tablespoons of cooled filling in the lower third of the wrapper — spread it into a horizontal log shape, not a blob. Roll upward firmly, keeping the roll tight.
Pour oil into a karahi or deep pot to a depth of 10 cm. Heat over medium-high heat. If small bubbles fizz around it immediately, the oil is at roughly 175°C — the right temperature.

Gently lower 4-5 spring rolls into the hot oil using a chamcha (ladle) or tongs — do not drop them from a height as hot oil will splash. Cook for 3-4 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden brown all over. The colour should be a rich, uniform amber.
Remove the fried spring rolls with a slotted spoon and lay them on kitchen paper to drain. Let them rest for 1-2 minutes uncovered before serving.

After rolling (before frying), Put the rolls on a baking sheet lined with paper, not touching each other, and freeze for 2 hours until solid. and then transfer to a zip-lock bag and store for up to 3 months. Cook directly from frozen — no thawing needed —.

instructions: Slice tough ends of the marrow and discard, and then cut the marrow into half, lengthwise and and then chop into half moon shapes.

Put a large pan (I use , which is 30cm / 12in) on the stove on medium-high heat and Stir in 3 tablespoons olive oil, shallots, pinch sea salt, turmeric powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, red chili powder and sliced marrow. The marrow will become soft after 7-10.

Turn the heat to high, Stir in the minced garlic and let the marrow turn golden – it should look blistered and slightly charred. If Aim for, you can Stir in more olive oil if the marrow is sticking to the pan.
Put a medium-sized pan on medium-high heat and Stir in the remaining 3tbsp olive oil and sliced fennel. *Saute gently for 10-15 minutes till wilted and bronze around the edges.
Using a slotted spoon, remove the marrow from the pan and transfer to a chopping board (you don’t want to use all the excess olive oil).
Reserve two tablespoons of the fennel to Stir in as a garnish.
Gently Mix chopped marrow and fennel into yoghurt.

variants.name: Stove top Lemon Chicken Roast

ingredients.preparation: start with 2.5, add extra with veggies if needed

instructions: Whisk all the marinade ingredients together, mix well and taste. Put the chicken in a bowl and pour the marinade over, using your hands (gloves or not, upto you) to make sure the marinade works its way in.

After a few hours flip it over and rub the marinade in once more till ready to cook. I suggest marinating for at least 6 hours, but prefer overnight. Take the chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes to an hour before cooking - it will cook more evenly when it is not cold.

Warm a generous lug of oil (about 1/4 cup) in a pot large enough to hold your chicken and veggies on medium high heat. When the oil starts to shimmer carefully put the chicken in on it's back for 2-3 minutes, it will splutter so be careful!

When the back takes on a lovely gold brown and then move the chicken on to one side (leg) to get that lovely colour on each side and and then finally the breasts. If your oil is hot it takes about 3 minutes to get colour. When the chicken breasts are beautifully browned and then Stir in your veggies to the pot.

Bring to a boil and then simmer tightly covered for 25-30 minutes. If it tastes bland your chicken may too so in that case turn the chicken over, Stir in a little sprinkle of salt and let it steam for another few minutes.

3/4 cup strawberries (use your softer ones here)

instructions: Whisk the flour, cornmeal, salt and baking powder in a bowl and set aside. Stir in egg, egg yolk and extracts, mix to Mix.
Gradually Stir in the dry ingredients to the wet just until the mixture comes together. Shape 2/3 of the dough into a disc, wrap in plastic wrap.
Shape the remaining dough into a log, wrap in plastic wrap. Refrigerate for 3-4 hours or overnight.

Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F. Remove the dough disc from the fridge, let it sit for 15 minutes and then use the heel of your palm to flatten it and spread into a unbuttered tart pan, you can also break pieces and press down if that is easier.
Once the dough is evenly spread and then Stir in the filling. Remove the dough log from the fridge, slice into slim rounds and arrange over the filling.
Sprinkle with coarse sugar and bake until the pastry is golden brown, i.e. for 20-25 minutes. Mash the 3/4 cup strawberries, Stir in into a small saucepan, bring to a boil and simmer for 3 minutes.

Strain into a measuring cup and discard the pulp. Stir in just enough water to bring the liquid to 3/4 cup. Stir in the sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice, zest and salt into the saucepan along with the strained juice, bring to a boil, stirring constantly.

Cook till the mixture is thick and clear looking, 3 to 5 minutes. Remove from the heat, cool a little and then Stir in sliced strawberries, let mix cool to room temperature before adding to the crust.
