variants.name: Speedy Sooji ka Halwa: One Pot Recipe

ingredients.text: pinch of salt or sea salt
3/4-1 cup very warm or hot water

instructions: Stir in the butter and cloves into your pan on medium low heat.

Stir in the sooji and roast for 3-5 minutes, stirring frequently, until the sooji smells nutty. The color will darken a little - the aim is not to darken it, but roast it from the inside for the best flavor so don't rush the process! At high heat.
Stir in your sugar (starting with the 1/4 cup), salt, and dry roast for 2-3 minutes.

Stir in the cardamom powder, and let the halwa simmer, stirring occasionally until it starts to glisten. At that point (typically 7-8 minutes) the halwa is done, but you can choose to cook it more to get it to your preferred texture or Stir in water to loosen.
Garnish with chopped almonds or leave plain and enjoy!

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Before touching the suji, dissolve sugar in 2 cups of water in a small saucepan and bring to a boil. Stir in cardamom powder. Keep warm over very low heat.

Warm ghee in a wide, heavy karahi over medium heat. Stir in the suji and stir continuously with a wooden khuncha (spatula). Roast for 8-12 minutes until the suji turns a deep golden colour, smells nutty and toasty, and the ghee starts to look slightly separated.
Turn your face away and pour the hot sugar syrup into the roasted suji in one steady stream while stirring constantly.
Continue stirring on medium heat. The mixture will bubble vigorously, and then gradually absorb the liquid and thicken, 5-7 minutes.

The halwa is done when it pulls cleanly away from the sides of the karahi and holds its shape when you press it with the spatula. Stir in raisins and fold in. Taste — Stir in more sugar if needed (mix into a spoonful of hot water first.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: In a saucepan, bring 4 cups of water to a boil. Stir in sugar and stir until it has dissolved. Remove from heat.
In a heavy bottomed saucepan, heat ghee or oil. Stir in cracked cardamom. Cook on low heat till fragrant for about a minute.
Stir in suji (semolina flour) and roast it on low heat for 8-10 minutes till it begins to puff up. Ghee has a higher smoke point so it will take a longer time to roast.
Once the suji has turned an even golden brown, turn the heat off and Stir in sugar syrup. Turn heat back up and stir well for 5 minutes till the mixture thickens and you get a nice silky texture.
Stir in sliced almonds and stir till well-mixed. Remove from heat.

variants.name: Kashmiri Tabak Maaz
instructions: Rinse under cold water and pat dry with kitchen paper.

In a large, wide degh (pot) or heavy pateela, pour in 1.5 litres of full-fat milk. Stir in to the cold milk: whole fennel seeds, lightly crushed green and black cardamom pods, cinnamon sticks, cloves, turmeric, dry ginger powder, and salt. Stir to Mix.

THE LONG MILK POACH — 60 TO 90 MINUTES: Cook the ribs in the spiced milk at a gentle simmer for 60-90 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes and scraping the bottom of the pot. The milk will gradually reduce, thicken, and turn a beautiful golden colour as the.

THE FRYING STAGE — WHERE THE MAGIC HAPPENS: In a wide, heavy-bottomed karahi or a deep frying pan (the wider the better — Aim for space), heat 3 tbsp of ghee over medium-high heat. Stir in the reduced spiced milk. It will immediately begin to sizzle, bubble, and.
Cook the ribs in the hot ghee-milk mixture over medium-high heat, turning every 3-4 minutes. As the milk caramelises, it will coat the ribs and turn them deep golden-brown.

The finished Tabak Maaz should be deep golden-brown to amber in colour on the outside, with some darker caramelised spots — especially on the fatty sections of the ribs where the fat has rendered and crisped.
Transfer the Tabak Maaz to a wide serving bartan or platter. Pour any remaining caramelised milk from the pan over the top — this is the sauce.

variants.name: Tabak Maaz — Crispy Kashmiri Rib Chops

ingredients.preparation: lamb rib chops / rack of lamb
ingredients.text: 1 kg Chaamp (lamb rib chops / rack of lamb)
1.5 tsp Badiyan ka phool powder (fennel seed powder)

instructions: Mix milk and yogurt together. Whisk in fennel powder, dried ginger, cardamom powder, and salt until combined.

Pour the milk mixture over them — it should come halfway up the ribs. Stir in whole black cardamom and cinnamon stick. Cook covered on medium heat for 45-60 minutes, turning halfway, until the ribs are very tender and the milk has reduced and curdled into a thick.
Remove the ribs and let them air-dry on a rack for 10 minutes.

Warm ghee in a wide, heavy pan until shimmering. Stir in the ribs in a single layer — do not crowd. Cook on medium-high heat for 4-5 minutes per side until the coating is deeply golden-brown and crispy.
Drain on paper towels for 1 minute. Serve immediately — the crunch is at its peak in the first 5 minutes.
Arrange the golden, crispy tabak maaz on a flat platter.

variants.name: Taftan

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp tel ya ghee (oil or ghee)

instructions: In a tiny bowl, Stir in the saffron strands to 3 tablespoons of warm milk. Let it steep for 20 minutes minimum.
Mix the lukewarm water, 1 teaspoon of the sugar, and yeast in a small bowl. Leave 8–10 minutes until foamy.

In a large paraat, Mix flour, remaining sugar, salt, and cardamom powder. Stir in the yeast mixture, warm milk (not the saffron milk), egg yolks, oil or ghee, and half the saffron milk. Mix and knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth, silky, and elastic.
Oil a bowl, Put the dough inside, cover with a damp cloth. Leave in a warm Put for 1–1.5 hours until doubled.
Set your oven to 220°C (430°F). Heat for 30 minutes.
Punch down the risen dough and divide into 5–6 portions. On a lightly floured chakla, roll each portion into an oval shape about 20–22cm long and 6–8mm thick.
Slide the taftan onto the preheated surface in the oven. Bake for 5–7 minutes until the top is golden — darker than sheermal, lighter than bakarkhani.

Remove from the oven and brush once more with any remaining saffron milk or a little melted ghee. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving — unlike naan, taftan benefits from resting briefly, which allows the steam inside to distribute evenly and the crust to soften slightly.

instructions: Warm ghee/oil in a heavy pot. Stir in zeera and let it splutter 30 seconds. Stir in sliced onion and cook until golden.
Stir in tomatoes, haldi, lal mirch, dhania, and salt. Cook on medium heat until tomatoes break down and oil separates, about 8 minutes. Stir in hari mirch whole.
Stir in aloo quarters and stir to coat in the masala. Cook 3-4 minutes on medium heat.
Stir in 600ml water to the pot. Bring to boil. Stir in soaked basmati.
Open, fluff gently, and scatter fresh dhania over the top.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Warm oil in a medium-sized stockpot. Lower heat and Stir in crushed ginger and garlic. Cook for 30 seconds, making sure they don’t burn.
Stir in kalonji, turmeric and red chili powder and Cook for about a minute till they stop smelling raw.
Increase heat and Stir in potatoes. Stir in salt. Cook till they are cooked through, about 10 minutes.
Stir in rice and stir it in with the potatoes.
Stir in 4 cups water and bring to a boil. Lower heat to a simmer and let the water boil out, another 10 minutes. Remove from heat.
Turn the heat back up and dial to lowest possible point. Let the rice steam for another 10 minutes.
Remove from heat, and serve with a curry of your choice, or simply a side of yogurt or chutney.

Time to Stir in your meat, make sure to brown it evenly, once it is browned on each side Stir in two cups of very hot water and cover your pot. For instant pot Stir in 1.5 cup water. Bring the liquid in the pot to boil, and then simmer for 45 minutes or an hour to get the meat super tender.

Dry up the water in the pot till the masala looks decidedly jammy and Stir in your tomato paste, check for seasoning. Stir in your garam masala, half your green chillies and half your cilantro. Give it a whirl and let it cook on low for 3-4 minutes and then take it off the heat.

variants.name: Tandoori Roti

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp ghee ya makhan (ghee or butter)

instructions: Stir in warm water gradually — start with 1⁄2 cup and mix with your fingers. Stir in more water slowly, a tablespoon at a time, until the dough just comes together. Knead for 6–8 minutes until smooth.
Divide the rested dough into 6 equal balls — slightly smaller than chapati balls since tandoori roti is rolled thicker.

Dust a dough ball lightly in flour and Put on your chakla (rolling board). Roll with the belan (rolling pin) to a circle about 16–18 cm across. Rotate the dough a quarter turn after each roll to keep it round.
If you have access to a tandoor: get it very hot (minimum 20–30 minutes of heating). After 2–3 minutes: charred spots will appear on the surface, and the roti will puff slightly.
Turn the oven to its maximum temperature (250°C / 480°F) and switch on the grill/broiler function. Allow the oven and pan to heat for at least 15 minutes — the pan must be scorching hot.

Carefully remove the hot cast-iron pan from the oven using thick oven mitts — it is extremely hot. Slide the pan back onto the top rack under the broiler/grill. Bake for 3–4 minutes, watching through the oven window.
Using a pastry brush or simply by smearing with the back of a spoon, brush a generous layer of ghee or butter over the hot surface. The ghee should melt immediately and soak slightly into the bread.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Mix chicken with yoghurt, ginger garlic paste, half the spices, and salt. Marinate 30 minutes.
Warm oil on highest flame. Sear marinated chicken pieces until deeply browned on all sides, 8-10 minutes total.
In same pan, quickly cook tomatoes with remaining dry spices on high heat for 8 minutes until very thick.
Return chicken to masala. Toss to coat. Stir in green chillies.

variants.name: Tawa Chicken — Lahori Street Style

ingredients.text: 6-8 whole or halved hari mirch (green chillies)
1 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)
0.5 tsp kali mirch powder (black pepper powder)

instructions: Before you turn on the heat, have everything ready: chicken pieces on a plate, tomatoes chopped into large chunks, green chillies halved lengthwise, ginger julienned, garlic sliced, all spices measured and combined in a small bowl, butter and oil measured, and coriander chopped.
Put your largest, heaviest tawa (flat griddle) or cast iron frying pan on the stove over HIGH heat. Leave it to heat for 3-4 minutes until it is extremely hot.

Stir in the oil to the hot tawa, and then immediately Stir in the butter. The butter will melt and immediately begin to foam and brown — this is fine. Working quickly, Stir in the chicken pieces in a single layer.

Stir in the sliced garlic and julienned ginger directly onto the hot tawa around the chicken pieces. Use the khurpa (spatula) to keep them moving — at this heat they can go from golden to burnt in 30 seconds. Stir and scrape constantly for 1-2 minutes until the.

Stir in the chopped tomatoes and green chillies to the tawa. Stir in all the spices (salt, red chilli powder, coriander-cumin, turmeric, black pepper) over the top. Use the khurpa to vigorously chop, stir, and scrape everything together — press the tomatoes against the hot iron to break.
After 10 minutes of vigorous tawa cooking, check if the chicken is cooked through.

Sprinkle the garam masala over the tawa and stir it in — garam masala is always added at the very end because heat destroys its volatile aromatics. Stir in another tablespoon of butter and let it melt into the dish. Use the khurpa to give it one final.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Warm a large concave tawa or heavy wok on highest flame. Stir in oil. When smoking hot, Stir in chicken pieces and sear on all sides for 6-8 minutes.
In the same tawa, Cook onions until golden, 6-7 minutes. Stir in ginger garlic paste, Cook 2 minutes. Stir in Kashmiri mirch, regular chilli, coriander powder, black pepper, and salt.
Stir in chopped tomatoes to spiced onion masala. Cook on high heat for 10-12 minutes until completely broken down and masala is thick. Mash tomatoes aggressively as they cook.
Stir in green chillies and toss to coat.
Cook on medium-high for 15-18 minutes, tossing every 3-4 minutes. Stir in 1 tbsp butter halfway through.
Stir in remaining butter, garam masala, and crushed kasuri methi. Toss vigorously for 2 minutes.

variants.name: Karachi Tawa Chicken

ingredients.text: 2.5 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
1.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Warm tawa or karahi on maximum heat with oil. Stir in chicken and sear aggressively for 5-6 minutes. Karachi cooking is done on higher heat than Lahori — crank it up.
In the centre, Cook onions for 5-6 minutes until golden. Stir in ginger garlic paste and Cook 2 minutes. Mix with chicken.
Stir in all dry spices to the tawa. Stir aggressively for 1 minute. The spices should bloom and coat the chicken directly, not just in a separate masala.
Stir in tomatoes and cook on high heat for 10-12 minutes. Karachi masala should be slightly more liquid than Lahori — don't reduce it completely.
Stir in green chillies and bhuno on high heat for 12-15 minutes until chicken is fully cooked and masala coats everything.
Toss quickly to coat. Garnish with fresh coriander.

variants.name: Tehri - a Chatpata Version

ingredients.item: to 2 cups potatoes sliced into 1/2 cm thick squares
ingredients.text: 1 1/2 to 2 cups potatoes sliced into 1/2 cm thick squares

ingredients.item: a glug of neutral oil - enough to cook the bottom of your pan
ingredients.text: a glug of neutral oil - enough to cook the bottom of your pan

ingredients.item: optional: lemon for squeezing, green chilies for garnish
ingredients.text: optional: lemon for squeezing, green chilies for garnish

instructions: Take out a nice big pot, preferably non stick, but if you use a heavy bottomed one and then increase the oil and make sure you keep checking for sticking (Stir in a little water).
Warm the oil and Stir in in your cumin seeds, nigella seeds, and curry leaves.
When it gets spluttery and aromatic Stir in your onions and green chillies and saute on until the onion starts to brown at the edges.
And then Stir in the rest of your spices and stir Cook until they darken slightly, if they stick to the bottom of the pan Stir in a splash of water.
And then Stir in your tomatoes and cooked till the 'wetness' sautes out and you're life with a rich paste with the oil rising above it - in Urdu we call this Bhunna.
Stir in your potatoes and saute for a minute or two.

Stir in your rice, and and then Stir in just enough water that you have approximately half an inch of water rising above your rice. some brands cook quicker than others so please adjust the water accordingly. In a pinch you can Stir in more, but taking water.
Bring the water to a boil, and cook on medium till the water level drops to that off the rice, and then simmer on low heat to tender fluffy perfection.

variants.name: The Best Chicken Jalfrezi!

ingredients.text: 1 large chunk of ginger (minced (about 1-2 tbsp, minced))
1 tsp tomato puree/concentrate (optional but highly recommended)
2 tsp paprika or Kashmir chilli powder

ingredients.item: boneless chicken, cut into bite-sized pieces, preferably thigh
ingredients.text: 1.8 lb boneless chicken, cut into bite-sized pieces, preferably thigh

ingredients.preparation: preferably different colours, diced into bite-sized pieces
ingredients.text: 3 capsicums (preferably different colours, diced into bite-sized pieces)

instructions: Prepare all ingredients before heating the pan.
Warm the cooking fat and cook onions, whole bulb of garlic, minced, chunk of ginger (minced (about 1-2 tbsp, minced)), green chillies until softened and aromatic.

Stir in green chillies, paprika or Kashmir chilli powder, crushed black pepper, coriander powder, cumin seeds, turmeric powder, then add the whole bulb of garlic, minced and coat it thoroughly in the masala.
Add the listed liquid ingredients as needed, cover and simmer until the main ingredient is fully cooked.
Reduce the sauce to the intended consistency, adjust the seasoning and finish with chunk of ginger (minced (about 1-2 tbsp, minced)), coriander powder, Fresh coriander.

variants.name: The BEST Green Beans Sabzi

ingredients.item: Green Beans cut into 2 cm pieces
ingredients.text: 3-3.5 cups Green Beans cut into 2 cm pieces

instructions: Warm the oils in a large pan/wok on medium high heat.
Stir in the seeds and let them sizzle.
Stir in the crushed ginger, give it a quick stir and Stir in the green beans.
Stir in in about a teaspoon of salt, your 1/2 tsp of chili powder and the 1/4 tsp of turmeric and stir to Mix.
Let cook uncovered without stirring for 4-5 minutes, the beans will start to char.
Move them around cook for another 4-5 minutes and test for doneness and seasoning.
Stir in your sliced green chilies, mix, cook for a minute more and serve.

variants.name: The EASIEST Chicken Broth EVER
instructions: Put the chicken bones, water, whole spices and listed aromatics in a deep pot.
Bring to a boil and skim any foam from the surface.
Lower the heat and simmer gently until the main ingredient is fully cooked and the broth is flavourful.
Strain if a clear broth is required, remove excess fat and adjust the salt before serving or storing.

variants.name: Balochi Tikka

ingredients.text: 700 g gosht ya murgh (mutton or chicken)

instructions: Mix yoghurt, grated ginger, garlic, crushed black pepper and cumin, salt, oil, and lemon. Coat meat cubes thoroughly.
30 minutes to 2 hours is enough.
Skewer meat and grill over maximum charcoal heat for 3-4 minutes per side. Grill whole green chillies alongside.
Let kebabs rest on skewers for 2-3 minutes. Season with a final pinch of crushed black pepper and a generous squeeze of lemon. Arrange alongside the grilled green chillies.

variants.name: Lahori Tikka Boti

ingredients.text: 1 kg Bakra Gosht / Mutton Boti (Bone-in Mutton Chunks)
2 tsp Kachri Powder (Raw Papaya / Green Papaya Powder)
1 tsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)

ingredients.item: (citric acid) or 2 tbsp (lemon juice) Khatai (Citric Acid) or Lemon
ingredients.text: 1 tsp (citric acid) or 2 tbsp (lemon juice) Khatai (Citric Acid) or Lemon

instructions: In a large bartan (bowl), Mix the hung dahi (yoghurt), adrak-lehsan paste, tikka masala, lal mirch powder, zeera powder, kachri powder, haldi, khatai or lemon juice, oil, and namak. Mix thoroughly until you have a uniform, thick, brick-red paste.

Stir in the scored mutton pieces to the marinade and work it in with your hands — get the paste into every cut, under any loose flaps of meat, and coat every surface thoroughly. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or transfer to a zip-lock bag and refrigerate.

If using a charcoal grill or sigri, light the coals well in advance — Aim for them to be fully ashen and glowing red-orange, with no visible black coal remaining. Good coal is grey, glowing, and radiating intense, even heat. If using a gas grill, preheat on high.

Thread the marinated boti onto metal skewers — heavy, flat skewers (not thin round ones) hold the meat better and conduct heat through the centre. Put the skewers over the hot coals and don't touch for 3-4 minutes.
This step is non-negotiable and almost universally skipped at home. Once off the grill, rest the tikka boti on a plate loosely covered with foil for 5 minutes.
For the full Lahori restaurant experience, heat a cast-iron plate (or a regular heavy metal plate) on the stove until screaming hot.

variants.name: Karachi Tikka Boti

ingredients.text: 1 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)
1.5 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)

instructions: Cut boneless chicken into uniform 1.5-inch cubes.
Mix all marinade ingredients. Even 1-2 hours of marinating is enough for small boti pieces — the surface area to volume ratio means the marinade penetrates faster than with large pieces.
Grill on highest heat available for 3-4 minutes per side.
Remove and check — cut into a piece.
Boti is best eaten the moment it comes off the grill.

variants.name: Timatar Aloo Ki Bhujia

ingredients.text: 1 tsp red chilli powder (or to taste)

instructions: Prepare all ingredients before heating the pan.
Warm the cooking fat and cook red chilli powder until softened and aromatic.
Stir in cumin seeds, turmeric powder, red chilli powder, chopped coriander, then add the oil and coat it thoroughly in the masala.
Add the listed liquid ingredients as needed, cover and simmer until the main ingredient is fully cooked.
Reduce the sauce to the intended consistency, adjust the seasoning and finish with chopped coriander, chopped mint.

variants.name: Alcohol-Free Tiramisu
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.
instructions: Brew the coffee and cool it completely before assembly.
Beat mascarpone, icing sugar and vanilla briefly until smooth. Do not overbeat mascarpone because it can split.
Whip the cold cream to medium peaks and fold it gently into the mascarpone mixture.
Dip each sponge finger quickly in coffee and arrange a snug layer in the dish. Spread over half the mascarpone cream.
Repeat with another dipped sponge layer and the remaining cream. Cover and chill for at least 8 hours.
Sift cocoa over the top immediately before serving. Keep refrigerated.

variants.name: Turkey Sandwiches Three Ways

ingredients.item: Sprinkling of your favourite spice mix - Cajun, Tandoori, Salt + Chili Powder + Cumin
ingredients.text: Sprinkling of your favourite spice mix - Cajun, Tandoori, Salt + Chili Powder + Cumin
2 tbsp buffalo hot sauce (if using other omit ketchup)

ingredients.item: slices deli turkey meat, cut in half for easier filling!
ingredients.text: 6 slices deli turkey meat, cut in half for easier filling!

instructions: Layer on half the turkey, roll up, and cut into spirals.
Mix the first 6 ingredients for the sauce.
Cut croissant across making sure not to separate it into two pieces and slather on some buffalo mayo on both 'sides'.
Stir in the turkey, greens, and cheese.
Butter both sides of the bread, spread the chutney, Stir in the turkey, cut into tiny sandwiches for prettier presentation.

dish_families.name: Velvety Caramel Custard or Caramel Flan

variants.name: Velvety Caramel Custard or Caramel Flan
variants.dish_family: Velvety Caramel Custard or Caramel Flan

ingredients.preparation: Whole preferred, but nothing lower than 2%
ingredients.text: 2 cups Milk (Whole preferred, but nothing lower than 2%)

ingredients.preparation: Whipping or Table, either is fine. Half in Half works too
ingredients.text: 1 cup Cream (Whipping or Table, either is fine. Half in Half works too)

instructions: Preheat your oven to 325 degrees F and Put the roasting pan with an inch or two of water inside the oven. Pour the water into a heavy bottomed pan and and then sprinkle your sugar over top. Do not stir.
Keep the pan on medium heat and keep a close eye on the sugar, but again do not stir. As soon as it turns a beautiful amber colour pour it into your custard dish.

There is loads of beautiful caramel flavour still in the pan you used for caramelizing the sugar so pour your liquids into the pan along with the sugar and the salt and warm through stirring occasionally. Take your milk off the heat. Crack 6 eggs into your blender along with the vanilla extract and pulse/blend slightly to create an even mix.

While your blender is running on low pour the milk mix into the blender through the feed tube/opening, stop running the blender as soon as it is all in. If you are not comfortable pouring while blending and then just wait for your milk to cool to room. Pour the mixture into your caramel dish, you can remove the foam from the.

Put the pan inside the roasting pan with water and gently pour in more hot water so that only the top inch of the pan isn't submerged. Bake until the sides are set and the center is still jiggly, 50- 55 minutes for a loaf pan, 40-45 for a round pan.

Cool completely (4 hours+ in the fridge) and then run a knife along the edges to seperate them. Invert in a dish with high sides and pour the remaining caramel sauce in the pan into another small bowl for your grateful loved ones.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Velvety Caramel Custard or Caramel Flan

variants.name: Walnut Crumb Cake
instructions: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F, grease a square cake dish - mine is 8**.
Cut the butter into small pieces and Mix it with the remaining ingredients in a small bowl, crumbling the mix together with your fingers.
Stir together your flour, baking powder and salt in a small bowl.
Cream the brown sugar and butter together till creamy and fluffy - 3 to 4 minutes.
Stir in eggs one by one, mixing 30 seconds between each addition.
Stir in in the vanilla, mix till combined.
With the mixer on low alternately Stir in the dry ingredients and milk, mix until combined.
Bake for 30 minutes or until a skewer inserted in the middle comes out clean.

dish_families.name: Weeknight Dahi Chicken (Chicken with Yogurt Curry) Recipe

variants.name: Weeknight Dahi Chicken (Chicken with Yogurt Curry) Recipe
variants.dish_family: Weeknight Dahi Chicken (Chicken with Yogurt Curry) Recipe

ingredients.item: (about 1 pound and 1 ounce) chicken with-bone, preferably thighs, cut in medium-sized pieces
ingredients.text: 1/2 kilogram (about 1 pound and 1 ounce) chicken with-bone, preferably thighs, cut in medium-sized pieces

instructions: Roast the spice blend in a small frying or saucepan over low heat for roughly 2 minutes or until fragrant. Remove from heat and let it come to room temperature. Transfer to a spice grinder and pulse until coarsely ground.

Stir in yogurt, salt and garlic and ginger paste to a large bowl, and whisk until well-mixed. Fold in the freshly ground masala, and mix well. Stir in chicken to the yogurt marinade, and coat it well.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat oil over medium heat. Once it begins to shimmer, Stir in the chicken with the yogurt marinade. Bring heat to low, and cover with a tight fitting lid.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Weeknight Dahi Chicken (Chicken with Yogurt Curry) Recipe

variants.name: White Sauce Chicken Pasta Bake

ingredients.preparation: chopped into bite size pieces and seasoned with salt and pepper
ingredients.text: 150-200 g chicken (half a chicken breast) (chopped into bite size pieces and seasoned with salt and pepper)

ingredients.item: shredded cheese (monterey jack or cheddar preferred) )
ingredients.text: 200 g shredded cheese (monterey jack or cheddar preferred) )

ingredients.item: pasta - shells , penne, bow tie, small rigatoni
ingredients.text: 8 oz pasta - shells , penne, bow tie, small rigatoni

instructions: Put two pots on the stove - one with salted water to boil pasta and one with two tbsp of oil. When the oil is hot Stir in the chicken pieces, cook one side on medium high for 2-3 minutes, and then flip over and cook until the chicken is cooked through - another 2-3 minutes.

Remove the chicken from the pot, leave any extra oil and Stir in the mushrooms on medium high heat - saute until cooked through, season with salt and pepper. Stir in the chopped spinach until it wilts and and then remove the spinach into the same dish as the chicken.

Stir in the butter and when it melts Stir in in the green chilies and diced onions. Saute for a minute on medium heat. Sprinkle the flour over stirring frequently until the color changes and it smells a little toasty - 3-5 minutes.

Stir in a cup of the milk and whisk and then gradually Stir in the rest. Put your pasta into boil - boil according to package directions until al dente if you like it soft (it will bake in the oven) or a minute less for more of a bite. Remember to reserve a cup of pasta water when you drain it.

Stir in the bouillon cube (crumble it by hand), and bring the mix to a boil and then simmer (stirring frequently) until thickened - about 10-12 minutes. Once the white sauce has thickened turn off the stove and stir in the nutmeg, chicken, mushrooms, and half cheese (optional). taste for seasoning - Aim for to Stir in a fat pinch of pepper.

Stir in the cooked pasta, adding the reserved pasta water to loosen the sauce if needed - how much tends to vary by shape. Bake at 400F for 15-20 minutes to meld the flavors and then broil for another 2-3 to get that lovely crispy cheese.

dish_families.name: Winning at Life Soft Cinnamon Rolls

variants.name: Winning at Life Soft Cinnamon Rolls
variants.dish_family: Winning at Life Soft Cinnamon Rolls

ingredients.preparation: hot to touch but not boiling
ingredients.text: 1 cup very warm milk (hot to touch but not boiling)
3/4 cup brown sugar (packed, dark brown works best)

ingredients.preparation: if you're a cinnamon fan then you can go up to 3
ingredients.text: 2.5 tbsp cinnamon (if you're a cinnamon fan then you can go up to 3)

instructions: Mix your warm milk and sugar in a large bowl, scatter over the yeast and let it stand for 5-10 minutes or until very foamy (it'll smell like you're baking bread). Stir in in your egg (whisked) and melted butter.
Stir in your remaining dough ingredients to make a craggy dough. Tip the dough out onto a lightly floured board and knead it for 5-8 minutes until smooth and form into a ball.
Put the ball in a lightly greased bowl and cover with a clean kitchen towel. Mix all the filling ingredients in a bowl and set aside.

Roll it out in to roughly an 14*18 inch rectangle - the shape doesn't have to be perfect but if yours is very uneven and then simply trim the edges. Spread the cinnamon filling over top - it will be a thin layer.
Roll the dough into a tight spiral starting from the 18 inch side and and then cut into 12 even pieces. Bake at 350F for 20-22 minutes or until golden.
Mix 4 oz cream cheese and 1.5 tbsp room temperatue with an electric mixer till smooth. On low speed Stir in in 1 cup icing sugar, 1/2 tsp vanilla, and 2 tbsp milk until well combined.
Let the rolls cool for a few minutes and then slather with cream cheese frosting, get a generous layer on top.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Winning at Life Soft Cinnamon Rolls

variants.name: Zarda - Pakistani Sweet Rice
instructions: Rinse and soak the rice, then boil it in plenty of water until almost tender and drain well.
Warm the ghee with the whole spices; add the sugar and listed liquid ingredients to make a light syrup.
Fold in the rice, food colour, fruit and nuts without crushing the grains.
Cover tightly and finish over very low heat until the syrup is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Rest for 10 minutes, fluff gently and add the reserved garnish.

variants.name: Shahi Zarda

ingredients.text: 0.25 tsp Peela Food Colour (Yellow Food Colour)

instructions: Rinse the basmati chawal (rice) under cold water until the water runs clear — this removes excess starch that would make the grains sticky. and then soak in fresh cold water for 30 minutes. While soaking, bloom your saffron: warm 4 tbsp milk or water to just hand-hot.

Bring a large pateela (pot) of water to a rolling boil — at least 4-5 litres for 3 cups of rice. Stir in the crushed elaichi pods (cardamom), laung (cloves), and a pinch of salt. Drain the soaked rice and Stir in it to the boiling water.

In a wide degh (heavy pot), Mix the cheeni (sugar) with 1.5 cups water. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves. and then stop stirring and boil for 3-4 minutes until you have a light one-string syrup.

In a separate small pan, heat 2 tbsp of the ghee over medium heat. Stir in the drained kishmish (raisins) first — they plump and caramelise in about 1 minute, so watch them. In the same pan, Cook the slivered badam (almonds) until faintly golden, about 2 minutes.

Pour the remaining ghee into the degh over medium heat. Stir in the parboiled, drained rice and gently fold it through the ghee — try not to break the grains. Pour the saffron sugar syrup over the rice and fold gently to Mix.

To do dum, first spread the rice in an even layer in the degh. Put a flat tawa (griddle) under the degh — this distributes heat and prevents the bottom from burning. Cover the degh with a tight-fitting lid.

Turn off the heat and leave the lid on for 10 minutes without opening — this resting period lets the steam settle and the flavours meld. Transfer to a serving platter and scatter the remaining fried nuts on top.

variants.name: Zarda — Pakistani Wedding-Style Sweet Rice
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil with a generous pinch of salt. Drain the soaked basmati and Stir in it to the boiling water. Cook for 6-7 minutes until the rice is 70% cooked — it should be tender outside but still have a chalky.

In a separate wide karahi (wok) or heavy pot, Mix sugar with 200ml water. Cook over medium heat, stirring until sugar dissolves, and then bring to a boil. Cook for 5 minutes until a slightly sticky one-thread syrup forms.
In a large, wide karahi, heat ghee over medium heat. Stir in whole cardamom, cloves, and bay leaves. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the parboiled rice to the spiced ghee and stir gently to coat. Pour the sugar syrup over the rice. Stir in saffron water and food colour if using.
Reduce heat to the lowest setting. Cover the karahi tightly — use foil under the lid for a good seal. Cook on dum for 20-25 minutes until the rice is fully cooked and has absorbed all the syrup.
Remove the lid. Taste — if it needs more sweetness, Stir in a spoonful of sugar syrup.
Arrange extra nuts and raisins decoratively on top.

variants.name: Sindhi Zarda — Fragrant Sweet Rice with Coconut
instructions: Boil a large pot of water. Stir in soaked, drained basmati and cook for 6 minutes until 70% done — grains should be tender on the outside with a visible white centre. Drain completely and spread on a tray to cool slightly.
In a karahi, dissolve sugar in 150ml water over medium heat. Boil for 4 minutes to form a light syrup. Stir in saffron water and stir.

In a separate large, wide karahi, heat ghee over medium heat. Stir in cardamom pods and Cook 30 seconds. Stir in grated fresh coconut and Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until it turns light golden.
Stir in the parboiled rice to the karahi with the coconut mixture. Pour the saffron syrup over everything. Gently fold to Mix without breaking grains.
Seal the karahi tightly with foil, and then the lid. Cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes.
Plate on a wide thaal and garnish with extra nuts and a sprinkle of reserved coconut.

source_attributions.recipe_title: Sindhi Zarda — Fragrant Sweet Rice with Coconut

variants.name: Zeera Rice

ingredients.item: neutral oil such as corn or sunflower
ingredients.text: 1/4 cup neutral oil such as corn or sunflower

ingredients.item: yellow onion ((this is about 1/2 of a medium onion), sliced into 1/2 moon shapes.)
ingredients.text: 1/2 cup yellow onion ((this is about 1/2 of a medium onion), sliced into 1/2 moon shapes.)

instructions: Put a medium-sized heavy-bottomed pot on medium heat and Stir in oil.
Stir in sliced onions to this and sauté for 15-20 minutes till the white of the onion is no longer visible and the onions have turned a dark golden-brown colour.
Stir in peppercorns, cloves, black cardamom, cinnamon stick, and cumin to onions. Drain rice and Stir in to the pot.
Turn the heat to high and pour in boiling water. As soon as it starts to bubble, cover with a tea cloth and lid and turn the heat to low.
Allow rice to cook for 15 minutes, do not open the lid before the total time has elapsed.
Remove rice from the burner and allow it to rest for another 15 minutes without opening the lid.

variants.name: Zinger Burger — Pakistani Street Style
instructions: Prepare the chicken marinade: In a large bowl, Mix white vinegar, mustard paste, garlic powder, white pepper, paprika, red chilli powder, and 1⁄2 tsp salt. Mix into a smooth paste. Stir in the pounded chicken breast fillets and coat thoroughly, massaging the marinade into the meat.
In a medium bowl, Mix finely shredded cabbage and grated carrot. Stir in mayonnaise, a pinch of sugar, and a splash of vinegar. Mix well, cover, and refrigerate.
Whisk until smooth and uniformly pink-orange. Taste and adjust: more chilli garlic for heat, more ketchup for sweetness.

In a shallow dish (tray or plate), Mix all-purpose flour, cornflour, rice flour, 1⁄2 tsp salt, 1⁄2 tsp white pepper, 1⁄2 tsp garlic powder, and 1⁄2 tsp paprika. Mix thoroughly with your fingers. In a second shallow dish, beat 2 eggs with 1⁄2 cup milk until well combined.

Double-coat each fillet: Take a marinated chicken piece, dredge it thoroughly in the dry flour mix, pressing firmly so it adheres. Return the fillet to the dry flour mix and coat again, this time pressing harder to create craggy, jagged peaks on the surface — these nooks and.

Warm oil in a deep wok (kadhai) or heavy-bottomed pot to 170°C (medium heat). Cook the coated fillets in batches — do not overcrowd. Cook for 5–7 minutes per side until deep golden brown and cooked through.

Toast the burger buns: Heat a tawa (flat griddle) or non-stick pan over medium heat. Spread a thin layer of butter on the cut sides of each bun. Put butter-side down on the hot tawa and toast until golden brown with visible butter sizzle marks, about 1–2 minutes.
Stir in a layer of cold coleslaw. Stir in a cheese slice if using.
